#7,323
Achilles was loving the tour of the castle. He was full of questions, pointing out everything of interest to him and wanting to know all about it. 'What material is that chandelier made from?' 'What magic causes that stone to glow?' 'How did you come to possess skeletal servants?' I patiently answered everything he asked me. A smile stayed fixed on his face throughout.

"I think that's enough for now." I said at length. We'd arrived in the wing of the castle I'd marked off for his rooms. "Allow me to show you your quarters, then I'll leave you to get settled in."

Achilles followed behind me, pausing for a moment, listening. He turned around. I followed his gaze and smiled. A woman in purple robes was following us down the hall.

"Medea," I greeted.

"Master," my Queen returned, though her focus was on my companion.

"Medea, meet Achilles, my new Knight. Achilles, meet Medea of Colchis, my Queen and second in command." I quickly introduced them.

"Welcome, Achilles." Medea said. "Your father was a great man and a greater friend. I expect we will get along well."

Achilles watched her closely. "I have heard many stories of you, Medea."

Medea smiled, amused. "I imagine few of them were pleasant. I will just have to change your estimation of me then. I believe arming you would be a good start, no? Come, I will have you fitted for armor and weapons in short order."

Achilles looked down at himself. He still wore the simple grey robe that had appeared around him upon his reincarnation. A sturdy, though plain, sword was sheathed on a belt at his waist. "I would appreciate new armaments. I was unable to bring those I had in life with me to the Underworld. I would also like an opportunity to stretch my legs. It has been too long since I fought a true battle."

Medea chuckled, shooting me a knowing look. "I am sure Coal would be more than willing to assist our new Knight."

"Coal?" Achilles said, shooting me a questioning look.

"One of my Pawns. Before he became a devil, he was the Colchian Dragon that guarded the Golden Fleece." I clarified.

Achilles froze. A grin slowly spread across his face. His breathing picked up, excited. "Forgive me, Medea, but might I be fitted for armor after I face Coal?"

Medea nodded easily. "Of course. I can begin without you present. What weapons would you like me to begin working on?"

"A spear, a sword, a dagger and a shield if you would. Where might I find Coal?"

Grinning, I held my hand up to my mouth. A small Hole opened in my palm. "Coal? You feeling up to a spar?"

"Always, master! Are you trying to stretch your legs?" came Coal's eager reply.

"Not me. Our newest Knight. Achilles expressed interest in training after so long in the Underworld."

There was silence on the other side of the Hole.

"Coal? Are you still there?" I called out, confused.

"Master… Is this Achilles the Achilles?" Coal asked, awe in his voice.

That's right. I hadn't told Coal who I was going to recruit. Not through any intention to keep information from him. He'd just been out with Aqua when Medea and I were planning things.

"He is." I confirmed.

"Can I go get Regulus first? It'll only take a minute. Aqua can transport us."

I pursed my lips. I really didn't want the fact that I had Achilles in my peerage to get out before the Rating Game.

"Who is Regulus?" Achilles asked.

"The Nemean Lion." Medea supplied helpfully.

Achilles's teeth were practically shining with how bright he was smiling. I couldn't take this away from him. He seemed way too excited.

"Fine." I said. "But make sure Regulus knows he can't tell anyone outside of Sairaorg's peerage about Achilles. We're trying to keep him a secret for now."

"You got it, master!" came Coal's excited reply. "Tell Achilles I'll meet him in the Coliseum in a few minutes. Aqua! Aqua, where are you!" I heard crashing through the Hole as Coal ran off to find Aqua. I closed the Hole.

"You remember how to get back here, right?" I asked Achilles.

He nodded, distracted.

"Alright. Your rooms are right over there. They should have everything you need. If you're missing anything, either tell one of the animated armors or press one of the stones in the walls and say either my name or Medea's. We'll get whatever problem you have sorted out. Coal will meet you in the coliseum in a minute. There's plenty of weapons and armor in the armory there. Feel free to use whatever you want." I opened a Hole. "This'll take you right to it. I'll…see you later." I finished lamely. He'd practically leapt through the Hole the moment I told him it would take him to battle the Colchian Dragon and the Nemean Lion.

Medea chuckled to herself. "I believe he will fit in well around here."

"I hope so. He's stuck with us forever. It would be a shame if we didn't get along." I said.

"Only one left to recruit now. Are you still intending to find someone before our Rating Game with Roygun?"

"That's the hope. I have someone in mind if you'd be willing to look into them?"

"Of course."

"Thanks, Medea."

Music started playing. It took me far too long to realize my phone was ringing. I used it so rarely that I'd forgotten what the ring tone sounded like.

"Hello?" I said as I picked up.

"Are you busy?" a very tired sounding Serafall said.

"Not at the moment. What can I–"

"Come to my office." The line went dead.

"Trouble?" Medea asked, frowning.

"I'll let you know when I figure that out. Can you make sure Achilles gets settled?"

She nodded. "Leave it to me. I'll make sure everything is to his liking when I deliver his weapons."

"Thanks, Medea. I don't know what I'd do without you." I leaned in and stole a quick kiss, then stepped backwards into a Hole.

Serafall's secretary waved me through the second I walked through the doors. It was a short trip up to her office. I knocked on the door and it swung open to allow me inside.

Everything was the same as the last time I'd been here. Everything save Serafall herself. The last time I'd been in her office, she hadn't been laying on her back atop her desk with her eyes closed and a stack of papers under her head as a pillow.

"Serafall?" I said, hesitantly stepping closer. "Everything alright?"

"No." she said, eyes still closed. "Everything is not alright. I have spent the last fourteen hours sprinting between meetings and phone calls trying to avert a war. I am tired. I am pissed off. And I'm not even supposed to be here!" she sat bolt upright as she finished, hair flying wildly around her, eyes murderous. "I took the whole week off to shoot my show! Then some Grecian dumbass tries to kill a bunch of way too important devils! Then a bigger dumbass goes and blows up a fucking island!" Serafall rounded on me. I froze in terror underneath her gaze.

"You!" she snarled, jabbing a finger at me.

"What did I do!" I tried to sound dignified when I said it. It came out as more of a squeak. Serafall could be downright terrifying.

Serafall levitated off her desk, hair floating around her shoulders. The air shuddered as she drifted towards me. "You are going to take me on a nice vacation somewhere where I don't have a cell signal, and you are going to do it right now. Okay? Consider it thanks for dealing with all of this bullshit on your behalf."

"Um… By no cell signal, do you mean…?"

"Anywhere other than here." Serafall growled.

"Copy that. Anywhere else, coming right up." I connected to Bedeze's King Piece and opened a Hole to the first world that came to mind.

Serafall stomped past me through the Hole. I followed, sedated, behind her. I emerged onto a dirt road in the middle of a forest.

Ahead of me, Serafall let out a long sigh, as if she'd just escaped a load greater than that of Atlas. She fell to the ground on the side of the road and just lay there, breathing deep with her eyes closed.

"Um… Serafall?"

"Sorry for being a bitch." she said, voice quiet. "I'm just really overworked and needed to take an hour or so to myself. Every time I tried, some asshole would burst into my office or light my phone up until I answered. Most of it turned out to be pointless nonsense. You're my excuse to not talk to people right now. If anyone asks, I interviewed you about your experience during the attack."

"Copy that." I said easily, relaxing now that I realized I wasn't the person that had managed to piss her off. She was just venting frustration.

Serafall let out another long sigh, then slowly forced herself up into a sitting position. Eyebrows furrowed, she looked around. "Where are we?"

"Faerun, a little outside of Neverwinter. This is the first place I took you."

"The place where all your mines are?"

"That's the one. They aren't all here, but the vast majority are."

"Do they have wine in Faerun?"

"They have just about every liquor you've ever heard of and a fair few you haven't."

"Good." Serafall stood, dusting herself off. "Let's go find some."

"Don't you have to go back to work after this? Is day drinking really–"

"I'm a Satan! One drink isn't going to ruin me, Balthazar. Now hurry up and show me to a bar!" She started walking down the road.

"The city's in the other direction." I called after her, an amused smile on my face.

Serafall spun on her heel and started marching the other way. I fell in beside her.

"How far away is it?" Serafall asked.

"A fair distance. I can get us to the treeline with a Hole. From there, the city will be in sight. It'll still take a bit to get inside. We could just turn invisible and fly over the wall if you want?"

"Whatever gets us to a bar fastest." Serafall said.

I opened a Hole in front of us and cast a minor illusion charm over us as we passed through the Hole. Our wings caught us as the Hole dropped us in the air.

Serafall let out an appreciative whistle. "This is a massive city. I think I remember you saying their technology was still in the middle ages, right?"

"Yes and no. The magic makes things weird. Certain factions are more advanced than others, but the overall throughline is roughly equivalent to our middle ages."

"Is this a capital city then? A London equivalent maybe?"

"Again, yes and no. They don't have a good estimation of our empires. Well, they do, but… I could spend a full three hours discussing this."

"Do you see me complaining? Learning about another world sounds like a great way to get my mind off the shit storm I've been dealing with."

I shrugged, resuming my general overview of the Sword Coast's city states and the empires beyond.

We touched down in an alley that smelled like piss and feces. We quickly stowed our wings and dismissed the illusion covering us so we could walk out into the street to get away from the smell. The thoroughfare was filled with people moving about their daily business. Humans, halflings, elves, dwarves, tieflings, even an orc – all manner of races were present here. Serafall and I drew a lot of curious looks as we walked the street. It took me a moment to realize the clothes we were wearing were very out of place. I could have fixed it with an illusion, but Serafall didn't seem to mind, and I didn't care much either.

"Are those demons? Just…walking around?" Serafall asked, confused. She was eyeing a pair of red-skinned tieflings walking arm in arm down the road across from us.

"Tieflings. They technically aren't demons. They are either descendants of demons or descendants of people who had dealings with demons. This world has some…interesting facets in that regard. There's something I've been meaning to talk to you about actually, but I don't have enough information on it yet."

She raised an eyebrow at me. "Sounds interesting."

"When I know more, I'll let you know."

She shrugged. "Fair enough."

Medea and I had discussed it at length. Letting at least Serafall know about Vellia would likely lead to more advantages than liabilities. Showing the Satans undeniable proof that this world could help devils maintain their clan traits would instantly make me that much more vital of an asset to them. It would also hopefully lay the groundwork for their assistance in starting a branch of the Abaddon family with Vellia at its head if I decided to go through with that in the future. They couldn't help me navigate that political minefield if they didn't know what was going on.

We wandered for a few minutes, looking over the various shops lining the street. Candle makers, textiles, a cobbler – stores one would expect to find in a medieval city.

"Okay," Serafall spoke up after several minutes spent wandering. "I'm ready to find a bar now."

I paused in the center of the square, looking around. "I actually don't know where one is."

Serafall scowled. She scanned the crowd, picking out a random human. "Excuse me?"

The man had dark hair and was wearing a simple green tunic, patched in places to fill in holes. His eyes widened as Serafall approached him. He hastily bowed. "How can I assist, milady?"

"Milady?" Serafall muttered, confused. Shaking her head, she said, "Where's the nearest place a girl can get a drink around here?"

"The Tipsy Troll is a short walk down this road, milady." the man said, eyes trained on the ground.

Serafall lightly patted him on the shoulder, causing him to flinch. "Thanks for the help." We started walking in the indicated direction.

"That guy seemed like a spooked rabbit." Serafall said quietly.

"He probably thought you were a noble. We are dressed fancy and weird compared to most people here. Besides, he wasn't really wrong. You outrank everyone in the city as far as nobility is concerned."

"I came here to relax, not get put on a pedestal." Serafall grumbled.

"I can put an illusion over us?"

"No. If they think we're important, they'll let us go where we want. We'll just keep to ourselves when we finally get to the bar."

It was a short walk to the Tipsy Troll. A sign hung from rusted chains outside with styled script held the name of the establishment. It was a three story wooden building twice as wide as the nearby stores. From the exterior, it looked to be a sizable tavern.

Serafall pushed open the doors and strode inside, a wide smile on her face. I followed a step behind her.

Immediately, I felt dozens of eyes land on us. Looking around the interior, I saw a number of circular tables with patrons enjoying meals and drinks. Serving girls in aprons and linen dresses moved between the tables with trays of food and booze. A bar ran along the far wall with open seats. A board behind the bar held many papers pinned to it with large, bolded writing I couldn't read and numbers. If I had to guess, it was a bounty board. That guess was backed up by the bar's patrons. Almost everyone in the bar was wearing some form of armor or traveling clothes. Everyone was armed with a weapon ranging from spears and bows to axes and daggers. Serafall and I were very out of place here. It seemed like we'd walked into an adventurer haunt.

Serafall paid no mind to the suspicious looks of the other patrons, strolling proudly up to the bar and claiming a stool. "What do you have that's strong?"

A portly woman behind the bar with fiery red hair looked her up and down, appraising her. "Stongest I have is Demon's Blood Whiskey. I'd recommend starting with something a little–"

"That!" Serafall said, a wild gleam in her eye. "I'll take the whole bottle."

The bartender raised an eyebrow. "I'll have to ask for payment up front. Demon's Blood is one of my pricier brews. Twenty-five gold please, my lady.

Serafall grumbled. "None of that. Just call me Sera."

"So long as you pay, I'll call you whatever you want."

Serafall blanched, looking around. I imagine she was trying to figure out what kind of currency people were using.

I reached into my coat and opened a small Hole out of everyone's vision. I sat down next to Serafall and dropped a neat stack of five platinum pieces native to the Sword Coast onto the table, more than enough to cover a single bottle of whiskey.

"I'd like to open a tab please." I said.

The barmaid grinned at me, swiping my coins away. "Consider your tab open." She slammed a bottle down in front of Serafall. She placed two glasses down in front of it.

Serafall didn't even bother with the glasses. She pulled the cork out and lifted the bottle to her lips, taking a long swig. She came away from the bottle with a satisfied gasp. "Damnation that's good. We need to bring some of this back with us."

"We'll buy some more when we leave." I said. A single platinum piece was worth a lot in this world. I had thousands and could easily get more. Buying a little booze for my friend wouldn't put me in the poor house.

Serafall laid a hand on the table. I felt a pulse of magic as she placed a charm over us. She was obscuring our words. People would still hear us talking, but our words would be indecipherable.

"Thanks for this, Bal. I really needed a breather."

"Any time. Sorry you're having to clean up after me again."

She shook her head as she took another drink. "It's not your fault some dickheads tried to murder you. Don't apologize for refusing to let them kill you."

"How… How bad is it?"

Serafall turned to look at me, lips pursed. "Honestly, things have gone really well considering the circumstances. Athena's irate, but I would be too if someone blew up a swathe of my territory."

I blinked confused. "I didn't blow anything up though?"

Serafall raised an eyebrow at me. "Did you not hear? Zekram Bael responded to the attempt on Magdaran. He destroyed Thrinacia. He took the cows and their guardians before he annihilated the island."

I sat there slack-jawed. Thrinacia? The island from the Odyssey? Odysseus's men killed like three cows and invited the wrath of Zeus. Zekram destroyed the island?

That… How the fuck were we not at war?

Serafall chuckled darkly. "Now you see why I'm so stressed out right now."

"I'll buy you all the booze you want."

Serafall lifted her bottle in a salute. "To your deep pockets." She took a long drink.

"How bad is it?" I asked again.

Serafall shook her head. "Things are bad. Luckily for everyone involved, I'm a miracle worker. Things aren't calm, but I'm confident I can get us out of this. Once the worst is behind us, Zekram and I will be having words." She was seething when she said his name.

"I hate to ask this, I know you've already got a lot going on, but do you think I'm safe from Helios for the time being?"

Serafall nodded slowly. "You should be. Watch your back though. Don't spread this around, but Helios and Boreas have both vanished. The Greeks can't get in touch with them."

"Isn't that bad?" If Helios was unaccounted for, he might be organizing to strike again.

"It means they don't have any support anymore. They're probably planning something, but it'll take them a while to actually do anything. You should be safe for now. I already have my people looking into it. Your wards might ping a few of my people at the edges of your land. You'll know they're mine. If anyone else shows up unannounced, let me know immediately."

"Thank you, Serafall. I sincerely appreciate the support."

Serafall smirked. "I'm just protecting an investment. How else am I supposed to get new booze? And don't think I've forgotten that you still owe me two magical girls. Sirzechs won't shut up about Rias's newest peerage member. The deal was every one you gave to him, I got two magical girls. You owe me, Bal."

I chuckled good naturedly. "I'll get with Medea and see if I can't do something about that. It might take a bit. Between almost being assassinated and a Rating Game next week, I've got a lot going on."

Serafall shrugged. "Take your time. I understand better than anyone what you're dealing with right now." She took another long drink, sighing contentedly as she finished off the bottle. She raised the empty bottle, looking at the barmaid at the other end of the room. "Can I get another one of these?"

The barmaid nodded and started walking back towards us.

Serafall kicked her feet under the counter, humming happily as she waited. Her eyes tracked behind the bar to the board and the many papers stuck to it. She blinked, then leaned forward. She held up a hand and a paper flew off the board to land in her hand. She stared at it intently, uncaring of the many adventurers who'd frozen and were now watching us warily after seeing Serafall's casual telekinesis.

"Um…Sera, maybe–"

"What's this?" she asked, cutting me off. She turned the paper around so I could see it.

I looked over the paper. All I saw was a bunch of scribbles that meant nothing to me. "I can't read that." I said.

"Oh, right. I still have my translation spell active." Serafall said dumbly. She waved a hand in front of my eyes. The words on the paper started shifting, rotating into letters I recognized, allowing me to read it.

At the top of the page in big, bolded letters it said, 'Abaddon Mining Needs Guards! Competitive Pay for Light Work!'

I tilted my head in confusion, taking the paper from Serafall and reading over the rest of the flyer. Someone was looking for protection for miners at an iron mine.

"This isn't one of mine." I said, confused. "Maybe there's another Abaddon here?"

Serafall took the paper back, eyes scanning the document. "'Those interested should report to the Loralee Estate.'" she read around. Serafall spun around on her stool to address the tavern. "Does anyone know where the Loralee Estate is?"

The idle chatter in the bar quieted as everyone's attention turned to Serafall. Many watched her suspiciously. Some seemed intrigued, like they were trying to solve a puzzle. An elderly man in a blue robe traced his finger on the table in front of him, muttering words beneath his breath as he watched her.

I tapped my finger on the bar. The magic the old man had been building scattered into nothing, much to his surprise.

"Up in the Blacklake District." a muscular woman wearing furs with a battleaxe strapped to her back said. "Surprised you don't already know that, milady." She said the word mockingly.

Serafall smiled easily. "We're new in town. I appreciate the help though. As thanks, how about a round for the house?"

The mood in the tavern instantly changed from suspicion and tension to excitement and gratitude. Adventurers whooped their approval, slamming mugs on tables and demanding more drink.

Serafall shot me a smirk out of the corner of her eye. "You're good for it, I trust?"

I shook my head, an amused smile on my face as I reached into my coat again. I dropped twelve platinum pieces on the table. That would more than cover a round of cheap drinks, but I didn't want to risk shorting the bar. When the barmaid came by to collect them, I handed her twenty additional platinum pieces and told her to bring me every bottle of Devil's Blood Whiskey she had.

Servers moved between the tables filling mugs and passing out bottles. When the barmaid came back carrying a crate full of bottles of whiskey, Serafall scooped the box up and leaned over to whisper in my ear. "Let's go see who's impersonating you, shall we?"

I followed her out the door, accepting grateful pats on the back from the adventurers on my way out.

As we walked down the road, I motioned to the crate Serafall was carrying. "I can send that home for you if you like?"

Serafall considered it for a moment. She pulled a bottle out of the crate then held it out to me. "Put it on my desk please."

A Hole swallowed the crate, sending it back to Serafall's office.

"Thanks for the drinks, Bal. Now! Let's solve the mystery of who stole your name!" She lifted her bottle of whiskey above her head like a standard and started running down the street. Peasants shuffled out of her way as she charged towards nothing.

Shaking my head at her antics, I followed behind her.

Through a combination of asking around and a few minor bribes, we received directions to the Loralee Estate. It was on the other side of the city, so we ducked into an alley and took to the sky under an illusion. Once airborne, it didn't take long at all for us to reach our destination.

"Fancy place." Serafall commented as we observed it from the sky.

A white stone structure rose several stories out of the ground, decorated with brass griffins, silver sphinxes, and blue tabards. A wrought iron gate fenced in a perimeter expanding beyond the large home. Lush gardens with flowering bushes and canopies of trees covered a cobbled stone walkway leading up to the manor.

"Whoever lives here is obscenely rich." I added. Being able to afford a home like this in Neverwinter required 'fuck you' money.

"Should we go knock?" Serafall asked.

"Might as well."

We landed out of the way and dismissed our illusion. We strolled up to the gate and searched around for a moment. I found a bell and pulled the cord. The bell rang out a deep resonant sound. A moment later, the stylized 'L' in the center of the gate began to glow a bright blue.

"Greetings," a voice said from the gate. "I have the privilege of serving as groundskeeper for the Loralee family. May I ask what your business is?"

Serafall and I exchanged a look. She held up the flyer we took from the tavern. "We're here about the mine job. We'd like to speak with the Abaddons."

"I'm afraid the owner of the company is not present, but I will inform my lady you are coming. You may enter."

The gate let out a sharp metallic sound as if unlocking, then swung inward on its own.

"Faaancy." Serafall said exaggeratedly. She skipped through the gate. I followed behind her, looking around for anything that might be a problem.

The door to the manor was etched in gold, tracing eloquent patterns. The doors swung open as we approached.

A male elf wearing a blue tailcoat bowed shallowly as we approached. "Welcome. I am Rath Lain, groundskeeper. You are here to see Lady Cyvis about the job posting, yes? Please follow me."

Serafall and I exchanged a look before following him. He led us up a set of stairs that spun, climbing in a circle.

"The lady is currently in a meeting, but you may wait in the adjoining room until she is ready to receive you." he said as we climbed.

"Thank you." Serafall said with a smile. She seemed to be enjoying this immensely. I was mostly here to humor her. I was mildly curious about my name being used for a mine I didn't own, but I could figure that out later. I had other things to occupy my focus right now. Namely, a Rating Game and two Greek Gods who wanted me dead.

Rath held open the door to a small room with cushioned chairs. Two windows let in streaks of daylight. Another door at the far end of the room was locked shut.

"Please wait here. Lady Cyvis will be with you when her meeting concludes." Rath said, polite.

"Thanks for your help!" Serafall said, falling into one of the chairs.

Rath gently closed the door, leaving us alone.

"Isn't this exciting?" Serafall asked. "We're about to meet your imposter!"

"Or, someone else who shares my name. Maybe they just made the word up and thought it sounded cool?" I said.

Serafall shook her head. "No," she said with certainty. "My gut says that whatever this is, it's going to be very interesting."

I shrugged. "I'd never mistrust your gut instinct."

Serafall grinned. "I knew you were smart."

We sat around for a while, making idle chatter about the city and the room itself. It wasn't terribly long before the door at the far end of the room unlocked and swung open. Two figures emerged, finishing a conversation they'd been having on the other side.

"…me know when you are ready. I am very anxious to meet him." a beautiful elven woman said. With elves, it was hard to tell age, but she looked young to my eye. Silver hair was kept in check by long pointed ears. Her skin was smooth and fair. Her eyes were blue, matching the sapphire earrings she wore. A noble blue dress embroidered with silver highlights hugged her form as she moved into the room. She tilted her head, curious as she noticed Serafall and I sitting in the room.

"Hello," she said, distracted. "Forgive me. I forgot Rath said we had guests. I am Cyvis Loralee, daughter of Sylas and Thaelis Loralee. Welcome to our home. This is… Vellia?" She motioned to her companion, intending to introduce them. She was surprised to find her companion kneeling on the ground at her side.

When I saw Cyvis's companion, I realized why the company had my name attached to it. In hindsight, it should have been obvious. Then again, the last time I saw her, she'd been a long way from this city. How did she get here?

"My lord," Vellia, the red-skinned tiefling who served as my warlock, said as she knelt before me, eyes fixed on the marble floor.

Cyvis looked between Vellia and I with a puzzled look on her face. "I don't understand. What is–"

"My lord," Vellia interrupted her. "May I introduce you?"

"You may." I said tiredly.

"Cyvis," Vellia said, still facing the floor. "I present Viscount Balthazar Abaddon, Lord of the House of Abaddon, my lord and master."

Cyvis's eyes went wide as saucers. She looked at me as if she was looking at the sun. She quickly averted her eyes, pulling up the hems of her dress as she fell into a deep curtsy. "My lord, it is an honor to host you in our home."

"Bal?"

I turned to see Serafall smiling evilly at me.

"Now would be a good time to fill me in, don't you think?" Serafall said in a sweet tone that promised murder.

I sighed, rubbing my forehead. "Vellia, please stand up. The whole bowing and kneeling thing isn't necessary. The same goes for you, Cyvis. It's good to meet you by the way."

"The honor is mine, my lord." Cyvis said. She was standing straight again, but she still wasn't looking me in the eye.

"So you know them." Serafall said leadingly.

"One of them. Vellia? Come here please."

Vellia was at my side in a moment. "How may I help, my lord?"

"You can relax, Vellia." I said tiredly as I stood up next to her. "Serafall, I'd like you to meet Vellia, my first, and currently only warlock."

Serafall had a considering expression on her face as she looked between us. "You contracted a magician?"

I sighed. "No. That isn't what's going on here. This is…much more. I told you this world has some interesting facets where demons are concerned when we first arrived here. She," I motioned to Vellia. "Is the topic I've been meaning to discuss with you at some point."

"Forgive me, my lord," Vellia said hesitantly. "May I ask who I am being introduced to?"

"A good friend of mine who also happens to be one of the four rulers of the Hell I hail from. Vellia, meet Serafall Leviathan, the Satan of Foreign Affairs."

Vellia froze, sucking in a deep breath. After a moment, she began trembling. A moment later, all of her muscles locked in place and she fell into a deep bow. "It is an honor to stand before you, my lady."

Serafall raised an eyebrow at me. "You're telling her who I really am?"

"For a reason. You might want to stay seated. If all of the other bullshit I've pulled on you hasn't given you a stroke yet, this might just do it." I said warningly.

"Bal, I'm supposed to be relaxing right now." Serafall said warningly.

"This is a good surprise, I promise. Will it probably be a headache? Yes. Will it solve one of the greatest problems facing devilkind? Also yes."

Serafall closed her eyes and rubbed her eyelids as she sighed. She looked up at me. "Alright. Hit me with it."

"Vellia, please show Serafall the power I gave you to move between spaces." I said.

"Yes, my lord." Vellia said. She held her hand out to her side. With a sound like reality fracturing, the longsword I'd given her when we'd forged our contract appeared in her hand. She slashed the sword down, opening a dark cut in the air. She slashed again, opening another hole a short distance away. She stepped into one tear, appearing from the other.

Serafall was on her feet in a moment. Spell circles surrounded her, drifting through the air as she scanned the cuts in reality. "Balthazar, is this really what I think it is?"

"Yes and no. It isn't the same. It lacks the versatility and power of a true Hole." I said, punctuating my words by opening a Hole next to the tear for Serafall to compare. "Functionally though? I'm sure you can see why I've been keeping this to myself for now."

"How did you manage to give her Hole?" Serafall asked, gone was the fun relaxed demeanor she wore only a moment ago. She was in Satan mode now.

"It's a feature of this world. Mortals contract with entities from other planes for power all the time here. I made a contract with her to work as my business's figurehead here. It had unintentional side effects."

"Can you replicate it?" Serafall asked, deep in thought.

"I haven't tried yet. As part of the contract, she draws on my power. If I contract too many people, they will be an active drain on me."

"How did you contract her? I need a step-by-step description. A demonstration would be preferable. I need to know if this is a one off thing or if you can duplicate the results."

"My lord?" Vellia said hesitantly. "Please forgive the interruption."

"I'm not going to punish you for speaking, Veliia. What is it?" I said.

"Thank you, my lord. I have been meaning to contact you for some time now. I have made substantial progress in the goal you set before me. Much of that progress can be attributed to Cyvis's contributions. All she asked in return was the opportunity to speak with my patron."

I shared a look with Serafall before turning to Cyvis expectantly. "You wanted to speak with me?"

Cyvis started wringing her hands, clearly uncomfortable with suddenly becoming the center of attention. "Yes, my lord. Vellia already told you I have been working with her. My parents own the majority of the iron mines in the region. They were called home several years ago to see to matters there. I have been left in control of their holdings here in the meantime. They were unable to complete my education before they departed."

"Your education?" I asked.

Cyvis held up her hand, a magical rune appeared in the air above her hand, glowing blue. "My family has a proud history of strong abjuration wizards. I… I did not take to the family magic as well as they hoped I would. They brought my younger brother back with them to present to the elders as their heir. He is more skilled with abjuration magic than I am. But I have other talents!" she added hurriedly, seeming panicked. "I… I found many books detailing hidden infernal magic. I have taken well to them. It is no boast to say I am gifted in the use of infernal magic."

"What does this have to do with me?" I prompted, watching her closely.

Cyvis closed her hand, banishing her magic. She looked at the ground, wringing her hands nervously. "After working with her for some time, I revealed my demonic pursuits to Vellia. It was a risk. I could be imprisoned for my activities. She told me she possessed a patron, but could not tell me much more. I… I have been seeking my own patron for some time, my lord. Many of the accounts I have found describe such relationships as abusive at best, catastrophic at worst. The relationship Vellia was able to describe, limited though it was, was different. I… I was hoping you would allow me the opportunity to seek your patronage, my lord." she finished quickly.

"Her magic is powerful, my lord." Vellia added quickly. "She has been a tremendous help furthering your goals in Neverwinter and beyond. For what little my endorsement is worth, she has it."

Cyvis shot Vellia a grateful look. She saw me watching her and quickly looked at the floor again.

"We couldn't ask for a better opportunity. I'll take notes." Serafall said, pulling a pen and notepad out of nowhere as she looked at me expectantly.

"Really?" I asked her.

"Come on. Make with the warlocking!" Serafall said, motioning towards Cyvis.

"Making a warlock involves tethering someone to your demonic power. It's not something you should do frivolously." I protested.

"You said the first time you did it was an accident. That seemed to work out. Your first warlock vouches for her. I say go for it." Serafall countered.

"You're just saying that because you need more information."

"Maybe, maybe not. Are you making a new warlock or not?"

I let out another sigh. I opened a Hole. "Medea? Can I borrow you for a minute?"

"Give me a minute, honey." Medea sent back.

I left the Hole open, waiting patiently for Medea to speak again.

"Okay!" Medea called. "I'm ready."

The Hole expanded. A moment later, Medea stepped through it. She looked around the room. "Oh my. What have you dragged me into, dear?"

"I might be contracting a second warlock. Serafall wants to watch the process. Vellia vouches for her. I wanted your opinion and, if you approve, your help writing the contract." I explained.

"I see." Medea walked up to Cyvis. Cyvis was taller than her, but she still shrunk under Medea's gaze.

"What is your name?" Medea asked.

"Cyvis, my lady." Cyvis said quickly.

"Do you know who I am?"

Cyvis kept her eyes fixed on the floor. "No, my lady. Vellia's contract prevented her from saying much about her patron. Forgive me."

"There is nothing to forgive. I'm glad the contract is working as intended. My name is Medea. I am Balthazar's Queen."

"It is an honor to meet you, my lady." Cyvis said, quickly entering a shallow curtsy.

"Balthazar's well being is my number one priority. Vellia appears to believe you can be an asset to us. Whether that is true or not, what concerns me more is the continued safety of my King."

"My lady, I would never jeopardize Lord Abaddon's safety." Cyvis said, sounding scared and desperate.

Medea watched her for a moment before smiling. "I believe you. I want you to work hard for our King, understand?"

"I will, my lady."

Medea smiled and nodded, satisfied. "Good." She turned back around to face me. "I like her. I say go for it."

I pursed my lips, then nodded. "Alright." I wasn't opposed to the idea of contracting another warlock. I hadn't done it because my time had been occupied with other things. Giving Vellia a partner to help her further her already impressive progress towards the goals I laid out for her was a good idea. It would also let me test if all of my warlocks would gain the Hole-like ability Vellia obtained, or if she was the only one.

Medea and I drafted a contract while Serafall watched us intently. Vellia whispered encouraging words to Cyvis in the corner, placing a hand on her shoulder and smiling comfortingly. If Cyvis was having second thoughts, she needed to speak up soon. Medea and I were almost done with the contract.

Unlike Vellia's contract, this one was an intentional warlock contract. In exchange for working to further my goals in Faerun, I would empower Cyvis. It still had all of the clauses preventing Cyvis from sharing information about me or my peerage outside of what was absolutely necessary for the business, but there was less focus on the business aspects of our relationship. The last time had been an accident. It was time to see if I could do this intentionally.

"Looks good." I said, having looked over it a second time.

Medea took the contract, pursing her lips as she read it over. "Something's missing. We gave Vellia a sign on bonus, didn't we?"

"Yes, my lady." Vellia answered. She held out a hand and a dark-bladed sword covered in pulsing runes appeared in her hands. "You gave me this sword and my armor."

Medea pointedly looked at Cyvis. "I'd assume you don't want a sword?"

"I would accept whatever you offer, my lady." Cyvis said quickly.

"Well that's not very helpful. I feel a hint of empowering magic in your necklace. I take it you're skilled with magic?"

"I am, my lady." Cyvis confirmed.

Medea smiled, victorious. "I have just the thing." She closed her eyes, bringing her hands together in front of her. I felt a point of pure magical power explode between her hands. Medea opened her eyes, grinning. She threw her hands forward.

A powerful caw echoed in the room as a shadowy raven flew away from Medea's hands, circling the room before it flapped to a halt atop Cyvis's shoulder.

"She'll take good care of you." Medea said, watching as the spectral raven studied Cyvis curiously.

Cyvis was frozen in place. Hesitantly, she raised a finger up to scratch under the raven's chin. It cooed happily, leaning into her touch. A wide smile spread across Cyvis's face. "Thank you, my lady."

"To business." I said, dramatically straightening out the contract in my hand. "Read this over. If you agree to everything, sign next to my name. This is permanent. Make sure you think everything through."

Cyvis took the contract with an unsteady hand. She swallowed audibly, slowly reading over the contract. After reading through it twice, she took the pen Vellia held out to her and slowly signed her name. She looked up in anticipation.

Nothing happened.

I tilted my head in confusion, taking the contract back from her and looking it over.

"What's wrong?" Serafall asked.

"I don't know." I said. "That should have worked."

"Maybe–"

The raven perched on Cyvis's shoulder let out an ear-piercing caw. Its talons bit down into her shoulder.

Cyvis let out a pained, surprised gasp. Power exploded from the point where the raven's talons pierced her skin. Magical energy snaked up out of her dress to the side of her neck, searing an arcane mark into the flesh of her lower neck and shoulder. The contract in my hands lit on fire. I felt as a second minor drain latched onto me, sucking away my demonic power. It still wasn't enough to worry me. If other warlocks pulled a similar amount, I could probably manage one or two more after Cyvis.

"Cyvis? Are you alright?" Vellia said as she held her friend's shoulder, concern etched on her face.

Cyvis looked up, an expression of pure euphoria fixed on her face. "I'm fine. I'm better than fine. I feel… I feel invincible."

Vellia grinned. "I know what you mean."

"Sorry to break this up, but I need to know if you can make the same Holes she can." Serafall interjected, stepping forward and smiling encouragingly. "Give it a shot, if you wouldn't mind?"

Cyvis nodded seriously. "Of course, my lady." She took a deep breath and held up her hands. After a moment, her features twisted in frustration.

Vellia stepped up beside her. "Don't think about it too hard. It should feel instinctual. Just let it happen."

Cyvis took a deep breath and closed her eyes. She raised her right hand, dragging her index finger behind. A snow-white tear in space opened behind her finger. She raised her left hand, creating the same effect on her other side. She stepped into the tear on the right. When she emerged from the tear on the left, a magical layer of protective frost clung to her body.

Serafall whistled appreciatively. "I'm suddenly feeling a lot more optimistic about…well, everything really."

"Do you have anything important planned for the rest of the day?" I asked Vellia and Cyvis.

"No, my lord." Vellia answered, an excited grin on her face. I think she knew where I was taking this.

"Cyvis, I'd like to see what you can do. Would you like to test out your new abilities?"

"I would love to, my lord." Cyvis said, sounding drunk on power.

I opened a Hole. "This will take us to my lands. I'll be able to set up a controlled area to let you try everything out when we get there. After you."

Cyvis took a deep breath, then held her head high, walking through the Hole without pausing. Vellia was right behind her. Medea, Serafall and I followed.

A great roar shook the air the moment I was through the other side. I'd transported us to one of the many viewing boxes in the coliseum.

Pandemonium reigned on the field beneath us. The serpentine form of Coal wound around a western dragon I recognized as Ladora Bune, Sairaorg's Rook. Matatabi's giant flaming form clung to the back of a Golden Lion, slashing and biting at Regulus's impervious hide. Shang Tsung was rapidly swapping between forms – Matatabi, then Runa, then Medea – as he tried to trap Kuisha before she could escape into a Hole.

A thunderous boom shook the space as Sairaorg and Achilles collided in the center of the arena. Sairaorg was coated in the pearl-colored energy of his touki. His fist slammed into Achilles's spear, snapping it in half. Achilles discarded the useless weapon and traded blows with his fists. Sairaorg landed only a single blow on him to Achilles's twelve. Achilles did not seem affected by Sairaorg's enhanced strength in the slightest.

"Hi, Bal!"

I looked up. In the viewing box to my right, Magdaran sat with the rest of mine and Sairaorg's peerages, content to watch the others try to kill each other.

"Vellia, Cyvis, I apologize, but we'll have to reschedule this. I'll be in contact." I opened a Hole and sent them home before they could protest. Everyone present knowing about Achilles was one thing, them knowing about my warlocks was another matter entirely.

"So much for keeping Achilles a secret." I grumbled, heading over to join Magdaran.

"This is chaotic." Serafall idly commented from my side, watching the combatants below try to kill each other.

"This is what happens when you give a bunch of battle maniacs open access to a place they can beat each other up in." I said tiredly.

"Sorry to barge in like this." Magdaran called out as we approached. "I was visiting Sai when Coal arrived. He was very vocal about an opportunity to fight a reincarnated Achilles. Regulus and Sai practically leapt at the chance. The rest of us tagged along to watch. When were you planning to tell us you managed to reincarnate Achilles?"

"Don't take this the wrong way, but I wasn't." I said. "I was planning on keeping his presence a secret until the Rating Game next week.

Magdaran nodded. "That makes sense. I'd want to go into that fight with a few aces up my sleeve too." He grinned. "Achilles is quite the ace. You wouldn't happen to have any others would you? Have you finished your peerage?"

"I'm still missing a Bishop. Medea and I are working on that. How about you? Have you made any additions to your peerage?"

Magdaran shook his head. "Father hasn't let me out of his sight for the last few days. Something about the attack spooked him. I've never seen him so scared."

I frowned. I hadn't checked in on him or Latia since we'd been attacked, had I? "How are you doing, Mag?"

He smiled. "Don't worry about me. You got me out of there before I even realized there was any danger. It… I did not handle it well once I realized just how much danger we'd been in, but it was a wake up call. I was meeting with Sai today to see if he would be willing to help me train." He motioned down to the field. "That brings us here."

I looked over as a hand delicately gripped my shoulder. The moment my eyes met Serafall's, her grip turned vicelike. I let out a grunt of pain as she smiled at me with murder in her eyes.

"Balthazar, my good friend," Serafall said sweetly. "You and I have had many discussions about warnings and headaches in the past, so I know you wouldn't reincarnate Achilles, Zeus's great-grandson, without telling me. I know you certainly wouldn't do such while the Greeks are already irate. My faith in your intelligence isn't misplaced, right?"

"In my defense, I didn't know about Thrinacia. I thought they were pissed for no good reason and didn't care what they thought." I said, choosing my words carefully. "Also, I bought you a lot of booze. That warrants a stay of execution, right?"

Serafall glared at me before sighing. "You're lucky I don't have the time or the energy to be mad at you right now. I need to talk to Ajuka about what we discussed then get back to my office. Expect me to be in touch soon. We'll need to discuss that thing you just showed me. It's too important to put off, especially now."

Serafall released me and walked a short distance away. A teleportation circle spread out from her. Moments before she teleported away, she glared at me with narrowed eyes. "And don't reincarnate any inter-pantheon incidents while I'm gone! You're on your last strike, pal!"

Serafall disappeared in a flash of pink magic.

Medea laid a hand on my shoulder.

"I'll be returning to my lab to finish up Achilles's armor. Call if you need me."

I nodded. "Thanks, Medea."

She scattered into spectral butterflies and was gone.

"Balthazar,"

I turned around, surprised to find Kuisha had suddenly appeared behind me. She was wearing blue sweats with her hair tied back. Sweat beaded her brow from having just been exercising.

"Hey, Kuisha. It's good to–" Whatever else I might've said was halted as Kuisha pulled me into a crushing hug.

"I'm glad you're okay." she whispered, hugging me tight.

I slowly returned the hug, patting her on the back. "I'm fine, Kuisha. It'll take more than some amateur assassins to put me down."

Kuisha pulled back, scowling at me. "Don't tempt fate like that. Magdaran told me they blocked teleportation. Things could have gone much worse."

"Believe me, sis, I'm aware. I've already taken steps to…" I trailed off, my eye catching on a reflective glint of metal on Kuisha's finger.

"Balthazar?" she said, confused. She flinched as I reached out and grabbed her left wrist, pulling it up in front of my face.

A silver band with a large diamond set into it rested snug on her third finger.

Kuisha blushed furiously. "Balthazar… This isn't… I… Eep!" She let out a squeak as I dragged her behind me to the edge of the viewing box.

Everyone on the field below was still thrashing about, punching, clawing and biting at one another. The only two missing from the earlier fray were Kuisha and Shang Tsung. Kuisha was with me. Shang Tsung had joined Mothra and Aqua a short distance to my right.

"Sairaorg!" I bellowed. The enchantments built into the coliseum's foundations magnified my voice into a thunderclap. All activity halted. Coal still had Achilles's invulnerable leg in his mouth. Matatabi paused with her paw above Regulus's nose, primed to swat at him. Sairaorg looked up, still holding Regulus's snapping jaws apart lest they crush him. Dead silence reigned in the coliseum.

I pointed at the ring on Kuisha's finger. "What is this!"

Sairaorg went pale. I could have sworn I heard him audibly gulp. Regulus slowly backed away, leaving his King alone.

A Hole rapidly opened and closed, depositing Kuisha and I on the coliseum floor a few steps away from Sairaorg. He flinched.

"Balthazar! Uh… You see… That is a… Um…" He was scratching his head, desperately trying to think of something.

I couldn't take it anymore. I started laughing.

Sairaorg's entire body went slack with relief. "Don't do that to me, Bal. You almost gave me a heart attack."

I grinned as I got my laughter under control. "Sorry, I couldn't help myself." I pulled Kuisha into a crushing hug. "My baby sister is getting married! I'm so happy for you."

"I… What! I'm older than you!" Kuisha protested, affronted.

I shook my head sagely. "As Lord Abaddon, all other Abaddons are my little siblings. I don't make the rules, Kuisha. I just enforce them. Speaking of…" I turned to Sairaorg. "I have to put on my asshole Lord Abaddon hat for a second here. Bear with me please."

Sairaorg stood up straight, nodding. "I expected this."

I let go of Kuisha and fixed Sairaorg with a serious look. "First of all, I would assume she will be joining your house?"

"She will."

"Will she become Lady Vapula? It would aggravate me to learn you've taken my sister as a mistress."

"Bal," Kuisha hissed. "He wouldn't–"

"It's alright, Kuisha." Sairaorg said. "I'd be worried too." Facing me, he said, "When I become Lord Vapula, Kuisha will become Lady Vapula. I don't care much about the whole pureblood thing. That's not why I'm marrying her, but others do. A former Abaddon becoming Lady Vapula looks good for the clan; a nice bonus to marrying a wonderful woman."

Kuisha's blush turned nuclear. She wouldn't look anyone in the eye.

I smiled. "In that case, you both have my blessing. I'm expecting a wedding invite."

Sairaorg smiled brightly. "You'll get one."

"I'd stay to celebrate the engagement, but I've got too much going on right now. Seriously, congratulations to you both. Achilles!"

"Yes, my king?" Achilles called from across the arena.

"I'm preoccupied at the moment, so I can't rightly do my older brotherly duty of giving Sairaorg a proper beating to make sure he knows not to mistreat my little sister. Would you mind filling in for me?"

"I'm older than you, you brat!"

I ignored Kuisha's affronted scream.

Achilles grinned, eyes tracking with intent towards Sairaorg. "It would be my pleasure, my king."

Sairaorg gulped nervously.

I patted him on the back as I walked past. "Don't worry. He won't beat you up too bad. Mothra will fix you up, so there'll be no permanent damage. I'm looking forward to that wedding invite!" I stepped into a Hole and was gone.

I really did have things I needed to do, otherwise I would've stayed. I had a week until my Rating Game with Roygun. I wanted a full peerage when I faced her. In order to give my potential Bishop time to adjust, I had to go recruit them today if possible.

I'd initially wanted to give Achilles another day or two to adjust, but that didn't really seem necessary. The son of Thetis had hit the ground running as a devil and already seemed overjoyed with his new surroundings.

Now all I needed was a Bishop to finally be done with my peerage. I'd asked Medea to look into a potential recruit's location. They would work really well with the makeup of the rest of my peerage if they accepted. If they refused, I'd improvise.

"You wouldn't happen to have found that Bishop candidate would you?" I asked Medea as I appeared in her lab.

Medea smiled knowingly without turning around, still making notes in the open book in front of her. The ink glowed a dark blue. "Well, master, what would you give me if I had somehow managed to reach across realities to locate a single individual in less than a day?"

I walked up behind her, wrapping my arms around her waist and laying my head on her shoulder. "What does my Queen desire?"

Medea turned a page in her book, not looking at me. "Your sister seems happy."

I froze for a moment, then forced myself to relax. She was scrying on the coliseum. She knew about the engagement and was very purposefully mentioning it. I'd have to be dumber than a rock not to get that hint.

"I've been working on something, but it's not ready yet." I said honestly. Part of my plan was already in place. The second piece was proving…problematic. It didn't help that the Helios fiasco had completely sidetracked me. "It'll be ready after the Rating Game. I promise." I said, locking myself into an ironclad time table. I should be able to figure something out in that time, it just might not be what I originally intended.

Medea let out a short huff, then leaned back into me. "I'm going to hold you to that, Balthazar. My grandfather and his cronies tried to hurt you. I don't want to waste any more time."

I pressed a kiss into her cheek. "It'll be worth the wait, I promise."

"I found the Bishop." Medea gently ran her hands over my forehead, sharing the information she scry'd with me. "I'm looking forward to next week."

"You're the best, Medea. I'll let you know if the Bishop accepts." I pulled her in for a brief kiss then fled through a Hole. I suddenly had even more work to do.

My wings shot out of my back, holding me aloft over a large body of water. The lake was massive, extending almost to the horizon. In the far distance, a cut led a stream down into the lake.

I took a deep breath and held it, breaking the surface of the water and sinking deeper. The water was crystal clear. I approached a fantastic underwater castle. The doors swung open as I approached.

I stepped into the castle. A warming charm dried the water from my clothes as I entered the open interior.

"Balthazar," Idyia greeted me as she emerged from a nearby hallway. "To what do I owe the pleasure of your company?"

I stood up straight. "I have come to ask for your blessing to marry your daughter."

Idyia paused, tilting her head. "It's about time. I was beginning to think you would wait forever."

"Recent events have kept me distracted." I said diplomatically.

"Yes, I imagine they have. You wish to marry Medea despite the threat posed by Helios?"

"She told me she doesn't want to wait anymore. I share her sentiment."

Idyia had a happy smile on her face. "Good. You have my blessing. How do you intend to ask her?"

She led me to a sitting room and served refreshments while I told her my plan. She was silent through my explanation. When I told her of the preparations I still had yet to make, she spoke.

"Your intentions are wonderful, Balthazar, but she does not require so much as that."

"I disagree. She deserves everything I can give her and more."

She made a considering sound. "Do not let your pursuit of perfection stall your future together."

I nodded seriously. "Whether I am ready or not, I will ask her after the Rating Game."

Idyia nodded. "Good. If there is anything I can do to help, I will assist."

"Thank you. Forgive me for my abrupt departure, but–"

She waved me off. "Go. I take no offense. Be safe. Medea would not forgive herself if you got yourself killed trying to impress her."

"I will be cautious." I assured her, then stepped back through a Hole, walking to a different world entirely.

Vellia and Cyvis exploded out of the chairs they'd been sitting on their feet. Vellia knelt and Cyvis curtsied.

"My lord," Vellia greeted.

"Please relax. You don't need to grovel every time you see me."

"You are our lord," Vellia said, gaze fixed firmly on the floor. "We would not dare to disrespect you."

I sighed, rubbing the bridge of my nose. Having them act so formal was really making me uncomfortable. I'd need to get used to it if I wanted to be seen more in public as Lord Abaddon, but I did not like the whole groveling thing.

"My lord…" Cyvis began hesitantly.

"Yes?" I said.

"The creatures we saw in your home, were they invaders?"

"What?" I asked, confused. "No. That was my peerage and my friend. Right, you don't know what a peerage is. Think of them as my most trusted servants." After thinking for a moment, it made sense why Cyvis might have assumed I was under attack. From her perspective, there were giant monsters fighting, then she was sent away. Not even Vellia, who had been introduced to members of my peerage before, would know about the monstrous forms of my peerage members.

A spark of something I couldn't identify lit up in Cyvis's eyes. "Those creatures serve you, my lord?"

Vellia smiled proudly at Cyvis's side, nudging her shoulder and shooting her a knowing look.

I wasn't sure what the byplay between them meant, but I didn't come here to figure that out. I had something else to do.

When they'd both refocused on me, I continued. "I apologize for barging in so soon after our prior meeting, and I'm sorry you didn't get a chance to test out your powers, Cyvis. I'll try to arrange something for the near future."

"It is no trouble, my lord." Vellia said. "I was just telling her I would show her how I have been training with my power here."

"Yes," Cyvis said with an agreeable nod. "Thank you, my lord, but please do not inconvenience yourself on my account. Seeing your home was a great honor even on its own."

I pursed my lips, uncertain. "If Vellia can take care of you, I don't have an issue with that. Feel free to reach out if you need assistance." I shook my head. "But that's not why I came here. I'm sorry to do this so soon after contracting with you, but I have a task for you."

Cyvis's back went ramrod straight. An excited grin was on her face as she said, "Please, my lord, allow me the opportunity to serve you."

That was a little more enthusiastic than I was expecting, but I wasn't going to be disappointed about the fact she was willing to work hard.

I slowly outlined what I wanted them to do, being sure they understood the task I was giving them in its entirety. They listened with rapt attention as I outlined the details.

"When you have something, contact me using one of these." I said, handing each of them a flyer with my symbol on it.

"Of course, my lord," Cyvis said, bowing her head. "My family has collected an extensive library over the years. I expect I will be able to make use of it on your behalf."

"Thank you. Please work quickly. I have a strict deadline here. Contact me when you have something. And don't be afraid to call me if either of you need something to make your other work here run more smoothly." I stepped back through another Hole.

I sighed as I fell into a chair in mine and Medea's bedroom. I was going to give myself whiplash with all the places I was travelling to, and I wasn't even done yet.

I took a deep breath, then stood. Time to complete my peerage, or at least try.


X


A young man stood in nothingness. Dark hair fell past pointed ears. A white robe with gold trim hugged his body. A pair of circular spectacles shielded shut eyes.

He came awake with a gasp. He looked around, frantic, not knowing where he was or what was happening.

Where was he? The last thing he could remember, he was sitting at his computer. Now, he was standing in an empty void. There was nothing around him but darkness in all directions.

He looked down at himself, trying to ascertain his assets. He inhaled sharply, shocked. He…was different. The robes, the red staff in his hand – he recognized them, but they weren't his. They belonged to a character he played in a video game. What was going on?

"Hello, Shiroe."

The man spun around. His grip on the staff in his hands tightened subconsciously. He wasn't alone in this space. Another man stood across from him. He had golden hair. He wore a dark suit and an easy smile.

"Who are you?" Shiroe asked, hesitant. He didn't have enough information. For the moment, the man across from him didn't appear hostile. Maybe he could learn something from him.

"My name is Balthazar Abaddon. I'll expand on who and what I am in a moment. For the moment, I imagine you want to know what's going on, right?"

"I do." Shiroe said slowly, watching the man across from him carefully.

"Are you familiar with the concept of an isekai?" Balthazar asked.

Shiroe frowned, eyebrows furrowing in thought.

An isekai? Is that what this was? It would certainly explain the dark vortex around him. This didn't seem like a dream, so something out of the ordinary was happening. What was the last thing he could remember? It was fuzzy. Shiroe couldn't place where he was or what he was doing before he got here.

"Am I dead?" Shiroe asked.

Balthazar shrugged. "I can't say for sure what circumstances led to you being here. All I can say for certain is that the you in front of me is very much alive."

That wasn't as helpful as Shiroe would have liked. He needed more information.

"If you mean to imply I'm being isekai'd, are you the god who will offer me power and send me on my way?"

Balthazar chuckled. "No, I believe you've already received the power boost associated with the genre. And I'm not a god. I'm an outside context problem."

Shiroe's eyes narrowed. "I'd appreciate an explanation."

"One is forthcoming." Balthazar said, smiling. "I'm not a god, Shiroe. I am a devil."

Shiroe took a step back, raising his staff reflexively as demonic wings exploded out of Balthazar's back, spreading wide behind him.

Balthazar raised a hand. "Peace, Shiroe. I mean you no harm."

"Did you bring me here?" Shiroe asked, trying to remain calm. If this really was a devil he was speaking to, he needed to be rational. He didn't know what the devil was capable of. He didn't know what he himself was capable of. From all appearances, it seemed he was in the body of his Elder Tales character. Did that mean he could use all of the magic and abilities his character possessed? If so, how? Shiroe wasn't in a position to get into a fight with a devil. He needed to resolve this amicably if possible.

"I did bring you here." Balthazar said. "As I alluded to, you were in the process of being isekai'd. I interrupted your transition to whatever world you were being sent to and brought you here so we might speak."

"Why?"

"Because I'd like to make you an offer."

Shiroe took another step backwards. "And if I refuse your offer?"

Balthazar shrugged, holding up his hand.

Shiroe flinched as a dark sphere appeared close to him, expanding large enough for a man to walk through.

"If you refuse, or decide that you've had enough of my company, that will send you back on your way. You'll arrive in whatever world you were originally intended to. It may be a world you recognize or one wholly alien. I'm sure a man of your talents will find a way to survive and perhaps even thrive regardless of where you end up, but I'd like to offer you an alternative if you're willing to listen."

Shiroe regarded the hole in space carefully, lightly tapping his index finger against his staff as he thought. He didn't have enough information. It was possible he would be sent to the world of Elder Tales since he was currently in the body of his game character. Then again, he'd heard of some isekai anime and manga where a game character was sent into an entirely different world. There was no telling where he would end up. Even if he did land somewhere he recognized, he'd be alone without resources. That would put him in an undesirable position. What was the worst that could come of hearing the devil out?

"What's the alternative?" Shiroe asked.

Balthazar held up a hand. In a flash of red light, a glowing red chess piece, a Bishop, appeared, pinched between his thumb and index finger. "As I told you, I am a devil. I come from a different world than the one you left, though it is similar in many aspects. The devils of my world created a method of reincarnating other individuals into devils, empowering them in the process."

Shiroe looked closely at the Bishop. "The method is based around chess?"

"Yes."

"Do you have other pieces?"

"I do, but I cannot show them to you. I have already used every piece except this one." Balthazar lifted the Bishop for emphasis.

"What piece do you represent? If you were using others, does that make you the King?"

Balthazar smiled. "It does."

"So you would be in charge. What would a Bishop's position be?"

"Each peerage, that is what we call these assortments of reincarnated devils, is different. The roles in my peerage are more loose than others. I am in command with my Queen as my second. The other members of my peerage are largely free to operate as they will outside of this simple command structure. Provided you accept my offer, I see you eventually becoming my third in command."

That intrigued Shiroe. "Why?"

Balthazar smiled fondly. "I adore my peerage, but many of them are…unstructured. I don't currently have anyone to fill the role of a strategist and planner. That is what I envision for you. Your magical power is not as great as the others, but the Bishop piece will enhance your potential."

"The piece has effects other than reincarnating others as devils?"

"Yes. Each piece boosts an aspect corresponding to its role. The Bishop will magnify your mana and magical power considerably if you accept."

"I have never used magic in my life. Isn't it possible that a Bishop would not suit me?"

"You may be unfamiliar with magic, but the body you inhabit is not. I sense a great deal of strength in you. My Queen and my second Bishop would be capable of tutoring you and showing you how to make the best use of your strength."

Shiroe filed that away for later. One of his larger immediate concerns involved in ending up in a random world, aside from dying of exposure or starvation, was not having any guidance on how to use the abilities he supposedly gained. In isekai, that typically wasn't a concern, but he'd been subtly trying to activate his character's skills from the game for over a minute now to no effect. There were no menus. He was having to work off gut instinct. So far, it has failed him.

"Why should I accept your offer instead of taking my chances in a new world?" Shiroe asked.

"Ultimately, it's your decision. All I can do is outline the many benefits that come with accepting my offer."

"Such as?"

"When devils in stories offer people their heart's desire, there are typically strings attached involving the loss of one's soul. That isn't the case here. Not only am I a powerful devil, but I'm also obscenely rich even by devil standards. What do you want? I can buy it and have it ready for you in a few hours at most. I am a Viscount of Hell with more money than many gods. Ask and ye shall receive."

Money would certainly prevent him from dying of starvation. "What other benefits are there?"

"You'll stop aging. Devils live basically forever so long as they don't do anything stupid, so immortality comes as part of it. Phenomenal power. You get to live in a castle. Seriously, it's not a matter of what I can offer you. The list of what I can't give you would be shorter."

"Then what can't you offer me?"

Balthazar grinned. "Much like a genie, I can't make anyone fall in love with you. Sorry if I crushed your hopes there."

Shiroe's eyes narrowed as he watched the devil. "This sounds too good to be true." Common sense and every story he'd ever heard told him that a deal with a devil that sounded too good to be true, was too good to be true.

"I'm being genuine." Balthazar said. "All I really have to back that up is my word, so if you don't trust it, then I guess we're done. I'll be straight with you Shiroe. I want you in my peerage, but I'm not going to jeopardize the stability of my existing peerage to bend over backwards for you. If you make any outrageous demands or I feel like you'd make any of the existing members of my peerage uncomfortable, then you're out. Presently, I think you'd be a good fit, so the offer's on the table."

Shiroe looked back at the broken hole in space. "What can you tell me about the world I was going to before you showed up?"

Balthazar held his hand up to the Hole. "You are welcome to experience it firsthand for yourself. Caveat: This is a one-time offer. If you walk through that Hole, I'll leave you to forge your own path. My offer leaves with me and you'll never see me again."

Shiroe frowned. So here was the other shoe dropping. He could take his chances with the devil who presented a very tempting offer, so tempting as to be suspicious, or he could risk a complete unknown. Maybe he'd end up in a town where he'd have shelter and easy access to food. Maybe he'd wind up deep in a forest surrounded by monsters or in the fantasy equivalent of the arctic with no shelter in sight. It wasn't a risk he wanted to take.

"What would be expected of me as a member of your peerage?" Shiroe asked, purely to better weigh his options.

"As I said, each peerage is different. For a while, I'll leave you to your own devices for the most part. You'll be free to pursue your own interests so long as you're there when I need you. In the near future, that will involve participating in a Rating Game and potentially being on standby in case we're attacked. I've managed to make a couple powerful enemies."

Shiroe's eyes narrowed. "What enemies?"

"Helios and Boreas." Balthazar admitted easily.

Shiroe felt his mouth go dry. Surely he didn't mean…

Balthazar nodded, reading his shock. "Yes, that Helios and Boreas. Greek Titan of the Sun and the god of the North Wind and Storms. I told you I'd shoot straight with you Shiroe. I'm not going to hide the bad just to get you to agree. That might piss you off and leave us both stuck in a shitty situation. This peerage thing is permanent, so I need to be sure that you and I understand each other and can get along. I don't expect you to fight a Titan one on one in your first week, but if he sends his minions at us, I'm going to expect you to fight with the rest of us. We also have a Rating Game in about a week, and you'll need to at least be on the field even if you refrain from fighting."

Shiroe swallowed, trying to get his vocal chords to work again. The casual admittance that he might be asked to fight against the Greek Titan of the Sun had shifted the scales quite a bit. The arctic was still certain death, but maybe he could survive a forest infested with monsters?

"What's a Rating Game?" Shiroe asked, trying to fill all of the gaps in his knowledge.

Balthazar pursed his lips, considering how to answer. "Giant, flashy combat scrimmages between devil peerages. We fight in a controlled area with every safety precaution available to let us train and practice. The match we have coming up is against the second strongest peerage in the Underworld. Our last match was against the previous third seed and we beat them even with only half of our peerage. We have way more manpower and strength now. All we're missing is our last Bishop." Balthazar waved the chess piece in his hand dramatically.

"How many allies do Helios and Boreas have among the Greek pantheon?" Shiroe asked, focusing back on the Titan in the room.

"None." Balthazar said with an evil grin. "They've gone to ground. Olympus has cut them loose. Anything we face from them will be only what they personally can front."

From what little Shiroe had researched into Helios's court, that little amount still amounted to a lot. He quickly tried to weigh his odds fighting an army of nereids with devils for backup over his odds of surviving a forest full of death monsters on his own.

"Can I have some time to think about this?" Shiroe asked.

Balthazar raised an eyebrow. "So long as you hang out here, the offer is on the table. When you leave, you're on your own."

Shiroe nodded, moving away from the devil and from the swirling vortex that would send him on his way.

Shiroe took a deep breath. He held his hand out in front of himself, concentrating. He grit his teeth. He willed something to happen, anything.

Nothing.

Shiroe let out a frustrated huff, standing up straight and withdrawing his hand. His odds of surviving in a potential murder forest just dropped to zero. If he was sent anywhere where there wasn't immediate safety, he ran the risk of dying before he could learn how to use his character's powers. This wasn't a story written to ensure the main character made it through. This was real life with real consequences. He had no guarantee he would live to tomorrow if he walked through that portal. He would wake up tomorrow if he went with the devil. He could figure everything else after that. But first, there was one thing left for him to ask.

"Can you send me home?" Shiroe asked, walking back over to join Balthazar.

Balthazar considered him carefully. "What do you mean?"

"Can you send me back to the world I was isekai'd from."

Balthazar was quiet for a moment. "I'll be honest with you. I don't know. I have a very broad reach, but some places are locked away from me. I haven't tried to reach out to that world. I was more focused on reaching out to bring you here. I could potentially send you back, but I have no reason to."

Shiroe narrowed his eyes. "Not just to help me?"

Balthazar fixed him with a flat look. "Shiroe, I'm going to stay honest with you. I'm a devil. I'm not as much of a bastard as some of my brethren, but I'm not a shining example of nobility either. There is very little I wouldn't do for my people, but you're not one of my people right now. You're some random guy I am offering a position in my peerage. I have other options. You are definitely my first choice, but not my only one."

"If I join you, would you try to send me back?"

Balthazar was quiet for a moment. "No. I'd probably try to find the world you came from so you could visit on occasion if you wanted, but I wouldn't send you back permanently. If you choose to join my peerage, Hell will be your new home. You'll be a member of my family. You'd have to live with the family."

Shiroe nodded. "Thank you for your honesty."

"It's the least I can give you."

Shiroe gripped his chin in thought. He turned to look at the portal, watching the dark magic shift to and fro.

"You said I'd be a member of the family." Shiroe said, distracted. "Is your peerage a family?"

Balthazar smiled, warm and happy. "I like to think so. Some kings treat their peerages poorly. Some are servants, others are little better than slaves. We're different. My peerage is free to do whatever they want so long as I don't need them. Some spend that time bashing each other's teeth in because they're battle junkies, others drop thousands of dollars at Build-A-Bear every week. We all get along well. We help each other when we need it. We're there for each other. Isn't that what a family is?"

Shiroe's mind wandered back to many long nights spent alone, eating cup ramen heated in the microwave. Was that really all that awaited him in his old world?

"If I accept," Shiroe said slowly, turning to face Balthazar. "How does this work? Will I grow horns and a tail?"

Balthazar shook his head. "Wings. Nothing more. I just push the Bishop into your chest and it's done. There might be a moment of discomfort, but it will fade quickly."

Shiroe nodded. "Okay. I accept."

"You're sure?" Balthazar asked seriously.

Shiroe nodded. He wouldn't have said it if he hadn't already thought it through.

Balthazar stepped forward and pressed the chess piece into his chest.

Shiroe's breath caught as fire filled his veins. He gasped as wings exploded from his back. His vision went white. When he could see again, he was staring at his hands, huffing, feeling as if he'd just been struck by lightning…only the lightning didn't leave, it still crackled through his veins, swelling like a bound storm. Shiroe looked around in shock. The black void was gone. He was standing in an opulent hall with a high ceiling. A violet carpet sat atop dark floors. Gems dotted the walls.

Balthazar laid a hand on his shoulder. "Welcome home, Shiroe. It's good to have you here."
