#7,578
Shiroe walked quietly at my side as I gave him the standard tour of the castle. When he saw something he didn't understand, he asked pointed questions. I answered his questions patiently and did my best to help him settle in. He'd only been a devil for somewhere around sixteen hours at this point. I'd shown him to his rooms when we arrived yesterday and gave him the opportunity to rest. He jumped on it.

Each section of the castle set aside for one of my peerage members had a host of its own rooms to give them their own private space. A bedroom, sitting room, study and bathroom were the main amenities. Each member of the peerage altered them to better suit their needs. Matatabi's rooms had been terraformed into a sea of cushions all over the floor and some even stitched into the ceiling to give her a better vantage point to nap from.

Shiroe seemed a little overwhelmed by all of the space. I wasn't sure exactly what his situation had been like in his prior life, but it was safe to say his current residence was better.

I'd put off the tour for today because I wanted to give him a chance to get his bearings. It seemed to have worked wonders. He wasn't nearly as skittish as he was yesterday afternoon. I let him have a meal brough to him by the skeletons, then picked him up when he returned the dishes.

"I appreciate the tour, Balthazar," he said, thankfully not hesitating to use my actual name instead of some grandiose title. "But, will I not be meeting the other members of the peerage?"

"My original plan was to show you around a little more, but I can introduce you if you want?"

Shiroe nodded. "I would prefer to meet those I will be living with. You mentioned your Queen and my fellow Bishop could help me learn to cast magic."

"I did. Come with me." I opened a Hole and walked with him through it.

"Just a moment, honey." Medea said over her shoulder, not turning away from the work bench in front of her. She held a glowing needle, gently engraving a shining breastplate on the table in front of her.

"Is that for Achilles?" I asked as I moved closer for a better look. I still maintained enough distance to avoid getting in her way.

Medea nodded, distractedly. "It is. I already finished his weapons and other armaments. This is the final piece."

"Achilles?"

Medea turned with me to find the new voice, when she saw Shiroe standing somewhat awkwardly behind her, she smiled warmly. "Hello. Am I correct in assuming you are our newest Bishop?"

Shiroe's thumb ran over his staff nervously as he nodded. "Yes. My name is Shiroe."

"It's good to meet you, Shiroe. My name is Medea. I am Balthazar's Queen."

Shiroe looked at me, seeming overwhelmed. "Achilles, and now Medea? Are they…?"

Medea chuckled. "We're the real deal, sweetie. You'll find our peerage is full of remarkable individuals."

"Shiroe was hoping you could help him get a handle on his magic. He's very new to all of this." I explained.

"Of course," Medea said easily. "Just let me finish this armor. I'll be right with you." She turned around and continued her engraving.

"If I'm intruding, I can leave you be." Shiroe said, shuffling awkwardly.

"And done!" Medea declared proudly. She spun around and clapped her hands. "Now let's see what we can do for you."

"Thanks, Medea. I'll leave you to it."

Shiroe's head snapped to look at me. "You're leaving me?"

I smiled and gave him an encouraging pat on the shoulder. "You're in good hands. If you need me, just reach out through the gem network or have Medea give me a shout. I'll see if I can track down Irene to come give you a hand." I stepped back into a Hole, leaving Shiroe in my Queen's capable hands. I wasn't the best teacher. Most of what I knew I learned from Medea or forced myself to figure out through sheer stubbornness. I wouldn't be much help tutoring someone with no magical experience.

"Hey, Bal!" Aqua greeted happily. She was sitting cross-legged on a couch with a bunch of stuffed animals strewn about her. She had an oversized teddy bear dressed in medieval knight armor sitting in her lap. The lights were all off, leaving the only source of illumination to be the tv in front of her.

"Hey, Aqua. How's it going?"

"I'm good. What's up?"

"I was hoping to enlist your help with something if you're not too busy."

"Sure. This is boring anyway." She turned off the TV and hopped to her feet, scurrying over to my side. "What are we doing?"

"I need your help finding a different world."

She frowned. "I'm happy to help, but Medea's better at finding places. I'm better at just going places."

"True, but I can't ask for Medea's help with this."

"Why not?"

"Because I'm trying to surprise her."

Aqua fixed me with a suspicious look. "Surprise her with what?"

"I'll tell you when we're out of the castle." I didn't think Medea was watching me right now, but she could view almost any room in the castle whenever she wanted. The only places she couldn't view were the private areas for my other peerage members and two of my guest rooms. I had a set of guest rooms for people I actually liked and trusted and a host of guest rooms for random people I didn't know that Medea was free to spy on.

I opened a Hole, pulling Aqua and I away from the Castle. I brought us to Lucifaad, entering a coffee shop to buy her a scone and a sugar-filled, caffeine drink while I explained what I wanted. The more I talked, the more excited she became.

"What are we waiting for?" Aqua demanded, grabbing my arm and dragging me out of my chair. Her Keyblade appeared in her hand. With a flick of her wrist, a Keyhole opened in space, sucking the two of us into it.


X


My search with Aqua was fruitful. We were going over the finer details of my plan when I was interrupted by something I wouldn't have expected. A mortal holding one of my flyers was reaching out to summon me. If I recall correctly, an angel and a wraith each had one of my flyers, but I'd only given them out to two mortals.

"Aqua?" I asked.

"Yeah?"

"Do you want to meet my new warlock?"

"Do you really have to ask? Let's go!"

I pulled us away with a Hole.

"My lord," Cyvis greeted me, dipping into a curtsy. Vellia knelt at her side.

"Please stop doing that." I said, waving for them to stand up.

Aqua pushed past me and waved, smiling wide at Cyvis. "Hi! We haven't met yet. I'm Aqua, Balthazar's Knight."

"It is an honor to meet you, my lady." Cyvis said, bowing her head.

"Uh uh." Aqua said, scowling. "None of that. Call me Aqua. I'm not above you, okay?"

Cyvis and Vellia shared an uncertain look.

"As you wish…Aqua." Cyvis said uncertainly.

Aqua nodded, satisfied. "Much better."

How come they listened to her when she told them to be more relaxed but not me? Was I not their boss?

I kept my internal grumblings to myself, instead looking around. This wasn't the room I'd met them in before. Shelves filled with aging books of all different sizes stood tall all around us. A number of tables stood in the center of the room. One table was laden with half-open books and stacks of others waiting to be read through.

"Did you already find something?" I asked, surprised. I'd asked them to look into something for me, but I kind of assumed it was a long shot. If I really wanted results, I should have asked much sooner.

"We did, my lord." Cyvis said proudly, hurrying over to one of the open books on the table. "My parents cultivated a library filled with many stories as well as copies of first-hand reports of various expeditions. This details a group that braved the Underdark to find Kharad-Veth. They had a brief encounter with Maltherion that ended with several members of the expedition being killed."

"Kharad-Veth? Maltherion?" I asked. The names meant nothing to me.

Vellia walked around the table to grab another one of the open books. "Kharad-Veth was a mining settlement close enough to the surface that it sometimes did business with Cyvis's ancestors. Maltherion is a lich said to travel through the Nine Hells and the Abyss collecting artifacts and specimens that interest him, my lord." Vellia said, handing the open book to me.

I thumbed through it. There wasn't much detail, just a lot of assumptions made about some great tragedy that befell the city after they uncovered something they shouldn't have. There was some speculation about demonic dealing and an ancient wizard who bargained with the Hells to learn the path to lichdom, wandering the lower planes collecting more power and knowledge in the wake of his 'ascension'. The guy sounded like a budget Acererak, just much less scary.

"You couldn't find any other leads?" I asked, knowing it wasn't likely. I'd asked them to track down an Amulet of Planes for me. I knew the amulets existed, but I also knew they were nearly impossible to come by. Honestly, it was a miracle they'd turned up anything. Even if I'd rather not tangle with a lich if I could avoid it.

Cyvis frowned. "I'm sorry, my lord. This was all we could find. Perhaps if we were given more time I could…"

I waved her off. "My timeline is pretty ironclad. It's not your fault that I didn't give you time to look for alternatives."

Aqua read the book over my shoulder with a curious look on her face. "Why did you have them looking into this guy?"

"He might have a magic item that lets him travel between worlds. I want it for the same reason I wanted your help today."

"Oh. Oh!" Aqua's eyes widened. Her lip quivered, tears were gathering in her eyes. "That's so sweet, Bal."

"It might not work out if this is our only lead." I said, rubbing my chin thoughtfully. "A lich rumored to travel the planes was seen in the Underdark seventy years ago? That's not much to go on."

"We can't not try, right?" Aqua insisted. "Think of how perfect it would be!"

I scowled, intently looking through the book again. I wanted an Amulet of Planes to give to Medea as an engagement gift. Currently, she was reliant on me and Aqua to travel to other worlds. My thought was, if Aqua was able to unlock the amulet's potential with her keyblade, Medea should theoretically have a method to travel independently.

I guess I could just put this whole thing off and wait until the wedding itself. I was artificially rushing myself because I wanted to make the moment I asked Medea to marry me special. That was the only requirement she'd given me when the topic of marriage was broached the first time.

"Cyvis, do you think you could find an alternative with a little extra time?" I asked.

Cyvis nodded. "I believe I can, my lord."

"Oh, come on!" Aqua said, scowling at me. "We're not even gonna try? Let's at least check if the shriveled idiot is there first. Between the two of us, it won't even take an hour."

"I'm wary about brazenly walking into what may or may not be a lich's lair without support. They're dangerous, Aqua." I protested.

She fixed me with a flat look. "And we're not? If you're worried, we'll pop back home and grab some back up first. Achilles would probably love to delve into the depths of another world to fight an undead monstrosity. If whatever is down there is too much for us, we can just teleport away. It's worth at least looking, right?"

I pursed my lips, looking back at the book in my hands. There was a rough illustration of the lich in question on the page. He wore a necklace with a dark chain. A circular pendant was affixed to the chain with a hole in the center.

I really wanted that amulet.


X


The Underdark both lived up to my expectations and failed to meet them. It was nearly pitch black down here. Wonderful and terrible flora grew from the ground and walls, glowing softly with orange and blue bioluminescent light. One of the plants tried to spit poison needles at us, but it was trivial to block the needles with a magical barrier.

I was sure this place was deadly for mortals, but I operated on an entirely different scale of power than this place. So far, we hadn't encountered anything that wasn't easily dealt with. Even the group of giant spiders that descended on us from the ceiling were incinerated by elemental fire before they got within thirty feet of us, and they had the element of surprise on their side.

I'd done my best to keep our group small while still overpreparing. I wanted us to be able to overwhelm anything we faced, but I also wanted Aqua and I to be able to rapidly evacuate everyone if the need arose.

Matatabi was napping, wrapped tight around my neck like a poofy, flaming scarf. She said to wake her up if we needed her. The warmth of her flaming fur licking my skin was oddly comforting.

Achilles walked at the head of our group, unafraid as he forged a path into the dark. Aqua walked at his side, making idle chatter with her fellow Knight.

Shang Tsung walked at my side with Mothra perched atop his head in her moth form. Mothra was loving the Underdark. She would periodically fly off of Shang Tsung's head to nibble samples of the various glowing plants. She seemed to particularly enjoy the poison plant that had tried to shoot needles at us.

I wanted to bring Irene to help us scry a path of where to go, but she and Medea were currently helping Shiroe get a handle on his magic. From what little I saw when I poked my head in the room, they were making substantial progress. Shiroe had a corona of bright blue energy surrounding him that flicked around as he flexed his fingers. I didn't want to pull one of his teachers away when they were starting to make real progress. Shang Tsung had been taught personally by Medea and could mimic her magic. He'd serve well enough as our mystical scout.

My two warlocks completed our merry band, walking in between my Knights and Shang Tsung and I where they were as protected as I could make them. Initially, I'd planned to leave them behind where it was safe. Then Aqua offered to let them come before I ordered them to stay. Achilles seemed to love the idea, and the warlocks both instantly jumped on the chance to charge headfirst into the Underdark with a party of devils.

Vellia already had armor from Medea. I pulled a mithril chainshirt out of storage for Cyvis and gave her some jewelry with other protective enchantments. Then I gave her a staff for good measure. Cyvis and Vellia had firm orders to leave most of the fighting to us. If they saw something that they thought they couldn't beat, they were to run to me or Aqua immediately so we could get them out of here. I wasn't going to lose my warlocks because I was looking for a necklace in the Underdark.

We'd been walking for close to two hours by this point. The Underdark was a maze of twisting tunnels and dead-ends. Spaced at random intervals, the tunnels gave way to massive caverns large enough to house a city. These gaps were simple enough to traverse. Shang Tsung would pinpoint the next tunnel we needed to travel down, then we would teleport to that tunnel across the vast cavern through a Hole. The tunnels themselves were more difficult to navigate. I could open Holes through them without issue, but blindly transporting us into different tunnels ran the risk of losing track of our intended destination. Walking was slower, but we were still making great progress. A journey that would have taken a mortal adventuring party weeks of careful traversal had cost us a couple hours of our time.

"We're close, my lord." Shang Tsung, wearing Medea's form, said as he blinked the scrying spell from his eyes. "There are ruins matching the description given in the report ahead."

"Everyone stay sharp. We don't know what we're walking into." Realistically, even a lich shouldn't be able to cause too much trouble for me, let alone with so many members of my peerage backing me up. Still, it was better to be careful.

The tunnel we were walking in opened into another monstrous cavern, yawning wide into a dark abyss. A sheer cliff dropped into a sloping pit. Even with my devil's sight, I could only barely make out the outline of a crumbled stone structure far below in the dark.

"Do you sense anything living?" I asked.

Shang Tsung shook his head, briefly flashing green as he assumed his true appearance. "I am unable to detect any living presence, my lord."

"Keep quiet. Keep your eyes peeled. Follow me." I ordered, curt. I opened a Hole and stepped through it first.

I emerged amid the ruins of a circular stone tower. Jagged rock and vines fell away from a half-collapsed second level. Brass cups and metal shelves lay shattered and broken around me.

Stepping around the tower, I got my first look at the city proper. It was far larger than I'd expected, spanning the entire floor of the cavern. Additional sections sat under overhangs cut into the rock. Most of the buildings were in various states of disrepair, collapsed inward or blasted apart by some unseen force. A scant few structures remained standing. Glowing vegetation had scaled their walls and overrun their roofs. No one was maintaining this place. It was a ghost town.

"Kharad-Veth," Cyvis breathed reverently, eyes wide. "It's still here. We really found it."

"Cyvis, where did the expedition encounter the lich?" I asked. Impressive as the newly discovered lost city was, it wasn't why I was here. Cyvis could send the location back to her people and have them catalogue it if she so desired. I didn't see much use in sifting through the ruins of a city in the Underdark when I already had so much going on.

"I…" Cyvis shook her head. "Forgive me, my lord. We came here for a purpose. The expedition never made it to the city itself. They were closer to the surface than we are now. I believe it would be best if we found a tunnel going upwards."

We all began looking around, eyes trained up towards the cavern walls to find an opening we could use to ascend.

Matatabi flinched, slowly unwinding until she was perched on my shoulder. She sniffed at the air in disdain. "Something stinks. Something rotten."

I sniffed at the air. I smelled the plants and the dusty interior of the buildings and the droppings of some creature that had made the ruins its home. I couldn't smell anything rotten.

"Do you know what it is?" I asked.

Matatabi shuffled her feet on my shoulder, arching her back into a mighty stretch. She hopped off my shoulder and started trotting forward. She turned to look over her shoulder and said, "Follow me. It's close."

Our party followed the small ball of azure fire as she patted along the dark stone ground. Matatabi nimbly weaved around debris, hopping over fallen walls and crumbled roofs without making a sound, pausing periodically to make sure we were keeping pace. She stopped at the mouth of a tunnel, obscured by a large boulder and blooming yellow foliage.

Matatabi's tails danced through the air behind her as she sniffed the air. She hissed in displeasure. "There is death in this cave."

"We seek the dead." Achilles said, an excited shine in his eye. His spear rested against his shoulder, shield affixed to his left arm.

I stared down the dark tunnel. Unlike the others we'd walked through to get here, there was no fauna of any kind. Bioluminescent flowers and fungus were common along our journey. Far down this tunnel off to where it turned out of sight, there was nothing. Maybe it was a coincidence.

"Keep your guard up. Matatabi, let me know if you smell anything else out of place. Shang Tsung, be on the lookout for magical defenses. Achilles, you're in front with me." I quickly ordered.

Achilles practically skipped up to my side. Matatabi leapt from the ground back onto my shoulder. Her tails wound around my neck and shoulder to secure her, eyes narrowed as she stared into the tunnel.

The others fell in behind us as Achilles and I led the way down the tunnel. After the first turn, I began to smell what Matatabi had described. There was something rotten. Something decayed. Something dead.

We might just be in the right place.

We followed the tunnel for several minutes. With each step deeper, the smell grew more repugnant until it was all encompassing. A final turn hooked to the right then opened into another chamber. I held up a hand to stall the others behind me, intently looking over what I could see of the room. Matatabi quietly hissed on my shoulders, the flames of her back licking back into the air like hackles.

The chamber ahead was far smaller than the massive cave that held the city of Kharad-Veth. It was roughly the size of a city block. The ground was mostly flat save for small clumps of material. The ceiling rose high into darkness so true even my devil sight couldn't pierce it. That shouldn't be possible. The only way something could best my devil eyes was through magic or some other supernatural phenomenon.

Shang Tsung slowly crept up to my side, his careful steps barely made any sound as he approached. Leaning in close, he whispered, "There is a large gathering of magic ahead."

"Tell Aqua to be ready to pull people out of here." I said quietly back. I flexed my power, opening small Holes near the ears of everyone around me. "Stay here until I say otherwise. Be ready for anything." I whispered through the Holes. I looked at Achilles and nodded.

He returned my nod with a grin, swirling his spear into a ready position. Together, we stepped into the cavern.

Achilles walked in the lead. I stayed close behind him to cover his back. The entire ceiling was coated in the impossible darkness. I couldn't perceive anything past it. On the ground littered around us were piles of rock and other clumps. Bones with crushed skulls and splintered femurs were set into neat piles at precise intervals.

I did not like this.

"You are not the first group of adventurers to find this place." a cold, disinterested voice spoke, echoing down from the dark. "You will not be the last."

Matatabi leapt to her feet, clambering up to the top of my head, hissing in warning up towards the ceiling. A low, rumbling growl emphasized by sharp clacks called back. A shape poked through the darkness. Impossibly white. Sharp. A fang.

Whatever illusion covered the ceiling unraveled around the fang, revealing a massive form clinging to the ceiling like a bat.

It had no skin. No flesh. No muscles. The skeleton of a massive dragon hung upside down from the ceiling, its wings of bone spread wide. A sinister green energy pulsed in the cavity of its chest. Its eyes glowed with undead light as it opened its mouth in a roar of challenge.

Matatabi's hiss turned into a roar to match. I felt her slowly expanding, growing larger.

I held up a hand. "Not yet."

Matatabi tensed atop my head, but slowly shrunk back down.

The creature I assumed to be a dracolich had yet to move, as if waiting for a command.

I gently pushed against the space with my magic, searching for anything out of place. There.

I ignored the dragon looming over me, turning to face an empty section of air to my right. "This does not need to devolve into a fight. I came here for a specific purpose. Once that purpose is met, I will leave."

Silence filled the cave for several seconds. Even the dracolich stopped shifting to leap towards us.

The air before me shimmered as an invisibility spell faded to reveal a wan figure floating fifteen feet off the ground. Shriveled skin clung to his bones, leathery and boiled with rot. The skin of his face was peeled away in places revealing the molars at the back of his mouth and an empty eye socket glowing with unholy power. In stark contrast to his flesh, his clothes were immaculate. Royal blue robes gently billowed around him as he moved through the air. A bronze staff in his hand held runes running along its length that glowed bright orange with magical power. A silver amulet with a blue saphire fixed to it hung from a chain around his neck. A simple gold band was worn about his head. Strips of leather held a book loosely against his hip like a satchel. He wore a ring on each hand. On his left, a gold band held a mirror that shined with power. On his right hand, a silver band housed a gem that seemed to contain a galaxy, nebulas and stars shifted within the gem.

"I am impressed you could sense my presence." the lich said, voice scratchy and unnatural.

"I am not the same as the adventurers you have killed en masse before. All I want is a single item. I heard from reliable sources that you frequently travel the lower planes." I said, keeping my voice even, calm. If I could avoid a fight and still get what I wanted, I'd consider that a win. If things devolved into a fight anyway, I needed to know this guy actually had an Amulet of Planes, otherwise this would all be for nothing.

The lich's cracked eyelids drew together as he narrowed his eyes at me. The effect was almost comical given I could see an empty socket where one of his eyes should be. "You are well-informed indeed. After I kill you, I will seek out those who told you of me. I enjoy my privacy."

"All I want is an Amulet of Planes. If you provide me with one, I will leave this place without destroying you. I am willing to purchase it from you. What would you ask in exchange?" I said. Matatabi bared her fangs and growled low atop my head.

The lich threw his head back and laughed. "You have come to court certain death for such a trifling thing? You are a fool, young man. I have had no need for such worthless trinkets in years. My creation is far superior." He held up his right hand, thumbing the ring he wore with stars in its gem. "You are amusing if nothing else. I will remember your foolishness. The same cannot be said for many I have killed. Farewell, mortal. Die."

I stepped in front of Achilles and hastily erected a violet barrier. Black, necromantic energy slammed into my barrier, shot forth from the head of the lich's staff. The dracolich above let out an unholy shriek as it let go of the ceiling, wings folding in close as it dove towards us.

"Attack." I said, into a Hole.

Matatabi leapt off my head, snarling as she rapidly grew to her true size. She met the dracolich's charge in midair, swatting at the skeletal dragon's head just as it released an acidic spray of necromantic ichor, slapping the attack off course to harmlessly flay the cavern wall.

Achilles dashed, body blurring with his speed as he closed the distance to the lich. Even I was shocked with how fast he moved. It was no surprise the lich was caught flat-footed.

Achilles's spear pierced the lich's chest as the undead tried to cast a spell. The point of Achilles's spear glowed with crimson energy as it punctured the lich's chest.

The lich howled in pain. A magical protection flared to life, blasting Achilles from point blank range.

Achilles was able to get his shield up in time to block the blast of magic. The lich used the opportunity to pull himself off his spear. Once free, he vanished in a puff of mist.

"My lord!" Shang Tsung called.

The ground split open behind me. A mound of bones behind me was engulfed in a volcanic inferno.

I frowned, looking around. Each mound of bones was slowly pulling itself together. Some split into four independent skeletons. Others collected together into large, misshapen monstrosities.

Mothra flew off of Shang Tsung's head, bobbing in the air as she slowly grew in size. A loud wail echoed off the sheer walls of the cave as the monstrous moth fell atop the dragon as it tried to shake Matatabi off. Her weight sent the beast careening into the ground. Pinned by Mothra, the dragon was helpless as Matatabi began rending it apart with her large claws.

Thunderous booms sounded behind me. Vellia and Cyvis had spread dark rifts and shimmering opal vortexes all around the area. Vellia stepped between them, slashing into the assembling skeletons while Cyvis supported her from afar. Aqua tore apart any creation that got too close to Cyvis.

I felt reality crack around us. A fiery vortex opened on the cavern floor. A large, furred arm reached out, grabbing the ledge and hefting itself up. A large ape-like beast with massive arms and bulging shoulders roared as it charged towards me. I felt the fiendish nature of the creature. The lich was summoning demons.

I opened a Hole in front of the demon. A spear flew out of my Hole as if fired from a ballista. The spear took the demon in the chest and knocked it backward to the ground. Three more Holes opened above its body, sending three more spears into its wriggling form. It stopped moving.

To my left, Achilles had engaged a mass of moving shadow shaped like a man. His spear cleaved through the semi-corporeal monster, tearing at its immaterial body as easily as if it were made of styrofoam.

A second form clambered out of the vortex my first opponent crawled out of. Clay-colored skin was taut across bulging muscles, boiling unhealthily in places. Dark spines stood up from the creatures back like obsidian daggers, poised to cut and puncture.

The pure darkness of the cavern was banished as elemental fire poured down on the hulking creature from every direction. The beast let out an agonized screech as fire from the creation of the world scorched its body into nothingness.

"Balthazar!"

My head snapped around at Aqua's desperate shout.

Aqua was frantically pointing to the far side of the cavern. "He ran! He used that ring before I realized what he was doing. I can follow him if we go right now!"

I looked around at the state of the cave. The dracolich was still pinned, thrashing futilely under Mothra's weight in an effort to escape as Matatabi ripped it apart bone by bone. Shang Tsung and Achilles wove between the skeletons and demons, cutting them apart. They rapidly moved around the cave, using Cyvis's opal vortexes and Vellia's dark rifts to teleport freely. My two warlocks supported Shang Tsung and Achilles, following them around and covering their flanks while they dealt with the weaker skeletons to let my Pawn and Knight fight the greater demons.

"Go, my King!" Achilles called happily, a bright smile on his face as he cut down another demon. "Leave this to us!"

"Call through a Hole the instant you need us!" I called back. I didn't like the idea of leaving them alone. I especially didn't like the idea of leaving them alone without Aqua, effectively trapping them here. Shang Tsung would be able to teleport them back to safety if the need arose, but they'd be stuck without any means of planar transit.

The idea of letting this prick of a lich get away irked me even more.

Aqua's keyblade was already aimed at a distortion in the air. As she channeled her power through it, the rift grew large. Reality wobbled unnaturally as she forced space to comply with her demands.

"We need to go right now!" she shouted.

I appeared at her side through a Hole. She wrapped an arm around my shoulders and dragged me forward. A dark keyhole opened in the rift in front of us, sucking us through.

We stumbled to a stop, our footsteps clapping on cold grey stone bricks. We were in what appeared to be the interior of a medieval castle. Torches of black metal hung on the walls around us. The room was square. A single wooden door in front of us was the only exit.

Standing opposite the door near a wall of stone bricks, the lich held his robes open with one hand, poking at the puncture wound in his undead chest left by Achilles's spear.

His head snapped up in shock as we appeared. "Impos–"

The rest of what he said was drowned out by the crackle of dozens of magical traps activating simultaneously.

I unceremoniously dragged Aqua down to the ground beneath me, standing over her as I erected layer upon layer of amethyst shields around us.

The first layer of shields was sundered under the force of five glyphs firing black death magic at us. The next layer crumbled under the force of twelve green rays of pure destruction. Layer after layer of shields was broken by fire, lightning and necrotic power. Outside the barrier, a thick green acidic mist crackled against the air, swirling about as it sought a path through my shields.

Aqua reached up. Her hand closed into a vice-like grip around my belt. She stabbed her keyblade into the floor beneath us. Another keyhole opened, sucking us both down.

We spilled onto the floor of the cavern we'd just left.

I rolled to my feet, calling my Sacred Gear to my hand in its glaive form to bisect a lumbering demon charging towards us. I sent a wave of fire into a group of approaching skeletons, turning them to ash.

"I have the location of the place he fled to now." Aqua said, slamming her keyblade through a massive skeleton, sending bone fragments flying in every direction as it was destroyed. "We have to go back quickly. He might try to flee to another world again. We need to be there when he does or I might lose him."

I looked around. The demons and skeletons were steadily shrinking in number even as more demons were summoned by magical glyphs carved into the ground and the walls. My peerage was simply too much for the army the lich summoned to fight us. The dracolich's once furious struggles had grown weak. Its ribcage was gone. Matatabi was prying its head from its elongated neck.

Seeing they had things well in hand, I nodded to Aqua. "Let's go."

She opened another keyhole. I held a violet shield in front of us as we emerged from the keyhole. We returned to the same room. The air was still thick with the acidic mist. I forced it away from us with my barrier.

The lich was nowhere to be seen. The stone floor in the center of the room where we'd appeared was a maze of sundered stone. Whatever spell traps the lich had laid had done a good job of completely destroying the floor.

I looked around the room, frowning as I reached out with my magical senses.

"Come on, we need to hurry!" Aqua said, making for the door.

I grabbed her arm, stopping her from moving forward, eyes narrowed suspiciously at the door.

The lich had centuries to trap both the cave and this space, what I assumed to be a demiplane of his own creation. He wouldn't make anything easy on someone who made it here and was trying to kill him.

If he really was a budget Acererak, then it was safe to assume that everything here wanted to kill us and that the only way to beat his games was to follow a very specific path through the hell we were in.

I looked back to the other side of the room where the lich had been when we'd arrived. He'd practically been standing against the wall.

I opened a hole, blasting pure demonic power into the wall where the lich had been standing.

The wall was sundered under the force of my power, blown outwards into a concealed hallway.

Immediately, even more magical traps triggered, sending more death magic and elemental horror towards us.

I was more prepared for it this time.

Dozens of Holes opened in the path of the magic, swallowing each spell and trapping it harmlessly in one of my pocket spaces.

When the magical assault faded, a long stone corridor was revealed, ending at a wooden door at the end of the hall.

I didn't trust anything in this place. Every brick was probably trapped and every door likely led to the Abyss for all I knew.

I opened dozens of small Holes connected to points along the hall. I fired precise bursts of demonic power through the Holes, punching small holes in the stone walls of the hall and the door at the far end.

The hallway turned into a vibrant lightshow as even more traps triggered, sending spells flying all over the place. I absorbed any that came near us into Holes, watching the hall intently. In the right wall, only ten feet from the room we were standing in, another corridor was revealed through the fractured stone.

I opened a Hole to the space connected to where I stored an army of Medea's skeletons and Shang Tsung's animated armors, dropping a single skeleton into the hall.

More explosions sounded as the skeleton triggered innumerable traps by its mere presence, sundered under the force of the magical traps. This lich had set every brick in this place to kill any intruder.

I'd call him paranoid, but his protections paled in comparison to the absolute death trap my castle would be for any hostile force that tried to invade it. Medea had been downright wicked as she had her army of skeletons assemble our home, a trait I openly encouraged. A few glyphs set to trigger at an enemy's presence was nothing by comparison.

"Let's go." I said, stepping into a Hole. Aqua followed behind me.

We stepped over fragments of purple bone and crumbled rock, emerging into a large chamber. I kept my eyes and mystical senses peeled for further traps, but I saw and sensed nothing. It appeared as if we reached the heart of the lich's demiplane.

The room was built like a large stone box. The ceiling rose high enough to accommodate a dragon. Sheer walls boxed us in on all sides.

The space itself was cluttered. Every space was filled with something. Floating workstations drifted lazily past bookshelves anchored to points high up the wall. Chests overflowing with gold and racks displaying glowing swords and axes rested along the perimeter of the room. Weak skeletons moved between large basins and heated vats, carrying vials of glowing liquid. Piles upon piles of magical scrolls were neatly cataloged in a specially designed rack. In the center of the floor, a pulsing golden magical circle glowed with power. Bands of arcane runes snaked away from the circle, running along the floor and up the walls. I felt a great protective energy pulsing from the circle. It shielded the demiplane, protecting it and hiding its presence. It should have been almost impossible to locate. Whatever was powering the magic circle was strong.

"There." Aqua said, pointed with her keyblade, eyes narrowed.

The lich was here, feverishly fiddling with a scroll. The front of his robe was still pulled open, revealing the gaping wound Achilles gave him.

The lich snarled when he saw us. "You've made a grave mistake coming here. Mortis!" He pointed his finger at me, calling out a word of power.

I erected a barrier. The magic passed right through my shield to impact me in the chest. I felt it connect. I felt a wave of power wash over me…and do nothing.

The lich staggered backward, shocked that I still stood. His surprise quickly gave way to fury.

Dozens of Holes opened all around him. The lich was assaulted from all sides by scorching elemental flame. He hastily erected shields, desperately fending off the fire.

I switched tactics. Concentrated blasts of demonic power fired from the Holes, punching through his shields with ease to assault his body. My attacks sent the lich pinballing back and forth, battering him from all sides. In a burst of silvery mist, he escaped my death trap, falling into a heap on the ground near the far corner of the room.

The skeletons paused in their work, dropping what they were doing to charge towards us.

Aqua's body shimmered, splitting apart into nine echoes. Each copy charged a different skeleton, easily blasting the weak undead apart. Three others charged towards where the lich was frantically scrambling to his feet.

The lich growled in anger as he saw Aqua approach. He gripped the pendant on his neck. Spells woven into the pendant activated. Layers of mystical protection fell over the lich as he flew up into the air. "Contractus aeternus! Virexa Sarexa Lien!" he shouted, teeth clacking together viciously.

Faint, far away, I heard a cry of pain. The cry was quickly forgotten.

I felt magic gather into a tidal wave in the archway leading to the hallway behind me.

I stepped through a Hole to dodge what I assumed was an attack. It wasn't.

A yawning, dark portal rimmed with opal energy expanded into being right before the hallway. The flaming tip of a dark sword was the first thing to emerge from the portal.

A dark gauntleted hand followed. A bipedal form slowly stepped into the chamber. A dark cuirass hugged her form close. She carried a flaming dark chain in her opposite hand. Two small, pointed horns rose away from her coal-black hair. Dark wings with feathers like those of a raven spread wide behind her as she fully entered the chamber. She wore no helmet, revealing fair skin and sinister orange eyes.

"Kill them!" the lich ordered, firing a beam of sickly green energy at one of the Aquas charging him. His spell impacted the copy, scattering it into motes of golden energy. He cursed as he was forced to teleport in another puff of silver energy lest two other Aquas cleave him apart with their keyblades.

For now, Aqua seemed to have the lich on the backfoot, I turned to fully face this newest arrival.

Unlike the demons the lich summoned in the cavern, the creature across from me radiated immense power and authority. She was leagues above the others on the fiendish totem pole.

I was a moment away from opening Holes all around her to pincushion her with magical spears when her eyes widened and she took an unconscious step backwards.

She gasped. I heard a sound like shattering glass. Motes of magical energy drifted out of her right gauntlet, scattering into the air.

In a move that shocked me, catching me completely flat-footed, the woman placed the tip of her sword into the ground and knelt before me, averting her gaze.

"Forgive the disrespect, lord." she said, eyes fixed on the floor. "Infernal law dictated I must serve Maltherion."

Heat waves shimmered over her shoulders as she looked up to glare at the lich. He was frozen in complete shock in the middle of the air, allowing one of the Aquas to slash him from behind.

The woman stood, murderous fury coming off her in waves. "Centuries as your thrall. You utter fool, our contract restricted you from turning me against the powers of Hell."

"Cease your blathering and kill them!" the lich shrieked.

The woman dropped her chain to the ground. She raised a hand towards the lich, closing it into a fist.

For a fraction of a second, the lich froze in place. He shook off her spell almost instantly, but the moment's pause was enough for another Aqua to cut into his midsection.

I kept an eye on the woman, not fully trusting her sudden allegiance shift, but the opportunity to destroy the lich before he could escape was too useful for me to pass up.

Holes opened all around the lich. He was able to deflect the first three spears with magical shields. After a punch of demonic power shattered his shield, the next four spears connected, driven half through his body before they got stuck, sending him spinning to the ground.

Four Aquas were on him in an instant. The lich closed his right hand into a fist channeling his power. Before he could complete whatever he was attempting, one of the Aquas cut through his wrist with her keyblade, severing the lich's hand from his body.

The lich let out a roar of frustration and pain, raising a hand to blast Aqua's copies away. The lich was pinned to the ground, his magic forgotten as a flaming sword pierced through his chest. The horned woman leaned over him, wings spread wide around his body, grinning evilly as she twisted her sword in his chest.

Using the opportunity, I opened another Hole right above the lich's head.

The lich screamed in rage and agony as elemental fire engulfed his head, spreading down his withered form to char his entire body.

The horned woman laughed, a merry, delighted sound as she watched the lich writhe and burn. "Our contract is complete, Maltherion." She taunted. "Now I will collect my price."

The lich desperately raised his remaining hand to blast her away. One of Aqua's copies severed that limb as well before he could do anything meaningful with it.

After that, it was just a matter of seconds before my fire melted the lich to ash. His body collapsed in on itself, lacking any structure. Any nonmagical material he had been wearing was gone, slagged with the lich himself. The magical vestments he wore – the robe, the crown, the book, the staff, the amulet – rested buried within his ashy remains. His severed hands rested on the stone floor away from his body, the magical rings on his fingers glowed softly.

One of Aqua's bodies quickly ran to the lich's severed right hand, ripping the ring from his finger and secreting it away before she turned to face the horned woman, watching her suspiciously.

I fell in next to two Aquas, closing ranks as I watched the woman tear her sword free of the stone it had pinned the lich to. She rested the sword's crossguard against her hip. A strip of dark leather moved of its own accord to secure the blade to her side. She turned to face me. Once more, she surprised me when she knelt.

"I was unable to properly greet you, lord. I am Virexa, Erinyes of Dis. I served as Lord Dispatar's emissary to the fool you have slain." she said. Her voice lacked the venom from when she mocked the lich. She was clinical, listing facts, and unemotional.

I forced myself to stay relaxed, to breathe easily. This little jaunt to find an Amulet of Planes had just escalated into a very large potential problem.

The politics of the D&D lower planes were a convoluted nightmare. I was fairly certain I had managed to avoid detection on their radar up to this point due to luck and the overlapping layers of bureaucracy. My warlocks were blips on Hell's radar, but insignificant ones. This? An erinyes claiming to have been dispatched personally by the lord of the second layer of the Nine Hells? This was not a small blip. This was a wave, potentially a tidal wave. I needed to be careful with how I handled this.

She clearly recognized that I was a devil, though it seemed she wrongly assumed I was a devil from the same cosmology as her. She apparently could also somehow sense that I was a lord among devils. I couldn't even begin to guess how she could sense that. I'd worry about it once I sorted out this mess. I needed to be careful here lest I accidentally start a war with Hell.

"What was the purpose of your contract with the lich?" I asked, more to buy myself some time to think than out of actual curiosity.

"Maltherion beseeched my lord centuries ago for the secret to eternal undeath. My lord ordered me to negotiate on his behalf. In exchange for the secrets he sought, Maltherion would attempt an impossible service for my lord." Virexa frowned. "Maltherion accomplished his task, invoking clauses in his contract that forced me to serve under him until he broke his contract." Her grin returned as she turned to look up at me. "Now that he has broken the terms of his contract, his phylactery is forfeit into my possession. You will allow me to collect what is mine by infernal law, won't you my lord?"

I nodded easily. I did not need to piss off all of Hell over a lich's soul. My only concern was him reconstituting his body and coming after me or my warlocks out of a desire for revenge. If Hell had him, that was practically an impossibility. "I will not interfere." I assured her.

Virexa nodded, as if she had expected my answer. "A moment please, my lord." She stood, raising a hand. The flaming chain she'd dropped moments after exiting the portal flew across the chamber into her waiting hand. She placed it on her other hip. It wound itself orderly and another strap extended from her cuirass to secure the corded chain.

Virexa took flight on her wings, flying to the ceiling of the room.

I moved close to Aqua as Virexa punched through the brick into a secret compartment, batting aside fiery magical traps that attempted to roast her alive.

"I want you to go check on the others." I said quietly to Aqua. "Once we know they're safe, we'll try to find what we came for quickly and leave."

Aqua's copies merged into the form at my side. She pressed the lich's ring into my hand. It was the silver band with a living galaxy in its gem. "This is better. I'm taking the other items he wore. Cyvis might be able to use them."

"Take the book for sure." I said, looking at the tome where it lay amongst the lich's ashes. If the lich had lived as long as Virexa claimed, that book was worth more than any amount of gold to a young wizard. A centuries old lich's spellbook? There was literally nothing more valuable to a young wizard than the knowledge housed in those pages.

Aqua nodded. "I don't trust her. Be careful. Call me if you need me." She hurried over to the lich's remains and gathered up his staff and other armaments, being sure to secure the book. With one last distrustful look up at Virexa, she opened a keyhole and was gone.

I looked up as Virexa's wingbeats grew closer. Cradled in her hands, she held a glowing diamond that fit in her hand. Inside the diamond in a hollowed out chamber glowed with unnatural green energy. She secreted the diamond away in her cuirass.

"There is one more thing I must do before I depart, lord." Virexa said as she landed in front of me, tucking her wings behind herself.

I readied myself for a fight as I asked, "What is that?"

"My lord's task he put before Maltherion was to defeat an angel. Elariel had forestalled his interests in the mortal world for some time, always ensuring her actions were just shy of violating celestial treaties. Maltherion was not of Hell. He could act against her without any breach of contract. We expected him to fall in the attempt." Virexa frowned. "He proved more capable than we assumed. His minions weakened her. He used them as pawns to tire her, then he defeated her. Rather than kill her, he put her to another purpose." Virexa motioned to the glowing magical circle etched into the floor of the chamber.

It took me a moment before I realized her meaning. "He imprisoned her. He's using her power to fuel the wards around his demiplane." Suddenly, the cry of pain I heard earlier made sense. The lich pulled Virexa through the wards by force. The angel likely felt that as a physical blow. She didn't react to Aqua's departure because Aqua's keyblade allowed her to simply bypass such defenses.

"The angel must be dealt with before I depart. She cannot be left alone here lest someone find this demiplane and free her." Virexa walked to the wall to the left of the hallway's opening. She pressed a specific brick. The wall opened into a hidden stairwell, descending down in a spiral. She motioned for me to follow her.

I wasn't beholden to her. I didn't need to follow. Curiosity got the better of me.

Before I entered the stairwell, I opened Holes all around the chamber, pulling anything that looked interesting into a pocket dimension. I could sort through all of the loot from the lich's lair later, but I wasn't sure if killing the angel would destabilize the demiplane, and I wanted everything secure before anything happened to the angel.

When I entered the stairwell, the chamber behind me was empty save for scattered bones from destroyed skeletons and broken rock from erratic spells.

The stairwell wound back around to face the direction we'd entered. Virexa had waited for me at the foot of the stairs. She led me through a simple stone hallway. An intricate brass door stood at the end of the hall. The door lurched, locks unlocking to swing open as we approached.

I half-expected a trap until I realized Virexa held the lich's soul on her person. The defenses were likely programmed not to function while he was present.

The room beyond the door was small and circular, only as large as the spell circle etched on the floor above.

Virexa had told me Maltherion kept an angel prisoner down here. I knew what to expect, I was still surprised by the brutality of it.

The angel hung suspended from the ceiling in thick magical chains. The white dress she wore was torn and blackened by soot and grime, no longer able to preserve her modesty. Her golden hair was matted, hanging wildly down from her limp head. Her pearl-white wings were pinned to a magical circle on the ceiling, mirroring the one above. Thick, magical nails were driven through her wings, securing them to the magical circle as they sapped her strength. Her palms were similarly nailed to the ceiling. Her feet dangled from the chains wrapped around her midsection, cracked and bloody.

How long had she been trapped like this? It was barbaric. I wasn't a saint, but the sight awakened a murderous rage in me.

"You were so proud once." Virexa said, slowly approaching the bound angel.

The angel flinched, as if only just realizing she had company. Weakly, she lifted her head. Pure golden eyes peeked through the dense veil of her hair. "Virexa," she said with cracked vocal chords, the words a strain. Her eyes focused on the diamond Virexa lifted up before her eyes. "Is it over then?"

Virexa nodded. "Maltherion has breached our contract. His body is destroyed. I am taking his soul back to Dis."

The angel's head fell to hang limp once more. "Finish it, then." Her voice was weak, resigned. She'd given up.

Virexa made a considering sound as she approached. She gently brushed the angel's hair behind her ears. "That would be such a waste, Elariel. Wouldn't you like to hear my alternative?"

"I don't care anymore. Play your games, then be done with me." Elariel said weakly.

Virexa gently petted the angel's head. "Your god and your siblings have abandoned you to rot here. Why not find a new home? A new beginning? I will draft a contract. I will free you. In return, you will come home with me."

"I will not become a devil. Just kill me." The angel's voice was still weak. A faint trace of resolve firmed her broken voice when she declared she would not become a devil.

"Oh, but that isn't the deal I propose. You will return with me. You will reside in Hell for one-hundred years, serving as an arbiter of justice. At the conclusion of the century, you will be free to go where you will. The contract will only persist if both parties agree to extend the duration." Virexa's voice was like honey. She gently caressed the angel's broken flesh.

The angel was silent. "You will put it in writing. I will go free." The faintest trace of hope clawed its way into her eyes.

"After one-hundred years, you will be free to go where you will." Virexa agreed easily. She flicked her wrist. A flaming parchment with glowing orange infernal writing appeared in her hands. She held it up so the angel could read.

Many minutes passed as the angel read the contract again and again. Finally, she said, "My hands… I cannot sign." She pulled ineffectually at where her palms were nailed to the ceiling.

An infernal pen appeared in Virexa's hand, she held it up to the angel's mouth.

The angel glared at her, accepting the pen after a moment. She scribbled a messy signature onto the page. The flaming parchment exploded, vanishing into the air.

"It is done." Virexa said, a content smile on her face. "Lord, will you help me?"

It took me a moment to realize she was talking to me.

I was all too happy to smash the nails pinning the angel to the ceiling. She let out a cry of pain with each nail destroyed.

My Sacred gear appeared in my hand in its halberd form. I cleaved through the chains holding her like butter. She fell to the ground in a heap. The moment she touched the ground, I felt the magical protections around the demiplane sputter and die. The magical circle on the ceiling faded, now inert.

I reached into a Hole and withdrew a simple grey gown, offering it down to her.

With bloody, trembling hands, she accepted it. I turned around while Virexa helped her into it. I heard tearing as the fabric was made to accommodate her wings.

Virexa helped the weak angel up the stairs. Once we had returned to the chamber, she quietly said, "Contractus aeternus."

Once more, a yawning portal opened in the hallway leading away from the chamber.

Virexa helped the angel limp through the portal. She paused once the angel was through, turning to face me. She bowed her head. "You have done my lord a great service. You have freed me from my contract, destroyed Maltherion's body, allowed me to claim his phylactery, and assisted in the binding of a once powerful solar to his service. May I have your name, lord, so I might inform my master of the assistance you provided?"

I considered her request for a moment. Ideally, I would have stayed on the far periphery of Hell's radar. That was no longer possible after this encounter. Even if I'd wanted to silence the Erinyes by killing her, she would just reform in Hell once slain, allowing her to speak of me all the same. I'd rather Hell have a positive first impression of me than a negative one. If things devolved too far into hostilities, I could just leave and lock the world behind me, annoying as that would be.

"I am Viscount Abaddon, Lord of the House of Abaddon." I said, giving her enough, while withholding my first name. I knew D&D devils could utilize true names to create problems. I wasn't sure if they could use my name in such a way, but it was better to be safe than sorry. Or were those demons that used true names? Maybe it was both of them? I needed to brush up on my knowledge of the Hells and the Abyss yesterday. I'd get Cyvis on it once I was done here.

Virexa frowned minutely, studying me like a puzzle. "Lord…Abaddon…?" she said it as if it didn't fit. I could tell she believed me, but something wasn't computing in her mind.

"Forgive me, lord, I am unfamiliar with your house." she said leadingly.

"Unsurprising. I am independent, but I am willing to work with your master and his allies. Please give your master my greetings. I sincerely hope the angel and the phylactery are of some use to him."

Virexa dipped into a shallow, respectful bow. "You honor my lord, and in so doing honor me, Lord Abaddon. I will extend your greetings to the Master of Dis. Farewell, lord." She turned and strode through the portal. It snapped shut behind her.

Two figures shimmered into being at my side as their invisibility spell faded. I felt them arrive when Virexa and I were speaking to the angel. They'd stayed hidden, watching in case I needed backup.

"I think she could see us. She looked right at me and smiled." Shang Tsung said, a displeased frown on his face.

"She did the same to me." Aqua said, eyebrows furrowed.

"For now, she isn't an enemy. If that changes, we'll keep that in mind." It wasn't uncommon for high-ranking devils to be able to see through illusions in D&D. "How are the others?" I asked.

"Everyone's fine." Aqua assured me. "Everything in the cave was dealt with. I brought the others back to Cyvis's home before we came back here. There wasn't anything interesting in the cave aside from a bunch of magical traps meant to summon demons and raise the dead. I think the lich just lured people there to make it easier to kill them with his demons and the dragon."

Shang Tsung smirked. "He wasn't expecting Mothra and Matatabi."

I pulled out the ring Aqua had given me. "You said this was better than the Amulet of Planes we came for?"

Aqua nodded. "He used that to flee here. He tried it again when we were fighting him, but I was able to block it once I knew what he was doing. The amulet you described had an element of uncertainty to it. That ring does not."

"I'll have Irene look it over for curses and other nasty surprises when we get back. She'll be able to tell me what all it can do." If there weren't any issues with it, then this ring would work as my intended gift. If Irene, a master enchantress, and Aqua, a Keyblade master, could improve it then it would be even better. I looked around the chamber once more, ensuring I'd already packed up everything of value. Satisfied, I opened a Hole. "Let's get out of here."

Today would likely have some unsavory consequences as far as my presence in D&D was concerned. If things got too scary, I'd withdraw from the world, likely grabbing my warlocks and bringing them with me. I hoped it wouldn't come to that, but I'd be watching just in case.

#7,737
Medea was in her lab, back to the door and a glowing gem in her hand. She hummed a gentle tune as she used the gem to carve runes into a metallic disk on the table before her.

"Hi." I said, walking up behind her and slowly wrapping my arms around her.

"Hi, honey." she said, still focused on the disk on the table.

"I'm sorry if I'm interrupting."

"I'll be done in a moment. Please give me a bit of space until then."

I nodded, stepping back and quietly watching her work.

Medea tapped the gem against the disk. It let out a shrill ring as it glowed a bright, verdant green.

Setting the gem aside, Medea turned around. "What did you need?"

"Are you busy right now?" I asked.

"Not particularly. Why?"

"Would you like to go on a little trip with me?" I asked.

Medea's eyes narrowed in suspicion. "Irene told me she would handle Shiroe's training today. She refused to let me help her. What did you put her up to?"

I smiled knowingly. "I only asked her to make sure you had some free time today. So!" A Hole opened to my right. I held out my arm for Medea to take. "Do you feel up for a little jaunt?"

Medea's lips curled up into an amused smile. With slow, deliberate steps, she walked to my side and took my arm, leaning into me slightly as we walked. Side by side, we stepped into the Hole.

The moment we emerged from the Hole, I covered us in illusions. Medea layered more advanced illusions over mine a moment later before looking around curiously.

We stood atop a hill overlooking a vast plain of tan dirt. To our right, ranks of armored men with spears and shields yelled out war cries as they began a charge. The men wore armor of various designs. They were grouped together among others wearing similar apparel, but they all answered to a man riding one of the few chariots sprinkled through their formation.

Standing with shields and spears raised ready to meet the charging force was another group. Men all wearing the same bronze armor stood disciplined as they awaited the charge. Ranks of the men stood in defense of a tall wooden gate. The walls around the gate were made from tan stone bricks the same color as the dirt that rose high into the air. On the ramparts of the walls their allies stood with bows and arrows, strings already drawn. The defenders loosed their arrows as one, raining death on the charging attackers.

The two forces met. The ranks of defenders buckled under the sprinting charge of the attackers before the men in the second rank supported the first, keeping them upright and able to continue fighting. A cacophony of warfare assaulted the air. Spear hafts slamming down atop shields. Screams of impaled men. The ring of swords meeting. The thunk of axes buried into shields.

"Where are we?" Medea asked, looking over the field quizzically. "I imagine you wouldn't bring me to a random battlefield."

"This is the first battle of the Trojan War." I explained. "Actually, I guess it would be more accurate to say that this is the first battle of a Trojan War given how many worlds throughout the multiverse seem to have this same conflict play out roughly the same way."

Medea's eyes widened. "Another Achilles is down there?"

I nodded. "A different version, not as skilled nor as powerful as our Knight."

"Ajax? Odysseus? Hector?"

"All present."

Medea pursed her lips. "So many of Greece's greatest legends partook in this one conflict."

"It's a little humbling to observe it. This conflict shaped the course of history." I looked at Medea as she began to quietly laugh. "What is it?"

Medea smiled up at me, amused. "Honey, you are shaping the course of history. Whether you are aware of it or not, your actions in our world will have far-reaching consequences that echo throughout the entire world. Why watch history when you can shape it?"

I pursed my lips as I thought over her words. Between my business, my ability to walk between worlds, my peerage, the whole mess with Helios and Boreas, and now the warlock thing, I guess I was shaping history. Suddenly, the conflict below didn't seem so awe-inspiring.

With the battle having lost its luster, I shrugged, turning to Medea. "Well, the battle wasn't what I brought you here to see. It was just a primer."

Medea raised an eyebrow. "If not to witness history, why have you brought me on this little 'jaunt'."

I smiled knowingly. "It's a surprise. Come with me." I gently tugged on her hands, pulling her towards another Hole in space. We walked through it, leaving the carnage at the gates of Troy behind us.

The expanse of tan dirt was gone. We stood on another hill overlooking lush verdant fields. Grass, brush and sparse trees all shone vibrantly in the afternoon sun. In the distance, a massive city stood, bisected by a wide river. The walls were grey and black stone. Within the city, a palace atop a hill was visible, surveying all around it.

Medea's breath caught. It was rare that Medea was ever surprised or shocked into inaction. This was one of the rare occasions where she completely locked up.

"Medea?" I asked, concerned. I took her hand, rubbing gentle circles on the back of it.

Medea squeezed my hand tight, her eyes fixed on the palace in the distance. "Aea." she said, voice barely a whisper. "We're in Colchis."

I nodded slowly, watching her reaction carefully. "It isn't the Colchis of our world. As you saw, the Trojan War is still going on here. This is as near as I could find to the Colchis you knew."

"I… What is your plan? Why bring me here?" Medea asked.

"That's up to you, Medea. What do you want to do? Would you like to leave?" I hadn't expected being here to stun her so much. Maybe this was a mistake.

"No!" Medea said quickly. She closed her eyes and took a deep breath. Her shoulders visibly sagged as she relaxed. "No, let's go into the city. I want to… I want to look around."

"Okay," I said slowly. "You lead. I've never been here before." That, and I wanted her to move at her own pace, only going where she wanted to.

Medea cast another illusion over us. Her wings shot out of her back and she took to the sky, racing towards the city.

I hurried to catch up.

We flew in silence. Medea drank in the city and the small buildings around it, eyes wide and a brilliant smile on her face.

"I haven't seen the city since I was exiled. It's…strange to be back." Medea said slowly, as if even she wasn't sure how she felt about returning.

"We'll take it slow. If you want to leave at any time, let me know and I'll take us away."

"We can't leave now." Medea said, fixing me with a look of false sincerity. "We've only just arrived!" Medea's wings banked as she turned into a dive, heading down towards what looked to be a market district. I followed.

We landed in an alley out of line of sight and undid our illusions after our wings were gone. Medea cast a different illusion over us, altering our clothes and changing the features of her face so she wouldn't be recognizable. Hand in hand, we walked into the thoroughfare.

For the next hour, Medea dragged me along behind her. We visited stalls selling trinkets of carved wood and sculpted metals. We sampled fresh fruit brought in from neighboring farms. We had a drink in a tavern. We watched small ships launch onto the river, heading out towards the Black Sea.

Medea laughed as she pulled me along to watch a wrestling match. Two large, muscular men nude as the day they were born grunted and roared, doing their best to throw each other out of a drawn ring in a sandpit. It was an…interesting experience. The culture shock hit hard with that one.

We found a square with musicians playing music and citizens dancing. Medea dragged me with her into the center of the square, forcing me to dance. I only made a slight fool of myself. She did a good job of keeping me from tripping over my own feet.

As the sun started to descend, casting an orange glow across the sky, Medea seemed to have her fill of Aea. I asked her if she wanted to visit the palace before we left.

She frowned. "That isn't my home anymore. There is nothing in that structure of any significance to me."

Sensing the minefield I was treading through, I let the subject drop, following her to another alley. We cast more illusions over ourselves and took to the sky. We left the city. I let Medea take the lead, following wherever she wanted to go.

Upriver there were a series of rolling hills. Medea landed atop the tallest one. There was a single alder tree growing from the crest of the hill. Medea sat down with her back resting against the tree and looked at Aea in the distance. I joined her.

"I used to come here often." Medea said, her eyes far away. "I never could sit still. When my lessons failed to entertain me, I would run through the hills to find something that caught my attention." She looked up at the tree. "This isn't the same as the spot in my world. The tree was much older. Taller." She closed her eyes and leaned back. "But it will do well enough."

I gently took her hand.

Medea smiled, shuffling across the ground to lean into me, resting her head on my shoulder. We stayed like that for a long time.

"This was a good day." Medea finally said, opening her eyes and looking out at the sun setting over Aea. The sky was going dark.

"I'm glad you enjoyed it." I said, running a hand through her hair.

Medea looked up at me with a knowing smile. "Not that I don't appreciate the lovely trip you arranged to spend time with me, but I seem to have a nagging suspicion that you brought me here for a reason."

I smiled. I didn't expect I'd be able to hide my intentions from her. One of the main reasons I made her my Queen was her intellect. "I doubted I'd be able to surprise you, but I wanted to make it special."

Medea feigned confusion. "Special? Whatever could you mean, master?"

Chuckling softly, I gently extricated myself from our embrace and stood. "I know I said this would likely happen after the Rating Game, but, through no small assistance from our peerage, I was able to arrange everything earlier than I anticipated."

I knelt on the ground. Medea watched me like a hawk as a Hole dropped a small, velveted black box into my hand. I pulled the box open, revealing a silver band. A gem was affixed to the band. It seemed to contain an entire cosmos. Gleaming stars and colorful nebulas gently flowed through the gem.

"Medea," I began. "My Queen, the love of my life, would you do me the honor of– Oof!" I was knocked backwards as Medea leapt forward to tackle me in a hug.

"Nothing would make me happier." Medea said, leaning down atop me to claim my lips in a hungry kiss.

I reached up to the back of her head to hold her against me.

Medea grabbed my hand pulling it off her as she pulled away from me. She didn't let go of my hand. My left hand.

In a flash of violet energy, a ring appeared in Medea's hand. A golden band with a small, sculpted amethyst set into it. The inside of the band was covered in glowing red runes so small as to almost be unreadable.

Medea brought the ring close to my finger, then hesitated, features growing conflicted.

Frowning, I asked, "What's wrong?"

Medea nervously fidgeted with the ring. "I finished this ring some time ago. It took me a long time to make. I put many bindings into it in addition to its beneficial effects."

"What kinds of bindings?" I asked, reserving judgement for after her explanation.

"We'll be connected. Forever." Medea admitted quickly. "I will be able to share your mana. You will be able to share mine. Much like a Master-Servant bond, we will share our thoughts and dreams. No matter where you go, we will be able to feel each other. If you are ever in danger in another world, I will know. It will shield your mind from all but me. If anyone tries to control you or turn you against me, the ring will prevent it. It–" She abruptly caught off.

"What is it, Medea?"

She looked away, not meeting my eyes. "You will never be able to take it off. Once on your finger, it will stay there. We will be bound for eternity. Should you ever die, your soul will not be claimed by any power. You will stay with the ring. It will ensure you always find your way back to me. If you put this on, you will be mine forever."

A long time ago, Medea loved a man named Jason. She sacrificed everything she had for that man, her home, her family. That man left her with nothing, scarred and alone. I knew that Medea still bore the scars of her past – the scars Jason inflicted. I knew that despite how much time had passed, she still held that fear deep down inside, despite her best efforts to smother it, that I would do the same thing he did, that she would be alone again after losing everything a second time.

I reached up with my right hand, gently gripping Medea's chin and turning her face so I could look her in the eyes. "An eternity spent with the greatest love I will ever know?" I released her chin, covering her hand with mine and guiding it to my left ring finger. "I can't think of anything I'd want more." I helped her put the ring on my finger.

I felt a pulse, emanating from the ring and reverberating throughout my entire body, a wave of energy that lit my nerves on fire. The wave left my body, echoing through Medea. She gasped, eyes flying wide.

I felt an unbreakable bond form, a connection between the two of us. I could feel her magic. I could feel her.

'Medea?' I thought in my mind, reaching for the connection.

Medea fell on top of me. Her lips crashed into my own, tongue plunging into my mouth.

'Mine!' I heard Medea's voice shout in my head as she crushed herself against me.

My hand found the back of her head. My other arm snaked around behind her back, pressing her down into me.

'My fiance! My husband! MINE!' Medea's voice echoed in my head. She pulled away from me, looking down at me with a look of pure joy and desire. Her hair fell around us, like a veil shielding us from the problems of the world.

Medea laid a hand on my chest. My shirt began to disintegrate, spreading out in a wave from her hand.

"I'll make you another. I need you now." Medea said quickly, leaning back down to claim my lips. Her hands wandered all over me. Her fingers brushed against my leg. I felt my pants begin to disintegrate along with my shirt.

Two could play that game.

I ran my hands over Medea's back. Fire danced across my fingers, burning her dress away with carefully controlled licks of flame. I dragged a hand around her side to her front, sliding my palm down her stomach and lower, trailing demonic fire that burned away her dress. I extinguished my hand and curled two fingers down when they reached her mound, plunging inside her.

Medea broke from our kiss with a gasp. I reached up to grab her neck, pulling her back down to my lips as I spread my fingers inside her. She clenched down on my fingers. They were already coated in her juices.

'I need you right now, Balthazar.' Medea said in my head, our lips still locked together in a desperate kiss. She reached down, hurrying along the destruction of my pants to grab me.

I pulled away from our kiss, sucking in air as she guided me to her entrance with a firm hand. Medea leaned down, reclaiming my lips, refusing to let me escape.

'You're mine now, my love.' Medea said in my mind. 'I'm never letting you go.'

Medea fell onto me, taking my full length in one motion. Our lips came apart in a mutual gasp only to immediately rejoin as we pulled each other close.

I pulled Medea down on top of me, rolling to the side so she was laying in the grass and I was on top. I kept our lips pressed together and pressed myself deep into her to maintain our connection.

'You can't say things like that and not expect me to respond.' I said in her mind as I began to thrust myself into her hard. Her words mixed with the sensation of her presence in my head was driving me crazy. I needed her just as much as she needed me.

Medea moaned, trying to escape our kiss. I didn't let her, claiming her lips again as I drove into her.

'I love you!' Medea screamed into my mind. 'I love you, Balthazar!'

'I love you, Medea.' I said back. 'I'm yours.'

Everything was too much for me. The feel of Medea under me. The touch of her presence in my mind. The ring on my finger hummed as if joyous. I couldn't last.

Medea felt my struggle in my mind. Her legs wrapped around me, holding me against her.

'Inside, my love.' She said in my mind, mouth occupied by kissing me like she was trying to steal my air. 'I need it.'

With one final thrust, I came undone, grunting and falling atop her. Medea's legs tightened around me like a constricting snake, ensuring I stayed right where she wanted me.

We held each other, both of us were spent, desperately trying to catch our breath.

Both happy.

Night had fallen on Colchis. Medea and I lay side by side in the grass atop a hill, nude as we looked at the sky together.

Medea was pressed up against my side, idly running a hand over my bare chest with a happy smile on her face.

"Faerun has many items that facilitate travel between the planes connected to it. I thought that if I could find one, Aqua and Irene could help me improve it or make something better using it as a base. That happens to be the strongest item of that effect I have ever heard of. Aqua unlocked its potential and Irene layered some more enchantments on it to bind it so it can't be taken from you. It now has the ability to transport the wearer between worlds instead of just between the different planes connected to that one specific world. I wanted you to have the same freedom I do. I want you to be able to come with me wherever I may go. I want you to be able to go wherever you want to go. Afterall, it's a husband's duty to see his wife happy."

Medea watched, transfixed as I took the ring out of the box and lifted her left hand, sliding the ring onto her finger. It was too large, but the moment it was on her finger the band shrunk down to fit her perfectly. Another bit of magic Irene worked on the ring.

Medea closed her eyes, concentrating for a moment. With a pop of magical energy, Medea disappeared. She was gone completely from the world. I still felt her presence through our new connection. She was far, far away. Another pop. Medea returned, immediately tackling me to the ground. Her lips were on mine.

'It's perfect; better than I could have ever expected.' Medea said in my mind, voice full of gratitude and love.

I held her against me enjoying her warmth. 'Only the best for the future Lady Abaddon.'

Medea locked up, freezing on top of me. She pulled back, looking deep into my eyes. "Say that out loud."

I smiled up at her, gently cupping her cheek with my hand. "Only the best for you, Lady Abaddon."

An expression of joy mixed with hunger overtook Medea. She fell upon me again, greedily claiming my lips. Her hands roamed over my chest.

'You don't get to sleep tonight.' she said in my mind, already reaching down to guide me inside her.

For some reason, I couldn't bring myself to care about a little lack of sleep. I wound my arms around my fiance and loved her through the night.
