Growing up, Vellia did not have many prospects available to her. After her parents abandoned her, her grandmother tried her best to give Vellia the skills she would need to lead a good life, but her grandmother never learned skills one could use to live an ordinary life.

From a young age, Vellia was taught to fight and forage, to hunt and make a comfortable shelter for the night. Her grandmother was a wanderer. It was all she knew, so she taught it all to Vellia.

Selling her sword kept her fed, but it did not allow her to make plans for the future. She had no future. All there was was the next meal and the next job. Vellia expected that was how it would always be until she would one day face a foe that she couldn't beat. Then her brief, if exciting and well-travelled, life would end.

Vellia never planned for Balthazar Abbadon.

Overnight, Vellia finally attained something she'd lacked, something she'd spent her whole life searching for; purpose.

Vellia often fantasized of being called to one of the Sword Coast's city-states to serve as a noble lady's body guard or a knight in a lord's charge. She would have steady meals, her fill of adventure, and a place to return to when her travels ended; a home.

Now, Vellia had all that and more. She had a lord. She had immense power the likes of which even her grandmother would be awed by. She had a purpose. She had a friend that shared that purpose.

"He is far greater than I could have imagined." Cyvis said, staring blankly at the ceiling. It had been several minutes since their lord and his peerage left them in Cyvis's home. The elven woman collapsed onto the nearest sofa and stared up at the ceiling, a faraway look on her face.

"What do you mean?" Vellia asked. She had been content to leave Cyvis to think until she spoke. After spending so much time with her, Vellia learned that Cyvis had moments where she desired silence or to be alone. Not because she didn't enjoy Vellia's company, but simply because she needed a moment to herself.

"I expected a barbed devil. Maybe a bone devil at best. I knew you couldn't speak about him, but I didn't expect your master to be a Viscount of Hell who travelled at the side of one of Hell's rulers."

Vellia smirked. "Our master."

A small, happy smile pulled at Cyvis's lips as she met Vellia's gaze. "Yes, our master." She sat up straighter. "A month ago, I never would have imagined any of this was possible. I never expected to find a devil patron that wouldn't immediately demand my soul. I never expected to brave the underdark and best an ancient lich, a dracolich, and their army of demons with a company of devils whose powers defy the wisdom of every text ever penned about their kind."

"Not like the stories, are they?" Vellia asked.

Cyvis shook her head. "No, they are not. But it's not just the stories, Vellia. When I learned I had a talent for summoning demons, I sought out every academic text I could about demons and devils both. Lord Abaddon…he is different. There is no mention of Serafall Leviathan in any text I have read. If one of Hell's rulers were named Serafall Leviathan it would certainly be notated, yet there is nothing. I have researched the Hells extensively. I know the name of the lord of each layer. I have sought out knowledge of the infinite layers of the Abyss and know many of its lords as well. Serafall Leviathan and Viscount Balthazar Abaddon do not exist."

Vellia frowned. "What are you saying?"

Cyvis shook her head, a happy laugh bubbling up from her chest. "I'm saying that our master is a hidden gem unknown to the wider world. We've witnessed the proof of his power with our own eyes. His servants put the legends of great dragons to shame. His estate was vast. I only saw it for a moment, but I was filled with awe. He gave me an enchanted mithril shirt and the spellbook of an ancient lich as if they were paltry things! His power is flowing through our veins, making us so strong." Cyvis held up a hand. A pearl-white line in reality appeared above her hand. She stared at it, transfixed. "In all my readings, I have never found mention of a power like that which he has given us."

Vellia relaxed, a happy smile on her face. She already knew that her lord was great. Cyvis's praise only confirmed her own feelings.

"He'll make us strong." Vellia said, thoughts drifting back to the dark sky and vast expanse that was Lord Abaddon's seat of power. Vellia had always wanted to serve a great lord. Balthazar Abaddon was the greatest lord one could serve. She would need to work hard, prove herself. Only then would her master entertain the idea of letting her serve him in his home.

Maybe one day, Vellia could call that place home?

"Come," Cyvis said suddenly, standing. "We have much work to do. There is business to see to. I believe we should reach out to some other powers in the city and negotiate to expand our reach beyond merely iron mines. Kharad-Veth was once a great mining settlement before it fell to unknown demonic interference. I think it is safe to say that Maltherion and his dealings with the Hells were that interference."

"What are you getting at?" Vellia asked.

Cyvis grinned, eager. "Once we have sufficient workers, we can reopen the mines in Kharad-Veth. That will expand our options considerably. We'll need more guards, more miners, more supplies…but we can do it."

Vellia raised an eyebrow. "Setting up in the Underdark seems risky, doesn't it?"

"Kharad-Veth is close enough to the surface to avoid most of the issues that come from the Underdark. So long as we hire capable guards, there should be no issues. Failing that, I can summon and bind demons to act as security."

"Didn't the city fall because of extraplanar interference? Should we really be summoning demons down there?"

"Maltherion likely didn't care what happened to the city so long as he got what he wanted. I'll be more careful. I'm not suggesting we do this overnight. We have time to take the proper precautions. I'm sure Lord Abaddon would be willing to supply us with more aid if we outlined the rewards we could reap from the city's ruins. But that can come later. We'll need a larger workforce. It would be better for us to expand on the surface first, then move down to Kharad-Veth. It is unlikely anyone else will discover the ruins for some time, so we can prepare."

Cyvis took a deep breath. "I would like to draft up some proposals before returning to my studies. This gift…" Cyvis hugged a faintly glowing, leather-bound tome to her chest. The spellbook of a powerful lich that had lived for centuries, and Lord Abaddon had just given it to her. The ink on the pages within the book was more valuable than diamonds. It would be some time before Cyvis would be capable of using the full breadth of what she'd been given, but she would work hard to take full advantage of her lord's boon. "There is so much to do."

Vellia stood, grinning in anticipation. "Then let's get to it."

Circe sat at her loom, humming a gentle tune to herself as she worked. She was making a sea green gown. She took her time with the process, imbuing each fiber with her magic. It was a practiced exercise, one she'd done many times before. Relaxing. Enjoyable.

Circe frowned, ceasing her work. She looked out the window of her small home. Someone had entered the wards at the edge of her island.

Sighing, Circe stood. She put aside her work and walked to the door. She closed and locked it behind her as she walked down to the beach. There was someone there waiting for her.

Floating a few feet off the ground was a beautiful man. He wore a simple white cloth around his waist, barely preserving his modesty. Hair like golden ambrosia danced in the breeze. His shoes had wings, fluttering at a stable rhythm to keep him aloft. He held a caduceus staff in his hand.

"Hermes," Circe greeted, polite but not welcoming. "Why have you come?"

The messenger god's typical playful smile was nowhere to be seen. Hermes's expression was serious. "You went to Hell."

Circe nodded easily. "I did. I was visiting my niece and my former sister-in-law."

"Your former…?" Hermes's shocked expression gave way to cold indifference. "Father has banned all travel to Hell."

"Lord Zeus does not control where I travel."

Hermes seethed. "Do you not know what they did to us, Circe? Thrinacia is gone. They took Lampetia and Phaethusa."

"I left before the attack. I only learned of it upon my return. I would have gone regardless."

Hermes snarled. "Circe, they are the enemy!"

"Zekram Bael is the enemy. He was the one to ruin Thrinacia. My niece and her lover had no hand in it. Their only crime is defending themselves from my father's foolishness."

"Not all of us are as impulsive as your father, Circe."

"Yet all devils should be judged as one? That is hypocritical, is it not?"

Circe had rarely seen Hermes angry. He was too free-spirited to let much of anything bother him too much. She saw his ire now. His narrowed eyes, the curling of his hand into a fist.

"Father wants to talk to you." Hermes said, tone dangerous. "He needs to know what you did in Hell."

"I have already told you. I visited my niece and her lover. You may inform Lord Zeus of my activities yourself." Circe turned, beginning the walk back to her small home.

The sound of feverishly flapping wings assaulted Circe's ears. Hermes was a blur. He flew around in front of her, blocking her path.

"Father will speak with you, Circe. It wasn't a request." Hermes said, low and threatening.

Circe paused, eyes narrowing. Over the years, her relationship with Hermes had been easy. He often visited her island. She enjoyed their conversations, but she never fooled herself into believing the flighty god considered her a true confidant or friend. It was not his way. He never allowed himself to become too invested in anything or anyone lest it tie him down. Circe had no doubt he would drag her before Zeus without a moment's hesitation if he felt it necessary.

"I have no desire to meet with your father." Circe said.

"You will meet him regardless." Hermes slowly drifted closer.

Circe scowled. "Many of you on Olympus look down on those of us you believe lesser. We do not reside on your mountain, so surely our value must be less. We must be weaker. That arrogance has always irritated me."

The wind picked up, dancing between the trees, growing into an angry howl. The messenger god shifted to accommodate the wind blowing into his floating body.

"Just come with me, Circe. I do not want to hurt you." Hermes said, his expression morphing into that of a concerned friend. Circe saw right through the practiced mask.

"You won't." she said with certainty.

A great roar shook the sky. Hermes froze in place. That sound was not the wind.

A great rhythmic thumping like the beat of a drum drew nearer. Circe did not look away from Hermes as a giant metallic dragon swooped to the ground behind her. Its giant head appeared over her right shoulder. Elemental fire swam between its teeth as it bared its fangs in a deadly growl. Silver scales flaked with gold caught the light as the dragon's tail curled protectively around her.

"You come to my island. You make demands. When I do not submit to your demands, you make threats. You expect me to bow and grovel simply because you come from the sky. You forget, Hermes, you are not on Olympus. This is my home. You will not inflict your will upon me without consequence." Circe said coldly, her gaze boring into Hermes.

Hermes watched the dragon carefully. Its golden eyes did not blink, meeting the god's gaze unflinching. Hermes could sense the powerful magic animating the great dragon. He could likely overcome it. He would not do so unscathed. It was rare that an Olympian needed to consider consequences such as pain or retribution. Hermes was frozen in indecision.

Finally, Hermes came back to himself, scowling unhappily. "I will tell my father of this. Do not expect the next messenger to be so accommodating." With that, he was gone, flying off into the sky to disappear amongst the clouds.

Circe shook her head, frowning unpleasantly. "All bluster. It's all he's ever been good for."

The dragon purred softly, leaning down to nudge her shoulder with its large nose.

Circe's melancholy was banished. She looked up at her creation with a bright smile. "Thank you, my friend. I'm sorry for moping." She scratched under the metal dragon's chin as she ran a hand over its foreleg.

This dragon, Anankos as she'd named it, was one of her greatest creations. Circe had brewed many potions over the years, some great and powerful, others barely able to bloom a flower.

A concoction she completed centuries ago had stayed on her shelf for years, waiting for the proper time to see use. That time came when Circe returned home from Hell with dragon scales and mythical metals she would likely never have access to again.

Circe worked her magic, breathing life into the metal. Anankos was born. Curious, Intelligent. Compassionate. Strong. He was a good friend. Circe had been excited to introduce him to Artemis. That meeting would have to wait now.

Circe was no fool. By banishing Hermes from her island, she had slighted Zeus. Zeus did not respond to slights well at the best of times. Now? After his unshakeable image had been threatened by the barbaric actions of Zekram Bael? He would make an example out of her.

Circe had lived on this island for many long years. She knew its every secret and loved all of its flaws. When Zeus came for her, he would destroy everything around her. So long as she was here, he would be able to find the island.

Circe gently petted Anankos's head, sighing sadly. She would need to leave. Her illusions would protect the island, hiding it from mortals and gods alike so long as she was not present. If she was elsewhere, her home would be safe.

Now, she needed to find somewhere to shelter from Zeus's retribution.

She had an idea or two.


X


Remiel calmly walked through the underbrush, making his way through the trees. Blessed as he was with his visions, it was rare he was surprised. Still, finding Boreas in this place was a surprise.

It had taken longer than normal for Remial to turn his sight on the storm god. Boreas had covered his tracks well.

"This is the location, your grace." Father Martin said, bowing in deference as they emerged from the treeline. Ahead, a small, two story building with boarded up windows stood alone amongst the trees – an abandoned homestead that once belonged to the Pendragon family. How Boreas came to be accepted through the wards was a mystery that still eluded Remiel's understanding.

"Thank you, my son. For accompanying me, and for shouldering this burden." Remiel said, laying a comforting hand on the mortal's shoulder.

Father Martin bowed even lower. "It is an honor to be called to serve our Lord, your grace. I will do whatever is required of me."

Remiel's sight warned him of impending danger. Moving quickly, he pulled Father Martin close, covering the human with his body as he rapidly repositioned.

Ice and lightning rained down where he once stood. Elemental manifestations of frost and storm energy rose from the ground at the perimeter of the building.

"I have not come to fight." Remiel declared, his grace carrying his voice with authority through the clearing. His surroundings were bathed in holy radiance as Remiel revealed his true self, robed in the purest white with ten angelic wings spread wide behind him.

Father Martin fell to his knees behind him, clutching a crucifix and whispering a feverish prayer.

The elementals paused, surprised by the appearance of such a powerful Seraph.

"We share a common enemy." Remiel said. "I would speak with the god of the northern wind."

Frost gathered atop the grass, condensing as it rose in a clump. Sparks of lightning zipped through the fog as a face appeared, then a body. Boreas stood before Remiel, watching him with suspicion. "What business does Heaven's Guiding Light have with me?"

"I have had a vision." Remiel explained. "You will fight Balthazar Abaddon."

Boreas grinned, eager, anticipating. "Good. That bastard took my daughter from me. I will–"

"You will die." Remiel interrupted him. His vision had been clear. Boreas would face Balthazar. Boreas would be overwhelmed, having underestimated just how absolute the young devil's mastery of his clan trait was. Balthazar would appear behind the god, a glowing golden-pointed spear in his hands. The spear would pierce the storm god from behind. Boreas's flesh would rapidly wither and decay until he was no more. This was the vision Remiel had seen, the vision he had come to prevent.

As Remiel expected, Balthazar was too dangerous to the stability of the world to allow him to live. His potential to kill a god was dangerous enough on its own, but he also incited other devils into a frenzy. Zekram Bael had destroyed Thrinacia in defense of the young upstart, driving the precarious balance of the supernatural to the brink of war. Remiel needed to act. Balthazar must be dealt with now, but he must be dealt with in a way that would prevent further suffering. Boreas was the perfect choice to eliminate the devil.

The Greek pantheon had cut Boreas loose. He no longer enjoyed their protection or their support. If Boreas killed Balthazar, the devils would respond against Boreas alone. The rest of the Greek pantheon and, more importantly, the rest of the world would be protected from devilkind's wrath. This was Remiel's best chance.

Boreas was silent for several seconds. A flurry of emotions passed over the god's face. Resolve hardened in the wake of the storm.

"If your purpose here is to tell me to flee, I will not. I will kill the devil, regardless of what you have seen." Boreas declared.

Remiel smiled. "I am glad you are so resolved. I have not come to caution you into hiding. I have come to offer assistance. Father Martin?" Remiel turned to the mortal at his side.

"Just say the word, your grace." Father Martin said, resolve firm.

"Who is this?" Boreas asked, looking down on the mortal.

"This is Father Martin, a gifted exorcist in service to the church. He carries one of my father's gifts to mankind." Remiel explained.

At Remiel's nod, Father Martin held out his hand. An ornate silver staff appeared in his hand. A crucifix at the staff's head glowed with holy power.

"Balthazar Abaddon is able to defeat you by using his devil power Hole. Father Martin's Sacred Gear, Trick Vanish, has the power to seal the power of a supernatural creature. Preventing Balthazar Abaddon from using Hole is within Father Martin's capabilities." Remiel explained. Remiel did not recognize the spear Balthazar used in his vision. It was likely a creation of Medea, and therefore difficult or impossible for him to influence. Balthazar's ability to use his clan trait was something Remiel could influence.

Boreas considered Father Martin in a new light. "What do you ask in exchange for this power?"

"Kill Balthazar Abaddon." Remiel said, expression serious. "He is a grave threat to the stability of our world. I have seen it. Treat Father Martin with dignity and respect, and accomplish our shared purpose. At the end of it, you will make no mention of Heaven's aid to you."

Boreas slowly broke out into a grin. "I can agree to that. The mortal will be in good hands here."

Remiel turned to Father Martin. "You carry a heavy burden, my son. Carry my blessing with you to lighten your load." Remiel bent down, lightly kissing Father Martin on the forehead, imparting a fraction of his grace into the man.

Father Martin made the sign of the cross and spoke another prayer. "Thank you for setting this task before me, your grace. I will triumph in the name of our lord."

"Go in peace, my son." Remiel said, a warm smile on his face.

As Boreas and his elementals welcomed Father Martin into the home, Remiel frowned. The sight behind his eyes showed him the same picture, Balthazar Abaddon driving a golden spear through Boreas's back.

Remiel shook his head. His visions often did not account for his own actions. It was one of the curses he carried in exchange for his sight. He had faith in Father Martin. He had faith in Boreas's, a god's ability to kill a near-infant devil. He would put his faith in his father's memory. All would end as it was meant to.


X


The sun boiled with fury. The air around Helios's form hissed as he passed. It had been eons since he last felt such pure, concentrated hatred.

Thrinacia, his shining jewel, his light in the mortal world, was gone. Its remains did not even lay in the ocean. The very memory of his paradise had been erased from reality.

His prized cattle were stolen, displayed in a devil's menagerie like trophies.

His beautiful daughters…enslaved.

The world warmed as the sun's rage grew into an inferno.

Boreas, the gnat, pleaded with Helios to deal with their shared enemy first. Helios left the weak god to his vendetta. Balthazar Abaddon had slighted Helios when he reincarnated Medea. That slight was not forgiven. However, after a difficult conversation with his daughter Circe, a conversation that involved lots of yelling on his offspring's part, Helios's ire towards the devil had dimmed.

Circe had always been fiercely protective of her niece. She would not advocate for the Abaddon lord unless Medea had truly joined him of her own free will. The revelation that Idyia not only lived but had chosen to take up residence in Hell with her daughter and Abaddon gave Helios pause. Balthazar was not the vile cretin the sun had assumed, merely a vile hellspawn like the rest of his cursed race. Balthazar Abaddon and the debt he owed the sun would keep.

Helios had a new enemy, one he must now focus the entire breadth of his power towards eliminating. Zekram Bael believed himself to be untouchable. The ancient devil thought the entire world was too afraid of him to openly defy him. He believed that he could destroy Helios's holdings and steal his daughters against their will without consequence.

Zekram Bael was currently hiding in the Underworld. Even the sun could not brave Hell alone. He would have to draw the filth out.

Balthazar Abaddon was not the only devil with holdings in the mortal world. Zekram Bael's vast holdings made Balthazar's look trivial. This is where the Sun would start. He would burn away Zekram's powerbase until nothing remained, just as the devil did to his beautiful Thrinacia.

Zekram Bael's Power of Destruction would break before the might of the Sun.


X


Virexa knelt before an iron throne. Centuries ago, the lord of the second sent her to meet with a mortal wizard, later offering her service to him as the price of a near-impossible feat completed. Since falling under Maltherion's thrall, her status had drastically diminished. When not summoned to accomplish some benign task for the lich, she still resided in Dis, but she had not set foot in Dispatar's iron tower in centuries. Today, she returned as a conqueror.

Before Virexa's kneeling form, elevated by three unholy steps, sat a devil atop the iron throne. His face was humanoid, with sharp, handsome features and cunning eyes. Horns curled up from his forehead. An opulent ruby robe hung from his shoulders. A cloven goathoof rested against the floor in place of his left foot.

"You did well, Virexa." Dispatar, Lord of the Second Layer of Hell, commented idly. In his hand, he held a glowing diamond. The archdevil inspected Maltherion's phylactery with an amused curl to his lips. "The lich will serve us well. The knowledge and secrets he learned in his travels through the Abyss are now ours. More importantly, You returned with Elariel, under contract no less!" Dispatar leaned forward on his throne, handing Maltherion's phylactery off to a succubus at his side, already having forgotten the presence of the millenia old lich's soul. "She is a prize we have not seen in a thousand years. Legally bound of her own will, there is no challenge that will allow her fellows to retrieve her. She is ours now. She will make an exceptional general as soon as she accepts her new home."

"I merely took advantage of an opportunity to further Hell's interests, my lord." Virexa said, features carved from stone. Internally, she could not stop the satisfying swell of pride singing in her chest. Hundreds of years spent serving that doddering fool of a mortal had grated on her patience, but she was eternal. What she had gained far exceeded the minimal time she had lost.

The lich spent many years cataloguing the goings on of the Abyss. The secrets they would tear from his soul would give the Hells a great advantage in the Blood War. Similarly, the submission of an angel as great as Elariel was a prize that had no equal. Her contract stipulated she could go free. The angel was foolish, holding on to false hope. After even a decade basking in the Hells, she would come to know it as her new home.

Dispatar sat back in his chair, watching her closely. "The lich's phylactery is a great prize. Elariel is a prize the Hells have not seen in an age. Yet…I find my attention drawn to something else." With a flick of his wrist, a rolled document appeared in his hand.

Virexa recognized it. It was the report she submitted about her experience upon her return to Dis.

Dispatar unrolled the report. His eyes idly panned over the words written on the page. "The devil that Maltherion ordered you to kill, breaking your contract, what was his name?"

"He introduced himself as Viscount Abaddon, my lord. I did not recognize him, but I felt his standing as a lord of Hell." Virexa responded. She had not been among the nobility of Hell for some time now. It was possible, even if it was unlikely, that new blood had risen through the ranks.

When Virexa first came face to face with Viscount Abaddon, she was shocked. A devil lord of his standing so casually able to infiltrate a demiplane, unbound to the Hells where all devils resided, it shocked her. When she felt the full weight of his authority, she was even more shocked.

Viscount Abaddon felt young, though that was likely an illusion maintained by the lord. The demonic power he wielded was evident to anyone with senses capable of perceiving it. His power could not be faked, nor could the authority written into his very being. Before her stood a devil that commanded deference. Strange though the devil's presence felt, unfamiliar though he was, Virexa bestowed the proper courtesies on the lord who freed her.

"How very interesting." Dispatar idly commented.

"My lord?" Virexa asked, confused at her master's reaction.

"There is no Viscount Abaddon in Baator."

Virexa froze. The fire in her veins turned to ice. That was impossible. She felt Viscount Abaddon's power. She felt his authority. He was a devil lord. She knew that truth in her bones. But her master would know any high ranking individual on any layer of the Hells. How was he unaware of Viscount Abaddon?

"Be at ease, Virexa. You are in no danger of incurring my displeasure." Dispatar said off-hand, as if it was of no importance to him. "You delivered Maltherion to me. You delivered Elariel to me. And you have delivered something even more interesting to me. Awareness. Awareness I previously lacked."

A burst of fire. Two more documents appeared in his hands. "Two warlocks were created in recent days. Such paltry mortals should be beneath my notice. They were beneath my notice. Now, the irregularities about them are a vital clue."

Dispatar had an excited grin on his face. "Baator's systems ensured the forging of their pacts. The name of their patron was left blank, to be amended later. Now we have found their patron. A devil, confirmed by the severing of your pact. You would not have been freed from your contract if he were some other creature pretending to be one of us. Powerful and of high standing by your report, yet there is no record of his existence in all of Baator. He is not one of us. He is an outsider. Peripheral. And he is not the only one."

Another document appeared in Dispatar's hand. He held a veritable stack of documents now. An excited smile stayed fixed on his face as he read over it. "Mortal agents reported an echo of great infernal power, many times superior to even the Viscount you encountered. A presence so powerful, her very presence left prints in her wake, whispers of a coming ice age. My agents say it was as if an Archduke of Hell had walked about the surface of the Prime Material. Yet no contracts were breached. No celestial retaliation was dispensed. Do you understand the gravity of this, Virexa?"

"I do, my lord." Virexa responded immediately.

Laws were the lifeblood of Baator. Agreements amongst themselves and agreements with those beyond the Hells safeguarded their power, enhanced their influence. If Viscount Abaddon truly did not belong to the hierarchy of Baator, he was an anomaly. A devil lord, capable of helping Baator reap great boons or suffer devastating losses.

"The devil freed you." Dispatar continued. "He surrendered the phylactery and Elariel into your custody. His warlocks spread influence in the mortal world not to compete with Baator, but to create an independent footing. Viscount Abaddon is not our enemy. His actions in his meeting with you have granted him a fair amount of leniency, but we must understand who and what he is. You, Virexa, will be my agent in this matter. Few among us can freely travel to the material plane. Among my Erinyes, only you have met with Abaddon. Only you have the beginnings of good rapport with him. Go to the material plane. Do not threaten the warlocks, but watch them. Observe their dealings. Report your findings, and inform me the moment their actions move against the interests of Baator. When Abaddon returns to them, greet him. Be cordial, do not threaten. He is not an enemy. Not yet. We have too much to gain from him to risk ostracizing him. Are my orders clear?"

"They are, my lord. I will not fail you." Virexa said with conviction.

"You never have. Go now. I expect constant reports of your progress." Dispatar waved his hand in dismissal. Already, another devil was entering the chamber behind her for their audience with the lord of Dis.

Virexa bowed her head and backed away from the throne. Once a respectable distance away, she turned and exited the chamber.

Succubi, cambions, hangers on who wasted their days gossiping about the goings on of Hell descended on her the moment she was away.

Virexa ignored them all. Her mission did not require her to entertain their stupidity. Once free of the tower, Virexa took flight, beginning her journey between the planes.

Most devils were bound to Hell forever, unable to leave unless summoned by mortal magics. Even succubi first needed to invade mortal dreams before manifesting in the material plane. Erinyes were different. They alone could travel freely, making Virexa the perfect agent to carry out Lord Dispatar's will. It was why he selected her to barter with Maltherion. It was why he now sent her to barter with the anomaly.

A magical disguise garbed Virexa's form as she walked among the mortals. Irritating though their presence was, her patience had weathered her stay in Maltherion's servitude. Weak mortals were inconsequential by comparison.

The warlocks were easy to find. They were recruiting help for a business venture. A business venture named after their master Abaddon. Virexa quickly penned a report about the reach the warlocks were trying to extend over the mortal populace and sent it back to the Hells. She approached the warlocks as a simple mortal mercenary. Securing employment in their business was frighteningly easy. When she spoke to Viscount Abaddon again, Virexa would need to ensure he installed proper security measures so such infiltrations could not happen in the future. It would not benefit Hell for such an interesting anomaly to be undermined from within.

Virexa worked in the warlock's employ. She observed. She drafted reports. She waited for Abaddon to return. Their conversation promised to be very interesting.

#7,927
I had only participated in a single Rating Game prior to today. That Rating Game pitted my unknown peerage against the third ranked peerage in the Underworld. Today's Rating Game, my second, saw my peerage pitted against the second ranked peerage in the Underworld. I'd also spoken to Diehauser before about potentially facing his peerage in a Rating Game. Perhaps my third Rating Game would be against the first seed. Facing the third seed, then the second, then the first seed in my first, then second, then third Rating Game. Wouldn't that be funny?

Of course, today was different from my match against Bedeze. I would not be fighting for the lordship of my house. This was a friendly match. Roygun had been fully transparent with her intentions. She enjoyed competing in Rating Games and wanted to see how her peerage compared against mine. She wasn't out to rob me of house and home, just have some fun beating my teeth in. After Bedeze, then the business with Helios, it was a welcome change of pace.

The circumstances of the Rating Game might be different, but I was well aware Helios and his cronies would be watching. Anything we used in the Rating Game would become common knowledge, something he could plan for and be ready to combat. As a result, Medea and I had agreed to hold some of our stronger abilities back. We'd both refrain from using our Sacred Gears, and we would hide the more esoteric abilities of certain members of our peerage.

The identities of our new peerage members wouldn't stay secret. It was practically impossible. After defeating Bedeze, and now with the frenzy kicked up by Helios attempting to have me assassinated, I had a sizable following in the Underworld, that was before my trade empire was even taken into account. Devils and many other supernatural creatures beyond were already tuning in to watch me face off against Roygun. Even those who weren't interested in me personally were still tuning in. The current second ranked devil peerage fighting the peerage that humiliated the former third seed? People wanted to see what happened here.

I had a brief conversation with Serafall this morning through a Hole, warning her about potential fallout from some of my new peerage members. The one who concerned her the most was understandably Achilles. Maybe pouring fuel on the Greek's rage so soon after Zekram sunk Thrinacia wasn't the best idea, but that wasn't on me. I had a Titan after me and needed all the support I could get. I couldn't ask for a better Knight than Achilles, and I had nothing to do with Zekram flying off the handle. Serafall was still displeased that I'd set another political landmine, but I promised to take her on another vacation to appease her. That woman worked way too much. She was going to crack one of these days unless something was done. I couldn't help but think it was partly my fault with all of the damage I'd done to international relations in recent days. Achilles probably didn't help.

Regardless, it was done. He would be revealed to the world today along with the rest of my peerage when we faced Roygun. It was strange to think that many in my peerage were still unknown. When we'd fought Bedeze, my peerage only consisted of Medea, Aqua, Matatabi, Coal, and Shang Tsung. We'd grown immensely in the comparatively little down time between that match and this one.

There was a gathering scheduled before the match much like a pregame interview one might find in mortal sports. I didn't attend. The main goal was for the fighters to play the media game, garnering support and showing off. I had no need to garner any more support and I couldn't care less what the talk shows would say about me. The results of the Rating Game, win or lose, would speak for me.

I did however agree to meet with Roygun prior to the start of the match. It was supposed to be a big dramatic moment where we squared off and taunted each other. Devils with cameras were pushing and shoving one another to get the best shot of the stage as I approached Roygun. We were both alone. Our peerages were waiting for us in the respective ready areas we were assigned.

I felt a tad overdressed as Roygun and I came to a stop a short distance from one-another. Where I'd come dressed in a dyed mithril shirt and pants Medea had made for me, Roygun wore a tight-fitting green dress. Most devils didn't wear much armor into combat, as stupid as that was. After watching some film from her past matches, I knew Roygun had a suit of armor she wore, but only on occasions where she faced powerful foes – Diehauser, Bedeze, other devils ranked in the top ten. Either she didn't think she'd need it against me, or she just hadn't put it on yet.

Roygun shook my hand with a warm smile on her face, ignoring the shouted questions of the reporters and the flash of their cameras. "It's good to see you again, Balthazar. Thank you for going through with this, even in light of recent events."

I shrugged. "You're doing me a bit of a favor here. I get to show off. Hopefully, seeing what you're about to face will make people think twice about messing with me again."

Roygun's smile turned anticipatory, excited. "I'm looking forward to seeing what you have in store for me. May the best devil win."

"Good luck, Roygun. Have fun. I know I plan to." With a parting nod, I stepped backward into a Hole, reappearing in the waiting area assigned to my peerage.

"Are we all ready?" I asked as Medea walked forward to greet me.

She nodded. "Shiroe is a touch nervous, but we are prepared."

I looked past her shoulder to where Shiroe stood. Our ready area was a VIP box with a good view overlooking the arena. Shiroe stood at the window, looking out over the crowd of thousands that had assembled for this match.

I walked up beside him, silently observing the masses below.

"Everything alright?" I asked.

His features turned impassive. "I'm fine."

I nodded. "Alright." I patted him on the shoulder. "Don't stress about this too much. It's not do or die. Roygun's a friend. This is more for fun than anything else, so try to have some fun."

The announcer called out the fifteen minute warning. We'd be teleported to the arena and given a short amount of time to ourselves per the rules of this particular match.

Roygun and I met a few days ago to go over exact details. As she challenged me, technically I had the benefit of being able to choose a lot of the rules. I didn't care too much, so I'd reached out to her and we'd arranged a setting and ruleset that fit both of us.

This would be a near-standard Rating Game. We'd fight for three hours. At the end of that time, whoever had the most material left would be crowned the winner. If either of our Kings or complete peerages were eliminated, the match would end early.

The venue would be a false recreation of the city of Lucifaad. Roygun suggested it. Normally, Rating Game arenas were much smaller than the massive former capitol of the Underworld, but arenas could be larger as shown with my state-spanning fight with Bedeze. I believe Roygun suggested the city to try to limit Matatabi's movement between the packed buildings on the streets. I could have suggested elsewhere, but how many opportunities did you have to rampage through a massively populated city with no repercussions? Matatabi and my larger peerage members would be fine. Roygun was underestimating their mobility and adaptability. Either that, or she also wanted to blow up the city during our fight.

In a flash of light, my peerage was all teleported into the arena. I looked around, chuckling as I recognized the building we'd been sent to. Evidently, my headquarters for this match would be the headquarters building of my business, right across the street from where Serafall Leviathan's own office building stood.

"Do we want to stay or move?" I asked Medea. She was in charge of setting up the defenses around our base. While we knew the building and the surroundings well, it was also a very obvious location for Roygun to target.

Medea pursed her lips. "I believe this will be sufficient. They will know where we are, but I will soon ascertain their location as well. Fighting where we are familiar will give us an advantage."

Medea grabbed Irene and Keno, directing them as they began to layer protections over the building and the area around it.

Achilles walked around the room curiously, idly poking at the walls with his spear. He wore a full suit of grecian-styled armor Medea had crafted for him complete with a helmet. Currently, his face was covered. His identity would inevitably be uncovered in this match, but he wanted to make a grand reveal.

"Where are we?" Achilles asked.

"Bael, Abaddon and Astaroth Trading Co's headquarters. This is where we run our business out of." I answered. "I haven't had a chance to show you around yet. Sorry for that."

"How many people work here?" Shiroe asked, opening the drawers on the desk, frowning when he found nothing. This was a recreation of the building, a slightly inaccurate one by the layout of the room. There wouldn't be anything in the drawers or cabinets.

"Technically, four people. In reality, Magdaran and I don't come in too often because we're busy making the products we sell. My sister hasn't been in as much recently because Sairaorg's needed her with him while he was named Heir Vapula. Latia is the only one who has been working full time." I explained.

Shiroe looked confused. "Why do you have a building this large if only one person is working? From what I understand, your business's reach is impressive. How can one person maintain that?"

"For one thing, Latia is amazing at what she does." I said easily, aware we were likely being watched by the entire Underworld as they observed our Rating Game preparations. Latia didn't get enough credit in the devil media for how much work she did for the company. Many thought we'd made her a partner only because we wanted the Astaroth name attached to the business to increase revenue. In reality, Magdaran and I basically didn't work here any more. The company wouldn't function without Latia.

"For another, there are technically more workers. In the real building, we have hundreds of skeletons and golems that handle minor tasks and paperwork. I'm guessing they didn't recreate that in the arena because it would give us an unfair advantage." Of course, I could still summon a hoard of skeletons through Holes, but I didn't want to say that part out loud. "That or, more likely, people still haven't managed to recreate Medea's method of producing skeletons."

"But it's so simple." Shiroe said, surprised.

I grinned. "Yes, but she taught you. Everyone else is trying to figure it out with nothing to go on." That, and they needed dragon teeth to use Medea's method, something I intentionally left out. In the modern day with dragons ranging from extinct to so powerful they could threaten pantheons, dragon teeth were very difficult to come by. That is, unless you had a regenerating dragon in your peerage that spent his days trying to gnaw through the impenetrable hide of an impervious lion.

Around my neck, my flaming scarf stirred. Matatabi slowly unwound herself from around my neck, perching herself on my shoulder as she arched her back in a stretch. She plopped her butt down on my shoulder, looking around. "Has the fighting started?" she asked, still sounding groggy from her nap.

I reached up with my opposite hand and gently scratched her head, eliciting a pleased purr from the cat as she leaned into my touch. "We've got a few minutes before the fighting starts. We were only just teleported into the arena."

Refocusing, I faced the present members of my peerage. Keno and Irene were still erecting wards with Medea. "Is everyone ready? We all remember our groups?"

After discussing it with Medea, we both came to the conclusion that the end result of this Rating Game wasn't overly important to us. It was a good opportunity to show off, potentially preventing other elements in the supernatural from wanting to mess with us. That could be accomplished well enough by cutting my peerage loose to do what they will on their own. I'd still be standing by to transport them with Hole if they desired, but I was leaving them up to their own devices for the most part. Some of them would be travelling around together. Others would be flying solo. If anyone got in over their head, I'd be able to support them, but this Rating Game wasn't serious. They deserved to have a little fun here as well.

"We are ready, master." Shang Tsung said eagerly. On his shoulder, a large moth idly nibbled on the collar of his shirt.

"You all have a method to contact me. Medea and I will be watching from here. If you need anything, let us know and we'll support you." I smiled wide. "Have fun, everyone."

Roygun Belphegor couldn't help the anticipatory smile that spread across her face as the start of the Rating Game was announced. She'd been looking forward to this for some time now. She enjoyed competing in Rating Games. She enjoyed seeing how her peerage, her friends, measured up against other devils in the Underworld. This match promised to be exceptional.

Despite her many attempts to reach out to him cordially, Bedeze Abaddon always scorned her advances. She would invite him to a party in her home. Bedeze would return a torn invitation.

Roygun never had malicious intentions. She only wanted to get to know the man better and perhaps build a friendship between their two clans that could potentially grow into something more. Bedeze was a prideful, jealous man. He could never see past his many defeats at her hands to see the benefit in cultivating a friendship with Roygun.

Like the rest of the Underworld, Roygun found herself intrigued when Balthazar Abaddon appeared seemingly from nowhere to challenge his uncle for the lordship of the Abaddon Clan. Like the rest of the Underworld, Roygun expected Balthazar to be humiliated, even if she secretly hoped he could take Bedeze down a peg or two. The results were beyond what she believed to be possible.

Balthazar not only defeated Bedeze, an old devil who had bested strong contenders from all over the Underworld, but he demolished Bedeze's entire peerage while greatly outnumbered.

The philosophy Bedeze followed while constructing his peerage differed wildly from Roygun's own. Bedeze used his vast wealth to surround himself with champions already proven in Rating Games, trading them away from their prior Kings for favors or wealth. When he prepared to face specific individuals, he would completely rework the roster of his peerage to better defeat them. Bedeze had attempted it many times against Roygun herself. It almost worked once.

Roygun's philosophy was different. She took her time gathering her peerage, over a century spent searching for the right people. Once her peerage was finalized, it never changed. Many members of her peerage synergized well with one another and they all got along. More important to Roygun than even her standing in the Rating Games was her peerage's well being. They were her friends, not her underlings. They fought for her not because they were under contract, but because they all genuinely cared for her as she cared for them. Perhaps that was why she prevailed against Bedeze time after time. Or perhaps Bedeze was simply inept against anyone with a counter to his Clan Trait. Roygun with Crack, Diehauser with Worthless, and Balthazar with greater mastery over the Abaddon trait Hole all bested Bedeze with varying levels of ease.

It didn't matter. He was bested, and now dead. Roygun couldn't bring herself to shed a tear over the arrogant prat's passing. When considering how things had worked out for her in the aftermath, she was almost glad he was out of the way. Every attempt she had made to ally her Clan with the Abaddons was met with failure because of Bedeze's fragile ego. The new lord of Abaddon had already been far more accepting of her advances, she just needed to push a little harder.

Balthazar Abaddon was far more interesting than his late uncle. The peerage he gathered around himself prior to facing his uncle was small, yet paradoxically impossibly large. Devils spent centuries searching for proper individuals to reincarnate for their peerage. Roygun was somewhat lucky in that regard. Her Queen's Clan Trait allowed her to help Roygun cut the necessary time to find certain individuals from decades to merely years. As far as Roygun was aware, Balthazar had no such advantage prior to finding his Queen.

Medea of Colchis – a prize the entire Underworld and many factions beyond would threaten war to attain. Roygun had watched from a distance as Balthazar built an empire with her aid. How did he come to meet her? How did he convince her to join his cause? Roygun didn't doubt that Medea was intelligent enough to know that greater offers would have come along, why did she choose Balthazar?

It was an interesting thing to think about, but ultimately irrelevant. Medea joined Balthazar. Was it her who found the rest? Aqua – a young girl with a Sacred gear none had ever seen. Matatabi – a yokai of immense power missing from the history books. The Colchian Dragon Coal – said to be trapped inside the Sacred Gear Perfected State yet somehow free. Shang Tsung – a seemingly insignificant mortal who was able to steal the power of a demigod. It was all so exciting!

Now, Roygun's peerage would face them all and more. Balthazar reported to her that he had completed his peerage in the time between his last match and this one. Barely more than a year and Balthazar's peerage was already complete. Even if the rest of his peerage were simple mortals, his peerage would still be one of the strongest in the Underworld, and Roygun sorely doubted Balthazar was unable to find more impressive individuals for his peerage. With Medea's help, he likely found more amazing people.

Roygun would learn soon. They would meet in combat.

She was so excited! She hadn't been this excited for a Rating Game since the first time she faced Diehauser Beliel. The handsome young Abaddon lord had already impressed her. Initially, he only had her eye, now he had her attention. He'd impressed her before. It was time to see if he could do it again.

"What are your orders?"

Roygun looked over her shoulder. At her side, the silver-haired form of her Queen stood waiting. Slitted yellow eyes like those of a snake peered out from a pale, long face. Grey and yellow scales dotted the woman's face and neck, disappearing down beneath her dark dress. Severance Valac was one of the few pure-blooded devils in Roygun's peerage. The Valacs treated Severance poorly as a child. The Valacs were one of the few Pillars to manage to have an abundance of children. As the youngest child of three daughters and two sons, the Valacs saw no value in Severance, trying to marry her off for miniscule favors. Roygun saw her potential, taking the young woman as her queen. Severance had repaid Roygun's faith hundreds of times over.

"We don't know what the new members of Balthazar's peerage are capable of. Until we know otherwise, we will assume they are all at least as dangerous as Shang Tsung. No one goes anywhere alone. We proceed as planned and scout with Juniper's Sacred Gear." Roygun ordered.

"What about me?"

Roygun turned around. Iona, one of Roygun's Pawns, stood with a frown on her face. The small blonde girl did not seem happy to be excluded.

"I'm no good here. You know that." Iona said. "Let me scout."

"We don't know what Balthazar's new pieces are capable of." Roygun protested.

"All the more reason to send me out as a scout." Iona countered.

"They might be able to find you even with your Sacred Gear." Roygun said.

Iona shrugged. "Then they find me. I'd rather be useful than sit here doing nothing."

Roygun shared a long look with Severance. Severance gave her a minute nod.

Roygun sighed, turning back to Iona. "Stay safe. If you find someone new, get away before reporting back, and stay far away from Medea."

Iona smiled. "Don't worry. I'll be fine." In a flash of red energy, a dark cloak appeared draped around Iona's shoulders. She pulled the hood up, winking at Roygun. "I'll let you know what I find." Iona stepped backwards, her body shimmering into nothingness.

Roygun watched the empty space a moment longer before turning back to the rest of her peerage. "Everyone else will stay here while Iona and Juniper's reflections scout the area. I don't want us overextending until we know what Balthazar's new pieces are capable of."

Severance nodded, looking pointedly at Juniper.

Juniper walked forward. Black hair was tied back into a high ponytail atop her head. Silver armor – amusingly purchased from Bael, Abaddon and Astaroth Trading Co. – made metallic clinking sounds as she walked. Juniper drew a long, slender katana from her hip. The back half of the blade was colored dark while the sharpened edge gleaned a deadly silver. A second blade remained sheathed on her opposite hip.

Roygun found Juniper more through luck than anything else. She'd been on holiday in the mortal world when she felt a strong magical presence. She found a young Juniper practicing with a sword. The girl was an orphan. Roygun offered her a home. Juniper had followed Roygun ever since.

"Kurogane, Eisil, are you ready?" Juniper asked.

"Let's do it!" a high-pitched, excited voice shouted from the sword in Juniper's hand.

Long, lanky, skinless limbs stretched forward. A creature of muscle and bone slunk forward. Ands of muscle tightened with each step as a misshapen monster approached. It looked like a horse, but there was a rider firmly affixed to its body as one entity.

"Readyyy." a raspy voice said as the horse's mouth and the mouth of the crippled rider spoke in unison.

Eisil, a nucklavee, sought Roygun out of his own accord. Offering her his service if she would protect him from a mistake of his past. Roygun was more than happy to take him as her Rook.

Juniper swung her leg over Eisil as he lowered his body, mounting his horse's body in front of the undead body atop him.

A small silver hand mirror appeared in Juniper's free hand. A blinding white light rose from the face of the mirror to envelop Juniper and Eisil.

In a flash, reality shifted, split in two.

Juniper grinned. A matching, identical Juniper grinned back directly across from her.

Junier's Sacred Gear, Mirror Imprint, was a marvelous thing. According to records of its previous holders, it should not be as potent as this. The Sacred Gear must have mutated when it chose Juniper.

So long as she was holding the mirror, Juniper could manifest a fully independent copy of herself, complete with her steed and armaments. When used in tandem with Kurogane and Eisil, the Sacred Gear's effect was that much more potent.

The copy of Juniper reared back her arm and threw her katana away. The sword spun through the air, growing longer, expanding outward. A small girl with dark hair and silver eyes grew out of the sword wearing a fanciful black dress.

"Go get 'em, me!" the sword in the true Juniper's hand called out happily.

The small girl spun around, grinning at the sword and giving it a thumbs up before turning and running off to begin scouting.

When Roygun reincarnated Kurogane, Ajuka Beelzebub himself had asked to meet with her. He hadn't expected it would be possible to reincarnate a sentient weapon as a devil. Kurogane's reincarnation showed it was possible.

Roygun found her locked away in a mortal collector's attic. Kurogane wanted nothing more than to fight once more. The sword was overjoyed to receive Roygun's Knight piece. Now, she fought as Juniper's blade and partner. The two Knights were practically inseparable.

The mirror Juniper dismounted the mirror Eisil and drew the second sword from her waist. Mirror Juniper and mirror Eisil went off in different directions from Kurogane as they began to scout.

Roygun's peerage would wait while Juniper's copies searched the false city of Lucifaad they'd been transported to. They would observe and see what Balthazar Abaddon had in store for them.

Roygun was hoping for a great surprise.

Keno walked at Aqua's side, eyeing the tall buildings around them suspiciously.

Keno was still adjusting to some things about her new home. The scale of cities in her old world paled in comparison to the metropolis she now walked through, one of many in Hell.

"Where are they?" Keno asked, frustrated, eyes panning between the buildings around them as she tried to peer through the opaque windows.

Evil Pieces were an amazing invention, one she intended to study when she had the opportunity.

Machines capable of showing stories and live events much like a scrying mirror, yet widespread throughout the world. Aqua often dragged Keno into the depths of Castle Abaddon where she'd made her lair, burying the former vampire in a pile of stuffed animals and forcing her to watch anime with her.

Keno was uncertain what was happening the first time. She'd grown to enjoy the moments where she and Aqua disappeared into the darkness of the castle's lower levels to watch random shows. Sometimes, Aqua even took her to Build-A-Bear afterward.

But that was not important right now. Keno was on a battlefield set to fight the peerage of Roygun Belphegor. Keno and Aqua spent many hours watching recordings of Roygun's previous Rating Games. Roygun's peerage was strong, better in many ways than the many different peerages Keno saw in recordings of Bedeze's peerages. Unlike Bedeze, Roygun never changed her peerage. Roygun's clan trait was also a fantastic counter to the Abaddon power of Hole.

They had to take this fight seriously. Roygun's peerage didn't know what most of Balthaza's peerage was capable of. The only ones who were known quantities were those that participated in Balthazar's match against Bedeze. Achilles, Mothra, Irene and Shiroe all shared similar anonymity. They needed to take advantage of that fact.

Keno hadn't been with the peerage long. She already owed everyone in it more than she could repay. Balthazar pulled a wandering monster from the fringes of society and gave her a home in a mystical castle the likes of which she'd never seen. As if that wasn't great enough, Balthazar took Keno elsewhere, freeing her of a burden she'd carried for far too long. Finally, Keno no longer bore the weight of her dead people crushing down on her shoulder.

Keno expected pushback or suspicion from the other members of the peerage when she arrived in her new home. It was common in her old world. The new guy always had to prove themselves to the existing group. Keno expected trials and maltreatment. There was none. She was accepted easily. Almost every day, Aqua chatted about how great their family was.

Family. When was the last time Keno had a family? Did her old friends qualify? Certainly not. They abandoned her, tossed her aside to carry on their own adventures without her. Being in Hell, living at castle Abaddon showed Keno what a true family could be.

It would never be equivalent to what she'd been given, but if Keno could help win this Rating Game for Balthazar and her new family, then she would do everything in her power to achieve victory.

Aqua lightly bumped her shoulder into Keno's. "Taking this seriously is good, but don't forget the stakes are way different than the last time Bal had to do this. Roygun's his friend. We're not fighting for our lives here. Try to win, but also try to have some fun, okay?"

Keno relaxed slightly when she saw Aqua's warm, encouraging smile. "I'll try to have a little fun." Keno quietly acquiesced.

Aqua nodded, content with herself. "Good. Now let's go look for trouble!"

"What do you–Eep!" Keno let out a shocked shriek as Aqua latched onto her arm and dragged her through a dark keyhole that spawned directly in front of them.

Keno's wings shot out of her back, holding her in the air high above the city as the keyhole faded behind her. Keno scowled at Aqua, the bluenette laughed at her expression, unbothered by Keno's displeasure.

"Maybe warn me next time?" Keno said.

"Where would be the fun in that?" Aqua asked mischievously. "Get ready, I'm about to make us a target."

Aqua raised her keyblade high above her head. A golden beam of light shot out from the keyblade's tip, reaching high into the sky. Keno felt Aqua cast a minor charm to enhance her voice.

"HEY. YOU. GUUUYS!" Aqua shouted, her voice reverberating through the streets. "It's Aqua! You know? The girl that stopped Bedeze from using Hole during the last match? Better come get me before I seal Roygun's Crack!" Aqua paused, tilting her head. "…That sounded more uncouth than I intended. Sorry about that." When Aqua was done with her speech, she shot Keno a thumbs up.

Keno stared slack-jawed at the other girl. Keno reached up to smack herself in the face. What kind of tactic was this? Just shout to the world where you are and invite the entire peerage to come after you? What was she thinking?

Aqua's copy swung her keyblade towards the monster. The rotten fleshy facsimile of a rider atop its back snapped forward. A long blade of bone shot from its arm into its hand. The rider batted the keyblade aside as the monster latched its teeth around the copy's leg. The rider drove its bone blade through the copy's stomach, scattering it into golden motes of energy.

Keno narrowed her eyes, glaring down at the monster. That was Keno's friend the monster just tried to skewer.

Big mistake.

Daggers and javelins made from diamond fired from the walls of nearby buildings, turning the street into a death trap for the monster.

The two devils flew lazily through the air, eyes peeled on the buildings beneath them. In the street, a pile of reflective shards lay forgotten.

Shiroe frowned as he stared at dozens of magical screens in front of him. When he played Elder Tales, he often had many screens open to monitor the resources of his party. Paul's story still made Roygun's heart ache. The man was once a priest. Not greedy, perverse and corrupt like many priests in the modern age. No, he was a good man, only wanting to help the people around him as best as he could. When the church learned he had a Sacred Gear, they took him to become an exorcist. When they realized which Sacred Gear he had, they locked him away.

Holy Martyr was one of the few Sacred Gears tailored towards healing rather than killing. Unlike Twilight Healing, Holy Martyr came at a cost. Holy Martyr granted Paul regenerative abilities nearly equal to Coal. In order to heal others, Paul needed to take their wounds onto himself.

The church saw Paul as a vital asset, but not as a person. The first time Paul tried to leave, they chained him beneath a church, forcing him to heal their exorcists. The second time, they locked him in an iron maiden to teach him a lesson, then kept him unconscious whenever he was not needed to heal anyone. The regeneration granted by his Sacred Gear prevented him from needing to eat. It didn't banish Paul's hunger, his thirst.

Desperate, Paul reached out to Roygun, a devil, seeking salvation from the church. Roygun took Paul into her peerage, killing the corrupt Cardinal who'd ordered Paul be kept as he was. Whether the Cardinal worked alone or worked with the Vatican's blessing, Roygun didn't care. They'd hurt her Bishop through incompetence or malice. Roygun had never liked the church. After reincarnating Paul, she grew to hate them.

Holy light emanated from Paul. Ancas sighed as many of his wounds closed. Paul grit his teeth as he began to regenerate the injuries he'd taken from Ancas.

"We need to go now." Roygun said, watching as Chilles burst through the roof of a building rather than try to navigate her barrier of Cracks. Roygun erected a dome of cracks above Achilles, locking him back down near the ground. She couldn't keep this up forever. She needed to rest too.
