Aqua threw her head back in a laugh, flying over Keno to smack her on the shoulder. "There you go! Let's do this!"

A shadow rose out of one of the buildings beneath them. A small, spectral crow appeared in their path, arcing left.

One of Medea's familiars. She was showing them the way.

Keno and Aqua wordlessly fell in behind the crow, following it to their destination.

After several minutes, the raven stopped in midair looking up.

Keno followed the raven's gaze and gasped in surprise. "Move!" she shoved Aqua to the side.

A blob of viscous green fluid fell between them, narrowly missing Aqua.

Aqua turned to look up with Keno, an excited grin pulling at her lips. "Do you want Ancas or Juniper?" she asked.

Above, Juniper sat on Ancas's back as the basilisk lazily twirled through the air. A reflection peeled off of the basilisk, charging down towards them.

"I'll just fight whoever attacks me." Keno said. She cast a number of preparatory spells; her body flashed yellow, green, blue and gold as she prepared herself.

"Luck of the draw it is." Aqua said, the latter half of the sentence turning echoey and disjointed as Aqua split into eight different copies. "I'll deal with the reflections. Let's go for the real ones."

Keno nodded. PLan made, Aqua and Keno took off into the air, arcing wide around the reflections while Aqua's copies charged straight on. Juniper would now need to decide whether to recall the reflection and attack Keno or leave the reflection to fight Aqua's copies. She chose the second one.

Juniper leapt off Ancas's back, wings appearing to catch her before she could fall. The Knight drew her sword and angled downward, towards Keno. Ancas spiralled down towards where Aqua was rising. Looks like their opponents had decided who they wanted to fight.

It made sense. Aqua was a known quantity and a rather intimidating one at that. Ancas was the stronger of the two and didn't have many things Aqua could seal. In contrast, if Juniper lost access to her Sacred Gear, her combat potentially would plummet. They were banking on Juniper being able to eliminate Keno fast so she could join Ancas in fighting Aqua.

It made sense, but it pissed Keno off. She'd show this girl the error in her judgement.

Keno stopped flying up, arcing back and away to gain altitude while still forcing Juniper to follow her.

Juniper's eyebrows narrowed. She swung her sword. An afterimage continued forward after the blade stopped, flying towards Keno.

Keno easily dodged the blade, dipping down to avoid a second and third as Juniper kept unleashing attacks, channeling her Sacred Gear through her sword.

Keno lifted her hand, a diamond-colored spell circle appearing before her. Jagged crystals the length of her forearm launched out of the spell circle.

Juniper tensed, then watched as the crystals arced harmlessly above her. Juniper fixed Keno with an amused smile.

Juniper really wasn't taking Keno seriously enough.

A black magic circle appeared before Keno.

Juniper's eyes flew wide as gravity suddenly reversed on her, causing her to fall up. The crystals above her altered course, raining down from above while Juniper was helplessly carried towards them.

Juniper slashed her sword down through the air. Afterimages of the blade created a perfect wall of steel between her and the crystals, deflecting them all before Juniper could be injured.

Keno grit her teeth, firing more crystals at Juniper only for them to be absorbed by another afterimage of Juniper's sword.

In the skies a short distance away, five Aquas flew down in waves, slashing at Ancas in an attempt to injure him. The snake nimbly moved out of their paths, biting and thrashing at them. He managed to connect to one of the copies, scattering it into motes of energy.

One Aqua paused in the air above him, holding her Keyblade high then thrusting it downward. A torrent of lightning assaulted Ancas. The bolts knocked him around, but his scales held strong.

Keno couldn't help but think maybe she and Aqua should have swapped opponents. It would be simple for Keno to overcome the Basilisk's defenses and Aqua would have no trouble circumventing the mirror shields Juniper kept using. It was harder for Keno to get around them when she had to keep her distance from the Knight.

Many of the other members of Balthazar's peerage were treating this match as a game. Keno wasn't. She wanted to win. This was her chance to start paying Balthazar back for giving her a new home. Giving her a family. Giving her a life. They were winning this Rating Game.

"Aqua!" Keno called, sending another volley of crystals towards Juniper to force the Knight back. "Switch!"

Keno sent one final crystal lance towards Juniper then flew through the air towards Ancas, increasing her speed with a minor enhancement spell. She really needed to get with Shiroe to see how he was able to make his enhancements so powerful with so little training. That man was so gifted in enchantments it was downright unfair.

Three Aquas had small frowns on their face, but they complied with Keno's request, disengaging from Ancas while a fourth distracted him and was destroyed for its trouble. Aqua gave Keno a small nod as they passed each other, then immediately brought her Keyblade up to bat away Juniper's sword before it could slash into Keno from behind. Juniper was fast.

Keno climbed through the air, already raining crystal dagger down towards the basilisk.

Ancas snarled as the daggers sunk through his scales to remain lodged in his body. He shook a few out before coiling upwards towards her.

Crystals grew around Keno's face, making protective glasses. It was now much harder to see, but Keno would almost certainly be unable to focus on a point so small as Ancas's eyes, making his stone-gaze useless against her.

Ancas was getting closer. The crystal daggers she sent into him seemed to annoy the basilisk more than anything else. She needed something bigger.

Keno sighed. She was hoping to keep this in her back pocket for later. This was a friendly match and she knew true enemies would come in the future. Balthazar's life had already been threatened once. That was why Medea and Balthazar were avoiding participating in this fight directly, they wanted to keep some of their abilities secret so they could surprise their enemies.

Still, showing just how powerful Balthazar's servants were would do well to make others think twice about attacking him. The Underworld believed Balthazar had some of the strongest Pawns in Hell. Shang Tsung was touted as an equal to Queens and Coal was said to be stronger than most of the strongest Rooks. It was time to show them that Balthazar's Pawns truly were the best Hell had ever seen.

Keno did not possess Coal's titanic strength or unparalleled regeneration. Keno couldn't absorb traces of people's souls to copy what made them special like Shang Tsung. But she did have a Talent.

Televisions were wonderful things. Keno spent many nights since her reincarnation watching movies with Aqua. That wasn't the only thing she used the televisions for. Keno was born with a Talent that let her copy any spell she saw used, regardless of what other requirements that spell might have. The downside was she could only use one spell at a time. For centuries, that Talent was restricted, occupied keeping her alive while she held the spell that killed everyone and everything she ever knew, turning her into a vampire that bore the weight of an entire country's dead on its shoulders.

Landfall they'd named her. Her country fell to someone else's magic, but she was the one to bear the guilt.

That was just one more thing Balthazar had done for her. That spell, that curse that she had carried for years was gone now. Keno was free. Balthazar freed her; he freed her Talent. Keno owed Balthazar a debt she could never repay, but she would spend the rest of her immortal life trying.

Keno held a hand down towards the rapidly approaching form of Ancas. A spell circle, black like a night with no moon rimmed in crimson energy appeared before her hand.

Keno had come to realize the devils of this world, much like those of the world she came from, were arrogant and prideful. The older and more powerful a devil, the more they basked in these sins. They would go on talk shows or hire camera crews to watch them work their great magics to show off their power.

After Balthazar freed her from her burden Keno watched a video of Lord Bael showing the strength of his bloodline. With Aqua's help, Keno saved that video onto her new phone along with many others. They would be available whenever Keno needed them.

The dark spell circle in front of Keno hummed as an orb of pure destruction fired down towards Ancas. Space shook as its antitheses parted the air.

Ancas was caught completely by surprise. He'd been charging towards her as fast as he could to eliminate her. He was too close now to dodge.

Ancas shrieked as the orb of destruction struck him just beneath his head. Immediately, his scales and flesh began to erode away where struck by the orb. Less than a second after he was hit, a flash of gold pulled Ancas away.

"Roygun Belphegor's Rook retired."

Keno lowered her hand, her crystal glasses crumbling away as she smirked at the empty space that once held a basilisk. Let the Underworld, let the supernatural itself stew on that. Balthazar's Pawn could use the Bael's prized Power of Destruction.

"Roygun Belphegor's Knight retired."

Keno looked over her shoulder.

Juniper was gone. Three Aqua's had surrounded her, blasting fire and lighting down towards her while a fourth slipped past Juniper's mirror shield to stab her in the stomach. Aqua's copies rejoined her as she wiped the blood off her sword. She flew up to Keno and gave her a thumbs up.

"Good job, Keno. Let's see if we can't find any of the others."

Keno nodded. There was still a Rating Game to win.


X


Things were pretty much over.

I sat with Medea on a couch while we looked over the screens she was projecting, showing what her familiars saw.

With Juniper and Ancas gone, the only heavy-hitters left in Roygun's peerage were Severance and Roygun herself. Severance was occupied running away from Achilles to distract him and Roygun… We didn't actually know where Roygun was. She'd figured out how Medea was tracking her and started using Crack to shatter Medea's scryings and familiars.

Regardless, we'd only lost Coal and Roygun's peerage was running on fumes. This was basically the end.

"Balthazar," Medea said, a slight frown on her face. "Rogyun is approaching. Matatabi is with her."

My eyebrows furrowed. What did she mean Matatabi was with her?

Medea enlarged a screen and brought it over to me.

I sighed as I took in the image on screen. "Somehow, I'm not even surprised anymore." I said tiredly as I took in Roygun and Matatabi. "I'll go talk to her. If she attacks, please back me up." I was confident I could beat Roygun, but without using my Sacred Gear things would get very tricky.

"I'll be nearby." Medea assured me. She leaned over and gave me a kiss on the cheek before fading from view.

I stood and waved a hand. The window in front of me shattered outward. My wings sprouted from my back and I took to the sky.

Roygun was waiting for me in the sky above the building. She made no move to attack as I approached, merely floating there. Atop Roygun's head, resting with her limbs wound around Roygun's horns, Matatabi was fast asleep. Her little body swelled and shrunk in rhythm with her breathing.

"I believe you misplaced your Rook, Balthazar." Roygun said, an amused smile on her face as I joined her in the sky.

"Sorry about her."

Roygun shook her head, reaching up to scratch Matatabi's head. "It's no trouble."

Atop Roygun's head, Matatabi slowly opened one eye, staring at me lazily.

"You know we're in a Rating Game right now, right?" I asked tiredly.

Matatabi huffed at me, not moving from her slothful position. "She isn't trying to kill you or steal our things. I don't need to fight her. And she smells nice. Her head has a sleeping platform."

I looked at the cat through half-lidded eyes. "Those are her horns, Matatabi."

Matatabi didn't answer, shifting on Roygun's head so she was facing away from me. I heard light snoring from the dramatic cat.

I sighed, looking back at Roygun. "I really am sorry about her."

Roygun laughed. "Don't worry about it. I've enjoyed her company." Roygun looked off into the distance, a content smile on her face. "Decades I have held my position as the second-ranked peerage in the Underworld. I was beginning to think no one would come along who could challenge me. I'm pleased to see I was mistaken."

"The Rating Game isn't over yet." I said, watching her carefully.

Roygun chuckled. "Please, we are both aware of the position I am in. Perhaps I could eliminate some of your pieces personally, but that would leave me exhausted when I faced yourself and Medea. No. I am beaten. Soundly beaten."

"If it helps, you did much better than Bedeze. I was genuinely surprised that you were able to take down Coal."

"Had he been taking things more seriously, I don't know if we could have. He seemed far too happy as we did our level-best to tear him apart."

"He just enjoys fighting. Even when he loses those fights."

Roygun grinned at me. "I am the same way."

Looking up, Roygun carefully lifted Matatabi off of her head. Matatabi looked around, dreary and confused, as Roygun cradled her to her chest. Roygun drifted closer to me in the air and handed Matatabi to me. Matatabi climbed up onto my shoulder and stretched out only to wind herself around my neck and go to sleep again. Truly, there was never a more lazy creature in all of heaven and earth.

"I think I have kept poor Severance fleeing from Achilles for long enough." Roygun said, an amused curl to her lips. "I'd like to invite you and your peerage to my home after the Rating Game. Even with everything I've seen, I find myself ravenously curious about your new peerage members. Mothra and Keno especially have drawn my eye."

"I'll have to check if everyone's willing to attend, but we don't have anything planned after this." I said.

"Please don't feel pressured. I merely wish to celebrate my new place as the third seat in Hell's Rating Games."

I raised an eyebrow. "You want to celebrate losing your position? I don't think you even will. This is my second Rating Game. They can't make me the second seed after two Rating Games."

"It is not so much a celebration of my loss as it is a celebration of finding someone new to test myself against. And whether your ranking is official or not, everyone will agree that the peerage you have gathered is worthy of the second seed. Perhaps you could even unseat the emperor himself. I'm sure Diehauser would be just as happy as I am to finally lose to someone."

Roygun sighed. "But I'm dragging this out, aren't I? Thank you for agreeing to face me, Balthazar. Next time we do this, I'll be sure to give you a better challenge. I resign!"

Roygun vanished in a flash of gold. The arena slowly unravelled around me as an announcement shook the space.

"Roygun Belphegor has resigned. Balthazar Abaddon is the victor!"

#8,066
Castle Belhegor was a sight to behold. Pure white walls stretching tall. Towers surrounding the keep. There was even a small settlement surrounding the keep, though it appeared mostly abandoned.

Unlike the original Castle Abaddon, Castle Belphegor still stood. During the Devil Civil War, the original castle Abaddon was sacked and destroyed, taking most Abaddons with it. That was why there were now only two of us left following Bedeze's death. The civil war hadn't been kind to the Abaddon family.

Castle Belphegor managed to make it through the war. As a result, there were more surviving Belphegors than Abaddons. I didn't know any of them, and today wasn't about meeting them. Roygun had locked us in a private wing of the castle. Upbeat rock music played while our peerages mingled, laughing and exchanging good-natured verbal jabs now that we weren't trying to kill one-another.

I didn't want to participate in any of the post match media circus, so Roygun brought us all back to her home straightaway, breaking her established habit of giving interviews after her matches. She said it wasn't a big deal and would rather spend the time with us.

I was surprised when, just before teleporting us all here, Roygun stopped by one of the VIP booths to grab another guest. I hadn't known the guest in question would be in attendance at our Rating Game, but it made sense in hindsight.

Mine and Roygun's peerage milled about the area, some quietly chatting, others drunkenly slurring boisterous taunts. They all seemed to be having a good time.

Myself, Roygun and our third claimed a small table out of the way while they had their fun.

"Cheers," Roygun said, lifting a wine glass overhead with a warm smile on her face. "To the Underworld's new second ranking Rating Game peerage!"

Diehauser, the guest Roygun had brought along, lifted his own glass, offering me a small smile. "To your peerage, Balthazar."

I raised my glass and took a drink. "Thank you, but I'm not second ranked. You still hold your title, Roygun."

I'd done a little more homework on how the Rating Game ratings were calculated. I still didn't know the finer details, but I did know that I couldn't make the top five until I had competed in more matches. Still, I'd jumped up to eighteenth place, something never before seen by someone after just two Rating Games, so that was something.

Roygun waved my argument aside. "Whether you hold the rank officially or not, the three of us are well aware where things stand. Hell as a whole knows where things stand. I'm genuinely surprised we were able to eliminate even one of your pieces."

"Most of my peerage was unknown." I said cordially. "You couldn't plan for them and had to hold back. That gave Achilles and Coal the perfect field to face you."

"True, but the end result remains the same. You won today." Roygun's lips pulled up in an excited grin. "But next time, expect a more interesting fight. We'll be developing strategies to face you, Balthazar."

I lifted my glass, a smile on my face. "Looking forward to it."

Roygun took another sip of her drink, fixing a look at Diehauser. "When are you planning to join in, great emperor?"

Diehauser sighed, setting his glass on the table. "Please stop calling me that."

Roygun smirked. "Can't. It's too fun."

Shaking his head, Diehauser said, "You know I'm open to a Rating Game almost anytime. I'd ask that we wait until after Sairaorg Vapula's wedding, but that is the only pressing engagement in my future."

I raised an eyebrow at him. "You're going to Sairaorg's wedding. Wait, they scheduled it already?"

Diehauser nodded. "My parents have been in close contact with Lord and Lady Vapula since Sairaorg was made their heir. It will reflect well on our growing relationship that I attend."

So the Beliels were trying to ally with the up-and-coming Vapulas, huh? That wasn't nearly as interesting to me as another tidbit.

'Did we get an invite to Sairaorg and Kuisha's wedding yet?' I asked in my mind, reaching out to the mental connection I shared with my Queen.

'We did. It arrived just before the Rating Game. They're getting married next month.' Medea said back, meeting eyes with me from across the room where she was quietly speaking to Severance, Thelisei and Irene.

'Cool. Thanks.' I sent back before refocusing on the people I was seated with. Apparently Sairaorg hadn't snubbed me. I didn't expect he had, but I would've had words with the man if he thought he wasn't going to invite me to my little sister's wedding.

"I guess I'll see you at the wedding, then." I said.

Diehauser nodded. "I'm looking forward to it."

"Weddings are great and all, but when will you two compete?" Roygun asked, looking between us. "I'm almost looking forward to this match more than the one I just participated in."

I raised an eyebrow at her. "You're awfully invested in this."

Roygun nodded. "I am. This is the start of what I spent so long trying to create with Bedeze. The top three Rating game champions all on pleasant terms with one-another working together to make themselves and the Underworld stronger. Not to mention how fun it will be."

"It does sound appealing." Diehauser said, smiling softly. "I've been looking for good-natured rivalries for some time. I find they are good for everyone involved. Roygun and I have pushed each-other to improve, but Bedeze always took his losses too poorly to join us."

"Think of the following we'd generate." Roygun said wistfully. "The top three! Grievously wounding each-other one second; sharing tea the next! The devilnet will eat it up."

I shrugged. "I've never been all that concerned with my public image, but I can't deny it would probably generate some good PR."

Roygun looked sidelong at me as she slowly took a sip of wine. "If I were you, Balthazar, I would start worrying about my public image. I've heard whispers that you're looking to build a settlement in your lands. It's hard to attract citizens if everyone is afraid of you."

I frowned. "Where did you hear that?" I was planning on starting that settlement plan soon, but I hadn't told many people about it. How were people already gossiping about it?

Roygun smiled softly at me. "I heard it during a party Lady Agares held. Devils talk, Balthazar. All the more reason to be the one spreading the information, lest others put words in your mouth that were never there."

I was still frowning, staring at the table. She made a good point. I wanted nothing to do with public relations campaigns, but I couldn't kid myself. I was living in Hell. I'd amassed too much power and influence to stay silent forever. Thanks to Medea running interference and Latia handling most aspects of my business, I hadn't needed to show my face too much. If I kept competing in Rating Games, that would probably have to change. The last thing I wanted was someone creating a false rumor about me that everyone else took as fact because I never came out in public and told people what was actually going on.

Diehauser laid a comforting hand on my shoulder. "Speaking to the public has never been my favorite facet of this profession either, but it is necessary. If you'd like, I can give you the contact information of the company I use to handle things. I still have to make appearances on occasion, but they handle all the scheduling and the more mundane tasks."

"That would actually be really helpful. Thanks." I said.

"Anytime." He lifted his glass. "To the beginning of a fruitful friendship."

Roygun and I lifted our glasses and we all drank.

Three Kings of some of the strongest peerages in the Underworld sitting around a table sharing a drink and enjoying each other's company. It felt a little surreal, but I was enjoying every moment of it.

Naturally, that was when my phone rang and ruined the moment.

Scowling, I looked at the phone to check the caller ID, intending to send it to voicemail. Only after reading the name of the caller did I realize very few people had my phone number.

"I'm really sorry," I said, standing. "I have to take this. It's Lady Leviathan."

Roygun raised an eyebrow at me. Diehauser looked surprised.

"Please," Roygun said, "Don't apologize for dealing with matters best dealt with immediately."

Nodding in thanks, I walked a short distance away and answered the call. "Hello?"

"Are you busy right now?" Serafall asked.

"Uh…I'm at Castle Belphegor with my peerage. Roygun invited us over after the Rating game."

Serafall made a considering sound on the other side of the call. "Is she there?"

"I can let you talk to her."

"Just put it on speaker."

I put the phone on speaker and walked back to the table. "You're on speaker. Roygun and Diehauser are here."

"To what do we owe the pleasure, Lady Leviathan?" Roygun said warmly.

"Would you be offended if I stole Balthazar for a bit?" Serafall said. "There's a matter I need his help with that really shouldn't wait."

"By all means." Roygun said. "We can continue this another time."

Roygun raised a hand. A scattering of pink energy fell around me. Smiling, she said, "There. You are now keyed to the wards. Visit whenever you like."

Blinking in surprise, I said, "Thank you. I'll take you up on that sometime. Is it alright for my peerage to stay here or…?"

"They can stay as long as they like. They seem to be enjoying themselves, and my peerage appears to be enjoying their company." Roygun said, looking over our two peerages happily mingling.

I caught Medea's inquisitive eye as I looked over my peerage.

'I'll let you know if there's any trouble.' I said through our mental bond. 'Can you look after everyone for me?'

'Of course. Let me know if you need help with Serafall.'

'Thanks. I don't know what I'd do without you.'

Across the room, Medea's lip curled up into the slightest grin.

'I'm sure you'd manage, but it is my pleasure to make sure you don't have to.'

"Thanks, Roygun." Serafall said through the phone. "Bal, come to my office." The line went dead as she hung up.

"Thanks for hosting me, Roygun." I said, pocketing my phone. "I'm sorry to cut this short but…"

"Pay it no mind." Roygun said, seemingly unoffended. "I'm glad we could have this little sit down. I look forward to more."

I held out my hand towards Diehauser. "It was good to see you again."

He stood and shook my hand. "It was good to see you as well. I'll pass along the contact information of that company I mentioned to your Queen. Once your business is concluded, I'll reach out to see about scheduling a Rating Game."

"Sounds good. Enjoy the rest of the party." I said, stepping back into a Hole. Roygun had keyed me to her castle's wards. I didn't even need Aqua's cheating hax to leave.

I walked into the lobby of Serafall's office building and was surprised to see dozens of people scrambling around. Typically, there was only the one secretary here behind the desk.

Said secretary caught my eyes as I approached the elevator set into the back wall. "Try to get her to take a short break if you can. We'll deal with the worst of the fallout until she's had some time to collect herself."

'Fallout'? That couldn't be good. I picked up the pace, lightly jogging over to the elevator.

As I stepped into Serafall's office, I was surprised to see there was someone else in the room with her.

He was tall. Wavy mint-colored hair was swept back atop his head. He wore a sea-green trench coat and a dark shirt beneath. Calculating eyes watched me as I approached.

Stopping, I bowed respectfully to the man. "Lord Beelzebub, it's an honor to–"

"Cut the niceties, Bal." Serafall said seriously. "We don't have the time for it."

"What happened?" I asked. Between the commotion downstairs and whatever this was, something was clearly wrong.

"Helios has reappeared." Ajuka Beelzebub, the Satan in charge of Hell's Technology Department, said plainly. "During your Rating Game, the Titan completely destroyed a number of facilities in the United States, killing the devils that worked in those facilities. The company that owned the buildings belonged to Zekram Bael. The devils slain all worked for him in some capacity."

Involuntarily, I sucked in a breath.

This was bad. Things were already precarious after Zekram blew up Thrinacia, but things looked like they might be calming down. If Helios just killed a bunch of devils…

"What do you need from me?" I asked.

The situation was bad. There was no denying that. Still, I couldn't see why Serafall had called me in. I wasn't a negotiator. I didn't know where Helios was. What did she need from me?

"Athena has been calling me nonstop for the last hour trying to set up a meeting." Serafall said. "She maintains that Helios is working alone and is doing what she can to keep us from responding. I've been putting off responding because I need to know what assets I have before I go to the negotiating table."

"What do you mean?" I asked.

"Serafall tells me you've bound mortals to yourself into something called a warlock." Ajuka said, watching me closely.

Slowly, I nodded. "I have."

"We have been unable to replicate the contract that created these warlocks." Ajuka said, expression unreadable.

"I need to know if others can replicate what you did before I talk to Athena." Serafall said. "Knowing we have that ace up our sleeve will change how I handle things."

I was silent for a moment, thinking about how I wanted to say this. In the end, I just spit it out. "I haven't told you about Virexa yet, have I?"

Serafall's eyebrows narrowed. "You made another warlock?"

"No. Not a warlock. A potential complication. I told you Faerun is what facilitates the contracts. That's technically true, but I just didn't want to get into the finer details of things while my warlocks were present and you wanted an explanation. The full mechanics of how it works rely on that world's Hells, there's nine of them, making and binding the contract. Without the Nine Hells's approval, there's no devil warlocks. At least, unless we figure out some way to replicate it on our own."

"And Virexa is an agent of these Hells that approached you?" Ajuka said, frowning slightly.

"Yes to the agent bit, no to the approached me part. We happened across each other by accident. She knows about me now and likely sent up a warning of some sort to her superiors, but there shouldn't be any burned bridges yet. I handled my meeting very delicately with her to avoid stepping on any toes and pissing them off. The point I'm trying to make is that Baator, the Nine Hells that is, are aware of what I've been doing now and might step in to make it more difficult or outright stop it."

Serafall was frowning too. "Can we negotiate with them?"

"Most likely yes." I said. "Baator thrives off of contracts. We have things they don't have access to which gives us a lot of bargaining power. Keep in mind though a lot of the higher powers there have been around since that cosmos was created and will do everything they can to wriggle every last advantage out of any contract they sign."

The corner of Serafall's lip pulled up. "I'm sure they're tricky, but I've had regular dealings with Nimue and Titania for centuries now. I'm aware of how to tread carefully."

Serafall sighed, falling into her office chair. "Well, there goes my quick and easy solution."

"We still need to know if it is viable." Ajuka said, standing at her side.

Serafall nodded tiredly. "Yeah. Who knows? Maybe working with these guys will give us a major advantage even Bal hasn't been able to find yet."

Serafall took a deep breath. "Okay." She stood up, looking at me seriously. "You need to take us to Faerun."

I looked between Serafall and the Beelzebub. "Both of you?"

Serafall nodded. "Yes. I'm going to try to create a warlock. Ajuka's going to take notes and observe the whole process. Maybe if he's present while it happens, he'll be able to replicate the effects here. I might have missed something important that he'll be able to pick up on. We put him in charge of research and development for a reason. If he can't find a way to replicate it, he'll probably head back with you at some point to try to make his own there."

"A private trip would give me the chance to discuss some other points of interest with you as well." Ajuka said cryptically.

I watched Beelzebub carefully, but the man didn't give anything away. I assumed he didn't mean me harm, but I wasn't a big fan of how indirectly he was speaking. He could have any number of intentions I wasn't aware of.

"I don't have a problem with taking you to Faerun, but you're aware a warlock is going to be directly anchored to your demonic power, right? Be careful who you pick. Don't just grab the first guy you see on the street." I warned.

"At least let me ask my warlocks if they know of anyone that would make a good warlock for you." I offered.

"Be my guest." Serafall said, waving encouragingly. "I don't want this to go wrong any more than you do."

Nodding, I opened a Hole and said, "Come with me."

As I stepped through the Hole, I felt for my connection to my warlocks, faint though it was, and followed it.

I emerged from the Hole in a small clearing. Iron carts on rails rolled around the area, gathering near a cut in the rock supported by sturdy wooden beams, the entrance to a mine dug into a tall mountain. Behind me, there was a dense forest packed with trees.

"My lord!" Vellia jumped, shocked as I appeared right behind her, two Satans following close behind. Ajuka was taking in every detail of this new environment he found himself in. I noticed him casting several minor spells to scan the surroundings.

"Thank you. Sorry for appearing like this. Keep up the good work." I opened another Hole, transporting us back to Cyvis's house.

A shocked shriek greeted me as I stepped into Cyvis's office. The elf hastily closed the book in front of her and stood, knocking over the chair she'd been sitting in as she hurried to wipe dust off of her green dress, falling into a curtsy.

She had a rather extensive list of criteria for that to be the case. Maybe she'd been thinking about this since she watched me contract Cyvis.

Mostly though, I had an idea for a character in my show that a tiefling would be perfect for." Serafall's eyes were gleaming, staring off into the distance at nothing in particular.

With recent events, she's had to reschedule again."

Frowning slightly, I returned my attention to a frustrated, pouting Serafall. "Sorry you're having to deal with all this."

Serafall shook her head. "It's not your fault. You're the source of many of my headaches, Bal, but not this one. So! Cyvis! Do you know any cute tiefling girls?"

Cyvis swallowed nervously, averting her gaze. "I cannot think of anyone off the top of my head, my lady. If you'd permit me some time to search, I'm certain I could find someone to your liking."

Failing that, I would be willing to contract someone if Serafall is unable to locate an individual that is to her liking."

Cyvis said, looking curiously at Ajuka, speaking hesitantly as if she was trying to figure out how to address him. "Perhaps if I knew what you were looking for?"

Cyvis's naturally pale skin turned a shade pale as the dead. She hastily fell back into her curtsy. "Please forgive the disrespect I have shown you, my lord."

Ajuka was already staring in the same direction, a small frown on his face.

If we were about to be attacked, I'd much rather her not end up dead from being in Serafall and Ajuka's proximity. Alaine's gaze was fixed on the ground as she knelt before Ajuka, completely disregarding everyone else. "My lord, it is an honor to be in your presence."

When Virexa noticed his attention on her, she immediately averted her gaze. "I would be honored, my lord."

If she wanted to cause problems, I imagine she could have just killed Vellia and Cyvis. I was more than a little anxious about the fact that an erinyes had been so close to my warlocks without them knowing. Cyvis and Vellia both grew in power following Maltherion's defeat, but I wasn't foolish enough to think they could take an erinyes that had the drop on them. 'I will speak to Shang Tsung.'

'Thank you.'

"I haven't met either of them personally, but from what I know, I wouldn't send any devil against Asmodeus except for Sirzechs Lucifer, and even then I wouldn't want Sirzechs to fight Asmodeus on his terms. Dispatar is probably more comparable to Loki or Hecate if a little weaker. He's a schemer and master mage that likes hoarding and collecting knowledge."

"I would like a female tiefling capable of using magic."

There is a section of the city dominated by a tiefling population. As I travelled here on my task, I witnessed many of the tieflings using magic. I would search there for your servant, my lady."

My eyebrows furrowed as I heard Virexa speak.

A mortal city in Avernus? Did Elturel already fall? I wasn't really paying attention to major events in the world because they didn't really affect me.

If Elturel is already in Hell, I might need to be proactive and go look for a chained up elder brain to kill it before it becomes a problem. The last thing I need is for Faerun to be dominated by a sea of mind flayers because the BG3 protagonists failed. It shouldn't be too hard to deal with the elder brain. A magic nuke could kill it, so a dozen tailed beast bombs should be able to handle it without issue.

But I could afford to wait a little while. I needed to sort out this situation with Helios first. At the end of the day, Faerun wasn't really my priority. I'd like to get ahead of any potential problems I might face in the world, but if all else failed, I could just grab my warlocks and bring them home. There were other worlds I could open mines in. The only people I really cared about in Faerun were Vellia and Cyvis. Everyone else could fend for themselves. They weren't my responsibility.

So long as you do not harm any devils or negatively interfere with our operations while you are there, you will have my lord's protection and permission."

A flaming parchment appeared in Virexa's hand. She laid the document on the ground and frantically scribbled hellish markings into the paper with a dark metal pen. She dramatically signed the bottom of the page and it vanished in a burst of orange flame. A moment later, a similar paper appeared in her hand.

Smiling, Virexa held it up, averting her eyes. "A writ of passage signed by my lord, my lady."

Matters back home require my immediate attention, but I will schedule a time to meet with your lord as soon as I am able."

The dark wings and flaming eyes faded until she once more appeared as a mortal woman in leather armor. She met Cyvis's eyes and gave my warlock a mocking salute. "I'm heading back out, boss!" she said in a deeper voice. "Call if you need me." With one final bow to Ajuka, Virexa – or was she Alaine now? – left the room.

'You're amazing. Thank you.'

I opened a Hole in the corner of the room. "If anything happens, go through that. It will take you to Vellia. Several members of my peerage are with her. They will keep you safe and be able to let me know if there is trouble."

Turning to Serafall, I said, "What about us? What are we doing now?"

Smiling, Serafall held up the flaming piece of paper in her hand. "Virexa went to the trouble of getting us a passport. It would be rude not to use it. Besides, I want my cute demon girl warlock, dammit!"

Smiling at her antics, I said, "Then I guess we're going to hell."

Serafall narrowed her eyes at me. "Boo. Bad joke. I've only heard it a thousand times."

Avernus was much like I expected it to be. Fire, brimstone, death – it did a good job of living up to the classical interpretation of what Hell should be. DXD's Hell was practically a paradise depending on where you ended up. Avernus looked like it would be miserable no matter where you lived.

It took a little scrying to figure out exactly where Avernus was in relation to the material plane, but once I found it it was just a matter of opening a Hole and now here we were. Further scrying showed us where Elturel was, but rather than opening a Hole and going there directly Serafall and Ajuka wanted to fly there.

Both Satans took in every detail of the Hell around them. Tall sharpened peaks of dark metal-like stone. Deep pits filled with tormented souls burning in hellfire. Twisted structures rising into fortifications every few miles. An endless expanse of blood-like rock that stretched in all directions.

Multiple times, devils of various shapes took flight and rose to intercept us. Whenever they came within a certain distance, they would immediately halt their approach, moving aside and bowing to us as we passed. Whatever Virexa was able to sense on me and later on Ajuka and Serafall, it was evident other devils could sense the same thing.

"It certainly takes you back, doesn't it?" Serafall said quietly as we flew.

"It does. I am pleased we have moved past this" Ajuka agreed, lips pulled into a solemn line.

"Our Hell used to look like this?" I asked carefully.

Serafall smiled sadly. "Not exactly, but it's close. There was more variety in color back home. Imagine hundreds of devils lying dead and you'll have a good picture of what the Civil War was like. It wasn't pretty."

"Doesn't sound like it. Can't say I'm unhappy I missed it." I said.

"You might very well live through something similar." Ajuka said plainly.

Frowning, I asked, "What do you mean?"

Watching me closely, Ajuka said, "You are young, yet you have already had a profound impact on our world. War with Olympus is not an impossibility now. In the chaos following that conflict, I expect certain other factions will make their move. The branch of devils still loyal to the Old Satans have been watching you. Mine and Serafall's agents have kept them at bay, but I imagine they will attempt to recruit or eliminate you soon."

"How likely is war with Olympus?" I asked.

"I'm working on it." Serafall said, eyes narrowed at Ajuka. With a sigh, she said, "But there's a reason I want to see if this warlock thing is repeatable. We need every advantage we can get right now."

"Is there anything I can do?" I asked.

"You're probably going to be playing taxi for me for a while." Serafall said seriously. "If this warlock thing works out, I'm going to need to meet with this Dispatar guy and try to work out a long term arrangement with him."

We flew in silence for a bit while I pondered our conversation.

I was confident my peerage could defend itself from most minor threats. If full war broke out with Olympus, we might very well have to fight gods. That was a daunting prospect, but Medea and I had been preparing for some time now. I was confident we'd be able to think of something. If not, I could always pick up everything and flee to some other world until the fighting died down. Considering nothing like this happened in canon DXD, it was likely mostly my fault relations were as bad as they were. I would like to help Hell fight off the Greeks, but I wouldn't risk my peerage's safety if I thought it was a losing battle.

"We've been flying for a while." Serafall said, pulling me from my thoughts.

"Have you not noticed?" Ajuka asked. "Distance is more of a suggestion than a concrete fact here. Space is expanding and shrinking as we move through it. We've passed the same fortress three times. Avernus has repositioned it to be in front of us each time. We have also been flying for longer than it seemed. Time is similarly flexible in this place."

"I hate spacial fuckery." Serafall sighed. "Bal? I've decided I don't want to fly anymore. Just bring us to the city please."

I opened a Hole, then frowned as I closed it. Closing my eyes, I scanned the location Elturel was in when we first entered Avernus. It was gone. Ajuka was right. Things were moving without showing any sign that they were moving. No wonder people went insane in Avernus.

Reaching out with scrying magic, it took me a little over a minute to find Elturel again. Opening another Hole, I led the Satans through the sky above Elturel.

Once pristine white walls surrounding the city were cracked and covered in demonic rot. Buildings held a red demonic stain. The city sat straddling a wide river flowing with dark, murky water. Few people roamed the streets. Most residents hid behind shuttered windows. No one wandered alone.

Bone-white, spindly creatures and living masses of iron chains wandered the street lazily, testing doors and frightening what few people were on the street away.

I wasn't sure how long Elturel had been in Avernus. Devils were openly walking on the street. That either meant the city had just arrived and hadn't managed to organize itself yet or it had been here so long people had given up trying to keep their city free of devils. Either way, it wasn't my problem. I came here for a specific purpose.

Ajuka and I followed Serafall as she descended to the ground. A nude, masculine devil with sandy skin turned as we descended. Lips pulled back to reveal snarling sharpened teeth. A clawed hand tightly gripped a long spear. The devil started as we came closer, hastily falling to a knee, his wings laid flat on the ground at his sides. Curled horns scraped the ground as he hastily averted his eyes.

"How may I serve you, my lady?" the devil said in a gravelly voice.

Serafall's wings disappeared. She walked forward and assessed the devil knelt before her. "I was told there is a section of this city inhabited by tieflings."

"There is, my lady." the devil said. "It would be my honor to lead you there." The devil rose, keeping his gaze fixed on the ground. He turned and led the way down a cobbled road.

As we walked through the city, humans and a smattering of other races – elves, dwarves, halflings – turned and fled when they saw us. What few devils we passed immediately vacated our path and bowed as we passed.

The immediate subservience of the devils, creatures known for twisted dealings and cruelty, made me a touch uncomfortable. Seeing such horrifying creatures submit to me without a moment's hesitation was strange. I'd tell myself it was Ajuka that terrified them, which was likely part of it, but Virexa, a powerful erinyes, had immediately knelt before me the moment she met me when I was on my own. The devils were able to recognize something in me that made them step carefully around me. That was good for dealing with devils, but they likely weren't the only ones who would be able to sense whatever it was that clued them in to who and what I was. I'd need to work with Medea to create some kind of illusion to cover myself once I was done here. I'd like to be able to move around Faerun in anonymity if at all possible.

"This is the section of the city inhabited by the tieflings, my lady." our devil guide said, turning and bowing his head to Serafall. "Is there any other way I can assist you?"

"No. Thank you for your help." Serafall said.

"It was my honor, my lady. With your leave…" The devil slowly backed away, quickly turning a corner and disappearing from view.

Looking around, the street was nearly identical to the rest of the city. Tainted walls and cracked roofs surrounded us. Maybe this part of the city once looked different when Elturel was still in the material place, but in Avernus, it was hard to tell anything apart.

"Where do you want to start? It might be difficult to find a spell caster." I asked. The streets before us were empty. The tieflings were likely hiding inside like so many other residents of the city.

Frowning, Serafall slowly began to walk forward, focused on something I couldn't see. "I can feel… There's someone very interesting here."

An explosion sounded from our right, followed closely by panicked screams and screeching devils. Metal clashed. Someone was fighting.

Ajuka and I looked off towards the commotion. Serafall's attention remains fixed ahead of her.

"Do you think that's a problem?" I asked.

"It is unlikely to be a threat to us." Ajuka said. "I will monitor the situation from here. If it grows to be a problem, I will deal with it."

"Respectfully, I'd worry for the surrounding city if you went over there and got dragged into a fight." I said. "I can check it out quickly and pop right back. If it's something we need to worry about, we'll deal with it. Otherwise, the local devils can worry about it."

"Call me if you need help, Bal." Serafall said, distracted. "I'm going to see if I can figure out what I'm sensing." Serafall started walking down the street, focused on something I couldn't feel.

Ajuka looked at me for a moment before nodding. "I will be standing by in case you require assistance. Be careful. You are the only one capable of transporting us home."

"Don't worry. I have no intention of biting off more than I can chew. I'll see you in a minute." I stepped back through a Hole. My wings caught me as I hovered in mid air, observing the city below me.

There was commotion a fair distance from where I left Ajuka and Serafall. The dark river that ran through the city had become ground zero for a massive melee. A small group of devils was being overwhelmed by a group of lumbering demons that seemingly appeared from nowhere, flooding over the bank of the river like an unholy flood. On the river itself sat an elegant boat. The boat was too small to have transported the demons. Only a single individual sat on the boat, lazily standing and stepping ashore.

The figure was feminine, but she was clearly inhumane. Horns curled up from her head. Dark spines stuck out of her arms and legs and jutted from her spine. A thin tail curled around her to stab a sharpened stinger through a devil charging towards her. Clawed toes clicked against the stone as she stepped off the boat, nude save for a cloth hanging loosely from her waist.

As she surveyed the area around her, the devils began to retreat, disengaging from the demons and retreating between the buildings.

With a flick of her wrist, reality tore apart. Massive, furred hands gripped the distortion in space, ripping it apart. A lumbering demon spilled into the city, followed closely by many others.

I frowned, eyebrows furrowed as I looked at the distortion. This bitch stole my trick.

Pushing my irritation away, I slowly descended towards her. "Could I ask that you refrain from whatever you're doing for another twenty minutes? It's rather distracting."

The woman turned to look up. Amber eyes narrowed as she saw me approaching. Her lips pulled up into a wide grin, showing off sharpened teeth.

"Now you seem fun." she said, ignoring the slobbering demons milling about around her knees. "I was promised there would be interesting toys here, yet all I've seen so far are weak little peons. You'll make a delicious pet."

I blinked, unimpressed. "I'll have to decline your offer. I'm in a committed relationship. Please stop blowing things up if you would be so kind."

The woman threw her head back and laughed, an unnatural screeching sound. "Oh, darling, you don't have a choice." She raised her hand to point at me. Immediately, the demons around her flew into a frenzy. Those with wings took to the sky, flapping furiously towards me. Those locked on the ground lumbered as close as they could, snapping up at me ineffectually.

I was originally planning to leave after asking her to give Serafall some more time to herself. I wasn't feeling so generous anymore. I had no interest in being this creature's pet. The fact she seemed so happy about forcing me into such a position had frankly pissed me off.

Holes opened all around me. In the sky. Near the ground. Around the woman and the tear in reality at her side.

The pained screech of dying demons filled the air as the city was bathed in elemental fire. The fire parted. I drifted to the side to avoid an orb of dark, demonic energy hurled upward from the ground.

The woman burst out of the fire, eyes manic, snarling at me as she hurled more magical orbs up towards me. She was clearly affected by my fire, but she wasn't destroyed immediately like the lesser demons were. Either she was much stronger than they were, or she had special defenses against fire.

My Holes closed, cutting off the torrent of fire. Several others opened as I erected a shield to absorb the woman's attacks.

The woman screamed, falling to the ground in a heap as four magical spears fired out of Holes behind her and drove through her back. I was surprised when she managed to struggle up to a knee, glaring hatefully at me despite the enchanted spears driven through her body. She was stronger than I thought.

She raised a hand to launch another orb at me. Her hand was slammed to the ground, pinned by a magical spear as another Hole opened right next to her.

She screamed, enraged as more spears and daggers impaled her, pinning her to the ground.

I held up a hand, intending to open another Hole over her head and end this.

"My lord!"

My eyes flicked to the side, following the voice. A writhing mass of chains with flaming eyes and dark cloth held in the facsimile of a bipedal frame looked up at me desperately.

"My lord, the arch-duchess wants this one alive. Allow us to secure her!" the devil called up, sounding meek.

I lowered my hand. "Be my guest."

The figure bowed. "Thank you, my lord. Secure her!"

More masses of chain joined the first. Together, they approached the weakened, struggling demon woman. She lashed out as they approached, but there were dozens of them. Chains lashed out from the devils, winding around the demon's arms, legs, chest and neck. The demon thrashed, screeching in rage, but there were too many chains pulling her apart. She was forced to the ground and quickly bound by the devils.

Seeing they had things well in hand, I drifted back through a Hole to rejoin Ajuka and Serafall. The Satans weren't where I left them. I turned in the direction Serafall had been so focused on and began walking. It didn't take long before I caught up to the Satans.

"What happened?" Ajuka asked as I joined him at the threshold of a small home, eyes still aimed into the house.

"Some demons got into the city. The situation is handled now." I said simply, following his gaze.

The house was really more of a shack. Wooden walls with a caved in roof. A single room with half-destroyed shelves and a barrel in the corner.

Serafall was inside, kneeling over a prone form.

It was a tiefling. Her skin was white like snow. I'd never heard of a white tiefling before. Weren't they supposed to all be shades of red?

Clothed in torn rags and covered in blood, she looked to be in rough shape. Many cuts along her arms and legs ended at gatherings of ivory scales growing out of her flesh. The scales looked like they'd protected her from whatever had cut her up. They were likely the only reason the tiefling was still breathing. She was unconscious, completely at the mercy of whoever might come through the door of her ragged shelter.

"She's hurt really bad." Serafall said, running a hand over the woman's forehead, gently parting her pale hair around the blue icy blue horns jutting out of her forehead.

"There are likely others." Ajuka said.

Serafall frowned. "No. I want her. There's something about her that's calling to me. I can't tell what, but…"

"It is possible there is something we do not understand at work here attempting to trap you." Ajuka said softly.

Serafall shook her head. "I don't think so. I can't explain it. I just…"

"Can I look her over?" I asked, stepping up next to Serafall.

Serafall shifted to the side, making space for me to join her.

Carefully, I ran a hand over the ivory scales on her forearm. They felt like Coal's.

"Dragon scales." I said quietly.

"What?" Serafall said, confused.

Pursing my lips, I looked at the tiefling in a new light. "Some people born in this world have traces of their ancestry manifest. Apparently, someone in her family tree got busy with a dragon. A white dragon by the looks of it. That explains the scales, the white skin, and maybe even why you felt something from her. Did it feel like ice?"

Serafall looked at me curiously. "Like winter."

I nodded. "White dragons in this world have powers over ice. She probably inherited a piece of her ancestor's magic." I wasn't expecting to stumble across a draconic sorcerer on this trip, but I guess anything can happen.

"We need to get her home. I have people there who can help her." Serafall said, already moving to lift the girl up.

"We will likely not be able to test your ability to create a warlock if we bring her back to our Hell." Ajuka said from behind us.

I held up a hand to stop Serafall, kneeling down at the tiefling woman's side. A Hole dropped several small vials onto the ground at my side. I pulled the stoppers off and carefully poured the contents over the woman's wounds, tilting her head back to pour the last one down her throat.

"Medea can't make Phenex Tears, but she and Shang Tsung have worked out some tricks of their own." I explained.

The tiefling's eyes shot open. Cold blue eyes met mine. Her arms rose to shove me away. She fell backwards, weakly coughing as she tried to crawl away.

"It's okay." Serafall said, comfortingly, holding up her hands placatingly.

"Please… Don't…" the tiefling said weakly.

"We're not going to hurt you." Serafall said gently, holding a hand down to the tiefling.

The tiefling looked at the hand suspiciously for several seconds before slowly taking it.

Serafall helped her up into a sitting position with her back against the wall, then sat down in front of her.

"What's your name?" Serafall asked.

The tiefling looked between us suspiciously. "Seraphine." she said quietly.

Serafall beamed at her. "My name's Serafall. We're both Sera! Isn't that great?"

"What do you want?" Seraphine asked, a slight tremor in her limbs. I couldn't tell if it was from fear or injury.

Serafall frowned. "What do you want, Seraphine?"

Seraphine let out a sound that was half laugh half sob. "I want to leave. Everyone is dead. The longer we stay here, the more people die. I don't want to be here anymore. I don't want to die."

Serafall frowned, laying a comforting hand atop Seraphine's own. Seraphine flinched. When Serafall didn't hurt her, the tiefling relaxed, looking up at Serafall with confusion.

"Do you want to go home?" Serafall asked.

Seraphine's features twisted in pain and fury. "This is my home. I never want to see it ever again. The devils and demons should have been the worst of it. They weren't the ones who tried to take advantage of me."

Serafall's expression darkened for a brief moment before her soft, encouraging smile returned. It was a rapid change. I caught it because I've gotten to know her pretty well. I doubt the tiefling caught it.

"What if I told you I could take you away from here?" Serafall asked softly.

Seraphine frowned, looking between Serafall, Ajuka and I. "You're not humans, are you?"

Serafall nodded slowly. "I'm a devil, Seraphine."

Seraphine's breathing picked up. She looked deathly afraid, but she didn't make any moves to escape. She was stuck in a broken down shack with three devils. She likely thought it would be stupid to try to run. "What do you want with me?"

"Do you know what a warlock is?" Serafall asked.

Seraphine froze, no longer breathing. After a moment, she said, "One of the men who attacked me was a warlock. The devils have been picking people they think are interesting and making contracts with them since we got here."

"I'm not like those devils." Serafall said, a hint of rage in her voice. "I'll treat you well. I'll take you home with me, a place far away from here where you can start a new life."

"Why… Why did you pick me? There has to be a reason." Seraphine said, looking between us suspiciously.

Slowly, Serafall raised her hand. A ball of ice appeared between her fingers. Fractals fell away from the sphere in shavings. An icy sculpture of a smiling Serafall standing hand-in-hand with a tiefling sat in Serafall's hand. "I felt your power. I think we'd compliment each other well." Serafall said.

Hesitantly, Seraphine reached out and took the sculpture from Serafall, turning it over in her hands, icy eyes intently focused on the small statue. "Will you take my soul?" Seraphine asked with a trembling voice.

"No." Serafall denied instantly. "I'll make you strong and give you a home. Your end of the bargain is to help me out when I need it. I won't treat you like the devils here treat their warlocks."

Seraphine was still looking at the statue. She closed her fist around it protectively and held it to her chest. "I was lucky to get away last time. I'm alone. I'll die if I stay here. Or worse." Looking up at Serafall, Seraphine said, "Will you abuse me?"

"Never." Serafall said, iron in her voice.

Seraphine swallowed. She took a deep breath and nodded. "Okay. As long as you get me out of here and protect me, I'll serve you."

"Ajuka," Serafall said, already pulling a piece of paper out of nowhere.

Ajuka was at her side in an instant. The two spoke in hushed tones as they worked out a simple contract and scribbled it onto the paper.

Serafall held the paper out to the tiefling. "Take as long as you need to read this."

Seraphine took the paper with trembling hands and slowly looked down at the page to read it. After several minutes, she shook her head, looking up at Serafall. "What are you hiding? No devil would be this generous."

"I'm not hiding anything from you, Seraphine. I swear it." Serafall said. "I want a friend, not a slave."

Seraphine looked back down at the paper, reading over it again.

"Fine." she said at last. "I'll deal with the hidden clauses when they come up. I won't be able to last long here with those bastards hunting for me. Give me a quill."

Serafall pursed her lips like she wanted to say something, but she held her silence, wordlessly holding out a pen for the tiefling.

Seraphine snatched the pen from Serafall and hastily scribbled her name onto the paper, like she was trying to get it over with before she could have any second thoughts. She dramatically dropped the pen, visibly bracing herself.

Nothing happened.

Slowly, Seraphine's tense muscles started to relax. "Is that it?"

Ajuka was frowning. "Is this how it worked last time?"

"No," Serafall said, eyebrows furrowed in confusion. "There was a light show and everything."

Wracking my brain, I said, "This happened both with Vellia and Cyvis. After signing the contract, I gave Vellia a sword and Medea gave Cyvis a familiar. Maybe that's what's missing?"

Serafall's eyebrows furrowed. She smiled brightly at Seraphine. Holding up her hand, a beautiful crown of ice with sharp gleaming crests like daggers extending up from it appeared in her hand. Serafall carefully set the crown on Seraphine's head. It nestled perfectly between her horns, tailor made for her.

"There!" Serafall said. "Now you can be a real ice princess!"

Seraphine opened her mouth to reply. Whatever she was going to say was forgotten as a scream tore free from her lips.

Atop Seraphine's head, the icy crown glowed a brilliant blue with vibrant power. Dark demonic lines dripped down from the crown across Seraphine's forehead like ink dripping off a canvas. The demonic markings burned blue, searing into Seraphine's forehead in the shape of an inverted crown, mirroring the one she wore on her head.

The contract in Seraphine's hand lit on fire. Seraphine's scream raised an octave. A flash of white was the only warning I had. I was barely able to summon a barrier in front of myself as a veritable blizzard of ice erupted from Seraphine.

The walls, the roof, the shelves, the floor – everything but Seraphine and the devils around her was frozen solid.

Seraphine was panting, looking around with wide, frantic eyes. She stared down at her hands in awe. "I feel… I feel…"

"Good?" Serafall said, lips pulled up into a grin.

Seraphine swallowed, looking up at Serafall. "Better than good. I feel as strong as a blizzard."

"I'm glad. What do you say to a tour of your new home, Seraphine?" Serafall held a hand down to her warlock. Behind her, Ajuka hastily scribbled notes into a small journal and cast several spells into the air to analyze every facet of what he'd just witnessed.

Seraphine swallowed heavily. Hesitant, she reached out and took Serafall's hand, looking at the Satan in awe. "I'll follow wherever you lead me, my lady."
