#8,210
Zekram Bael believed himself to be untouchable. Helios was proving the devil nothing more than an arrogant child pretending to be far more than he was. The weak peons of the supernatural feared Zekram's power. Zekram lorded his Power of Destruction over them to force them to comply with his demands. The moment an adversary appeared capable of surpassing the devil's power, Zekram hid like a coward.

Staring over the wreckage of another building in the mortal world, this time a manufacturing plant Zekram used as a front for spying on the local population that worshiped the Egyptian pantheon, Helios frowned. The Sun had worked his way through the most important of Zekram's holdings in the United States. Once there was nothing left but rubble and the corpses of weak devils pining for Zekram Bael's attention and favor, Helios moved on to Africa. He had made substantial progress, but it wasn't enough.

Was Zekram truly so cowardly? Helios had not sent underlings to work on his behalf. At every building, every farm, every location Zekram owned, the Sun arrived personally to eliminate the workers and dismantle the structures Zekram had paid great sums to erect. Yet, Helios remained unchallenged.

Many of the devils he slew while exacting his vengeance against Zekram had valiantly defended themselves to their last breath, but it was hopeless when they faced the Sun itself. The Sallos heir stuck out in Helios's mind. The Sun knew not why the boy worked in one of Zekram's buildings in New York, but the boy had impressed Helios enough to remember his name. He honored the boy's sacrifice by allowing several of the other devils to escape the just fury of the Sun.

Zekram's servants fought for their lives even when faced with the might of a Titan. Where was Zekram himself? Helios's intent in striking at Zekram's holdings was to lure the old devil out so they might settle their grievance. Zekram did not emerge to shield those beneath him. Zekram did not so much as order his direct underlings to act in his stead. The coward stayed sheltered behind the wards of his castle, dining gluttonously on Helios's prized cattle.

The Sun was not one to slaughter without reason. Clearly, his efforts in the mortal world did not matter to Zekram. He would cease his attacks in the mortal world and strike where Zekram would be forced to intervene.

Zekram stole Helios's beautiful daughters. Zekram struck them in their home, a peaceful paradise now gone. Zekram destroyed their home. Perhaps Helios had been foolish to think Zekram would care about anything beyond his sight.

Helios would strike Zekram where the devil would have no choice but to respond.


X


Zekram Bael's eyes narrowed in displeasure. "Do not think to issue orders to me, Sirzechs."

Sirzechs Lucifer did not flinch as he weathered the furious gaze of his grandfather. "I am Lucifer, Zekram, Satan of Domestic Affairs. If the actions of those residing within Hell risk the safety of Hell, it is my duty to step in."

Zekram angrily set his glass of wine aside, finally standing from his cushioned chair to stand even with Sirzechs. "That lightbulb is costing me far too much for me not to respond. If the destruction of his island was not enough of a message, I will take something he will actually miss."

"You will plunge devilkind into war." Falbium Asmodeus interjected, lips pulled into a hard line. The Satan of Military Affairs had been silent until now, letting Sirzechs take the lead in this meeting with his grandfather. Still, Falbium seemed to be more irritated than Sirzechs.

Zekram found it insulting.

Zekram waved away Falbium's concern. "The Greeks have cut Helios loose. Actions taken against him will not be viewed as–"

"Zekram."

Zekram paused, raising an appraising eyebrow as destructive power drifted off of Sirzechs' shoulders. Lucifer's eyes were glowing with furious power.

"Destroying Thrinacia enraged the Greeks." Sirzechs said, his words reverberating slightly, colored by Sirzechs' terrifying power. "Serafall has produced a miracle keeping them from retaliating in any noticeable way. Fueling the fire you started will pull us into war. Do you understand the implications of what you have set in motion? Will you step onto the field as some of the strongest gods in the supernatural descend to invade the Underworld. If we are able to overcome the Greeks, do you really think our other enemies will stand by and allow us to regain our strength? Heaven will descend upon us. The Grigori will take advantage of the chaos to attempt to eliminate us both. The Shinto will see an opportunity to finally be rid of the Abrahamic factions."

Zekram shook his head, sighing. His grandson was powerful, there was no denying that, but the boy always did have difficulty seeing the bigger picture. "Even if war breaks out with the Greeks, we will overcome them. The faction is split, far more than what is visible on the surface. The Olympians attempted to stoke the fury of the greater pantheon, further subjugating those beneath them. If Olympus is foolish enough to strike at us, they will face us alone. Few minor gods, so few as to be inconsequential, will join them."

Sirzechs had yet to blink. He stared impassively at Zekram. "My point stands, Zekram. Will you leave the protections of your castle to stop Ares from rampaging through Lucifaad? Or will you remain here, growing fat on cattle you stole from a Titan while Athena tears her way through the lower Pillars?"

Zekram's eyes narrowed. "Careful, Sirzechs. Your relation to me will only allow you to insult me so much."

Falbium stepped in front of Sirzechs, pulling Zekram's attention to himself. "Your private affairs are your own, Zekram, but you will not act in a way that puts our people at risk. Remain here. Do not respond to Helios's attacks. Serafall will get you compensation as part of her dealings with Athena."

Zekram made a considering sound. "And if Serafall is incapable of preventing a war?"

"Then I will see you on the field at my side, ancestor." Sirzechs said mockingly.

Zekram considered the benefits of rising to the taunt, ultimately allowing Sirzechs this one last jab. "It has been a pleasure as always to see you, my boy. Do visit more often. An old man's greatest pleasure is seeing his descendants thriving." Zekram said dismissively.

Shooting Zekram one last glare, Sirzechs spun around, Falbium close behind him.

Zekram sighed as the Satans left, falling heavily back into his chair.

Despite the front he put up before his grandson, Zekram truly did respect the boy. Sirzechs was living proof that the Bael bloodline was superior to all others. Alongside his fellow Satans, Sirzechs had ruled well, albeit with many mistakes. Those could be forgiven as a byproduct of Sirzechs' youth. He was still learning.

It filled Zekram with pride to see his spawn dominating those around them with their strength. Even if certain members of his family were complete and utter disappointments.

If only Sirzechs had been the inheritor of his Clan instead of 'Lord' Bael. The world would not have forgotten their fear of the Bael family. Their Clan would not have suffered embarrassment after embarrassment as Lord Bael's many mistakes and childish antics came to light.

Zekram understood that devils must, from time to time, engage in sin. It was their nature, best embraced rather than resisted. However, one must still maintain their decorum. Lord Bael slept the days away. He spent nights drunk and feasting on delicacies paid for with the Bael fortune. He whored his way through Hell with abandon.

Until now, Zekram had been under the assumption Lord Bael's indiscretions had not borne fruit. The agents he sent to observe the women his spawn had bedded all reported that nothing came of the trysts.

Why then, did Balthazar Abaddon manage to find a young woman capable of using his prized Power of Destruction?

The moment Zekram witnessed the girl call up his power in the middle of the Rating Game, Zekram set his agents uncovering any and all information known about her.

From what they were able to piece together from when the girl appeared in Aqua's company, she had not been with Balthazar for long. There was no indication of where she came from, but some sources indicated she was likely a vampire prior to her reincarnation.

This one fact spared Lord Bael from Zekram's wrath.

If the girl truly was a vampire, it was possible that any of his spawn may have sired the girl over his long existence. Several of his descendants were dead, having fallen in one of the many wars devilkind was subjected to. It was possible one of them had the girl and fell before informing him.

If that was the case, why did she not reach out to him? Was she afraid of his reaction? Did she believe he was so wasteful as to eliminate a bastard child of the Bael family? Perhaps that was why she finally surfaced in Balthazar's Peerage. She likely saw his rising power as shelter from Zekram's reach.

She would be wrong of course, but she was also foolish to think he would have her eliminated purely for unorthodox origins. Power was king. She possessed a Power greater than any in the world in the form of his bloodline trait. He would have welcomed her if only she had revealed herself to him. Ajuka Beelzebub's Evil PIeces were marvelous. A single piece would have been enough to correct her impure bloodline, as was now the case where she resided in Balthazar's peerage.

It didn't matter. Zekram was aware of her now. As he watched Balthazar, he would watch Keno. Whether the girl was aware of it or not, she was in a prime position to further herself immensely.

Rumors were circulating that Balthazar was engaged to Medea, offering her the position of Lady Abaddon. While a pureblood devil would have been a more attractive selection for Lady of such a powerful house, Zekram could not deny that Medea would fit the role well.

That did not mean that Balthazar would not take a mistress or two. Zekram would reach out to Keno to begin to form a relationship with the girl that should have been present since her birth. After establishing good rapport with her, he would begin to subtly remark on the advantages of the Bael blood lines mixing with that of the Abaadons. Zekram had already managed to spread his progeny through the Gremory and Vapulas. The Abbadons were merely the next step. With so few Abaddons left, it was paramount to preserve the bloodline before any misfortune could befall them, weakening all devilkind with their loss.

Yes, Zekram was a forward thinker. He knew how to make plans that stretched across millenia. Sirzechs still had much to learn. The boy had done well, but he needed to continue growing if he wanted to retain his title as Lucifer.

Zekram took a sip of his wine, unable to banish the frown on his face.

Being ordered to remain still by his descendant had irritated Zekram. The Great King had no great plans to strike against the Greeks any further. His quarrel was with Helios. As far as he was concerned, that score was settled with the destruction of Thrinacia.

Then the foolish Titan started killing Zekram's underlings.

Zekram could not be open in his response to Helios's foolishness, but he must respond. Zekram would lose the loyalty of Lord Sallos and many other pillar lords if the Sallos heir was not avenged.

Zekram needed to contact Lords Gamigin and Naberius. Helios wanted to strike at Zekram and his followers? Zekram would see how long the Titan's will could weather watching his daughters suffer for his actions.


X


"Why couldn't you keep the foolish child in line?" Athena demanded through grit teeth, glaring across the table.

Serafall's eyes narrowed. Her hands balled into fists under the table. "Forgive me, Athena. Last I checked, it was Helios slaughtering my people. What on Earth could you possibly be mad about?"

Athena's balled fist rose to slam back down into the table. Athena stopped herself, closing her eyes and taking a deep breath before resting her hand on the table gently. "I would have been able to help you Serafall. I want to help you. I don't want war with Hell any more than you want Olympus invading your home."

"Then help me appease the Pillar lords calling for Greek blood after one of their heirs was slaughtered in the mortal world." Serafall said, unblinking, her expression deadly serious.

Athena shook her head. "My father won't allow any concessions. He'll accept nothing but a minor apology. It took everything I had to even get him to agree to that."

"Saying sorry for murdering a Pillar Heir will do nothing to mend the rift between us." Serafall said coldly.

Athena's hand tightened back into a fist. "Then maybe you should have prevented Balthazar Abaddon from reincarnating Achilles. The brat took a legacy of Zeus as his servant; his devil servant. I haven't seen my father this insulted in a mortal age."

"He needs to get over it." Serafall said bluntly. "His pride must not prevent him from stopping a war."

Athena paused, fixing Serafall with a serious look. "Do you truly want to keep the peace between our people?"

"I wouldn't be here if I wanted to fight you Athena." Serafall said, irritated.

"Then give us Balthazar."

The temperature in the room dropped ten degrees. Serafall sat stock-still, hair drifting away from her shoulders as she glared with murderous intent at Athena. "What."

"I need to appease my father before he will help me make amends for Helios's attacks. As far as he is concerned, we have already cut Helios loose and as such are not at fault for his actions. He doesn't understand the perspective of Hell, that one of their own was just murdered by a Greek Titan. He doesn't understand that whether Helios was acting in our interest or not, others will still blame us for his crimes."

"I fail to see how surrendering a Viscount of Hell to Olympus will solve any problems." Serafall said, her voice carrying a dangerous chill.

"Medea was a slight. Coal was an irritation. Achilles is a personal insult to my father. Rumors have surfaced that Idyia, thought to be dead for hundreds of years, is now living in Balthazar's lands, not even deigning to inform us of her current whereabouts. Another insult to my father. Others will see his subjects leaving his care as weakness. He will not be able to see this issue in a rational light until the focus of his rage is removed."

"'Removed'. You want me to give you Balthazar so Zeus can kill him." The temperature in the room dropped another ten degrees. Frost gathered on the table, creeping up the walls around them, the room becoming colored by an icy blue hue.

"No," Athena denied, eyes pleading. "He'll work off his debt to Olympus with us for ten years. The items he sells will fill our armories. My father will be appeased and I'll be able to help you. We both know where this is going if we don't take immediate action to prevent the worst outcome."

"Let me summarize your position." Serafall said, voice devoid of emotion. "Helios slaughters twenty-seven devils, one of whom is a Pillar Heir, and hundreds of mortals whose only crime was working in a devil's employ, most even ignorant of the fact that they worked for a devil. Your solution to fixing this problem is for Hell to surrender one of its lords to Olympus to appease Zeus to the point he is willing to offer a meager apology. Would you say this is an accurate summarization?"

"Serafall, please," Athena said. "I swear to you, I will do everything in my power to make this right. I cannot do anything to help you while my father is ordering no compensation of any kind is to be paid to the devils."

"This was a waste of both our time." Serafall said, her voice carrying the frigid bite of winter. Serafall stood from her chair, turning her attention to the room's third occupant who had silently observed their conversation. "Thank you for hosting this meeting, Odin. I apologize for my outburst and the frost I have scarred your beautiful room with."

The elderly, one-eyed man shook his head. "I am not insulted by your reaction, Serafall. I am insulted that only one party came to this meeting of peace with any intentions to actually resolve this issue peacefully."

Athena stood, fists clenched tight as she leaned into the table. Ignoring Odin, she looked at Serafall with beseeching eyes. "Serafall, I swear on my domains, I will do everything in my power to–"

"Enough, Athena." Serafall cut her off, eyes glowing a dangerous, frigid blue. "I will do what I can to appease the devils calling for blood. If any further actions are taken against us, I will not be able to justify a position of inaction. Do not so much as allow a nymph to seduce a devil."

"Sera–"

"This meeting is over." Serafall cut Athena off, glaring daggers at her, daring the goddess to contradict her.

Athena sighed. "I'll do what I can. You should have trusted me." A golden flash enveloped her form and she was gone.

Slowly, the temperature in the room started to rise. Frost receded as Serafall took a deep breath to reign in her power.

Athena suggesting that Hell offer compensation for actions taken against Hell had enraged Serafall. Demanding that Serafall turn over Balthazar had turned her murderous. It took every ounce of control Serafall had not to strike at the arrogant, stupid bitch the moment she began outlining her moronic plan.

Serafall wouldn't have turned over any Devil lord to Olympus but Athena trying to take Balthazar?

Serafall would rather go to war with the Greeks than risk losing Balthazar. Athena had no idea what she was asking Serafall to part with.

"I expect things will get rather exciting in the coming days." Odin said, standing up from his chair, leaning on his staff as he stretched his back.

Serafall nodded in agreement. "I assume they will."

Odin chuckled softly. "For a moment there, I assumed Athena was smarter than I gave her credit for, then she kept talking and I realized she was somehow less intelligent than I initially assumed."

Serafall's eyebrows furrowed in confusion. "What do you mean?"

Odin watched her carefully, scratching his beard with the hand not holding his staff. "We have been buying raw materials from Balthazar's company for some time now. It's no boast to say we have some of the greatest craftsmen in the world working for us. Brok and Sindri have told me of their very interesting suspicions regarding those materials."

"I'm not sure what you're insinuating." Serafall said carefully.

Odin grinned. "Something about it being impossible for some of the materials to have been produced in our world. I don't understand the specifics myself, but I trust the experts. What a strange discovery, wouldn't you say?"

"I'm not sure I understand." Serafall said, confusion evident on her face. "Not produced in our world? What do you mean?"

Odin chuckled. "You're an exceptional actress, Serafall. Sometimes I wonder if you use the overacting on your show to fool people into thinking you can't spin a tale with the best of them. Anyone else would buy your confusion. Not me." Odin gently tapped the eye-patch he wore. "I gave up far too much for my insight to be fooled."

Odin's grin faded, expression turning serious. "A monstrous cat of flame never seen. A moth the size of a city with no records of its existence. Aqua, Medea, Shang Tsung, Irene, Shiroe, even Achilles and Coal – those you can explain away. Mothra and Matatabi? Maybe one of them could be excused. Both? It doesn't fit."

"I'm not sure what you're insinuating." Serafall said, staring at Odin seriously, trying to figure out what his game was.

Odin shrugged. "Nothing. Nothing save this: Asgard has benefited immensely from its dealings with yourself and Balthazar Abaddon. We would not stand by if such a valuable resource came under threat. I'm sure you can understand that, yes?"

Serafall was speechless, watching Odin for any sign of deception as she slowly nodded.

Nodding to himself, Odin said, "I was happy to host this meeting for you, but I'm afraid I must ask you to leave. There are things I must do today."

"Thank you for hosting the meeting, Odin." Serafall said.

"It was my pleasure. Wars between pantheons aren't good for anyone. I hope things work out for the best. Farewell, Serafall."

Serafall vanished in a flash of icy blue light.

"You're back!"

Looking up, Serafall couldn't help but smile as Ingvild charged towards her and launched into a tackle hug.

Serafall easily caught her, laughing as she lifted the smaller girl up.

"How'd it go?" Mami asked. She was sitting with Seraphine and a round table. Both had a book open, left forgotten on the table as they closely watched Serafall.

Serafall's words caught in her throat as she looked at Seraphine. The innocent hope in the girl's eyes nearly broke her.

"I… I'm sorry, Seraphine. I might have pulled you into a war." Serafall said, regretful.

Seraphine pushed her book away, standing and walking up to Serafall. "You pulled me out of certain death and gave me a new home, one I'm actually willing to fight for. Don't ever apologize for that."

Serafall smiled softly, shifting Ingvild to the side so she could pull her warlock into a crushing hug. Mami dashed across the floor, leaping into the hug and knocking everyone over, turning it into a cuddle pile.

Serafall laughed, holding her peerage and warlock close. Serafall would burn Olympus to the ground before she let anything hurt her family.


X


Amber hair billowed in a gentle current. Skin like ambrosia sparkled. Beams of light cut through the water to illuminate a feminine form. She floated alone, no fish or coral in sight. A lone shape in the infinite expanse of the deep.

She cradled a small mirror in her hand, eyes fixed on the image displayed in its face – a man in bronze armor smiling triumphantly as he held his spearpoint to the throat of a pale, snake-like woman moments before the two were swallowed by brilliant silver light.

The woman swiped against the mirror's surface, sending the image back, magnifying the man's face.

Delicate fingers traced the edge of his jaw as her eyes hungrily drank in the sight of him.

"My sweet boy." the woman said softly, voice twinged with heartbreak.

Thetis, Leader of the Nereids, Daughter of Nereus, minor Goddess of the Seas beheld the face of her son for the first time in thousands of years, unable to look away.

Achilles looked the same as he did the last time she'd seen him, that tragic day where he departed for Troy and his destiny beyond. Thetis had watched him go, unable to follow despite how desperately she wished to.

She never saw her son again.

Until now.

A thousand questions whirred through her mind. How did he become a devil? Where had Balthazar Abaddon found him? Was he happy? Was he eating well?

Thetis was overwhelmed by a sea of emotions warring within her. She only knew one thing for certain.

She needed to see her son.

Rumors had been circulating for some time among those who dwelled in the sea. Idyia, thought lost for millenia, had supposedly resurfaced, taking up residence in Hell to be near her long-lost daughter. Thetis hadn't believed the rumors. They sounded too fanciful.

She was willing to explore any possible avenue if it meant seeing her son again.

The mirror in her hand shimmered as Thetis reached out through the sea. The face of the mirror rippled like a disturbed pond, slowly settling as the face of a woman she thought she would never see again came into focus.

"Thetis." Idyia's far-away voice greeted her.

"I need to see my son." Thetis said. Catching up with the Knowing Goddess could wait until her boy was in her arms once more.

Idyia smiled softly. "I've been expecting you to reach out. Remain where you are. I will be there shortly."

Idyia's face faded from the mirror in Thetis's hands. Immediately, she brought Achilles's picture back, staring longingly at the visage of her smiling son.

Her son. She was going to hold her son again.


X


Reincarnation was a strange thing.

A man with dark hair pondered his existence as he sat alone at a bar, slowly nursing a glass of wine. The bartender had given him a strange look when he ordered wine to drink alone, but old habits died hard. His tastes from before followed him to his life now.

Was his first life a dream? It felt so far away, but when he'd lived it it felt so real, somehow more real than the life he lived now. How could it not? Great adventures. Fierce battles. Epic rivalries. The truest of friends.

What did he have now? Nothing that mattered. He was alone. A piece of his past was all he had left to convince himself he really was who he thought he was. Of course, it couldn't have been a part he rejoiced in remembering. No. The herald of his end had followed him here.

His first life had been good. He'd enjoyed that life. He was trying to enjoy this one too, but he was too restless. There were no great battles like before.

Well, that wasn't true. The church had already approached him several times. Initially, they'd been polite and gracefully accepted his refusal. They were becoming more and more insistent.

The man had no desire to be brought into their fight with anything they deemed unholy. By their metrics, he himself was likely a problem to be dealt with, spared their prejudiced hate because he had the potential to be useful to them. Nevermind he had no interest in serving them in any way.

Laughter from the back of the bar drew his attention. A group of friends gathered around a pool table, laughing and drinking together.

The man frowned, turning around to stare down at the bar.

That, more than anything, was what he missed. The camaraderie that was so prevalent in his first life. In this modern world, it was so hard for him to find anyone to relate to. Everyone he knew and loved from before had been dead longer than civilizations. There were so many new nations today, his home nothing but a distant memory, a sidenote in a different place's story.

The man took a drink, reaching in his pocket to retrieve his phone, hoping to distract himself from his melancholy. That was one thing he could certainly say about the modern age. People had perfected the art of distracting themselves from their problems.

He checked the news. There was nothing interesting.

Looking over his shoulder to ensure he was alone, he opened another browser, one that gave him access to news of the supernatural. He scrolled through reports while sipping his wine.

An image attached to one report caused him to choke on his wine, hacking desperately to clear his airway.

"Are you okay?" the bartender asked, approaching him with concern in his eye.

The man paid the bartender no mind, eyes fixed on the report open on his phone. A man smiling wide in bronze armor raised a helmet above his head in challenge, spear driven through the ground next to him.

The man opened the article and hastily read through it.

A Rating Game. Roygun Belphegor faced Balthazar Abaddon. Balthazar Abaddon's new peerage members were revealed. The man didn't care about anything but the identity of Balthazar's new Knight.

Achilles, son of Peleus, Hero of the Trojan War.

The man hastily researched where to find Balthazar Abaddon, locating a map showingBalthazar's vast lands within the Underworld. Getting to Hell would be difficult, he'd have to find someone or something willing to take him there, but for the first time in this new life, the man had purpose. He needed to get to Castle Abaddon.

The man slammed some crumpled bills on the bar as an afterthought as he practically ran out into the night.

With a thought, his Sacred Gear appeared around him. Dark bronze armor once worn by Achilles himself garbed the man's form. The armor he'd died in settled around him as he began running as fast as he could down the road, the air parting around him in a dramatic rush as he ran with the speed of a car.

Patroclus had one thought fixed in his mind. He needed to see Achilles again.


X


It was rare that Zariel, Archduchess of Avernus, was interested in the happenings beyond her home. Her duties kept her occupied. Avernus, the seat of her power, served as the frontline for the Blood War. Demons rode the River Styx, flooding into her realm and destroying everything in their path.

It was irritating, but Zariel was able to find joy in it. She lived to fight. Tearing through hordes of invaders thinking to steal her realm from her filled her with immense pleasure.

Still, her position as Archduchess of Avernus required her to sometimes deal with less interesting problems. Politics was one of her less favored tasks. She would rather fight her enemies than make nice with allies carrying honeyed words that concealed daggers.

Dispatar, Lord of the Second, Prince of Dis, sent Zariel a letter. It detailed that he had granted permission to three outsiders to enter Avernus and conduct their business however they see fit.

Zariel grit her teeth as she read the letter, reigning in her rage.

Avernus was hers. She decided who may come and go. Dispatar had overreached, trampling her authority without so much as paying lip service to her. He had not requested her permission, he had dictated what he had already done.

One thing kept Zariel from acting rashly against Dispatar's guests. Irritating though she found him to be, Dispatar never acted without reason. He was more cautious than her. Unlike Zariel, Dispatar actually enjoyed playing the political games Baator was so fond of. He would not have missed an opportunity to politic with a fellow lord of the Hells without good reason.

So Zariel stayed her hand. She ordered her spies to watch for the arrival of these guests and report their findings. That should have been the end of it.

Mere minutes after issuing her orders, several of her spies returned, groveling at her feet. They'd abandoned the task she set before them. They showered Zariel in excuses, begging for her mercy.

Zariel was beyond furious, but she could save flaying the failures for later. Amidst the sea of excuses, Zariel pulled several pieces of interesting information. Her servants believed her guests to be lords of the other Hells. They feared the lord's wrath if they were caught observing them.

Zariel's life was absorbed in conflict. She fell to Avernus to act as the stalwart wall that halted the approach of the Abyss. Nearly every waking moment was spent slaughtering demons and ridding her realm of invaders. These guests were intriguing, a break in the monotony.

Zariel left her palace, flying with haste to Elturel, the guests intended destination if Dispatar was to be believed. Zariel altered her form into that of a weak mortal, obscuring her power.

Zariel felt the guests arrive before she saw them. She understood why her underlings had been so afraid now, not that it would spare them her ire.

One of the guests was powerful. He felt like a major lord of one of the Hells. He was the weakest.

The other two radiated power equal to Dukes of each layer of the Hells. Zariel felt something she hadn't felt in ages as she looked upon the green-haired male.

Fear.

Zariel could count the number of devils whose power surpassed her own on one hand. This newcomer numbered among them.

It was intoxicating. After so long spent in the Hells, consumed by rage and the unending desire to destroy, the new sensation was novel.

Zariel maintained her weak, insignificant mortal form as she followed them at a distance. When a disturbance shook the city, she grew irritated. Feeling through her connection to her home to ascertain the nature of the disturbance made her murderous.

Of all times, a Demon Lord chose now to invade her realm? She'd finally found someone worth her interest.

Zariel prepared to squash the gnat that dared to interrupt her. She needn't have bothered.

The third devil, the weakest, dealt with the problem as if it were a trivial thing, like a minor Demon Lord were an insignificant mortal. It was delicious.

Zariel grabbed one of her chain devil servants, allowing a hint of her true self to be visible beneath her disguise, ordering the servant to take the demon alive.

Once she was confident her prize was secure, Zariel returned to watching her guests. The female made a warlock out of one of the mortals. They departed soon after.

In the present, Zariel stood before bars of hellish iron. A circular prison cell was constructed in record time to hold her new prisoner.

A domed room of dark iron and stone caged the demon lord. Sturdy chains bound her arms above her head, suspending her in mid-air. More chains wound around her legs and tail, preventing her from moving. A powerful binding circle sat beneath her, preventing her from calling upon her power to free herself. Glowing runes carved into the chains sapped away her strength.

Zariel grinned, turning away from the cell and walking away. Oublivae did not number among the greatest lords of the Abyss, but she was an excellent prize all the same, a prize delivered to her by these intriguing guests. The secrets she pulled from the demon lord would strengthen her forces. The power she drained from Oublivae would serve to strengthen her armies.

Zariel was enthralled by the mystery surrounding her realm's visitors. Dispatar was keeping most of what he knew of them to himself, that only meant Zariel needed to investigate personally.

Zariel tasked some of her stronger, more reliable underlings with uncovering everything they could about the three strange devils that had entered her realm, expressing a desire to learn as much about the man with mint hair as possible. She needed to know everything there was to know about him.

While her Cambions and Erinyes worked, there was little for Zariel to do herself but bide her time. She slaughtered demons, dealt with annoying politics, and marshalled her armies against the invading demons.

All the while, she waited for any news of the strangers who had swept through her realm.


X


Dispatar sat alone in his throne room, a glowing silver spear held in his hands. He idly ran a finger over the mythril point, smiling to himself as the enchantment sent a minor shock through his body, not nearly enough to injure him.

"Impressive," Dispatar said to himself, setting the spear aside as he picked up a report and read its contents for the third time.

It seemed he had acted correctly in regards to the news of an unknown devil lord interacting with one of his subordinates and creating warlocks with Baator's systems. The now fully named Viscount Balthazar Abaddon had used a number of spears similar to the one in Dispatar's possession to debilitate and capture the demon lord Oublivae, discarding the spears as if they were trivial things as opposed to the wondrous magical items they were. Mortals and devils alike would kill for access to the items Balthazar Abaddon discarded like unimportant garbage. If he could afford to use such powerful items as disposable projectiles, what nature of item did he possess that he deemed worthy of keeping?

The Viscount's apparent wealth aside, the far more important news to come from this most recent meeting with devils from beyond Baator was assuredly the appearance of Balthazar Abaddon's companions. Baator now had a name and face to match to the walking ice age whose presence had been detected in Neverwinter. Satan Serafall Leviathan, a devil so powerful she could rival the lords of the Hells themselves.

Then there was Satan Ajuka Beelzebub. When the reports of Ajuka Beelzebub's power first reached Dispatar, the Lord of Dis was sceptical of their veracity. More reports arrived, each corroborating the account of the first, some even showing the estimate of the Satan's power to be too low.

Dispatar's agents had followed the party's trip through Avernus. No actions were taken that ran contrary to Baator's goals. On the contrary, Balthazar Abaddon captured a notable, if of lesser power, demon lord and turned her over to Zariel's forces with no resistance. A great gift and asset in the Blood War.

Dispatar still knew frightfully little about these new devils. He did not know so much as where they came from or how they arrived, but they clearly desired to work with Baator to their mutual benefit. This was ideal. Baator already had far too many enemies. Even if Ajuka Beelzebub was the greatest among these foreign devils, even if their numbers were few, even if all they could offer would be more of the spears used by Balthazar Abaddon to defeat Oublivae, an alliance would still prove beneficial to Baator.

Dispatar looked forward to future cooperation, but he needed to know exactly what the foreign devils could offer Baator and what, in turn, they could provide to Baator. Facilitating the creation of their warlocks was a pittance, a minor thing. Surely these foreign devils would not ally with Baator for something so minor as utilizing Baator's framework to create warlocks. No, they would want something else. What that desire would be Dispatar could only guess.

Dispatar had updated Virexa's orders. After receiving her report of the powerful golems guarding the Loralee Estate and the mines it operated, Dispatar realized Balthazar Abaddon had taken a more proactive approach in ensuring the safety of his warlocks, an interesting fact considering many devils treated their warlocks as disposable pawns or playthings. He seemed to genuinely care about the wellbeing of his underlings. Serafall Leviathan had reportedly taken her own warlock back wherever these foreign devils came from. Perhaps she held similar care for the warlock even moments after the formation of her contract?

An important piece of the puzzle for certain, but there were still far too many gaps in Dispatar's knowledge.

When next Balthazar Abaddon appeared, Virexa was to do everything in her power to arrange a meeting between Balthazar Abaddon and Dispatar. Dispatar would clear his schedule of meetings with all except Asmodeus himself to meet with the foreign devils.

If arranging such a meeting proved impossible, Virexa was to offer her services as Baator's envoy. If Balthazar Abaddon brought Virexa back with him, she would be able to report to Dispatar many of the things he would need to know to deal with the foreign devils.

How many of them were there? What was their home like? How strong was the average devil? How strong were the weakest and strongest devils? What was their hierarchy? What could they offer Baator? What would they ask in exchange?

All questions Dispatar could only guess at. He needed more information. Balthazar Abaddon's actions in Avernus showed an alliance with these devils would be a great boon to Baator. He disabled a minor demon lord in moments. Serafall Leviathan and Ajuka Beelzebub were both far stronger than he was.

Of course, it was possible Balthazar Abaddon was one of the stronger devils. Perhaps the vast majority of their race was no stronger than an imp? Dispatar needed to know more.

Sighing, Dispatar set the flaming document aside. There was little he could do now but speculate. Virexa's report said Serafall Leviathan wished to arrange a future meeting with him in her capacity as the foreign affairs official of her people.

All Dispatar could do was prepare for that meeting, arranging a proposal of what Baator could offer these other devils in exchange for weapons like the ones Balthazar Abaddon had used against Oublivae. Anything else he would ask for would have to wait until he knew exactly what Serafall Leviathan could provide to him. He'd already notified the lords of the other layers of the situation and his intentions.

There was nothing to be done but wait.


X


Boreas, God of the North Wind, closely examined the map on the table before him. He wasn't sure where he'd heard it, but he remembered someone once telling him that revenge was costly. Boreas believed whoever told him was speaking in the metaphorical sense, staining one's soul and all that hogwash. Boreas had come to realize the truth. Revenge was expensive.

The task Boreas had set before himself must be completed. He would not allow Balthazar Abaddon to continue living his miserable, pathetic life. Unfortunately, Balthazar had amassed a sizable number of very capable allies. This most recent Rating Game between Balthazar and Roygun Belphegor highlighted even more complications with Boreas's plan.

Boreas originally planned to strike weeks ago. Following Remiel's warning, he decided it would be wise to be better prepared before moving against Balthazar. When he heard of the Rating Game, he postponed again to learn as much as he could about Balthazar's underlings. Boreas was glad he'd chosen to wait, but his bank account certainly wept.

Had Boreas undertaken this mission for any other purpose, he would have cut his losses long ago lest he fall into a sunk cost fallacy. As it stood, Boreas could not walk away and leave his daughter unavenged. Boreas, once a wealthy god, was now penniless. He'd spent every last coin he'd earned over the millenia, even selling a number of priceless artifacts to finance his revenge. When his coffers ran dry, he began offering favors and promises to secure further aid.

Wasteful perhaps, but Boreas couldn't help but be content with the force he had accumulated to facilitate his revenge.

"When do you plan to strike?" a human female with short hair wearing a dark hood asked, looking down at the map on the table.

"Soon." Boreas said. "Not everything is ready yet. Once we are prepared, we will strike." This woman – like many of those gathered in his now crowded mansion, his sanctuary safe from the prying eyes of gods and devils alike – was a mortal Boreas hired to act as a mercenary and facilitate his revenge. Remiel's warning gave Boreas pause. He would not allow any chance of failure. His once vast wealth was gone, used to buy the cooperation of a host of mercenaries from across the supernatural. Monsters, Sacred Gear holders, mages like the woman across the table from him – Boreas had paid for them all. In addition to his loyal servants who followed him into exile, Boreas now had a force capable of assaulting a great castle in Hell and leaving nought but a smoking crater in their wake.

Still, Boreas needed to be careful. The last thing he wanted was Balthazar to use whatever spear Medea had made that was capable of killing a god.

"Father Martin," Boreas turned towards the priest standing at the head of the table. "Will our current plan allow you to seal Balthazar's ability to use Hole? So long as he is able to transport his peerage with impunity, our task is doomed to failure." Even if they managed to destroy the castle, if Balthazar used Hole to flee with his peerage, or even if the coward fled alone, their efforts would have amounted to nothing.

Father Martin, the exorcist holding the Sacred Gear Trick Vanish entrusted to Boreas by Remiel, considered the map before nodding. "If the magicians can get me close to Balthazar without him detecting me, I will be able to lock away his power. Once that is complete, I will need them to transport me away swiftly. Balthazar and his peerage will attempt to eliminate me to allow him access to his power."

Boreas nodded seriously. "The magicians will teleport you away the moment you've accomplished your task. Failing that, Jeremy will be at your side the entire time. He'll protect you." Boreas could not allow Father Martin to be harmed after sealing Balthazar's Clan Trait. His entire plan hinged on Father Martin's ability.

The witch made a considering sound. "Then I suppose all that's left is to carry out the mission."

"Yes," a dark-haired young man in a black jacket said, an unimpressed look on his face. "We've been preparing for some time now. At this rate, the agreement we made will be at its end before we attack. When do we strike, Boreas?"

"He has already answered, mortal." a woman with frigid white hair wearing a dress made of pure snow said icily. She stepped up to Boreas's side protectively. "You need only concern yourself with doing your part. Whether the timeline is kept or not, you will join us. Killing the devils serves us both."

Boreas considered the map once more. He spent the last of his fortune on this, a detailed map of Balthazar's lands and the structures the devil had constructed thereon. His source was trustworthy, a dissident serving the New Satans wishing to defect to the Old Satan Faction. Boreas didn't care about the devil's allegiance, only that their intelligence was good.

"Soon. We will strike soon." Boreas said again, focused on the map. He needed to go over everything one more time. He couldn't afford to get this wrong.

The white-haired woman laid a gentle hand on his shoulder. Boreas saw the pain in his expression reflected on her otherwise radiant face.

"For Runa." she said, a single tear tracing its way down her cheek.

For Runa.

#8,429
I blinked in confusion, sitting up on the bed, watching Medea as she got dressed. I hadn't been awake for more than thirty seconds. Maybe I heard her wrong. "What?"

Medea's back was to me. She turned to face me as she finished pulling her dress up. "I want to get married today."

I blinked again. "That's what I thought you said. Um… You know we don't need to rush, right?"

"I don't care about having a grand ceremony. I only wanted the engagement to be special so I could cherish that memory. I want things to be official before my grandfather pulls us into a war." she explained. "My mother can officiate. The only person I would invite who doesn't live here is Circe, but she's already here."

"I… wait, what? When did Circe get here?"

"She arrived last night. I allowed her entry to the lands and told her to go to my mother's castle until we figured out what we wanted to do. She said she was seeking asylum."

"Did she say why she's seeking asylum?"

"Hermes attempted to force her to return with him to Olympus. She did not want to go with him and apparently slighted him and Zeus when she left. Something about telling Zeus to fornicate with a goat?"

I sighed, falling heavily back onto the pillows. "Of course it's another political incident. Why do I keep managing to piss off the Greeks? I didn't even do anything this time."

Medea walked up to the side of the bed and leaned down, gently kissing my forehead. "Don't despair, my love. I can assure you, they deserve every migraine you give them and then some."

"That doesn't save me from having a very uncomfortable conversation with Serafall." I complained. "You remember how precariously close to war we are right now, right? This might be the thing that tips the scales."

"I'm not turning away one of the few relatives I have a positive relationship with, Balthazar. She would do the same for me."

I sighed, nodding in acceptance. "I guess that means I have to make a phone call. You're sure you want to get married today?"

"I'm tired of waiting." Medea said, laying down next to me and resting her head on my shoulder. She gently ran a finger over the ring on my finger. "You're already mine, but I want everyone else to know it."

I closed my eyes, resting my head atop hers. "Okay. I need to call Serafall to tell her about the Circe situation. Provided she doesn't call me away for some emergency meeting or smite me for finally doing something she can't forgive, we'll get married today."

Medea kissed my chin, extricating herself from my embrace as she stood once more. "Is there anyone you would like me to invite while you speak with Serafall?"

"Kuisha, Sairaorg, Latia and Magdaran for sure. Probably Roygun and Diehauser too. I'll give Serafall an invite while she's chewing my ear off."

"It won't be so bad. She likes you, and you're far too valuable to her for her to alienate you. I'll go make some calls. Let me know if you need anything." With that, Medea left me alone with an impending doom hanging over my head.

Sighing, I sat up and swung my legs over the side of the bed. A Hole dropped my phone in my hand and I dialed Serafall. I would rather get this over with immediately so I'm not dreading it for an hour.

Serafall picked up on the second ring. "Bal? Is everything alright?"

"Define 'alright'?"

She sighed tiredly. "Please tell me you didn't somehow find more peerage pieces and reincarnate the Oracle of Delphi in the 24 hours I haven't seen you."

"Hey, this time I had nothing to do with the problem I'm about to create for you."

"I'll reserve judgement for when I hear what the problem is." she said, sounding sceptical.

"Your faith in me is the only thing keeping me going, Serafall." Sighing, I said, "Circe showed up here asking for asylum. Medea let her in and now she's in Idyia's castle."

"…what?"

"Circe asked for asylum and now she's staying in my lands."

Serafall sighed. "Balthazar, I swear, how does this shit keep happening around you?"

"Like I said, this one wasn't on me."

"Why did she even want asylum?"

"Apparently she didn't want to meet with Zeus and it turned into a whole thing. I don't have all the details yet. By the way, how'd the meeting with Athena go?"

"Terribly. Why did Circe go to you?"

I winced at her tone of voice. I knew things were bad, but if her meeting went 'terribly' with a side of venom, we might be screwed. "I couldn't tell you. I can ask her but–"

A voice in my head interrupted what I was about to say.

'Honey, you should probably come down to my mother's castle.' Medea's voice spoke into my mind.

With narrowed eyes, I responded, 'Why? Is something wrong with Circe?'

'Circe's fine, dear. It's just that Thetis is here now too.'

I stared off into space as Medea's words registered in my mind.

"Bal?" Serafall said through the phone.

"Give me a sec, Serafall." I said.

'Achilles's mother Thetis? Thetis as in the Greek goddess Thetis?' I clarified.

'The same. She won't let go of Achilles. It's actually kind of adorable how hard she's squeezing him. You'd think his invulnerability would make him immune, but he's still struggling to breathe.'

I let out a long-suffering sigh. "Serafall, things somehow got worse while we've been talking. Thetis is here now."

There was silence on the other end of the line.

"Serafall?"

"Open a Hole to my office." Serafall said tiredly. "I need to deal with this in person."

"Are you sure? I didn't mean to take you away from–"

"Now, Bal."

My heart thudded faster when she said the word 'husband'. I swallowed a lump in my throat. I still wasn't used to hearing her say that, but damn if I wasn't thrilled to hear it.

"Okay," I agreed. "Let's get dressed and meet Serafall."

Medea's smile turned into a mischievous grin. "You told her you'd meet her in half-an-hour…"

"I did."

Medea pounced on me, pushing me back onto the bed. "We have time for one more round."


X


Medea and I entered Serafall's office just over forty minutes after I'd spoken to her on the phone. I hadn't given Serafall a specific time, but it was clear she was waiting for us.

Sitting on the edge of her desk with her arms crossed over her chest, staring at the wall, Serafall looked up as we entered. She raised an eyebrow as when she saw Medea with me. "I was going to ask what kept you, but I think it's pretty obvious now."

Medea bowed her head shallowly, a content smile on her face. "Forgive the tardiness, Lady Leviathan. I was helping my husband prepare for the day."

Serafall waved her off. "Don't apologize. I'm the one imposing on you both the day after you were married. If I thought this could wait, I wouldn't have called. And I thought I told you to call me Serafall?"

"My wife will be accompanying us if that's alright." I said. "Capable witch that she is, she's figured out a way to travel to the same places I can go. The drawback to her method is that she can only transport herself."

"Should the need arise, I will be able to act as an emissary to facilitate rapid communication." Medea added.

Serafall fixed Medea with a considering expression. "Good to know. Now!" She pushed off her desk, straightening out the dark skirt she wore. "I think it's time we got this over with. Ajuka is standing by in case there are any problems. I want you to pull us away if they try any funny business, but I don't expect they'll try anything in an initial meeting. The sooner we sort things out, the sooner you two can go back to enjoying your honeymoon. I apologize again for dragging you away."

"I get it. This needs to happen." I said, understanding. "Let's just move things along. Did you want to go straight back to Avernus or were you thinking something else?"

"Can you bring us back to Cyvis's house?" Serafall asked. "I want to try and find Virexa to see if she can set up a meeting with Dispatar. There's only so much you can do between intermediaries. That, and if we jump right in, we risk them thinking we're attacking them. I'd rather go through what proper channels are available to me."

"To Cyvis's house then." A Hole opened in the center of the room. Serafall walked through first. Medea and I followed behind her.

I frowned as I entered Cyvis's office. The room was empty, dark. Cyvis wasn't here. I reached out for my connection to my warlocks, following the faint pull of two threads on my demonic power through the house. I walked down the stairs and turned down a hall. My warlocks were close.

I opened a door, stepping into a great dining room with a long wooden table. Four chairs stood along either side with a single at the head and foot of the table. Four sets of enchanted armor I recognized to be Shang Tsung's work stood sentinel around the room, stationed along each wall.

Cyvis and Vellia stood at the foot of the table, their backs to me as they studied a map laid across the table. There were two people I didn't recognize standing with them.

The first was barely able to see over the table, a dwarf male with acorn hair wearing a leather apron with tools dangling from a belt around his waist. The second was tall, a male human with dark hair. The human wore sturdy silver armor, rugged from years of prolonged use. A triangular shield was affixed to his back; a sword was sheathed at his waist.

The dwarf was the first to notice us, eyes narrowing suspiciously as he took a few steps away from us, nudging Vellia's arm as he slipped behind her.

Vellia looked up in confusion, eyes widening as she saw us. Vellia hastily fell to a knee, bowing her head. "My lord,"

Cyvis looked up and quickly fell into a curtsy. "My lord, it is an honor to see you again."

"Sorry to barge in like this again. We need to speak to…Alaine." I finished slowly, looking over the other two figures in the room. I didn't want to name drop Virexa while there were unknowns around, but I also didn't want to drag this out longer than necessary. It was clear Cyvis and Vellia were in the middle of something and I was interrupting their work. The sooner I was out of their hair, the better.

"Alaine is currently guarding the mine you visited me at before, my lord." Vellia said, unmoving from her position.

"I'm sorry," the dwarf said, still eyeing us with suspicion. "Who's this?"

"Our benefactor." Cyvis said simply.

"I didn't know we wasn't working for you." the dwarf said, sounding upset.

"You do not work for me. I work exclusively with Vellia and Cyvis." I said, hoping to limit the damage I was doing to my warlock's dealings.

I really should have knocked. Better yet, I needed to stop just teleporting directly into Cyvis's house. She and Vellia had their own lives to live. They didn't want me trouncing in and demanding their attention whenever I felt like it. They shouldn't have to worry about me randomly teleporting in front of them at any given moment.

"Their benefactor?" the human said, watching me with open interest. His eyes slowly tracked over Medea and Serafall before returning to me like he was sorting pieces of a puzzle. I felt the faintest pulse of power gather around the human. His eyes widened and he inhaled sharply before carefully schooling his expression.

I didn't like the way the human was watching us, nor the weird display I'd just witnessed. I watched him for a moment longer, but he didn't give any other sign that there was anything out of the ordinary. He returned his attention to the map on the table and completely ignored us.

Was that a bead of sweat on his brow?

Unimportant. I needed to get out of my warlock's hair.

Deciding to let it go, I turned back to Cyvis. "I didn't mean to interrupt. Thank you for your help. I'll try not to barge in like this next time."

"Please don't feel hesitant to approach us, my lord." Cyvis said quickly. "We are honored by your every visit."

"As Cyvis said. We are at your service." Vellia agreed.

"I appreciate that, but I'll try to be a little less abrasive in the future. I'll see you both later." I motioned Serafall and Medea back through the door. I closed it behind us, then walked down the hall a ways before opening a Hole, not wanting the human or the dwarf to witness my power.

We emerged at a tree line with clear visibility of the mine where Serafall and I had met Vellia when we'd come here with Ajuka.

"There." Medea pointed out an individual standing in front of a large tent.

Leather armor adorned the dark-haired form of the illusory body Virexa met us in the last time we were here. She was angrily conversing with two miners, pointing towards the mine and seemingly chastising them. She paused mid-shout, tilting her head inquisitively. Slowly, she turned, eyes scanning her surroundings until they found the treeline, slowly tracking along until she saw us.

I pursed my lips. "We really need to figure out how they're able to sense us so we can block it."

"I will work on the problem once we have completed our purpose here." Medea said assuringly.

"Thanks."

Serafall, Medea and I silently watched as Virexa left the miners she'd been scolding forgotten behind her, swiftly marching over the dirt to reach our position. She stopped a few feet away and knelt.

"Greetings, lord and ladies." Virexa said.

"Please stand. Showing deference to us here could potentially create problems for my warlocks." I said quickly, looking over Virexa's shoulder at the many miners not-so-subtly watching our interaction. I said a mental apology to my warlocks once more. I didn't mean to mess up what they were working on here. I'd need to do something to apologize and make it up to them.

"Of course," Virexa acquiesced easily, returning to her feet, though she kept her gaze directed at our boots. "My lord, may I request an introduction to your new companion?"

As I opened my mouth to introduce her, Medea stepped forward, running an appraising eye over Virexa.

"I am Medea Abaddon." Medea said with authority. "Lady of the House of Abaddon and Balthazar's wife."

Virexa briefly fell into a deeper bow directed towards Medea. "It is an honor to meet you, my lady. Viscount Abaddon is fortunate to have a bride so stunning and strong as yourself."

"While the flattery is appreciated," Serafall said, sliding in front of Medea. "We are here on business. I understand it is short notice, but I was hoping to arrange a meeting with your lord. If he is occupied with other matters, I am amenable to waiting or scheduling a meeting at a later date."

"I do not believe that will be necessary, my lady. My lord Dispatar has given me specific instructions to inform him the moment you requested a meeting. He is willing to clear his schedule to meet with you. If you will allow me a moment to inform him of your presence?"

"Please," Serafall said.

A flaming parchment appeared in Virexa's hand. She scribbled a quick note on it before it disappeared in a flash of flame. A moment later, a smaller document wreathed in golden flame appeared before her.

Smiling, Virexa held it out to Serafall. "My lord would be pleased to speak with you at your earliest convenience. May I show you the way to his home?"

"That would be appreciated." Serafall said with a nod.

"If I may," I said. "Could we move out of sight of my warlock's employees before we depart? I'm afraid they'll already have plenty of gossiping to do without seeing a group of devils flying off."

"Of course, my lord." Virexa said, stepping between the trees, into the woods to obscure us from the nosy miners' sight. "Forgive me if I was unclear. We will not need to fly to Dis. Leaving Baator is a challenge even for the erinyes. Returning?" Virexa grinned, lines of bright orange fire spread around her, tracing into a large, circular pentagram. "That is as simple as walking home. With your permission, my lady?"

At Serafall's nod, Virexa raised her arms. Fire poured forth from the pentagram beneath her, swallowing the surroundings until all I could see was flame. Just as soon as it appeared, it was banished. The forest around us was gone. Instead, we stood in a bustling square. The ground beneath us was made from dark metal. Buildings rose all around, forged from dark iron and jagged metals. Devils walked openly on the street around us. Some were tall with wings and horns. Others were little more than blobs of muck, sloughing along the ground as stronger devils ordered them on.

Activity around us halted as we appeared. Every devil in the vicinity turned to observe us, some hissing in fear as they hastily averted their eyes.

Virexa took a step forward and turned back to us, bowing at the waist. The illusion she wore unravelled, revealing her dark horns and feathered wings as she smiled proudly mid-bow. "It is my great pleasure to welcome you to Dis. Lord Dispatar extends his greetings and his protection. While within the city, you are to be treated as honored guests."

Serafall nodded. "We thank your lord for his hospitality and look forward to meeting with him."

Virexa rose from her bow. "If you would follow me, I will lead you to where Lord Dispatar awaits your audience." She began walking down the street at a sedate pace. She basked in the jealous, shocked gazes of the other devils in the street. A soft chuckle escaped her lips as devils parted around her to make a path for Virexa and her entourage.

I was a little out of my depth here, so I followed Serafall's lead, walking behind Virexa and looking straight ahead.

Virexa began pointing out points of interest as we passed them – a famous weaponsmith, a reputable slavepen dealing in exotic 'products', a brothel that boasted the greatest courtesans in Dis. Serafall was the perfect tourist, showing a keen interest in every location no matter how shocking or strange.

Throughout our stroll through Dis, a large, thin tower stood tall on the horizon, raised upright like a tube of iron stabbed into the ground. We continued to walk closer and closer to the tower, yet it seemed to remain just as far away as it was the last time I'd seen it.

It was likely another spatial effect like we encountered in Avernus. I couldn't say I was surprised, but I wasn't exactly thrilled either. If the local devils could manipulate the space of this realm, it might prove difficult to fight our way out.

Not that I expected that to be necessary, but it didn't hurt to be ready for it all the same.

I looked to the side as Virexa pointed out a menagerie holding monsters captured from across the multiverse. When I turned back to the direction we'd been walking, I was shocked to see a massive dark tower of iron less than one-hundred feet away.

"Finally," Virexa said, excitement creeping into her voice. "I present to you the Iron Tower, the home of my lord, the center of power in the Second."

"It is impressive." Serafall said, looking up at the tower. I noticed a touch of genuine praise in her demeanor. "I can feel the power coursing through this tower. Your lord must certainly be proud of his home."

Virexa beamed. "That he is. The corridors can be confusing to strangers. Please remain close to me as I lead you to my lord's throne room. He will receive you there."

There was no door in sight that would grant access to the tower. That did not deter Virexa. She walked straight towards the tower. When she was just a foot away, there was a great lurching sound as a rectangular panel of the tower swung inward to allow her inside.

Serafall, Medea and I followed Virexa into the tower, heeding her warning as we stayed close to her while she navigated maze-like corridors that snaked back on themselves and staircases that led up only to bring you lower than where you started.

The interior of the tower was a headache. It would be a nightmare to assault it. Part of me wondered if that was why Virexa was taking us the long way, to show us just how well-defended and powerful her lord was to construct such a home. Or, perhaps she was just proud of the tower. She continued pointing out interesting trophies or rooms, chatting happily about the history of each trinket and bauble.

I lost track of it after she pointed out a sapling that was supposedly borne of one of the first trees to bloom in Elysium, stolen during some ancient war with the heavens. The other treasures were similarly strange.

After walking for what felt like an hour, but weirdly also only three minutes, we arrived at a set of iron double doors. Torchlight from sconces on the walls cast dancing shadows on the walls as Virexa turned to face us.

"Beyond these doors lie my lord's throne room. He is awaiting your presence within. I would ask that you remain here until my lord calls for you to enter. I will announce you, then he will call you to enter." Virexa explained. After a moment, she spun around and pushed open the double doors.

The dull roar of conversation could be heard the moment the doors opened, but it was instantly snuffed out as Virexa entered. The only sound was the thunk of her heavy metal boots against the floor as she walked. Dispatar was not alone in the throne room. There was a crowd sizeable enough for many quiet conversations to contribute to a cacophony of noise.

"Address him as Lord Dispatar, but don't call him 'my lord'." Serafall said under her breath, barely able to be heard. She wasn't looking at us. Her lips didn't even seem to move as she spoke, and I felt a trace of magic in the air. She was preventing anyone or anything from listening in on what she was saying.

"Be respectful, but do not show deference." Serafall continued. "We're here as equals hoping to make a mutually satisfactory arrangement with a foreign power. We are not a lesser nation here to submit ourselves as vassals or seek their favor. Follow my lead. Only speak if they address you specifically, and keep your answers brief. I'll do the heavy lifting."

I wasn't stressed out about this meeting until this very moment. Intellectually, I understood I was going to meet an archdevil. It only really registered just how pants-shittingly terrifying that prospect was when I was standing on the threshold.

This was Dispatar. Right hand of Asmodeus. Hoarder of knowledge from times forgotten by history. A devil praised for his long-term plans and schemes whose entire race excelled in schemes. This being was legendary.

Medea slowly laced her fingers through mine, squeezing my hand comfortingly.

I looked down at her to find her smiling warmly up at me.

And just like that, all of my anxiety melted away.

I may be about to meet Dispatar, but I was accompanied by my wife, one of the greatest witches in history and Serafall Leviathan, the strongest female devil in my Hell.

'Thank you.' I said through mine and Medea's shared mental connection. She must have felt me freaking out through our bond and reached out to comfort me.

'Of course. Let's give these devils a show they'll never forget.' she said back.

"My lord!" Virexa's voice called from within the chamber, loud and filled with authority. "As ordered, I have escorted three guests to your illustrious throne. I present Satan Serafall Leviathan, Viscount Balthazar Abaddon, and Lady Medea Abaddon."

"Bid them enter." a sinister voice spoke quietly, yet the voice carried to every ear in the vicinity without difficulty. It was as if the tower itself carried the man's words.

"Follow me." Serafall said, an air of formal confidence about her.

Serafall pushed open the nearly closed doors and strode into the throne room, back straight and walking with sure steps. Medea and I flanked her, eyes fixed straight ahead as we crossed a gauntlet of prying eyes.

Dispatar's throne room was a circular chamber supported by iron pillars. Devils were scattered all around the room. There were a few devils of ice lurking behind pillars.

A single large, hulking devil stood to the right, naked save for a loincloth and belt with a large iron mace dangling from it. Red skin and powerful muscles covered in armored hide. Towering wings were cradled close to the creature's back. Short horns grew from its head at a sharp angle before terminating in sharp tips. If my guess was right, that was a pit fiend, the strongest of the devils that weren't archdevils themselves.

Still, the vast majority of the devils in the room were not made of ice, and there was only one pit fiend.

No, the majority were other erinyes, sporting wings of varying sizes and colors. Some had horns, others wore elaborate crowns or helmets fashioned to look like horns. Some wore armor and were laden with weapons. Others wore formal attire. A scant few wore just enough to cover their sensitive areas but no more. All watched intently as we passed. Many darted glares at Virexa where she knelt at the foot of a set of three steps.

A circular platform of iron rose with each step, ending at a circular platform with a terrible, dark iron throne atop it. A tall man sat upright in the chair. Horns curled up from his forehead. Skin colored like dull iron glowed in the soft firelight of the chamber. A single cloven hoof rested on the floor in place of his left foot. A staff was held relaxed in his right hand, forged from dark metal wound in two cords joining at the top where two viper heads met.

Dispatar, Lord of Dis, smiled expectantly as we grew closer.

"Lord Dispatar," Serafall greeted, stopping a few feet shy of the steps. "Thank you for agreeing to meet with us on such short notice."

"Of course." Dispatar said. "It is a pleasure to finally speak to you, Satan Serafall Leviathan."

"Satan Leviathan will suffice." Serafall said formally.

Dispatar smiled, amused, and nodded shallowly. "Satan Leviathan then. Welcome to my home. I trust the journey was pleasant?"

"It was. I appreciated the opportunity to explore your home. It is different from our own in many ways, yet similar in others. I believe there are many ways we can help one-another."

"I'm glad to hear it. I've looked forward to this meeting. Your people are a mystery. I have scoured records predating the rise of mortals, yet found no trace of any mention of you. Tell me, Satan Leviathan, where do you come from? How did you come to be here?" Dispatar implored, sitting forward in his seat as he stared intently down at Serafall.

"To discuss how we came here, I would require a private audience. The method is sensitive and should not be spread around." Serafall said apologetically. "I am, however, willing to freely speak of the where."

Serafall slowly raised her arms, wordlessly watching Dispatar as she began to cast a spell. At Dispatar's nod, Serafall hastened her casting. A great illusion rose in the center of the chamber, drawing all eyes to it. It was a projection of our home, our Hell, scaled down to provide little more than a brief look at the space as a whole. You couldn't make out any detail in the projection.

"As I said, our home is similar to your own, though it holds many distinct differences." Serafall explained patiently. "Unlike your Baator, there is only one layer of our Hell, ruled by the Four Great Satans. I am the Satan in charge of our foreign relations. Satan Ajuka Beelzebub, who visited Avernus with me, is in charge of our research and technology. Alongside two others, we rule our single layer of Hell. There are several slight exceptions to this rule where space is stretched or compressed into structures resembling different layers, but there is only one true layer. Like your home, our own is connected to a mortal plane, though a different one. There is no Faerun in our mortal world. No Sword Coast."

I repressed a smile. When we'd returned from retrieving Serafall's warlock, she pulled me into a room with her warlock for close to an hour, receiving a crash course on Faerun and Baator in preparation for meeting with Dispatar. I'd only explained things once, but Serafall clearly retained most if not all of it. She was far more intelligent than people gave her credit for. That was probably because of her Magical Girl obsession. Maybe that was all an act to throw people off their rhythm?

…No. Her obsession wasn't fake. I'd seen the evidence of that first-hand. She just happened to also be incredibly competent.

Whispers filled the room in the wake of Serafall's words. Dispatar silenced them all with a simple raising of his hand.

"A different mortal plane, you say? How interesting." The Lord of Dis intoned, eyes fixed on the illusion Serafall displayed, analyzing it. "If there are mortals in your home, why come to our mortal plane to create your warlocks?"

Serafall maintained a perfectly composed, professional smile as she accepted the question. It was a good thing she was running point on this. I wouldn't have known what to say without making us seem weak.

"Initially, it was an accident." Serafall explained. She motioned to me, standing at her side. "Viscount Abaddon attempted to create a contract with a mortal here the way we do in our home. The contract registered with the impressive systems you have created to facilitate the creation of warlocks and bound them in a pact. The next two warlocks we contracted were to test if such an accident could be replicated. While we contract with the mortals of our world, we do not have a direct comparison to your warlock contracts. We were intrigued."

Again, furious whispers spread throughout the room, silenced with a glare from Dispatar.

"You are unable to create warlocks independent of our systems?" Dispatar said, frowning.

Serafall smiled warmly. "We have not seen the need for several hundred years. Our greatest mind created something we have used almost exclusively ever since. We still create contracts with mortal mages to facilitate the increase of our power, but we have not needed warlocks for centuries."

Serafall grinned. "You would be correct in your assumption. As to the creation itself, if you would permit it, Lord Dispatar, I have brought you a gift, a token of our thanks for your willingness to deal with us and a symbol of the boons our two peoples will reap from cooperating into the future."

Dispatar's eyes were shining, lips pulled into a wicked grin. "I graciously accept."

With a flick of her wrist, fifteen red chess pieces glowing with infernal power appeared in the air in front of her, floating lazily through the air. Serafall raised her voice, speaking to Dispatar, but addressing the whole room. "These are Evil Pieces, created by Satan Beelzebub centuries ago.
