Different from your own method of creating new devils, the reincarnated target retains their prior form and power, allowing a dragon to become a devil while still maintaining its draconic form and power."

More whispering broke out through the room, cutting off as Serafall continued.

"Each piece amplifies the strength of those who receive the piece. As I am sure you've noticed, the pieces are modelled after pieces from the mortal game of chess. Each piece grants power corresponding to its piece. Rooks increase strength. Knights increase speed. Bishops increase magical power. Queens enhance everything. Pawns grant a minor bonus to everything while granting the power to promote into other pieces for a brief period of time."

"How complete is this reincarnation? How strong will the reincarnated devil be?" Dispatar asked inquisitively, eyes fixed on the floating chess pieces in front of Serafall.

Serafall grinned. "Every reincarnation is complete. The increase in the reincarnated devil's power is directly proportional to the strength of the devil holding the Evil Pieces themself and the original strength of the creature being reincarnated. If you desire an example of the effectiveness of the Evil Pieces, I present Lady Abaddon." Serafall said, dramatically motioning towards Medea.

Many devils gasped as all eyes turned towards Medea. Medea stood tall, weathering the attention without so much as an uncomfortable shuffle.

Serafall now openly addressed the room, turning her eyes from Dispatar for the first time since we entered. "Lady Abaddon was born to a goddess and a demigod. Her mother is the daughter of a Titan. Medea's ancestry is thick with power. Viscount Abaddon reincarnated her with his Queen piece and later took her as his wife. Viscount Abaddon is an extremely powerful devil. His Queen piece enhanced Lady Abaddon's already considerable power to the level you now see before you."

"I ask you, Lord Dispatar," Serafall said, returning her attention to the Lord atop his throne. "Was there any indication Lady Abaddon was anything other than a pureblooded devil?"

Dispatar's eyes were narrow, staring intently at Medea. Slowly, he shook his head. "There is no sign she is anything other than a powerful devil duchess. Only with your prompting am I able to sense a faint trace of lingering divinity about her. Thank you for entertaining my concerns, Satan Leviathan."

"Think nothing of it, Lord Dispatar." Serafall said, an easy smile on her face. "I am here to facilitate cooperation between our two peoples. I would be a poor envoy indeed if I did not address your concerns."

Serafall turned to Medea and I, motioning for us to stay where we were. She approached the steps leading up to Dispatar's throne, stopping at the bottom. "To continue with the gift I mentioned, my fellow Satans and I have decided to give you your own set of Evil Pieces, Lord Dispatar. I mean no disrespect, but in order to bind the Evil Pieces to you, I must approach and conduct a simple ritual. You have my word as Satan of my people that I hold no ill intentions towards you of any kind."

Dispatar watched Serafall for a moment. There was silence as the entire room waited on his word. Finally, he said, "Your word is appreciated, but unnecessary."

Dispatar stood from his throne and slowly descended the steps to meet Serafall. Each footfall shook the room. Even standing on even-footing, he towered over Serafall, standing seven feet tall. He looked down at the Satan with open interest. "If you wished harm upon me, there were far simpler ways you could have gone about it. Your actions and the actions of Viscount Abaddon thus far have granted you a measurable amount of my trust. I will accept your gift."

Serafall nodded respectfully. "Thank you, Lord Dispatar. This will only take a moment."

A glowing red ritual circle slowly expanded out from beneath Serafall to encompass Dispatar. The Lord of Dis hungrily took in every detail of the ritual circle as the Evil Pieces floating in front of Serafall drifted through the air to orbit around him.

Serafall clenched her fist. The circle and the pieces vanished.

That was far faster than when I received my Evil PIeces, but then again, Serafall probably helped Ajuka make the damn things. It made sense she'd be better at binding them to people than some random devil who worked for Ajuka.

Dispatar blinked for the first time since we'd entered the room. He raised his hand. A glowing red Pawn appeared between his thumb and index finger. "Remarkable." he said, inspecting the Pawn.

Serafall took a step back, a proud smile on her face as she said, "I am pleased you approve, Lord Dispatar. There are several points I must quickly go over regarding the piece's few limitations."

Dispatar nodded for her to continue, still inspecting the Evil Piece in his hand.

"While Viscount Abaddon was able to reincarnate Lady Abaddon, Evil Pieces are unable to reincarnate fully divine beings. True gods cannot be reincarnated. Similarly, if a creature is far more powerful than the devil owner of the Evil Piece, a situation I doubt you shall ever encounter personally, the Evil Piece will be unable to reincarnate that individual. As with chess, each Evil PIece has a metaphysical value attached to it. Some pieces are able to reincarnate stronger beings, with the Queen being able to reincarnate the strongest and the Pawns reincarnating the weakest. You can, however, use multiple pieces of the same kind to reincarnate someone stronger. Two Pawns, for instance, could be used on a single individual to reincarnate a being too strong for a single Pawn."

"Leading to fewer servants, but servants of greater quality." Dispatar commented, turning to look at Serafall.

Serafall nodded. "Correct."

"Aside from the divine, are there further limitations on creatures that cannot be reincarnated?" Dispatar asked.

"No. The only other limiting factor is the strength of the devil holding the PIeces."

Dispatar frowned. "Your explanation confuses me. Are the pieces capable of reincarnating beings that are already devils into devils?"

Grinning, Serafall said, "Yes. In our home, being accepted into a lord's peerage carries immense respect. Lesser devils work tirelessly to earn the attention and favor of lords in the hope of earning a place in that lord's peerage."

Several audible gasps sounded around the room. A fury of conversation filled the room, far louder than the whispers from before.

"Silence!" Dispatar barked, voice echoing like a thunderclap. "All of you leave us. Virexa, remain behind."

Devils immediately shuffled from the room, throwing last, desperate glances at myself, Medea, Serafall and the Evil PIece in Dispatar's hand.

When the room was empty and the great iron double doors clapped shut, Dispatar banished the Pawn in his hand, turning to Serafall. "You required privacy to discuss how you were able to venture from your home to Baator. You now have it. I ask again: How were you able to complete this journey?"

Serafall's smile fell. She was silent for a moment before speaking again. "Many devils in our home possess powers passed down through their bloodline. One such Clan Trait facilitated our arrival here."

Dispatar's eyes slid away from Serafall, landing squarely on me. "I would assume it is your power, Viscount Abaddon? In every report of foreign devils arriving here, you are always present."

As much as I wanted to look to Serafall for guidance, I didn't dare break eye-contact with Dispatar. He'd already figured it out, not that it was really all that hard to do, so denying it would only insult him and potentially harm the relationship Serafall was building.

"It is my power, Lord Dispatar." I said, sounding far more confident than I felt.

"We are genuine in our desire to work favorably to our mutual benefit, Lord Dispatar." Serafall cut in, lips in a hard line. "However, should any action be taken against Viscount Abaddon, Lady Abaddon or their subordinates, we will cease all cooperation immediately."

Dispatar nodded. "I am not so foolish as to risk the boons you offer with short-sighted blunderings. I will ensure my less intelligent underlings are suitably reigned in to prevent a misunderstanding."

"Good," Serafall's smile returned. "Then I look forward to a mutually beneficial future."

"As do I." Dispatar said. "You and those under you are free, of course, to continue using our systems to make warlocks as you please. The contracts strengthen Baator as a byproduct of being made. This is a paltry thing. What else would you desire from Baator?"

"At present, our only goal is establishing a relationship with Baator." Serafall said. "Matters back home require our immediate attention, but we wish to continue working with you. My fellow Satans will need to be notified about the result of this meeting. Following that, I will be able to more clearly outline what we wish from Baator."

Dispatar smiled. "In that case, may I suggest an exchange of envoys? I would like to send one of my servants back with you to better understand how Baator can help you. In exchange, I would be happy to host one of your own people here in my tower. They will be offered the opportunity to learn all they can of Baator and, more specifically, my layer of Dis."

Serafall considered for a moment. "That would be amenable, Lord Dispatar. If you will permit it, could we depart momentarily and return with my envoy?"

"Of course." Dispatar said. He waved a hand, and I felt as if pressure I hadn't been aware of was suddenly gone from my shoulders. "You are free to leave and return to my throne room."

"Thank you." Serafall said with a nod. "We will only be gone a few minutes." Serafall fixed me with a pointed look.

I opened a Hole. Medea, Serafall and I all walked through. Not knowing where else to take us, I'd brought us to Serafall's office. I figured she'd have the easiest time tracking down her envoy here.

Serafall looked around, realizing where she was. "Good. I'll be back in a second." She vanished in a flash of light.

I let out a long breath I hadn't realized I'd been holding. "I think that went pretty well considering all of the ways it could have gone terribly."

Medea nodded. "Dispatar appears eager to work with us. That, and your past interactions with Virexa, seem to have paved the way for a strong relationship."

Before I could comment further, Serafall reappeared, another person tagging along with her.

The devil looked young, but that didn't mean much when we were functionally immortal. He had brown hair and a warm expression on his face. He was dressed in a dark suit and held a suitcase in his right hand.

"Bal, meet Carter. Carter, Bal. I'd let you guys chat more, but we don't have time." Serafall said quickly. "Bal, take us back."

I opened another Hole, and we all walked through. Dispatar was quietly speaking to Virexa, still kneeling before him. As he saw us appear, he turned his full attention to us.

Serafall motioned to Carter. "Lord Dispatar, this is Baron Carter Uvall, younger brother of Count Treclan Uvall, Lord of the house of Uvall. He has worked with me for many years. He will serve well as our envoy."

Carter entered a deep bow directed towards Dispatar. "It is an honor to serve, my lord."

"It shall be my pleasure to host you." Dispatar said with a nod. He indicated Virexa. "Virexa shall serve as my envoy. She is knowledgeable about our home and has worked well with you in the past. I believe it would be beneficial for her to continue serving as our intermediary. Provided you approve, Satan Leviathan?"

"I have no complaints." Serafall said.

Smiling, Dispatar said, "Then we are agreed. I appreciate your visit, Satan Leviathan. It was pleasant to finally meet you. I look forward to our next meeting."

"I do as well, Lord Dispatar." Serafall said easily. "Thank you for your hospitality. I will be in contact soon."

Dispatar laid a hand on Carter's shoulder and guided him towards the double doors at the entrance to the room.

Sensing the meeting was over, I opened another Hole to Serafall's office. Serafall led Virexa through, then Medea and I followed.

Virexa looked around, taking in every detail of her new surroundings.

Serafall pulled me aside. "Thanks for your help, Bal." she said quietly. "Sorry I pulled you and Medea away. I'll take care of everything from here. If I need your help again, I'll give you a call."

"Happy to help. Take care." I said. I opened another Hole. Medea and I stepped through it.

The moment we were through, I fell face-first onto our bed, groaning.

I didn't really do much during that whole meeting, but just being there was exhausting. I didn't know how Serafall managed to do her job. Her secretary was right. She really needed a vacation. Maybe I could take her magical girl hunting sometime soon?

Medea laid down next to me and cuddled into my side. I rolled over so I could wrap an arm around her, pulling her into my chest.

Magical girl excursions could wait. I had a day's worth of cuddling and napping with my wife to catch up on.


X


A low rumble woke me up. I looked around, confused. The wards hadn't pinged anything, so why…?

An explosion had me jolting out of bed. Medea was on her feet a moment later.

A dozen magical screens showing the lands around the castle appeared around Medea. Magical barriers set into the grounds around our home were under assault from all sides. Explosions, lightning blasts, blades and more hammered against the shields. An amethyst mist spread all throughout the area, obscuring forms that shifted through it and caused Medea's scryings to flicker unnaturally.

Another explosion rocked the castle, held back by the barriers keeping us secure. On the ground, lumbering shapes made of crimson armor and twisting shadow tore through the barrier at the outer perimeter, sprinting towards the castle itself.

We were under attack.

#8,676
Holes opened all around me.

I frowned. I'd been trying to create more but I couldn't. Whoever was attacking us had warded the area against teleportation. The only connections I could open were local ones within the effect itself and those that Aqua had locked open.

Most of the connections Aqua had locked open were to the castle itself. I could reach out beyond the castle to the connection she'd made for me to the Elemental Plane of Fire and my office building in Lucifaad. Everything else was locked. I'd need to talk to her about making more connections to random locations once we smashed whoever was stupid enough to attack my home.

"We're under attack." I said through the Holes. "Everyone gather in the main hall. I don't want anyone trying anything alone. We don't know who is hitting us or how well they've planned for us. Aqua, I want you to take Keno and go get help. Tell Serafall and Sairaorg what's happening. With luck, someone will be able to come immediately." I closed the Holes around me as I heard a sea of affirmatives.

Medea was glaring at the screens in front of her, furious. "You will not take my home from me." she practically growled.

The crimson armors and twisted shadows were only a hundred feet away from the outer walls of the castle and growing closer.

Medea closed her fist.

On the screens, I watched as the ground exploded beneath our attackers, scattering fragments of red armor and vicious shadowstuff all over. A cacophony of screeches and clacking bones rose up in the silence created by the explosion.

Violet skeletons, animated adamantine armors and dark stone golems charged out of tunnels around the entire perimeter of our castle, crashing into the stunned line of attackers like a tidal wave, tearing through everything in their path.

Dark tendrils like the tentacles of a gigantic kraken slowly extended from the castle walls and up from the earth around them. The tendrils lashed about, crushing any enemy forces that made it past our constructs.

Gleaming gemstones set into the exterior walls of the castle illuminated. Beams of multicolored light shot forth from the gems, magical spells raining down like sustained machine gun fire, showing no sign of slowing as the rear lines of the approaching force were mowed down without mercy.

"That will buy us some time." Medea said, intently focused on the scrying screens in front of her. She hissed, frustrated as the images on several screens fizzled into nothing. Any time she focused too closely on the amethyst mist coating the grounds and sky around the castle, her scryings failed.

Shadows coalesced around her as dozens of spectral cats and ravens dove through the nearest window, flooding out to serve as her eyes and ears where her scryings failed.

"We need to regroup with the others." I said, opening a Hole next to us.

With one last furious look out the window, Medea stormed through the Hole. I followed behind her.

Several members of my peerage were already waiting for us. Shiroe frantically looked over screens, some fizzling into nothing the same way Medea's had.

"They're everywhere." Shiroe breathed, a spark of fear leaking into his voice.

"No matter how well they prepared to attack us," Medea cut in, voice full of fury. "They are not ready to face what lies in wait for them. They won't even breach our walls."

"We need to get out there, master." Coal said, staring at me impatiently. "They're blocking teleportation and scrying somehow. Let me hunt down the ones responsible so we have control of the battlefield again."

"I'm not sending anyone anywhere alone." I said. "We're well-prepared to defend ourselves, but I won't let them pick us off one-by-one."

A droplet of water fell from the ceiling.

I summoned magical shields around myself and my peerage, turning to face the ceiling. There were no water features here.

A vortex of water spun into being above us, slowly descending.

Medea laid a hand on my shoulder, pushing my arm down. I let my defensive spells fade away as I recognized Idyia, Thetis and Circe appearing as the water scattered. A massive silver dragon fell to the ground next to them, grunting.

"They have struck my lake as well." Idyia said clinically.

Frowning, I said, "We don't have the numbers to split up that far."

Idyia smiled, vicious. "Thetis and I will be more than sufficient to keep them at bay. Attacking two sea goddesses in a lake? I wouldn't have expected such foolishness. Forgive me, but we must leave now to deal with them."

I nodded. "Go."

"Wait!"

We all turned to find Irene running down the hall, a thick bundle held against her chest. Unhappy wailing filled the room as two small arms reached up, grasping.

Irene stopped in front of Idyia, holding her daughter out to the goddess. "I can't protect her and fight at the same time. Keep her safe for me. Please."

Idyia nodded seriously, taking the screaming child with great care. "No harm shall befall her while I still live." Idyia turned to me. "Contact me if the situation here requires my assistance." Idyia's form shimmered, losing substance as she faded into a puddle.

Thetis stepped forward and placed a kiss on Achilles's forehead. I felt a metaphysical hum fill the air as she blessed him.

"Fight well, my son. I will not allow you to leave me again." Thetis said, eyes locked on his. After a moment, she scattered into a splash of water like Idyia before her.

More explosions outside shook the foundations of the castle.

"Master, I need to get out there." Coal demanded.

I took a short breath, forcing the anger at someone brazenly attacking my home down so I could think clearly. "Circe, are you going back with Idyia?"

Circe shook her head. "Anankos and I shall help you here."

Good. That made things easier.

I turned back to Coal. "Take Circe and Anankos," I hope I hadn't butchered that name, but I didn't have time to worry about it. "See if you can get a better idea of what we're facing here and shut down whatever they're using to block teleportation and scrying if you can. Stay together and protect each other."

A small thrush made of spectral green energy flew away from Circe to land on Medea's shoulder.

"I will communicate to you through that familiar." Circe said, already following Coal towards the doors at the end of the hall. "Keep us updated on anything new you learn."

"Wait!" Shiroe called out, but Coal wasn't listening, already sprinting towards the door.

Cursing under his breath, Shiroe hastily summoned a dozen magical circles into the air around him. A rainbow of energy fell across everyone in the room as Shiroe empowered everyone with enhancement magic. I felt my muscles bulge and my mana swell in the wake of his spell.

Coal hadn't seemed to even notice the spells, throwing the doors open and leaping into the air, changing into his full serpentine body as he took to the sky. Anankos was a second behind him, leaping off the ground on powerful limbs and flapping his great wings, pausing only to allow Circe to sit astride his back.

Through the door, I could make out the barrier beyond our walls under assault from all manner of spells and attacks. The dull roar of clashing weapons and strikes against metal and bone told the tale of fierce battle on the ground between our constructs and whatever the hell those shadow creatures and red armored beasts were. The doors slowly shut.

"Achilles, Matatabi," I said, focusing back on the immediate problem before us. "I want you two to patrol the ground. Try to figure out what those creatures are and see if you can find if there is a general coordinating them. Watch each other's backs."

Matatabi leapt off the table she'd sat upon to land on Achilles's shoulder, winding her body around his neck until she was securely fastened.

Achilles hefted his spear in a brief salute. "They'll regret their decision to attack us." Without another word, he spun and was gone, body becoming a blur as he moved faster than I'd ever seen him. I could only make out a bronze smudge as he dashed away.

"What about us, my lord?" Shang Tsung asked. Mothra watched me intently from atop his head.

"Mothra is our best healer. I want you to stay with her to cover her in case anyone gets hurt. Otherwise, keep them outside the castle's walls. I don't know how they're getting through the barrier, but there will likely be a stronger force hitting us soon."

I turned to Medea. "With that teleportation block up, I can't coordinate as effectively as normal. I need you in charge of that."

Medea nodded. "I will handle things from here. I have already attached a familiar to everyone's shadow."

I nodded. "Good. Shiroe, Irene, come with me." I led my Bishops through a Hole.

Irene was the first to join me, hovering in the air above my castle. Shiroe staggered a moment before catching himself on his wings. Together, we took in the battle around us.

A dome of crimson energy separated the castle from the worst of the attack, but the barrier was failing, flickering and cracking under the incessant assault.

Spells rained down against the barrier from all sides. The grounds around the castle were surrounded by cloaked figures floating in the air. Figures made from pure fire, frost, water and air drifted between the cloaked figures, blasting the barrier with elemental power. Feminine shapes covered in feathers swept past the barrier, slashing their claws down into its surface with each pass. It wouldn't hold much longer.

It was hard to make out exactly how many attackers we were facing. That damn mist was everywhere. It had somehow made its way past the barrier and was even covering parts of the castle, though it was much thinner inside the barrier than it was beyond.

On the ground, skeletons, animated armors and golems duelled with soldiers of crimson rock and twisted creatures forged from shadow. At present, our forces were overwhelming the attackers, but I could see more of the enemy force marshalling beyond the barrier. Small groups periodically managed to get through somehow, but the magical turrets of the gemstones in the castle walls mowed them down before they could get too close.

Those gem turrets Medea had lining every square foot of the castle were a lifesaver. Whoever was controlling this force would see that and hopefully keep their main force back to avoid sending them into a blender, buying us time to figure out what to do.

Coal and Anankos flew past the front of the castle. Coal opened his maw and unleashed a torrent of flame, disintegrating a group of harpies that somehow managed to make it through the barrier.

"Elementals, mages and harpies." I said aloud, glaring. "Boreas." This was almost the exact same force he'd arrayed to murder Magdaran, Latia and i before.

A shadow stretched out of my shirt, briefly forming into a raven. "I will search for him." Medea's voice said. "The mist will make it difficult to find him. Be prepared for other dangerous individuals to be obscured by it. I have only been able to find weaker opponents so far." The raven scattered, its shadow flowing back down my shirt.

"What should we do, Balthazar?" Shiroe asked, looking around anxiously, though there was a fierce determination in his eyes.

"The barrier won't last long." I said plainly, watching as a section of the crimson barrier flickered once more. "When it falls, we bombard anything that moves. Aim out beyond the range of the castle's defenses. Let the others deal with what makes it past us and closer to the castle, but we annihilate everything along the perimeter. Understood?"

Irene grinned, an evil light sparking to life in her eyes. I could have sworn her teeth sharpened into fangs and a trace of smoke puffed out of her mouth as she said, "Gladly."

As if on cue, a section of the barrier shattered inward under the force of a great lightning strike. The rest of the barrier unraveled as the effect rippled along its surface.

Triumphant shouts and roars rose up from all directions as the floating mages, monsters and elementals charged through the now open area.

Holes opened around the entire perimeter of the castle. Mages screamed as elemental fire turned them to ash. Shadowy monsters screeched as explosions of demonic power punched them apart. Harpies wailed their death cries as enchanted spears and daggers rained down upon them.

Shiroe raised his arms, shaking under the effort.

As the enemy ground forces began to charge, twisting electric blue vines rose up from the grounds, biting into them and restricting the first wave of troops around the entire perimeter of the castle.

A Hole opened over the vine as I fired a knife out to cut the thorns.

Every creature caught in Shiroe's web wailed as electrical energy turned their insides into mush.

Irene laughed.

Sparing her a quick glance, I saw her hair and limbs were all alight with orange fire. She threw her arms up towards the sky. The dark clouds above rumbled, adopting a dangerous orange hue.

Balls of fire rained down from the sky like hail. Mages hastily erected barriers above them to save themselves only to be blasted from the side as Irene carefully picked targets with weaker, directed spells while her greater magic fell from the sky.

We were decimating the ranks of our enemy. At least, we were.

That damned mist condensed, withdrawing from the castle to fully cover the approaching force, obscuring them from sight. We continued firing spells into the mist, but it was almost like the spells were sent elsewhere the moment they entered the mist. It pissed me off.

This must be how people feel when I catch their spell in a Hole and move about unphased.

Irene abandoned launching spells by hand, diverting all her focus to unleashing hellfire rain. Airborne targets were knocked from the sky, falling dead into the mist as they were struck by her rain. It was very effective.

A cold front seemed to strike from nowhere, dropping the temperature by forty degrees.

The orange clouds Irene was cultivating above froze as if coated in permafrost. Light snow began to fall in place of fire. I'd never seen Irene so enraged as she was that moment after having her spell co-opted and scattered.

"Medea, tell Coal and Achilles to find whatever is making this mist and have them deal with it now." I ordered through grit teeth.

We continued launching spells at what we could see, but any of our attacks that struck the mist were less than useless, as if we hadn't even cast them.

All the while, the mist grew steadily closer, so thick as to hide any number of nasty surprises.

"Well done, son!" Coal yelled proudly as Anankos tore a harpy in two with his claws. "Make sure you don't let them surround you. Harpies are small and weak. Break them quickly and move on."

Coal reared his head back and unleashed a torrent of dragonfire, burning a trio of air elementals to nothing.

"Do not tire yourself too quickly, my son." Circe calmly lectured as she blasted a mage with a dark curse that flayed his skin. "There are still many enemies around us."

Coal grunted in irritation, looking down at their surroundings as his tail coiled and lashed out, bisecting another harpy. "This mist is a problem."

Circe let out a displeased sound, surveying the field below.

Medea's skeletons tore into shadowy beasts, dispatching many before being consumed by an unending tide. Shang Tsung's armors crushed crimson lumbering forms only to be crushed by three more. The quality of the defenders was far superior to the attackers. But the attackers seemed without end. Unless they could find the source of the mist and soldiers, this battle would be difficult to end.

"We'll need to…" Circe trailed off, looking up as the orange sky turned white. Snow fell all around.

Circe's eyes narrowed. It couldn't be. Unless…?

"What's wrong?" Coal asked, voice distorted by the mage he was chewing between his teeth. Clenching his jaws, he popped the mage's head, then spat the lifeless body out to fall to the ground.

"Boreas is not the only great power on the field." Circe said, eyes serious. "Follow me."

Anankos roared, following Circe's direction higher into the sky towards the pure white clouds.

Coal let out an eager shout, moments behind his son.


X


Achilles cut down another of the red monsters, an afterthought as he bolted around the battlefield.

"We need to find where the mist is coming from." he said, punching his shield into a mage's neck. He heard a crack. The mage fell limp as he sped away.

Matatabi snarled unhappily from where she was secured about his neck. "I can't smell. I can't hear. I can't see. It's blocking everything."

Achilles frowned beneath his helmet. That was a bit of a problem. Achilles had no idea what he was looking for. Despite his status as a legend, he was out of his depth where magic was concerned. In his new life, that wasn't a very big problem considering the great skill of those in Balthazar's peerage, but even they weren't sure what was happening right now.

"Down!" Matatabi hissed.

Achilles grunted as Matatabi rapidly grew to the size of a panther, pulling him backwards. They fell in a tangle of bronze armor and flaming fur, rolling across the ground as their momentum carried them forward. Both managed to find their feet, grinding to a halt as they turned to face the threat Matatabi had sensed.

Achilles watched through narrowed eyes as the point of a spear retracted from the ground, pulling away to disappear back into the mist. If Matatabi hadn't pulled him to the side, that spear would have struck him in the left ankle.

"So this is the great Achilles!" a mocking voice taunted. Achilles could just barely make out the outline of a man slowly walking out of the mist. "Greek legend lauded as one of the greatest warriors to ever live!"

The man was in full view now. He wore a dark hoodie and sweatpants. Dark, unkept hair fell erratically around his head. He wore no armor, carried no weapons. The only thing on his person was a small, golden apple held in his palm.

"I'm disappointed." the man said, taking an obnoxiously loud bite of his apple. Golden juice spilled down his chin. He distractedly wiped the juice away with the sleeve of his hoodie before tossing the apple over his shoulder.

Matatabi growled, pouncing on a large, lumbering red monster approaching from behind. She rapidly grew to her full, enormous height as more and more monsters of red armor and shadow flooded towards them out of the mist. Matatabi beat them apart with her tails. She sundered them with her claws and fangs. Azure fire slagged them into the ground.

The castle's defenses screamed to life, raining multicolored rays of light down onto the approaching enemy. Dark tendrils of shadow rose from the ground to bind the monsters and pull them apart, but there were just so many. For every one that was destroyed, there were five more charging out of the mist.

How were there so many of these things?

Achilles didn't turn his attention away from the man in front of him. His instincts warned him the man was dangerous before he casually discarded a divine apple no Greek would be able to mistake. Achilles wasn't sure what he was facing, but he knew it was important that he deal with it swiftly.

Achilles's muscles tensed. The next moment, he launched himself towards the man, spear reaching. His spear let out a shrill ringing sound as for the first time since Achilles had held the weapon, the point failed to pierce its target.

The man grinned at Achilles, his features quickly hidden by a flash of gold, leaving a sturdy golden helmet with flared horns. It matched the rest of him. His lazy clothing was gone. Radiant armor of golden scales hugged his body close.

"Come, Achilles," the man taunted, voice far deeper than it was before. Achilles watched as a long, snaking neck sprouted from the armor at the man's back. The neck ended in a dragon head with razor-sharp teeth, glaring hatefully at Achilles. Another grew, looking over the man's other shoulder. Then another. Then another.

Achilles took a cautious step backwards as ten dragon heads loomed over him, all sprouting from the man's back.

"Let's see which legend is greater!" the man called.

Snarling, three heads lashed out towards Achilles. Achilles easily sidestepped them. He tossed his spear into the air, drawing his sword to make three quick slashes before sheathing it again. He caught his spear and danced away as two more heads struck at him.

Three severed dragon heads lay on the ground, leaking golden ichor.

The man nodded appreciatively, holding his chin as he looked down at the severed heads. "Not bad, Achilles. I guess you're not all hot air after all. That's better." A great tearing sound assaulted Achilles's ears as three more heads grew from the man's back to replace those Achilles had just severed. "Killing you will mean a lot more if you really are everything people seem to think. No one is going to want to fuck with Achilles's bane."

Achilles dashed to the side, avoiding the grasping fangs of two more dragon heads. Immediately, four more charged towards him from all different directions. Achilles charged into one, shoulder-charging its neck and rolling down its flesh. His shield bashed another head to the side while he stuck his spear clean through another.

If severing the heads just caused others to grow back, what would happen if Achilles just killed the head and left it attached?

The heads ceased their attempts to bite him, instead caging him in from all sides, wrapping their scaled necks around him to trap him. Achilles was pulled backwards as the man in the armor ran backwards.

The amethyst mist behind him, until now slowly encroaching, rapidly expanded, hastily covering both the man and Achilles himself.

Achilles's sword flashed, severing four heads to cut himself free. Achilles sprinted away from the mist in the direction of the castle.

He made no progress.

The landscape did not change. He was surrounded by an absence of color on all sides. Darks and greys were the only break from the endless amethyst mist.

Laughter echoed all around him.

"Too bad," the man's mocking voice assaulted Achilles's ears. He sauntered out of the mist back into Achilles's sight. The heads Achilles severed had grown back. The head he'd stabbed his spear through had fallen away from the armor. It too was replaced by a functioning head.

"You have no idea what you're up against, do you? You might have had a chance if you hadn't let yourself get caught, but now you're fucked." the man taunted.


X


Matatabi roared, hurling blue fire all around her to slag her enemies into nothing.

The tiny creatures weren't a threat to her, but there were so many of them. No matter how many she tore apart, more emerged from the mist to replace them.

Matatabi frowned, sniffing at the air. Achilles's scent was gone.

Matatabi's eyes widened as she looked back and saw the demigod had disappeared. In his place was only mist.

"Achilles!" she roared, stomping on three more creatures as she leapt to where she'd last seen him. She sniffed around. His scent was in the area, but he was gone.

"You need to keep better track of your toys."

Matatabi spun around, claws already reaching.

A heavy paw beat hers aside as a massive weight crashed into her. Matatabi howled as sharp fangs sunk into her back.

Matatabi flared her fire, burning the mouth of whatever dared mar her. She bucked and rolled, tossing the creature away.

Matatabi rolled to her feet, tails flared threateningly behind her. She lowered her chin to the ground as she hissed threateningly.

Across from her, a large monster slowly stood, wiping blood from its mouth. The creature had the body of a great lion with massive wings extending from its lower body.

Matatabi's eyes narrowed. A sphinx.

"You attacked us." Matatabi said, voice low and dangerous.

The sphinx scoffed, slowly stalking around her. "Your King has fashioned a supernatural monopoly around himself. He didn't care how many he drove out of business with his immense greed and thirst for more. The market requires competition to thrive. His presence eradicates competition, spitting in the face of commerce. I will take my compensation from his home, and use its riches to restart the great trade empire his foolishness destroyed. Caruna Trading and its many worthy competitors will rise to prominence again."

"I don't care why you're here." Matatabi said, a growl creeping into her voice. "You attacked us. You die."

The sphinx barked out a short laugh. It opened its mouth to reply, only to squeal, its eyes going wide in shock as Matatabi pounced.

The sphinx rolled as Matatabi fell atop it. They traded blows with their claws. Matatabi flared her fire, scoring deep burns into the sphinx's underbelly.

The sphinx screeched. Blue energy gathered around its body.

Matatabi was blasted away as a magical circle struck her with the force of a speeding truck. Matatabi crushed many red monsters as she rolled to a stop. She smacked a few shadow monsters with her tails for good measure.

The sphinx huffed, standing up and dusting itself off. "You certainly act like the beast you appear to be. We could be far more civilized about this, but you insist on–"

"Die." Matatabi snarled, maw opening wide. A single point of pure darkness opened between her jaws, quickly swelling, growing as large as Matatabi herself.

"What are you–" the sphinx's cry was cut off as Matatabi roared, launching the Tailed Beast Bomb forward.

A magical sphere flashed to life in front of the sphinx protectively. Matatabi's Tailed Beast Bomb smashed through it like it wasn't even there.

The sphinx was too close to dodge now. The bomb stuck it in the side as it turned to flee. The sphinx's dying screech was swallowed by a titanic boom as the bomb detonated, blasting the sphinx apart.

Matatabi snarled, furiously unleashing another Tailed Beast Bomb into a group of red creatures, then another into shadow monsters.

When all the enemies around her had been blasted away, Matatabi rushed back to where she'd last seen Achilles.

What happened to him?

Shang Tsung's eyes were shut tight. A massive boom shook the air. The ground quacked with Boreas's fury.

Shang Tsung hesitantly opened his eyes. He lay on the ground at Sairaorg's feet. A hundred meters away, Boreas stood before a smoldering crater, glaring towards him hatefully.

Mothra fell from Sairaorg's shoulder to land heavily on Shang Tsung's chest.

A pained song of concern.

Shang Tsung sighed as a heavenly feeling spread from his chest throughout his body. Azure scales rained from Mothra's wings down upon him as the small moth frantically fluttered her wings.

"Sai, please watch over my Pawn while he heals." Balthazar Abaddon said, stepping in front of Shang Tsung protectively, placing himself between the wounded Pawn and the furious god.

"I can help you fight." Sairaorg said simply, watching Boreas with narrowed eyes.

"I know." Balthazar said. In a flash of violet light, a long staff appeared in Balthazar's hand. Balthazar slammed the end of the staff into the ground.

Laying flat on the soil as Shang Tsung was, he felt the ground itself respond to Balthazar's presence.

"But this is personal." Balthazar said, voice turning into a growl.

"Personal?" Boreas cried. "You took my daughter, Balthazar!" Lightning crackled around Boreas. The winds howled as the god slowly levitated into the air. "I will have my vengeance in blood. Martin, now!"

The air shimmered and a man in dark robes appeared. He hefted a brass staff and directed it at Balthazar.

Glowing golden lines of magical energy snaked up Balthatazr's legs, moving to encircle his waist when they shattered.

Boreas's eyes widened as he stared in disbelief.

The man in the robes staggered backwards, mouth opening and closing uncomprehendingly. He gasped as a long silver blade punched through his chest. Aqua stepped out of his shadow, kicking his body away to let it fall dead to the ground.

Balthazar raised an eyebrow at Boreas. "Was that supposed to do something?"


X


"Was that supposed to do something?" I asked, more disappointed than anything else. This bastard brought an army to my home with the intention to kill me and everyone I care about, and this was all he managed?

I'd be insulted if I wasn't so grateful he was an arrogant idiot. Had he been competent, we might have had a harder time dealing with the attack. As it was, he was the only one left.

Boreas stared in dumbfounded shock, mouth slowly opening and closing. I didn't know it was possible for gods to be flabbergasted, but here we were.

"No," Boreas said in a confused whisper. "No. This isn't… No!"

Power erupted from Boreas's body. The icy clouds above, left behind by Khione to slowly dissipate, thickened and darkened. A mighty wind roared over the grass.

"You will die, Balthazar! I will ensure it!" Boreas called. The sky rumbled above.

I'd had enough of this.

I hefted my staff, sighing as I felt it empowering me. Holes opened all around, filling the sky like hailstones. You couldn't move two feet without falling through one. Fire spilled into the air, roaring into a raging inferno that turned the sky orange. Spears, daggers, swords, axes – all manner of enchanted weapons sailed through the blaze to strike Boreas.

Boreas roared in fury. The flame was burning him, but he was far more resistant than the underlings he'd brought. The spears and daggers that managed to get through the tumultuous winds around him without sailing haphazardly off-course struck him with the force of a ballista, but they still only scraped his skin, leaving minor facts and abrasions. The god was much tougher than those I'd fought in the past.

Boreas threw his arms above his head and roared. The clouds above crackled with electric power. At Boreas's command, lightning thundered down from the sky towards me.

I stepped back through a Hole, appearing opposite Boreas, I needn't have bothered.

Boreas's features twisted in fury as the crimson barrier around the castle stretched upward, intercepting each bolt as they rained down.

Medea's voice reached into my head. 'I will protect you. Kill this bastard.'

I grinned. How could I disappoint my dear wife?

I floated through the air over Boreas, watching as his eyes tracked me. He tried to call more lightning down on my head, but Medea's shields took the strikes.

Seeing his attacks were ineffective, Boreas switched tactics, sending blades of sharpened wind towards me as he flew up into the air after me.

I opened Holes in front of each attack, harmlessly sending them away. What few I missed were swallowed by shadows or stopped cold by crimson barriers as Medea covered me.

I continued leading Boreas back and away from the castle. All the while, my Holes roasted him alive with elemental fire. His skin was beginning to char.

Roaring in pain and fury, Boreas exploded towards me on a gust of wind, hands clasping towards my throat.

I smiled, stepping back through a Hole. I appeared atop my castle and looked up at Boreas. I had brought him close to the edge of the castle's protections as I was leading him away. Maybe he thought I was making a mistake and was trying to get me further away from my peerage. I hadn't made a mistake. I just didn't want to ruin my lawn.

Five Holes appeared around Boreas, rapidly expanding to the size of a truck.

Five Tailed Beast Bombs erupted from the Holes, moving towards Boreas from all sides.

Boreas exploded upwards on a gust of wind. He managed to dodge three of the blasts. He was too close to avoid them all.

An explosion rocked the air as two of the Tailed Beast Bombs connected. The clouds were scattered. Blades of grass were buffeted so violently by the shockwaves and furious wind that they tore free of the ground.

Boreas's body was sent sailing down to the ground, leaving contrails in his wake. The god was visibly injured now. Golden ichor dripped from many wounds covering his body. I didn't know it was possible for divine entities to bruise, but Boreas's flesh was covered in discolorations, one taking up the entire right side of his chest.

Boreas slowly rose from the crater, panting painfully, glaring murder at me. "Next time, you fall, Balthazar."

My eyes narrowed as he summoned a cloud of vapor around himself. Like hell was I letting this bastard get away. Dozens of Holes opened around Boreas, burning away the water vapor with flame.

Medea seemed to share my sentiment.

Massive shadowy tendrils exploded out of the ground all around him, batting him around like a pinball, sending him tumbling away. Violet skeletons crawled free from the soil, charging towards Boreas with glowing spears and hammers.

Boreas snarled, sundering nearby skeletons with blades of wind and shocks of lightning that bounded between the skeletons.

I watched Boreas flounder from atop my castle. The staff in my hand lengthened, morphing into a golden-tipped spear.

With a roar, Boreas slammed both his fists down atop a larger skeleton, crushing it.

I stepped through a Hole.

Boreas gasped, arcing his back to look up at the heavens. Slowly, he looked down at the golden point of my spear pierced through his chest. Numbly, he reached up, incomprehending as he tried to pull on the spear.

I stepped back, tearing the spear out of his chest.

Spasming, Boreas fell backwards. He started to seize. Golden blood sprayed all around.

There was a massive, gaping hole in his sternum the size of a baseball. Dark, diseased lines grew along the edges of the wound, rapidly expanding outwards. As the disease spread, Boreas's flesh began to rot and crumble out in a ripple.

Boreas was blabbering like a child, eyes unfocused as his body twitched uncontrollably on the ground.

This was a god? I was sorely disappointed on behalf of all his followers.

I hooked a hand under Boreas's ankle, lifting it up and dragging his seizing body through a Hole.

When I emerged, I felt a weight lift off my shoulders.

Shang Tsung was standing now. Mothra was still attached to him, crawling all over his chest shaking blue scales of healing energy onto his form. He looked haggar, but he was alright.

"Shang Tsung," I said, drawing his attention. I yanked Boreas's leg, calling on the strength my Sacred Gear was granting me to toss Boreas at my Pawn's feet. "I have a gift for you."

Shang Tsung's eyes glowed as he stared down at the God of the North Wind. "Master…thank you."

"I'd hurry." I said, watching clinically as the diseased rot festering in Boreas's body began to eat away at his chest.

Blind to the world around him, Boreas was convulsing, unable to so much as manage to speak as he convulsed on the ground.

Shang Tsung bent down, grabbing a fistfull of the misty ice that was Boreas's hair, dragging the god's body up. "Like your daughter before you, your soul is MINE!"

Some far away part of Boreas's mind was able to register that he was in pain. A scream slipped past the god's lips as a hurricane of green energy was sucked out of his body into Shang Tsung. The rot slowly eating away at his chest dramatically hastened, spreading to disintegrate Boreas's abdomen and down into his legs.

Shang Tsung seemed to grow taller as the energy poured into him. What remained of the wounds he suffered were gone, healed by the torrent of energy flowing into him. His eyes glowed, arcane green then misty grey. Electrical energy crackled through his hair.

Shang Tsung's lips parted. A low growl grew into a loud, thunderous roar as the last of the green energy was sapped from Boreas.

The once powerful god's body fell to the ground, a sickly, malnourished mockery of its former glory. The black disease transmitted from my spear made quick work of what was left, turning the body black as bits and pieces fell away to scatter into the grass. Soon there was nothing left but darkened bones and muck.

Shang Tsung looked to the sky, arms out at his sides, every muscle tense as he roared. The green energy swimming around him settled into his body, fading.

That was not the end of the light show.

A sinister red light exploded into being, making all other lights seem dim by comparison. The glow emanated from Shang Tsung's chest. A small Pawn set in Shang Tsung's breast erupted with demonic power. The Pawn seemed to expand. Through my connection to it and to Shang Tsung, I felt as the Pawn changed.

Shang Tsung's scream tapered off with the red glow. He staggered backwards, panting.

I was at his side in a moment, laying a hand on his shoulder and looking him over. "Are you alright?"

Panting out of breath though he was, Shang Tsung's smile was brighter than the stars. "Master, I have never felt better."

"His Pawn mutated."

I looked up. Shang Tsung, Mothra and I weren't alone. We'd gathered quite the audience. With almost all of the fleeing mages dealt with, nearly everyone from mine and Sairaorg's peerages was present except for Coal and Irene who were tracking down the last of the ones that managed to slip away.

Sairaorg had been the one to speak, watching on in open-eyed fascination.

"What do you mean?" I asked.

"Evil Pieces can mutate when they make jumps in power that place them above where they should be relative to their King." Kuisha explained, stepping up to Sairaorg's side as she too looked at Shang Tsung. "He just…absorbed power from Boreas. He's too strong to be a Pawn anymore."

I frowned, looking at Shang Tsung. I could definitely feel the Pawn was different, but I wasn't sure it was just a simple mutation. I was metaphysically tethered to Shang Tsung in a way Sairaorg and Kuisha weren't. I knew there was something else.

'His Pawn mutated into a Mutation Pawn then forced him into a Queen promotion after he absorbed Boreas's soul.' Medea said in my mind, reaching through our own connection to examine what happened to Shang Tsung. 'I do not think there is a way to turn the promotion off. It feels locked on.'

I sighed, relieved it wasn't something damaging. So long as Shang Tsung wasn't about to burst from the power he'd taken, we could sort it out later.

I looked back up at Sairaorg. "Thank you for coming."

Sairaorg grinned at me. "I don't think you needed the help, but you're welcome all the same."

A blinding flash of pink light exploded into the space.

Tense as mine and Sairaorg's peerages were, many of them fired spells at the figure to emerge from the teleportation circle.

Serafall Leviathan emerged from the light, easily smacking the spells aside. She looked murderous. Instead of her usual suitcoat or magical girl attire, she was wearing a suit of thin platemail covered in cool blue arcane designs. I'd never seen her in armor before. I had to admit though, the dark metal and icy designs really suited her.

"I didn't realize the teleportation block was down. Where is he? Are you alright?" Serafall demanded.

Moments later, a dozen other pink flashes filled the air around her. A sea of devils I didn't recognize flooded into my lands, all armed and armored for war.

Mami and Ingvild appeared at Serafall's side. Seraphine followed a moment later with someone I hadn't properly met, but still recognized, a woman with bone-white hair and dark skin. Behemoth, Serafall's Rook.

A dark void opened in the air behind Serafall. A crackling storm of pure nothing emerged. Crimson hair whipped around as its owner scanned their surroundings.

Sirzechs Lucifer met my eyes, then slowly turned to look over my perfectly fine peerage.

Sirzech's destructive aura vanished as he drifted through the air to Serafall's side.

"Are you okay, Balthazar?" Sirzechs asked.

"I'm fine. It's done." I said, waving for Serafall and Sirzechs to relax.

Serafall's eyes narrowed. "What do you mean, 'it's done'?"

Sairaorg stepped up beside me, slapping me on the back. He had a wide, proud grin on his face, almost as if we hadn't just been fighting for our lives against a team specifically designed for the purpose of killing devils. "It means Balthazar is collecting titles like trading cards. Lady Leviathan, I present Viscount Balthazar Abaddon, Godslayer."

Sirzechs left soon after realizing he'd missed the action. Before coming to help, Serafall had thrown up a signal that marshalled their forces to a war footing in case there were other invasions. Sirzechs left to go control that before it spiralled out of control.

I invited Serafall and Sairaorg into the castle while our peerages helped organize the cleanup outside.

I quickly summarized events from the start of the fight to Boreas's death. Serafall was silent through it all, absorbing my words with a calculating glint in her eyes.

"How did they have so many Longinus Sacred Gears?" Serafall asked.

Sairaorg held up his hands defensively. "You don't have to worry, Bal. I saw a lot of weird things today, but you're my friend. You gave me my mom back and helped me become Heir Vapula. That, and you'll be my brother-in-law soon. No one will hear about any of this from me."

"I'm glad to hear that."

Serafall looked sceptical. "Alright. Surprise me."

'Serafall is our greatest ally. I would likely name Sairaorg our next greatest ally. I believe it is time to extend a little more trust. Sairaorg did risk himself and his peerage to come to our aid afterall.'

'That wasn't ominous at all.'

'Oh, it will be fine. Play along, husband.'

With Dimension Lost, it will be nearly impossible for anyone to ever attack us again. We will likely even be able to transport the castle to other locations through the mist. "Our armies?" I asked.

Opening her eyes, Medea looked up at me. "We will be going to war soon. Serafall cannot stop this now, especially after freeing and reincarnating Chimera, Ladon and Perseus."

"Perseus?" I asked.

"My new Knight." Medea said proudly. "You know I earned my Evil Pieces some time ago. I reincarnated Perseus after the fighting was over. Zeus will not be able to stomach the thought of his son and great-grandson both 'enslaved' to the same devil house. That reminds me. Achilles is in Lucifaad. He will return shortly."

"Is he okay?"

Medea had an amused smile on her face as she said, "He told me he would, 'Run right up to the High-Class center and rip a set of Evil Pieces from their hands if they didn't give him them willingly. He took Patroclus with him. He's going to make Patroclus his Queen."

"Is it only the two of them?"

"Kuisha volunteered to transport them. Shang Tsung and Mothra accompanied them for added security."

I nodded. "Good." I doubted anyone would be able to seriously give Achilles or Patroclus any trouble, but I was still on edge. If Boreas was able to hire so many Longinus wielders to help him, there might be others waiting to attack us.

I sighed, pulling Medea tight against me. "This could have gone really bad."

"But it didn't." Medea said. "We'll be even more protected next time. Two gods, a valkyrie, monsters, mages, and Longinus users failed this time. I will make sure next time we are unassailable."

I placed a light kiss against her temple. "What would I do without you?"
