#9,137
No.

This wasn't what was supposed to happen. He'd taken steps to prevent this outcome. How were things worse than his vision?

Remiel, archangel, Heaven's Guiding Light, moved about in a frantic panic. Through the blessing he bestowed upon Father Martin, he was able to observe events through the loyal priest's eyes. With so many powerful allies gathered around him, Boreas should have had no issue slaying Balthazar Abaddon. It should have been a slaughter.

It was. Boreas and his allies were slaughtered.

Balthazar not only slew Boreas as Remiel had foreseen, but his witch had committed an affront against God himself, stealing God's gifts to mankind and turning them to the cause of the devil scum.

Such sacrilege must not stand. Remeil knew Balthazar Abaddon was a threat to the world. His actions against Boreas only proved Remiel's fears were true. If the devil was not stopped now, he would grow far too large a threat for anyone to contain.

Remiel threw open the doors to the halls of Heaven, dashing past shocked angels in his haste.

Michael looked up from their father's throne, surprised at the sudden visit.

"Remiel, it is good to see you, brother." Michael greeted warmly, but confused. "I thought you were–"

"Balthazar Abaddon and the witch Medea are able to steal Sacred Gears from mankind." Remiel declared.

Silence fell in paradise. The ever-pleasant atmosphere of the halls of Heaven was corrupted by worry.

Michael's eyes hardened. "Are you sure, brother?"

Remiel didn't answer. Holy Light gathered from his halo, projecting images Remiel watched through Father Martin's eyes before the brave man's death.

Remiel had already welcomed the priest into Heaven. His fight was over. Remiel's had just begun.

Shocked gasps and worried conversation broke out as angels witnessed Medea rip Sacred Gears from their rightful holders.

Michael's expression was grave as Remiel dismissed the images. "I noticed a deviation in the Sacred Gear system. I assumed it wasn't cause for concern. Is the witch able to bind the Sacred Gears to others?"

"I do not know, brother." Remiel said. "Regardless, we cannot allow this to stand. Balthazar Abaddon has proven time and again he cares nothing for the world, only power. He has brought the world onto the brink of war. The Greeks and devils will surely battle now. Their conflict will ravage the mortal world that we are charged to protect. Balthazar and his witch must not be allowed to continue this. They already have multiple Longinus. For the threat they pose not only to the world but to our Holy Father's creations, we must act."

Michael appeared conflicted. Voices swelled behind Remiel as other angels voiced their support of Remiel's words. Others silently watched, awaiting Michael's mandate.

Michael's features turned grave. "We cannot allow humanity to suffer. If the devils are able to make use of these Longinus Sacred Gears they have stolen, if they are twisted to whatever purpose the devils turn them towards… Father's creations must be protected." Michael turned pointedly to Remiel. "I will attempt to resolve this peacefully. Should I fail, you have my blessing to deal with this threat."

Remiel approached Michael, bending at the waist to kiss the back of Michael's hand. "I will not fail you, brother." Remiel turned and levitated up on his wings, hurriedly exiting the hall.

Many angels joined him, pledging their support. Remiel would need them. He would gather other allies. Remiel had seen Balthazar's true strength through Father Martin's eyes. He would not be taken by surprise again. Remiel would turn his future sight against Balthazar. This time, he would not be led astray. He would leverage the information Father Martin gave his life to learn to ensure victory.

The devil would die.


X


Well this was certainly interesting.

Azazel, Governor of the Fallen, Cadre of the Grigori, reread the report in his hand, checking to make sure he hadn't misread it the first time.

Setting the paper aside, Azazel's brilliant mind began to work through the information he'd received.

It was no great secret that the different factions of the supernatural spied on one-another. Azazel knew the identities of most of the spies in his ranks. He didn't get rid of them because he could control what information he gave them. Azazel himself was slightly better at protecting his informants.

How else would he have managed to keep a true angel in Heaven supplying him with information for so long?

Michael had stirred his siblings up into a storm. The reason? Medea Abaddon could steal Sacred Gears from their mortal users and the Sacred Gear system itself.

The angels were frantic, not knowing how to respond to this information. They were panicking, terrified of the thought of devils with so many Longinus Sacred Gears.

Azazel was more reserved. He knew better than anyone that it was possible to separate a Sacred Gear from its host. He'd done it himself dozens of times now. But to remove it from the system itself? Azazel had to either bind his stolen Sacred Gears quickly or put them in a stasis to prevent Heaven's system from reclaiming the creations of his Father. If Medea could really destroy Father's hold on the Sacred Gears…

Color Azazel intrigued.

If only Azazel had learned about this before the world was poised to tear itself apart. The devils were all but certainly going to war with the Greeks. Heaven would likely try to take advantage of the chaos to kill as many devils as possible. Every faction would be watching closely, looking for any opportunity to take advantage of the chaos.

Azazel sighed.

Azazel was the Governor of the Fallen. His siblings looked to him to guide them. He'd grown to resent that. What he wouldn't give to thrust the title on to someone else so he could disappear into his lab to never resurface.

No. Azazel had responsibilities. He desperately wanted to approach the Abaddons, but he had to weigh the consequences for everyone who depended on him.

Why was nothing ever easy?


X


Three figures stood around a table. A report lay in front of them, a missive sent by one of their few spies in the New Satan's ranks. Their spy did not know everything that had transpired, leading to holes in the report, but it was better than nothing, enough to plan.

A tan-skinned woman, the only female present, said, "Balthazar Abaddon was already a figure of interest before. After somehow surviving an attack made by a god, we can no longer put off approaching him. He must be made to fall in line or eliminated."

A man in dark armor with brown hair shook his head. "After a god and multiple Longinus Sacred gears failed to dispose of him? Attacking him would be beyond foolish. No. Balthazar has worked for the betterment of devils since he unseated his uncle. If we approach him in the correct way, I am optimistic he will be willing to listen to us."

A pale man with dark hair slammed his fist on the table. "Balthazar is consorting with Serafall. It's no secret he openly calls her his friend. I will not ally with a fool who stands with the false Satans."

The woman narrowed her eyes. "Careful, Creuserey, that fool just killed a god."

"And in so doing," the brown-haired man said, "Brought the New Satans to the brink of war with Olympus. That will present an opportunity for us."

The woman glared at him. "I have no interest in ruling over a crater, Shalba."

"Hell will need to be remade one way or the other once we retake our rightful place." Creuserey said dismissively. "Think, Katarea, it will be all the easier to rebuild if the Greeks do the difficult part for us."

"Hell is not the limit of my ambition, Creuserey." Katarea countered. "How are we to lead devils to destroy our ancient enemies if there are no other devils to lead?"

"We will not allow Olympus to act with impunity." Shalba said appeasingly, drawing the attention of his compatriots. "The false Satans may weather the bulk of Olympus's power. We will protect those devils the New Satans forget. We will be seen as saviors, the true power we were always meant to be in Hell."

Creuserey frowned. "And the Abaddon?"

"You need not worry about him." Katarea said firmly. "You would act too rashly. Leave Balthazar Abaddon to me. He is a power we cannot afford to dismiss out of hand."

Shalba nodded. "Then I see no reason for this meeting to continue. I will marshall our forces. Expect to hear from me again soon."

One-by-one, the descendants of the old satans, the true rulers of Hell, teleported from the room.


X


Serafall had enough on her plate already. Boreas, god of stupidity, just tried to kill her golden ticket. Serafall was pissed, but she was tempering that rage. Flying off the handle wouldn't fix what was broken. Things were balanced on a razor's edge. She needed to move very carefully.

She had enough to deal with. Her secretary calling her and telling her Michael was demanding a meeting with her was not something she needed to deal with right now.

Serafall stormed into the mortal coffee shop, scanning the interior. On such short notice, she couldn't arrange security sufficient to let an archangel into Hell. Michael similarly didn't want her in Heaven. They'd selected neutral grounds in the mortal world to hold their meeting. Serafall hoped it would be brief.

Humans carried on benign conversations and sipped overpriced drinks as they milled around the area. A man in a pure white suit sat alone in a back corner. Golden hair framed intense features. He watched her closely as she marched over to the table and sat across from him.

"You don't meet with me in person often." Serafall said, skipping the formalities. "Whatever this is, let's just get to the point. We're both busy."

Michael's face was impassive. He watched her reaction closely as he said, "Yes, I imagine you have much to do following Boreas's attack. That is why I have come to speak with you. We must discuss the Sacred Gears Balthazar Abaddon has stolen."

Serafall's eyes narrowed. Frost slowly gathered atop the table beneath her balled fist as she glared into Michael's eyes. "So Remiel wasn't acting alone."

Michael's intense expression twisted as his lips dipped into an uncertain frown. "I do not know what you are insinuating."

Serafall scoffed. "Don't insult my intelligence, Michael. I know Remiel sent the priest to kill Balthazar. I know he's the reason Boreas brought so many mercenaries with him." Serafall grinned viciously. "Pass along my thanks when you see him next, will you? I never would have expected him to do me such a wonderful favor."

Michael's features hardened. "The Sacred gears must be returned, Serafall. Immediately."

"And why in creation would I ever turn our spoils of war over to you?"

"A single Sacred Gear is one thing. A Sacred Gear's host joining a peerage is another. So many unbound Longinus together in one place will upset the balance of power in the supernatural."

"You seemed perfectly fine with things being unbalanced when it was Heaven that benefited from the arrangement. Give me a reason to not walk away from this conversation right now."

Michael's eyes narrowed. "Serafall, I am trying to help you. You will go to war with the Greeks. It is almost certain now. How will the other pantheons respond when they see Hell has accumulated so much power? They will join with Olympus to eradicate you. Work with me and I will help your race avoid extinction. We have been enemies for so long, but I tire of our constant conflict. Returning the Longinus is the gesture we need to achieve true peace. Please, Serafall."

"So I give you what you want in exchange for a vague promise about maybe securing peace?" Serafall shook her head. Her chair scraped against the ground as she stood. "This was a waste of time. Next time, just go back to sending Gabriel. At least she is easy on the eyes. You…"

Serafall trailed off as a stone woven into her bracelet hummed.

Frowning at the interruption, Serafall adjusted the bracelet, brushing her thumb over the stone to activate it.

'Serafall!' Falbium's voice screamed into her mind. 'We need you! It's the Baels. We…'

"Serafall?" Michael said, confused as he watched Serafall's expression twist into a look of shocked horror.

In a flash of icy blue light, Serafall's skirt suit was replaced by dark armor. A pink teleportation circle whisked her away before Michael could get out another word.


X


Zekram Bael delicately cut into his steak. He took a bite, savoring the divine flavor of the meat. Truly, Helios's prized cattle were some of the finest stock he had ever consumed.

"I trust everything is to your liking?" Zekram said simply.

"It is delicious." Lord Gamigin complimented, raising his glass in a salute.

"It is, you are an exceptional host, my lord." Lord Naberius said.

Zekram didn't respond, leaving the devil lords to wonder if their groveling had any effect. It did not, but Zekram would allow them to think he welcomed their presence. They were still useful to him, doubly so after their shared conquest of Thrinacia.

Despite the financial hardship Zekram was experiencing as a result of Helios's tantrum, the ancient devil could not help but be pleased. His agents were second to none. He was notified of Boreas's attack on Balthazar Abaddon before anyone else. Zekram had been mobilizing his own forces to assist when Sirzechs Lucifer ordered everyone to stand down.

Balthazar had defeated Boreas alone. No. Not alone. Sairaorg Vapula, former heir to the Bael Pillar, arrived to support him.

Once more, the strength of Zekram's bloodline was proven to all. Soon, his bloodline would join with that of Balthazar Abaddon through Sairaorg's marriage to Kuisha. Zekram eagerly anticipated their child. With their uncle and their father as a guide, surely that child would rise to heights yet unseen.

As it should be. The Bael legacy was one of supreme power. It was only right that all of Zekram's descendants thrive.

"You brought your peerages as I instructed, I hope." Zekram said, not looking at his guests as he took another bite of his steak.

"Yes, my lord." Lord Gamigin replied immediately. "I assume you require Helios's daughters for some purpose?"

Zekram nodded, allowing Lord Gamigin a minor boost to his pride as if guessing something so obvious was worthy of praise. "I do. I am sure you are aware of Helios's…ill-advised retaliation against me. I intend to disabuse him of further actions. But before that, how have his daughters settled into your peerages?"

Lord Naberius grumbled. "She is rebellious. She refuses to accept the truth of her situation. My Rooks must discipline her constantly."

Zekram offered him an easy smile. "I'm sure that, with time, you will overcome her rebellious attitude. Now, to the reason I summoned you here."

Zekram frowned, feeling a ping through the wards at the far edge of Castle Bael's lands.

That was strange. Who would dare trespass in his lands?

The door to the room was thrown open.

"My lord!" the panicked form of the current Lord Bael, a disappointment in every sense of the word, staggered into the world. "Someone has–"

"Silence." Zekram ordered, wiping his mouth as he stood. "At least pretend to be competent."

Zekram stormed past his weak descendant. Even Magdaran, unmotivated thought the boy was, eclipsed Lord Bael's pathetic presence. Zekram was disgusted to have such weak spawn born of his blood. Every family must have at least one disappointment it seemed.

Dark energy gathered around Zekram's body as he teleported to the castle's exterior.

"My lord," a guard, armored with the Bael family's crest proudly displayed on his chest, greeted Zekram. Dozens of others were already gathering atop the wall.

"Who dares trespass on my lands?" Zekram asked.

"Our scouts will return momentarily, my lord." the guard replied. "I would request that you retreat to the safety of the castle. My men and I will–"

The dark sky of the Underworld was illuminated by a rage-filled golden glow. The horizon was lost in a blinding shine. It was as if a star walked through Hell.

Many of the guards let out shocked cries of fear.

Zekram's eyes narrowed. He refused to show weakness. Even in the face of what approached.

Standing astride a golden chariot pulled by mighty beasts of burden, Helios, Titan of the Sun, armored in divine metal, rode through the sky towards Castle Bael. Flanking the chariot on either side were dozens of forms Zekram couldn't even begin to identify. His attention was fixed on the Sun.

"Zekram Bael!" Helios shouted, raising a whip bursting with the power of the Sun above his head. "You destroyed my paradise. You enslaved my daughters! Retribution has come!"

"Marshall the defenses." Zekram ordered. "He was a fool to strike us here."

It seemed Zekram would have yet another opportunity to prove the Bael blood's supremacy. Much like Boreas assaulted Balthazar Abaddon, Helios would attack him.

Zekram would deal with Helios himself. This battle would be over before Sirzechs arrived to assist his ancestor.

"Guard, take your troops and–"

Zekram hissed in pain, clutching at his side.

"My lord!" the guard cried, slashing his sword through the air at Zekram's side.

An unholy shriek sounded as a spectral, serpent-headed form was cut apart by the guard's blade.

Growling, Zekram ripped the dagger out of his side. Energy crackled around his body as he glared up at the approaching chariot.

Zekram would smother the Sun.


X


Sirzechs Lucifer walked through rubble. Splintered wood and fractured stone crumbled as he walked past. Sirzechs' emotions were far away. He felt muted, subdued. He couldn't feel anything.

It was all gone. They were all gone. It was a blessing Magdaran was still at Castle Abaddon with his new Queen. Sirzechs didn't even want to think what would have happened if every Bael was killed in this attack.

Sirzechs flinched as Ajuka laid a hand on his shoulder.

"Are you alright?" Ajuka asked.

Sirzechs didn't answer. He couldn't even begin to express his feelings about this. The Baels were his kin, yet, despite Sirzechs' efforts, they always felt more like competition than family.

Seeing Castle Bael, a shining symbol of devilkind's power, reduced to splinters and nought but memory was haunting.

Why hadn't the Bael's called for help? Why hadn't Zekram reached out to him? Sirzechs would have come. He would have defended them. Why didn't they notify anyone that they were under attack?

"We need to respond." Sirzechs said, voice filled with iron.

"That was true when it was just Boreas." Serafall agreed, eyes scanning the ruins for any sign of life. "After this? There's only one option."

"War." Falbium said simply, eyes determined.

Sirzechs nodded. "Then we're all in agreement."

"I'll get in touch with Odin and set a meeting with Athena. It's best we do this officially. I don't want to give anyone any more ammunition to use against us right now. Things are precarious enough." Serafall said.

"Good. Let me know when you are ready." Sirzechs said. "I… I will stay here a moment."

Serafall and Falbium teleported away.

Ajuka stepped up next to Sirzechs' side.

"You don't have to stay. We have so much to do to prepare." Sirzechs said.

"Serafall and Falbium are exceptionally competent. At present, you require my presence more than they do." Ajuka said clinically, but Sirzechs was able to hear the emotion Ajuka attempted to hide.

Sirzechs smiled at his friend. "Thank you." His smile disappeared.

Together, the two Super Devils looked out over the ruins of what was once the greatest house in Hell.


X


Athena sat impatiently, tapping her finger on the table in front of her. "Where is she?" Athena demanded.

"She has not sent word that she is not coming. Be patient." Odin said. Once more, Serafall had insisted on using the leader of Asgard as their go-between. It was insulting, as if Serafall couldn't trust Athena to deal with her fairly.

Still, Athena couldn't fault the devil too much. Recent events had…strained things between them.

Athena and Serafall never had a positive relationship, but they were professional. Together, they were able to mitigate their two people's many grievances. In recent days, that had been a steadily failing endeavor.

Athena's father – Zeus, Lord of the Skies – was incensed. She hadn't seen him like this in hundreds of years. Minor gods and goddesses openly defied him at every turn, citing Zeus's overreach and their own desire for freedom from his 'tyranny'. Mortal worship had steadily dried up as the Abrahamic factions solidified their power in regions once devoted to Olympus. And, of course, Zeus's new target of rage.

Balthazar Abaddon.

Zeus never cared when devils reincarnated Greek individuals in the past. Most were beneath his notice, not even worth remarking about. Athena still did her job, squeezing concessions from Serafall for each talent poached from them. Athena understood their position was steadily weakening as time wore on. She could not afford to allow the devils to continue stealing prominent Greeks with no recourse.

Then Hephaestus complained to their father that fewer people were purchasing his wares. That was the beginning of Zeus's interest in Balthazar Abaddon. When Achilles was reincarnated, he took it as a personal slight. How dare a devil think to steal Zeus's legacy?

Zeus demanded restitution from Balthazar himself. He would work as Hephaestus's assistant as he learned his place. Zeus was mighty proud of himself for coming up with that punishment. He'd thought to solve both grievances at once. Wasn't he so great?

Athena knew Serafall would never agree to such lunacy, but it was the only thing her father would listen to. She'd only barely been able to talk him down from attempting to smite the Abaddon boy the next time he was in the mortal world.

Olympus couldn't afford a war. Not now. While the greater powers of her faction were exemplary, some of the strongest in the entire world, the median strength of the devils was superior to that of their forces.

And the devils outnumbered them 40 to 1. The number of their Pillar devils had steadily waned with time, but the number of reincarnated devils and devils without houses was vast.

At the best of times, it would be difficult to face them. Now? It would be a fool's gambit.

Too many minor gods openly defied Zeus. Many higher powers were steadily slipping free of his control as well. Hades scarcely responded to Zeus's call at the best of times, let alone now. The Titans that allied with Zeus against their ancient brethren did not appreciate his paranoid overreach nor his dismissal of Helios from their faction. Selene and Eos were enraged to hear Zeus would take no actions to recover their nieces, taken by Zekram Bael during the destruction of Thrinacia. Athena hadn't heard from them in close to a month now.

It wasn't the first time Zeus's followers found his rule lacking. Measures were put in place to prevent future resistance. Now, those on Olympus itself would follow him without question.

Olympus's power was great, but Athena did not wish to see it tested against the devils, not if she could avoid it.

All the more reason for her to feel irritated that Serafall was so late to their scheduled meeting.

The Leviathan contacts her out of the blue claiming that Boreas organized a force to kill Balthazar Abaddon and demands her presence to sort matters, hopefully averting a devastating war neither of them wanted. Athena dropped everything and appeared at the designated place and time. Nevermind Boreas was no longer welcome on Olympus. Zeus had cast the God of the North Wind out. Serafall knew this and was free to deal with Boreas as she saw fit. Still, in the spirit of peace, Athena came.

Yet Serafall still wasn't here.

Athena loudly pushed her chair back and stood, turning to Odin. "Serafall has wasted enough of my time. If she ever deigns to appear, tell her–"

Athena was cut off as a dark flash swallowed the room. Four figures appeared in a dark burst of teleportation magic. Athena opened her mouth to berate Serafall for her tardiness. Her mouth snapped shut as she noticed who had accompanied Serafall.

Athena was expecting to meet Serafall alone as she had done in the past. She hadn't expected to meet with each of the Four Great Satans of Hell at once.

Serafall stepped to the head of the group, adorned not in the skirt suit she typically favored, but dark armor glowing with icy blue magical power. It didn't escape Athena's notice that the stressed out, desperate expression she'd worn to their recent meetings was gone. In its place, was a furious glare promising pain.

"We had a deal, Athena." Serafall said darkly. "I would keep mine in check. You would keep yours in check."

Athena stood her ground, not willing to let the presence of the other Satans intimidate her as was likely Serafall's intent. "I have held up my end Serafall. Boreas was cast out. He no longer represents Olympus. Whatever has been done with him is of no concern to us."

Serafall's expression didn't shift in the slightest. She didn't blink as she stared deep into Athena's eyes. "What of Khione? Was she cast out?"

Athena frowned. Khione? Come to think of it, she hadn't heard news of the goddess since shortly after Zeus's decree to banish Helios and Boreas. Khione had petitioned Zeus for support and left in a rage when she was denied. Athena hadn't heard a tale of her since. Surely she wasn't stupid enough to join Boreas in his attack?

"If Khione was involved, then–" Athena was not able to continue as Serafall cut her off.

"What of Selene? What of Eos? Were they cast out?"

Athena's eyes narrowed. What was Serafall implying? "I can assure you, Selene and Eros have no reason to strike at Balthazar Abaddon."

"You're right. They didn't attack Balthazar. They assisted Helios as he completely destroyed Castle Bael and all of the devils within." Serafall said, voice cold and emotionless as ice.

Athena felt her skin go cold. Her eyes were unfocused. It was hard to breathe. "No… They wouldn't have…"

Falbium Asmodeus lifted something, hidden until now beneath the table, and tossed it atop the table.

Athena felt the air leave her lungs as the severed head of Khione stared deadly up at her. Golden ichor dripped from the severed stump of her neck to plop on the table.

"Consider this a declaration of war." Sirzechs Lucifer said coldly, dark energy fluttering around his eyes. "You attacked a single Pillar House while it was unprepared. I wonder how you will fare against the full might of the 72 Pillars joined together to destroy you."

Athena finally found her voice. "Serafall, listen to me. Let me–"

"It's done, Athena." Serafall cut her off, eyes murderous. "Leave and deliver our message to Olympus. From this moment on, we are enemies."

Athena swallowed, desperately trying to think of a solution to this mess.

She couldn't.

In a bronze flash, Athena returned to Olympus.

Sitting atop a Golden Throne wearing nought but a thin toga, the white-haired form of Zeus lazed. A trio of giggling nymphs petted at his arms and legs while one sat in his lap, tracing a finger over his jaw.

"Father," Athena announced.

Zeus dismissively waved her away. "Not now, Athena. I am busy."

"The Devils have issued a declaration of war." Athena announced.

All sound ceased. Dozens of heads turned to look up at Zeus atop his throne.

Zeus's amused expression turned to one of surprise, then eagerness. He jostled the shocked nymphs away and stood.

"Good," he announced. "It has been far too long since the mortal world witnessed our power. We will remove the parasites from the world and display our great strength!"

Athena swallowed a lump in her throat.

She did not expect this would end well.


X


The ocean was in turmoil.

Fantastic beasts dashed about erratically. Beautiful forms sculpted from all of the ocean's greatest beauties were marred by worry. The ocean's daughters gathered in a secluded pool.

"The devils declared war!" one cried, a feminine shape with golden skin and silver hair.

"Zeus is calling for us all." A dark-haired woman with pale skin said, wringing her hands nervously.

"Good," another said, amber hair cascaded around delicate shoulders as she challengingly looked around. "It is time to deal with the threat they pose. Have they not taken enough from us already?"

"No," a woman with eyes the color of the darkest depths said. Unlike her sisters, her expression was calm, resolved. "No, I will not fight Zeus's battles for him."

The third woman spun around, enraged. "You would refuse to answer the call of the Lord of the Sky? You would be a traitor!"

"Then a traitor I will be, sister. What has Olympus ever done for us?I can think of nothing but the pain their lust and greed has caused. I will not die in their war, not when my sister numbers among their enemy."

The third woman hissed. "Thetis and Idyia made their choice. Do not be so foolish as to replicate their folly. Am I not your kin as well?"

"You are a fool still lusting after Zeus's attention, begging him to take you as he has taken so many against their will. I will not join you in your desperate gambit to gain his attention. No. I will go to Idyia. She will take me in."

A tense silence filled the cove. The ocean's daughters looked between one-another anxiously. Expressions hardened as lines were drawn, sides were silently chosen.

"I cannot let you go." the third woman said threateningly.

Dark eyes narrowed. "Then stop me."

Water churned and roiled as a dozen goddesses unleashed their fury against one-another.


X


Sirzechs, Ajuka and Falbium were quick to leave after Athena departed. Serafall lagged behind, heavily falling into a chair as she sighed.

"That happened." Odin commented, expression guarded as he slowly sat at Serafall's side.

"It was the only way forward." Serafall said quietly. "Three Greek Titans nearly eradicated an entire Pillar. If it were just the attack against Balthazar we maybe could have figured something out, but this…?" Serafall shook her head.

"For what it is worth, I apologize for Hildr's role in the attack on Castle Abaddon." Odin said. "We did not realize she was gone until last night. She must have been coordinating with them in secret."

Serafall waved off his apology. "You wouldn't have ordered her to try to kill Balthazar, not knowing what you know. I know she was acting alone."

Odin tilted his head. "You do not desire concessions?"

"There's only one thing I want." Serafall turned to fully face him. "When I was here last, you said Asgard wouldn't stand by if it meant losing access to what Balthazar can give you. Did you mean that? Do you still mean that, knowing what it will entail? The Greeks will only be the first wave. Others will see us weakened and try to take advantage of this war. Michael himself practically admitted the Angels would take a swing at us."

A small smile spread across Odin's face. "Few of our adversaries have bothered to pay attention to us in recent years. They have failed to notice as we grew strong. We've only scratched the surface of what we can accomplish by allying with the Abaddon boy and we're already leagues ahead of where we were before him, and we were certainly not weak before. I think Zeus and his inbred pantheon have wreaked enough havoc on the world. I would rather reach a peaceful resolution to this conflict, but if it must end with their eradication, the world will be better for it, I think."

Serafall nodded slowly. "Alright. I'm going to send one of my people to coordinate with you. Lucifaad will be open to Asgard. Send your own agents there and have them come to my office. Please don't make me regret lowering the wards for you."

"You will not. A little raven told me Chimera and Ladon are free of their Sacred Gears. Why would I alienate an ally that could perhaps do the opposite and seal away the monsters that would bring about Ragnarok?"

The temperature in the room slowly lowered. "How do you know that?" Serafall demanded. Very few people had witnessed Chimera and Ladon's prisons breaking, and she doubted Odin had heard it from any of them.

"I sent Huginn and Muninn to Hell when I learned Hildr was gone. I was going to call them back when the battle ended, but they saw Coal leading Ladon and Chimera around before they came back." Odin explained calmly.

Serafall frowned. She hadn't noticed the ravens. Then again, she'd been focused on other things, and those ravens were created to be the best covert spies the leader of Asgard could ever ask for. Still, she'd set up some precautions later.

Serafall stood. "My agent will be here soon. Lucifaad is open to you. I expect we'll meet again soon."

Odin stood, offering his hand. "That we will…ally."

Serafall shook his hand with a nod. "Allies. Farewell."

Serafall stepped back and vanished in a flash of pink.

Serafall rushed through the halls of her home, feeling for a miniscule drain on her demonic power, following it.

"You're back!" Ignvild said, the first to notice her. Mami looked up and let out a relieved breath when she saw Serafall.

"Has anything happened since I left?" Serafall asked.

Mami shook her head. "We're all fine."

Serafall nodded. "Good." She walked past her Bishop and Pawn, walking right up to the third woman in the room.

Seraphine, Serafall's warlock, shifted uncomfortably from foot to foot. "Is something wrong?"

"We're officially at war." Serafall said plainly, not wasting any time or sugar-coating things. She needed everyone to know what they were now involved in. "It's inevitable that you will all have to fight. I want you to be as protected as possible."

In a flash of crimson light, a glowing red chess piece appeared in Serafall's hand. "Ajuka wanted to run tests, otherwise I would have done this straightaway. Seraphine…you don't have to accept, but it will make you safer and–"

"Yes," Seraphine cut her off, stepping forward to grasp Serafall's hand and guide the Evil Piece towards her chest. "I… I thought you didn't think I was good enough."

Serafall smiled softly. "Of course you're good enough. I'm so glad I found you, Seraphine." Serafall pressed the piece into Seraphine's chest, pulling her head down so she could kiss Seraphine's forehead.

Seraphine gasped. Power exploded all around her. Seraphine threw her head back and screamed. Her scream turned to a powerful roar. White scales gathered along her arms and legs. Seraphine's roar cut off and the scales receded. She panted, eyes wide, smiling from ear to ear.

Serafall was pushed backwards as Seraphine tackle-hugged her. "Thank you."

Serafall smiled, holding her newest Pawn close. "Thank you, Seraphine."

As Mami and Ingvild walked close to join the hug, Serafall couldn't help as her mind wandered.

With this war on, she needed to do everything she could to bolster the strength of devils. She'd need to coordinate with Balthazar to take every moderately trustworthy devil that wouldn't speak about his ability to move between worlds to create a warlock or two. They needed the extra strength, especially after losing the Bael Pillar so unceremoniously. It would also work to hopefully safeguard Clan Traits. If Magdaran had been at Castle Bael when the Titans attacked, devilkind's hold on the Power of Destruction would have grown dangerously weak. They needed to safeguard their powers any way they could.

Maybe that wasn't the extent of how Balthazar could help? Balthazar promised to take her to find more magical girls. Sure, there was a war on and other things would take priority, but she had enough time to find one or two more, right?

Bad Serafall! Focus on the survival of your race first. Magical girls could wait.
