#9,312
Amethyst mist swam in and out of Castle Abaddon's walls. Hulking constructs of red armor plating walked patrols through the halls. The castle itself seemed to hum with hidden power.

Medea, Aqua and Irene hadn't slept last night. They were locked up in Medea's lab the whole time. The end result? Dimension Lost and Annihilation Maker were now bound to the castle, their power at the beck and call of anyone whose name ended in 'Abaddon'.

I could feel it, a gentle urging at the end of my awareness. It was as if the castle was alive, gently coaxing me to make use of its newfound power, begging me to unleash it against my enemies.

As Lord Abaddon, I felt something akin to loyalty from the castle. Medea reported something similar, though to a lesser extent from her last name of Abaddon and more in the vein of a creation showing deference to its creator.

Through this strange feeling, I could alter the castle's newly manifested will to grant others a modicum of influence over it, but the castle felt resistant against those not carrying the Abaddon name. When I removed Kuisha from the system, the castle resisted, only relenting as I gently explained she would soon be a Vapula, leaving us behind.

Arguing with a newly semi-sentient castle about who should and should not have access to its apocalyptic powers was not on my bingo card, but here we were.

Medea wasn't entirely sure where the castle's new mind came from. Was it a freakish happenstance of magic born from the union of two Longinus Sacred Gears with an already magically saturated castle? Was it an unintended consequence of Aqua using her Keyblade to unlock the castle's potential so it could host Sacred Gears?

We didn't know, and we had other things to focus on right now. The castle wasn't hostile to us, quite the opposite. It felt almost zealous in its worship of anything and everything 'Abaddon'.

The castle's new semi-intelligence seemed to come with good and bad. The good was that Medea and I didn't need to manually control any of the new protections. Even the old defenses she'd set into the walls seemed to be operating under their own power now. The castle worked independently of us, doing what it believed would be most beneficial to its Abaddon masters. With a war with Greek Gods looming, that meant printing disposable soldiers with the efficiency of a newspaper publication and spreading defensive mist all through our lands to prevent any more surprise teleportations.

The bad? Well… The castle didn't like answering to anyone that didn't share my last name, even those in my peerage. It recognized them as members of my house who belonged within its walls and who it must protect, but it didn't seem to respect their authority to the same degree as myself and Medea.

I needed my peerage to have access to the castle's defenses and for the castle not to resent aiding them as weird as that was to say.

There was an easy solution. Something I'd been meaning to do for some time but hadn't got around to. After Serafall sent word of what happened at Castle Bael, it felt even more important to do this now.

The news of Castle Bael's destruction shocked everyone in Castle Abaddon. At the time, Sairaorg was still present with his peerage. Magdaran was also here, a small mercy. If he'd been in the castle when Helios attacked… It was a good thing he was here instead.

Magdaran broke down. It was expected. He just learned his childhood home, his family, and the many servants he was likely friends with in Castle Bael were all gone. He didn't know what to do.

Sairaorg took charge. Despite hearing his childhood home was nothing but rubble, he stood strong, gathering his peerage and distraught brother and taking them all back to the safety of Castle Vapula. He wasn't going to let his brother out of his sight. Before he left, Sairaorg told me to be on standby in case he needed my help protecting Magdaran. He thought it was possible Helios might try to finish the job and eradicate the last Bael.

Helios's battle was with Zekram. I didn't think he would attack Magdaran, but I also never would have expected the Titan to be so brazen as to attack Castle Bael.

I told Sairaorg he had my support. The looming threat of the Titan potentially taking issue with us was what drove Medea, Irene and Aqua to work through the night, working as fast as they could to bind the two Longinus Sacred Gears to the castle. We were able to fend off Boreas's attack. If three Titans came for us, I didn't know if we'd be so lucky. We needed a way to hide ourselves away so that we'd be unassailable – Dimension Lost.

It was done now. In their haste, the mystical craftsmen in my peerage had accidentally awakened an intelligence in my castle. We'd monitor the situation, but for now, the castle felt unwaveringly loyal to me, I needed to extend that to the rest of my peerage.

We were all gathered in a massive chamber Medea constructed to be a ballroom. The far wall held many windows overlooking my territory, obscured slightly by a thin mist swimming through the land. I hadn't hosted any balls yet, but there was certainly room to do so here.

"Thanks for coming." I said, stepping up onto an elevated stage meant for musicians to play live music. I turned and looked over my peerage. Perseus and Patroclus were here as well. Idyia and Thetis stood together at the back of the group. Mothra stood on Shang Tsung's head in moth form. Matatabi napped in the fire of a brazier on the wall. Every resident of my land was gathered.

"Have we heard from Serafall?" Shang Tsung asked.

I shook my head. "I imagine she's up to her neck in work right now. We'll try to figure out more of what's going on, but that can come later. There's something we need to take care of now."

I looked around, motioning at the castle walls. "I'm sure you've all felt the shift in the castle. Medea, Irene and Aqua succeeded in binding Dimension Lost and Annihilation Maker to it. An unintended side-effect is the castle is now partly alive. It's not a bad thing, but it is making certain things more difficult. The castle really likes Abaddons, to the point where it doesn't want to let anyone else use its defenses."

I paused, sighing. "Before all of this started, back when I was living in a small house with my sister, I had one major goal. I wanted to rebuild the Abaddon House. I wanted to bring us back to the standing we once held. Thanks to all of you, that goal was not only accomplished, but exceeded. The Abaddons have never been more powerful, but there's a problem. There aren't many of us. The Baels were just nearly eradicated, and they had far more people than we do. Once Kuisha becomes Lady Vapula, there will only be two Abaddons in Hell, myself and Medea. If I really want the Abaddon family to thrive into the future, we need to expand."

Aqua's eyes widened. "Is Medea pregnant?"

I was so caught off-guard by the question that I lost my train of thought. "I…what?"

"You need more Abbadons, so you're having a kid, right?" Aqua asked, excited. Her excitement slowly tapered off as she saw my evident confusion. "Or…not?"

Medea smiled softly, eyes far away. "While that would be great news, sadly, that is not the case."

I met Medea's eyes. In her mind, I said, 'You want kids?'

'Now isn't the time to discuss this, my love.' Medea said. 'Continue your announcement.'

Nodding in agreement to pause this conversation for later, I turned my attention back to my peerage. "No, Medea is not pregnant, but I do have a plan for expanding my house. At the start of all this, I came up with two potential ways to grow the house to what it once was. The first, and least personally appealing to me, was to follow in many other devil's footsteps and try to gather a harem and have a lot of kids. The idea of having a harem has never really appealed to me for a variety of reasons. Then I met Medea and found everything I would ever want or need, banishing any ember of thought that I might take that course. The second option was the one I always planned on using regardless. Are you all familiar with the concept of a branch family?"

Irene's eyes narrowed in thought. She gently rocked the slumbering form of Seri in her arms as she said, "You plan to bring outsiders into your house? I would caution you to choose wisely."

I smiled. "I already have. Most devils see their peerage as servants, some as slaves. I've never viewed any of you like that and never will. You're family. I think it's about time we make it official."

Some of my peerage looked around confused. Shang Tsung and Irene were the first to realize what I meant.

"Master, you…you want to make us Abaddons?" Shang Tsung asked, voice cracking with emotion.

I smiled warmly at him. "I'm extending the offer. Don't feel compelled to accept, but if any of you are interested, I'll gladly have you. I was planning on putting everyone who accepted the offer at the head of their own branch of the Abaddon family. We can sort out the finer details later, but if any of you are interested we can do this right now. I recently found out that as Lord Abaddon, what I say goes in regards to my family. If I name you an Abaddon, you're an Abaddon. It's that simple."

Silence fell over the room. My peerage looked between each other, some excited, others hesitant. Thetis and Idyia watched silently from the side, though I saw a knowing smirk on Idyia's lips.

Shang Tsung walked forward. All eyes were on him as he knelt before me.

"My lord Abaddon, words cannot express the depth of my gratitude to you. I was nothing. My destiny was to die in the dirt, forgotten and alone. You have elevated me far beyond even my wildest imaginings. I will gratefully accept your offer so I may continue to serve you for the rest of this great life you have given me." Shang Tsung said, almost choking on some of the words. I'd never seen him so emotional.

I walked down from the stage, bending down to help Shang Tsung back to his feet.

Smiling, I laid a hand on his shoulder. "I'd be overjoyed to have you. You've grown more than I ever could have expected since I reincarnated you. I'm excited to see where you go in the future. I name you Shang Tsung Abbadon, Head of the Shang Tsung Branch. We can workshop the name later if you want."

I felt a change come over Shang Tsung, myself and the castle itself. It was unexpected. When I made Medea Lady Abaddon, it had been simple, a matter of acknowledging the role my wife was already practically filling. This was different.

I felt a metaphysical thrum in the air as Shang Tsung became devil nobility in an instant.

My eyes narrowed. I reached out to Medea through our connection. 'You felt that, right?'

'I did.' she confirmed.

'Good. I think that's what the devils in Baator can use to sense us. We'll need to find a way to mask it when we're not swamped with preparations for war.'

'I will handle it, my love.' Medea said.

Shang Tsung fell to his knees before me. "I am honored, my lord. I will spend eternity serving this house."

"You don't have to kneel." I said awkwardly. "You're making me feel like an evil overlord."

A tingling query.

I blinked, looking at Mothra atop Shang Tsung's head. Her eyes stared up at me inquisitively.

"I mean, I don't have a problem with making you a member of the same branch house Shang Tsung is in. Shang Tsung, are you okay with that?" I asked my Pawn.

Shang Tsung looked up at me with a brilliant smile. "I would be overjoyed."

Shrugging, I said, "Mothra, I name you Mothra Abaddon of the Shang Tsung Branch."

Mothra preened, fluttering her wings. I felt the same change come over her that just went over Shang Tsung.

Behind them, Aqua hesitantly raised a hand. "Do I have to give a big speech and swear a lot of oaths?"

I smiled, amused. "That's not necessary."

"Cool. That's not really my style. I also don't really want a branch house. That sounds like a lot of work. Can I just be an Abaddon?" she asked.

"Aqua, I name you Aqua Abaddon."

She smiled, happy. "Thanks, Bal."

"Thank you," I countered. "So much of what I've accomplished wouldn't have been possible without you."

Achilles awkwardly shuffled from foot to foot. "Forgive me, my lord, but…"

I raised my hand haltingly. "If you don't want to take my name, then don't. I'm extending the offer, but I won't be offended if you don't accept."

Achilles visibly relaxed. "Thank you. I'm sorry, but–"

"You don't need to explain yourself. Like I said, I'm not offended. Does anyone else want to be an Abaddon?"

"Will anything change if I take your name?" Matatabi asked, one eye peeking open to look at me.

I looked up at where her fiery body was engulfed in the flame of the brazier. "Not if you don't want it to. You could build your own–"

"I'm good." Matatabi cut me off, her eye closing again as she shifted to get comfortable.

Chuckling, I turned back to the others. "Anyone else?"

"I accept, my lord." Irene said, dipping into a very shallow curtsy. "If you are willing, I would like my own branch as well. May I ask that you also give my daughter your name?"

"Irene, I name you Irene Abaddon. I name your daughter Seri Abaddon. I name you head of the–"

"Belserion." Irene cut in, a conflicted emotion passing over her face.

I nodded. "Irene, I name you head of the Belserion Branch of the Abaddon family." I looked up. "Anyone else?"

Coal smiled at me. "I appreciate the offer, master, but I already took a new name. I'm Coal. That's all I need."

"Understood. Anyone else?" I asked.

Keno hesitantly raised a hand. "I… Could I have your name? I don't need a house, but…"

"Keno, I name you Keno Abaddon." I said.

A bright, happy smile spread across Keno's face. "Thank you. I… Thank you."

I turned to the last member of my peerage. "Shiroe?"

Shiroe swallowed nervously, looking around as he became the center of attention. "I… Can I have some time to think?"

"Of course. This can happen any time. If you decide you don't want it, I won't be offended. Take all the time you need."

Shiroe visibly relaxed. "Thank you. I need to think about it."

Shang Tsung raised his hand. "Master, can you rename my branch to the Soul Branch?"

I raised an eyebrow at him. "You want to broadcast that you steal souls?"

Shang Tsung shook his head. "It's not that. It just… It feels right."

I pursed my lips. "Mothra, are you okay with that?"

Chittering agreement.

"Shang Tsung, I declare your branch is renamed to the Soul Branch."

Shang Tsung smiled softly. "Thank you, master."

"Don't mention it. That's all I needed from you guys. Thanks for meeting with me. If you need to rest after the attack or have preparations you need to make for the war that is definitely happening soon, you're released to do whatever."

Aqua and Keno left through a Keyhole. Shiroe and Irene both teleported away. The rest all slowly filed out through the halls. All except for Matatabi. She was still asleep in the fire of the brazier.

With that one move, the future of the Abaddon family was all but assured, regardless of what happened in this war.

I had no intention of letting the incestuous gods on Olympus kill me, but it would be arrogant and naive not to acknowledge that it was possible I wouldn't make it through this. Now, with or without me, my house would thrive.

We wouldn't even lose our oh-so-coveted Clan Trait Hole. Aqua's Keyblade, while not exactly inheritable in the same way a Clan Trait was, did just about everything I could do only better. Hell, Shang Tsung and Keno could use Hole itself, albeit with less skill than I did. Maybe they'd get better as time went on?

As the last of my peerage filed out of the grand ballroom, I turned to Medea at my side. 'Kids.' I said in her mind.

Medea smiled softly. 'Yes. I want children. But now is not the time. Fighting a war pregnant is not wise. We already have one infant to care for during this conflict in Seri. Adding another will complicate matters.'

'I don't want to rush. We just got married. Let's enjoy that for a while after the war. Assuming we don't die, of course.'

Medea scowled at me. 'Do not even speak of such things. You will not die. I will not allow it.' She walked forward and wrapped her arms around me, pulling me into a hug.

I sighed, leaning into her. It felt like I was in heaven.

Naturally, that was when my phone rang.

Grumbling, I pulled back from Medea to answer my phone.

"Yes?" I said, failing to hide my irritation.

"I need you, Bal. Are you free to come to my office?" Serafall said quickly, sounding distracted.

"What do you need?"

"I need transport. Shouldn't be said over the phone. Are you free?"

I shared a look with Medea. 'Call me if anything happens. I'll drop anything and come back.' I said in her mind.

She nodded. 'I will watch over things in your stead. With Dimension Lost, another attack against us is nearly impossible. We will be fine.'

"I'm on my way." I said into my phone. I hung up then leaned into Medea, pulling her against me into a deep kiss. She eagerly reciprocated. I lost myself in her embrace.

After what felt like centuries but also only a moment, I pulled back. "I'll see you soon."

I stepped back into a Hole. I emerged in front of Serafall's office building in Lucifaad and pushed the door open.

I froze in the entryway, falling into a defensive stance, demonic power thrumming through me.

Serafall's secretary was in her usual place behind Serafall's desk. There was another figure with her.

A tall, muscular, brown-haired valkyrie looked at monitors over the secretary's shoulder. The valkyrie looked up as I entered.

"Balthazar Abaddon, yes? The Leviathan is expecting you." she said. Her piece said, she returned her attention to the monitor, resuming her quiet conversation with the devil secretary at her side.

Watching the secretary and the valkyrie, I made my way to the elevator at the back wall.

I rode the elevator up and walked into Serafall's office.

Serafall stood with her back to the door, leaned over her desk.

"I ran into a valkyrie downstairs." I said conversationally as I entered.

"We've burned a lot of goodwill with the supernatural. Asgard is so far our only ally." Serafall said simply as she turned around, a stack of papers in her hand.

"You said you need transport. Faerun?"

She nodded. "We need every advantage we can get right now. Ajuka gathered a group of devils he's vetted as being trustworthy. I want to try to get them all warlocks."

I frowned. "How many people are we talking here?"

"Twenty."

I shook my head. "I don't see my secret staying a secret with that many unknowns."

Serafall sighed. "It already isn't a secret, Bal. Why do you think Asgard is allying with us? Odin already figured out what you can do. It's just a matter of time until everyone else does."

"What do you mean Odin figured it out?"

Serafall shook her head. "Something about the materials you traded them not being possible to have generated in our world. I don't know the specifics, but he put it together. We need to take full advantage of this before everyone figures out what you can do and comes after you. I've started organizing a team to guard your lands. They'll–"

"That's not necessary." I cut her off.

Serafall shook her head. "I get you don't want strangers around, but after Boreas, others will–"

"No, I mean it's already taken care of. Medea bound Dimension Lost and Annihilation Maker to the castle. No one will be able to touch us."

Serafall looked up, surprised. "Medea was able to bind a Longinus to an inanimate object? You bound two Longinus to your castle?"

"Castle Abaddon is now likely the safest place in our world. Even if someone arranges a force capable of assaulting us, we can just disappear into the mist. No one is going to attack my home again." I declared.

I still hadn't tested the limits of that, but I knew it was possible. If we activated Dimension Lost, would the castle just vanish from reality, returning when we deactivated the Sacred Gear? Or would we be able to transport the castle around?

I'd always wanted to live in Castlevania…

Serafall digested my words for a moment before nodding. "I'll disband that team I was going to send you. That lets me allocate them elsewhere. But I still need your help getting these devils warlocks. They're only the first group, the trial run. If it works, I imagine we'll be taking more. Can I count on you to transport them?"

I frowned. "I don't like this, Serafall. My power comes from my monopoly on other worlds."

"Yes, and now we're facing a pissed off Greek pantheon that has already demonstrated the capability and willingness to eradicate the strongest Pillar in Hell. We need the extra firepower."

I sighed.

I really didn't want to turn into a multiversal taxi, but if the Greeks kept slaughtering their way through the Pillars, then everything I'd built would be at risk. They needed to be stopped.

Still, I wanted to protect my monopoly.

"Fine." I said. "I'll transport this group. I make no promises for the future though. I have my own preparations to make. Have your devils bring a mortal with them that they like, maybe a contracted magician. We can use this as an experiment to see if we only need Baator's system or if it has to be people native to that world too. Hell, maybe see if they can make other devils into warlocks. That would be interesting."

Serafall pursed her lips. "What are you planning?"

"I'm trying to keep my cards close to my chest. None of them will have any reason to suspect they're going to another world. I have some facilities set up in Faerun that I can clear out to make it look like one of Ajuka's labs or at least a research site. We can say you're using me to transport them so no one knows where the location is. Bringing their own warlock candidates prevents people from Faerun spilling that they're in another world. If they figure it out anyway, then at least I can say I tried."

After a moment, Serafall nodded. "Okay. I'll need a minute to tell them to bring others along."

"Take your time. I need to go clear out one of the workshops near a mine. Call Medea when you're ready. She'll let me know and I'll open a Hole from right here in your office to the warehouse. Sound good?"

"Sounds good. I'll see you in a bit, Bal." Serafall vanished in a flash.

I stepped back through a Hole.

I looked around. Crystals, tools and carts lay discarded around the underground workshop. I'd need to clean this all up. Luckily, I could cheat.

Holes opened to swallow everything incriminating, sending everything back to Castle Abaddon.

I frowned, thinking. I stepped back through another Hole, heading home for a brief moment.

I walked up to the nearest wall of my castle and laid a hand on it. "I need creatures designed to thrive as miners. I also need a host of monsters that can protect them. How long will it take you to make them?"

The castle wall beneath my hand pulsed, as if the castle itself was thrilled, eager to serve.

A slinking form sloughed onto the floor behind a tapestry. A thick, bulky form rose from the ground, stepping out from beneath a table. All around me, misshapen monstrosities crawled from shadows.

Smiling, I patted the wall appreciatively. "Thank you. Please continue making them. Either Aqua or I will transport them where they need to go."

Holes opened around each of the monsters, sending them to my mines. I walked into the last Hole, returning to Faerun.

I stuck my hands in my pockets and leaned against the rough, rocky wall of my underground workshop. I'd finished cleaning and securing an even larger workforce in just around five minutes. Serafall likely wouldn't be ready for a while yet.

I waited for a few minutes in silence before frowning. Evidently, the devils she gathered weren't expecting to bring mortals with them. Some likely didn't have contracted magicians and were scrambling to find someone that would work. I'd apologize to Serafall, but even by agreeing to this I was doing her a massive favor. I knew it was inevitable that people would learn of my ability, just look at Odin, but I wanted to maintain what advantage I still had while I could.

Sighing, I pushed off the wall.

Serafall might be a minute. I didn't want to just sit around and wait. It had been a minute since I checked in on my warlocks. They also didn't know I was at war. They could use an update.

I walked into a Hole. I appeared beneath the shade of a large tree in front of Cyvis's ancestral home, hidden from prying eyes by vegetation and the large stone wall around the exterior of the grounds.

Hands in my pockets, I walked up to the front door. I pulled the cord on the bell and settled in to wait.

"My… My lord!" Cyvis's panicked voice answered almost immediately through the door's enchantment. "Please come in!"

"You're not busy are you?" I asked as the door swung inward on its own. "I don't want to create problems for you." The last few times I'd been here, I just barged in and left Cyvis and Vellia to awkwardly explain my presence to their subordinates. I was trying to do better.

"Your presence is never an imposition, my lord. Please, come in. Rath will meet you in the entryway and lead you to me."

I stepped inside and was immediately met by a thin male elf with dark hair I recognized as the groundskeeper Rath Lain.

Rath bowed deeply as I approached. "If you would follow me, my lord Abaddon. Lady Cyvis awaits you in her study."

I followed quietly as he led me up to Cyvis's office. I'd been here enough now that I knew the general layout of Cyvis's home.

Cyvis stood as Rath opened the door for me. She straightened out her dress and dipped into a curtsy. "It is always an honor to see you, my lord."

Holding back a sigh at the formality, I said, "You can relax, Cyvis. Haven't I said all that is unnecessary?"

"You have, my lord." Cyvis said, eyes averted. "But such disrespect would be improper. You are my lord. I shall respect you as such."

"Whatever makes you more comfortable I suppose." I said, resigned.

"Pleasurable as I find your visits to be, my lord, you rarely come without a purpose. May I ask how I can assist you?"

I winced. "Sorry about that. I have been barging in a lot recently, haven't I? It wasn't my intention to put you out, but events forced my hand. I apologize."

"Your apology is unnecessary, my lord. It is a privilege to serve."

"Well, you can relax for today. I don't need anything. I'm just here to check in."

Cyvis looked up finally, eyebrows furrowed. "To 'check in', my lord?"

"I just wanted to see how you and Vellia were doing and let you know about some developments back home. Actually, where is Vellia?"

"Vellia is in town recruiting for an expedition we have planned. I will recall her." Cyvis said, reaching into a pouch at her side.

"That's not nec–"

"Vellia?" Cyvis said, holding a stone up to her lips.

After a moment, Vellia's voice spoke from the stone. "I'm here, Cyvis."

"Our lord is here. Your presence is requested."

"I'll be right there." Vellia said, frantic.

I rubbed my forehead, sighing. "Tell her to find an alley or somewhere else out of view. I'll transport her."

As Cyvis relayed my order, I closed my eyes, reaching out to the small drain on my demonic power that would lead to my second warlock.

As I focused, I felt the drain. It was different than it was before. It felt…weaker. I thought something was wrong, so I reached out to my connection to Cyvis. Hers was the same. The drain didn't feel as strong as it once did. Did my warlocks siphon less of my power as they grew stronger?

…Did I somehow grow stronger, making the drain less noticeable? I hadn't been training nearly as much as I once had. Come to think of it, I hadn't done much of anything to grow in recent days. I'd been too focused on overseeing my peerage, my business, Serafall's contact with Dispatar… Damn. I've been busy.

Maybe killing Boreas did something? Did my Sacred Gear siphon power like Shang Tsung could? Or was this all something unrelated? Maybe killing a god in general just left after effects on the killer? I'd look into it.

But it got me thinking. I hadn't been growing recently. That hadn't really been a problem. In recent days, my challenges have been rating games. I could just cut my peerage loose in those and not worry. I was at war with Olympus now. I needed to do something. I couldn't hide in Castle Abaddon forever. Even if we could use Dimension Lost to pull our home away from reality, something we still hadn't tested, we couldn't spend eternity hiding behind its walls. I didn't want to have to leave DXD behind, I had too many friends there, too much invested. That meant we'd have to deal with Olympus and anyone else that might come after us.

I needed to get stronger.

"My lord," Vellia greeted as she emerged from a Hole. She knelt on the ground before me, head bowed low. "It is an honor to see you again."

"You can relax, Vellia." I said, giving up on ever getting her and Cyvis to cease with the bowing. It was likely just a product of where they'd lived their lives. Faerun was very different from the environment I grew up in. "It's good to see you too. Cyvis said you were preparing for an expedition?"

Vellia smiled proudly as she stood, still not looking directly at me. "That is correct, my lord. We are preparing a journey to Kharad-Veth. Cyvis believes we will be able to create a foothold there. With time, we could even grow to control the city, reestablishing it as a point of trade between the surface and the Underdark."

I nodded, impressed. "You two have certainly been busy. Let me know if you need anything. I can fund you and supply manpower pretty easily. If you need debris cleared or buildings repaired, recent events have made it trivial for me to supply you with manpower."

Cyvis's lips pulled into a small frown. "'Recent events', my lord?"

I waved away her concern. "A god attacked me. Well, two gods. Two-and-a-half? Three? I'm not sure how demigods count, but there were two of those in addition to the two gods. We killed them and took their toys. You don't need to worry about it."

Silence fell in the study. Vellia's eyes were wide. She looked frozen in place. Cyvis's jaw opened and closed. No sound emerged.

Right. Maybe don't casually admit to killing gods in the presence of people whose concept of divinity is different.

"They weren't the same as the gods you have here." I explained. "Much weaker. We have divine powers back home that rival and even surpass most gods here, but these two were certainly not among them. Well, at least the stronger ones."

"My lord," Cyvis said slowly, finally finding her voice. "I have borne witness to your power. I am still awed. I… Perhaps this is a foolish question, but is there anything myself or Vellia can do in our limited power to assist you?"

"Neither of you need to do anything. You're already doing marvelously here." I assured them. "I hadn't expected you'd try to take over that city. That's a great undertaking. You should focus on that."

"We intend to take Kharad-Veth to better aid you, my lord." Vellia said with passion. "The city is pointless if we lose your patronage."

Cyvis flinched slightly. "That is the primary reason, my lord. But…"

I raised an eyebrow. "Is something wrong? You don't need to worry about disappointing me, Cyvis. Just tell me the issue. I'll help if I can."

Cyvis swallowed nervously, shaking her head. "I would never add to your troubles after you were attacked by gods, my lord."

My head fell into my hand. "Cyvis, please, just tell me what's wrong."

Cyvis shared a look with Vellia. They seemed to have a silent conversation.

Cyvis stood tall, back straight, muscles tense. "My value to you will soon lessen, my lord."

I blinked, confused. "Um…what?"

"My parents sent word. They are returning next month." Cyvis said. "When they return, my father will once more be at the head of the house. I… I expect he will not be pleased with the actions I have taken in his absence. I am not his heir, yet I have used his treasury and influence for my own purposes."

"If money is the only problem, just tell me how much you need to pay him back and I'll cover it." I said easily. I was beyond rich. If throwing some money around could keep Cyvis on good terms with her family, I'd consider that money well spent.

Cyvis seemed shocked at my blase offer. She squeezed her eyes shut. Was she holding back tears?

"Thank you, my lord," Cyvis said. "But that is only one problem, the less important of the two. I… I am a disappointment. My parents selected my brother as their heir because I failed to live up to their expectations. I have acted in their stead to create your mining company. They will be displeased."

My eyes narrowed as I looked between Cyvis and Vellia. Vellia squeezed Cyvis's hand in support. Cyvis was doing her best to hold herself together.

So Cyvis wasn't worried about her parents being angry and damaging her relationship with them. If I was reading things right, she was worried what they'd do to her.

I'd never gone out of my way to be a good person. Other people's problems were their problems, not mine. On the contrary, I had the capacity to be a right bastard when I needed to. I didn't delight in causing pain, but you could be damn sure I'd do what was necessary to secure my future and that of those close to me.

The thought that some prick had reduced my warlock to this level of fear pissed me off.

"Cyvis," I said, pulling her attention to me. "First, I want to be very clear. I don't count your worth by what you can do for me. Losing access to the Loralee family's influence won't alter my appraisal of you one ounce. Second, if you are worried about retaliation from your family, don't be. If they want to act against you, they will have to go through me."

Cyvis gasped. Vellia sucked in a sharp breath. Both stared at me in awe.

Oops. I didn't mean to flex my Demonic Power at them like that.

Few things could get me angry. Hearing about people trying to mess with my people was at the top of the list. So soon after Boreas tried to attack my home, hearing Cyvis was afraid of her own parents of all people was setting me off.

"I…" Cyvis fell into a deep curtsy, head bowed low. I pretended not to notice a single tear falling away from her face. "Thank you, my lord. If there is anything you require, I am at your service."

I pursed my lips. "I know you said you were planning an expedition to Kharad-Veth. How urgent is that?"

"It is not urgent, my lord." Vellia said quickly. "The city will remain hidden as it has for centuries. If you require our presence, we are at your service."

I shook my head. "Not so much that. You've both done great work. How do you feel about a vacation?"

My warlocks shared a look. "A vacation, my lord?" Vellia asked.

"Do you want to come hang out in my castle for a while?" I clarified.

Vellia's eyes flew wide. Cyvis went stock still.

"I would be honored, my lord." Vellia said, falling back to they round to kneel before me.

I sighed. "Please stand up." As Vellia stood, I frowned. "Fair warning, things are a little crazy right now. The devils of my world just declared war on the pantheon that attacked me. My peerage will be preparing for war, but you're welcome to stay as long as you like."

Vellia's expression hardened. "You are going to war, my lord?"

I nodded. "It's inevitable. I'm…kind of important back home. I don't think I'll be on the frontline, but I don't see a way out of this where I'm not fighting in some capacity."

I held back a sigh as Vellia knelt before me once more.

"My lord, please let me fight in your name." Vellia said. "Send me against your enemies, for they are my enemies."

"Me as well, my lord." Cyvis said, eyes determined. "You have given us great power, let us use it in your name."

"I didn't come here to recruit you to fight in a supernatural war." I said slowly. "The enemies I have back home are strong. Even I will need to…" I trailed off, frowning in thought as I looked between my warlocks.

Back when Vellia first became my warlock, I'd brought her back to the coliseum to test our bond. Every time she killed a skeleton, I received a burst of power from her. Later, when we all went to Kharad-Veth, with every demon Cyvis or Vellia dispatched, I felt a swell of strength as their kill empowered me, almost like a tithe to their contract holder.

I needed to get stronger, but I was likely going to be very busy in the near future. I wanted to separate Cyvis from the toxic situation here and give my warlocks something of a vacation for the good work they'd been putting in for me. What if I could kill two birds with one stone?

"Do you two know of anyone else who would make a good warlock for me?" I asked out of the blue, a plan slowly forming in my mind.

They seemed caught off guard by the question. Cyvis was the first to recover.

"I have been passively searching for individuals that would be able to serve you, my lord. I know of two – my parent's butler Rath Lain and a paladin who works as security for us called Tristan Vale. Is there a reason for your interest, my lord?" Cyvis asked.

"I don't want you two fighting my enemies, at least not until you are much stronger." I said seriously. "But if you want to help me, then I think there is a way for you to empower me with your actions. If I contract more warlocks before we start, the effect will be that much stronger." Turning to Cyvis, I said, "Is your butler not loyal to your father? Will he accept a contract?"

Cyvis seemed hesitant to speak. Finally, she said, "Rath's sister ran afoul of my father many years ago. Rath offered his service to repay his sister's debt. He signed a magical contract to bind him to my father's service. He has long since repaid his sister's debt, but my father has not released him. Rath has not attempted to break free for my sake. He has helped me weather the worst of my father's disappointment since I was young."

"One second," I said, confusing my warlocks.

'Honey?' I said in my mind, reaching out for my connection to Medea.

It took a moment for her to respond. She felt far away. The connection was sluggish, but ever-present.

'Yes, my love?'

'Serafall hasn't called you yet, has she?'

'Was she supposed to?'

'She will in a minute. Can I borrow you really quick before that happens? I'm trying to contract some more warlocks and I need you to sever a magical binding before I can move forward. I'll explain later.'

'I will be there momentarily.'

'Thanks. Love you.'

"My lord, may I ask…" Vellia trailed off as Medea appeared right next to me.

Vellia and Cyvis quickly bowed their heads to Medea. "My lady," they greeted as one.

Medea smiled warmly at them. "It is good to see you again." Turning back to me, she said, "What's this about a contract?"

"Can you call Rath here?" I asked Cyvis.

Cyvis's eyes widened, her breathing picked up. She touched a glowing stone on her desk, shuffling anxiously.

A polite knock came at the door before it was opened. Rath Lain stood in the doorway with his arms clasped behind his back. "You called, my lady?"

"Cyvis tells me you're bound by a magical contract to serve her father." I said with no preamble. With Medea here, Serafall's point of contact back home to let me know she was ready didn't exist. I wanted to get this done fast.

Rath frowned. "That is correct, my lord Abaddon. May I ask after your sudden interest in me?"

"I asked Cyvis who she thought might make another good warlock for me. Your name came up." I explained.

Rath seemed surprised, looking past me at Cyvis before returning his attention to me. "I am honored, my lord, but I would be unable to faithfully serve you. Sylas Loralee owns my loyalty."

"'Owns' isn't a great way to describe that relationship." I commented. "Are you happy with your situation?"

Rath smiled softly, acceptingly. "Worse things have happened to better people, my lord."

"That definitely sounded like a no." I said.

"He can't show disdain for his position, my lord." Cyvis said, staring intently at the groundskeeper. "It is part of his contract."

"Definitely a no then." I said. "Lovely wife, if you would?"

"I shall." Medea said, a wicked dagger already in her hand.

"My lord, what–" Cyvis started, sounding panicked as Medea lifted the dagger towards Rath's chest.

"Rule Breaker." Medea intoned, lightly pricking Rath's shoulder with the tip of her dagger.

Rath gasped, staggering backwards. His eyes flashed with dark magic. A magical tattoo nearly hidden beneath his collar shattered into nothing.

Rath took a deep breath, a wide smile spreading across his face. "Thank you, my lord. I haven't felt like this in years."

Cyvis dashed across the room, throwing her arms around Rath in a crushing hug.

I stayed silent, letting them have their moment.

'I will return home and wait for Serafall's call. Will you need my assistance with the warlock contracts?' Medea asked in my mind.

'I've watched you make two of them and saw Serafall make hers. I appreciate it, but I'll manage.'

'Very well. I will see you later, husband.'

When I turned to look at her, Medea was gone. There was no magical flash. She was simply gone.

"Thank you again, my lord." Rath said as Cyvis finally pulled away, wiping tears from her eyes. "I will gladly serve you for freeing me."

"This wasn't a transaction." I said. "If you don't want to sign another magical contract, this one with a devil, I'm not going to force you. Take your freedom and run if you want. It's your choice."

Rath smiled warmly at me. "That choice is why I choose to serve you. I have seen how Cyvis has transformed in your service. You took a poor girl lacking direction and purpose and turned her into a capable, ambitious young woman poised to take on the world. I would like to see what she becomes."

"If that's your choice, then I'll gladly have you. Give me a minute to write up your contract. Cyvis? I think you said something about a paladin as well? They aren't promised to a god here, are they? Poaching a god's paladin will piss them off."

Cyvis nodded, composing herself. "I did mention a paladin. He is not beholden to any lord. That is why I believe he will be a good choice for you. I will retrieve him, my lord." She vanished in a blue flash.

I blinked, surprised to see her teleport. Since when could she do that without using the rift ability I gave her?

Shaking my head, I produced a pen and paper from a Hole and began writing up Rath's contract. The groundskeeper walked up beside me and read over my shoulder. I let him follow along, explaining what would be expected of him and expected of me. In essence, it really just boiled down to 'don't stab me in the back and work with me when I tell you to'. Rath seemed more than accepting of the arrangement.

A loud popping sound like a spark of electricity heralded a blue flash. Cyvis reappeared in the room. At her side stood a very confused man with dark hair. I recognized him. It was the knight I'd seen the last time I barged into Cyvis's home.

The knight, evidently a paladin, looked around the room until his eyes fell on me. He sucked in a breath and took an unconscious step back.

It had been a while since I'd had access to a DND module, but didn't paladin's have some kind of supernatural sense that let them pick up on demons and the like? No wonder he'd been so uncomfortable around me last time.

"I take it from your reaction that you know what I am?" I asked him.

The man swallowed nervously, hand twitching towards the sword sheathed at his side. "You are a devil." he said, voice steady despite his evident unease.

"I am. Cyvis? I'm sure you had a reason for recommending him. Would you mind telling me why?" Probably should have led with that before meeting him, but she kind of disappeared before I could ask any more in-depth questions.

Cyvis bowed her head. "Of course, my lord. Tristan has expressed interest in finding a lord to serve. He offered his oath to me, but I could not accept as I was not truly Lady Loralee."

Tristan's eyes narrowed. "So you offer my service to a devil?"

Cyvis looked at him out of the corner of her eye, expression hardening. "Lord Abaddon is unlike any devil you have ever heard of. My own oath to him prevents me from saying why, but I can assure you, he is greater than any of the politicking, prejudiced lords you would find in this city, or any other on the Sword Coast."

I shrugged, handing Rath's finished contract to him over my shoulder so he could read through it. "If you're not interested, then feel free to leave. I don't want unwilling servants." I ignored the paladin, focusing on Rath as the elf read through the contract. "Any issues?" I asked.

Rath shook his head. "None. I expected far more limiting terms than what you have outlined."

"Constricting those under me is dumb for several reasons. I'd have to micromanage you, which is a pain for me, and you'd grow to resent the control. I'd rather have a mutually satisfactory arrangement. What do you want for a sign-on bonus? Every time we've gotten this to work, we've had to give the new warlock something. Do you like swords?"

Rath smiled, amused. "Unforunetly, my lord, I am quite inept at swordplay." He raised a hand. Shadows slithered down his arm. It reminded me of Aqua. "I am gifted with magic if that makes your selection easier."

"Medea made a familiar for Cyvis. Would you want a familiar?"

Rath pursed his lips. "I believe I would prefer a focus of some sort."

"I'm sure I can find something. Give me a second." I shoved my arm shoulder deep into a Hole, rummaging through dozens of spell foci.

"Are you just ignoring me?" Tristan, the paladin, asked. He looked supremely confused about this entire situation.

"If you're not interested, you're not interested." I said simply. "I'm not going to force you. Aha!" I withdrew my arm, holding a small book up. The cover was a tanned burgundy. A dark eye was pictured on the front cover. This was one of the spellbooks Medea mass produced to sell to the supernatural community of our world. "Will this work?" I asked, holding the book out to Rath.

Rath took the book from me and laid his hand on the cover, closing his eyes. "Yes, I think… Agh!"

The book adopted a sinister red glow. The contract lit on fire, levitating into the air. I'd been so preoccupied searching for a focus I hadn't seen Rath sign it.

Rath pulled his hand away from the book's cover. The eye was gone from the book's cover, now tattooed onto Rath's palm. The glowing tattoo moved, blinking as the fire burning Rath's contract intensified.

Rath chuckled, experimentally clenching his fist. "I believe I understand what you spoke of now, Cyvis. I feel better than I have in years."

"Glad you're not having second thoughts." I said with a grin. "I suggest we get going. Cyvis, Rath, Vellia too if you have belongings here, I suggest you pack everything you want from this place. Don't worry about bringing too much. I can transport it all with ease. If you have people setting up for your excursion to Kharad-Veth, maybe tell them to find other work for a few weeks."

"What are you saying, my lord?" Cyvis asked.

I frowned. "I don't want you here when your parents get back. I'd rather you completely avoid that mess if possible. If you accept, I was planning on moving you three into my castle until we figure something else out. I need your help with something, but following that, I'll arrange for you to be able to come back and secure Kharad-Veth."

Vellia's breath caught. "We'll be living in your castle, my lord?"

"If you like. I don't want to take you against your will."

Vellia knelt once more. "I would be honored."

I held back a sigh at the excessive bowing and kneeling. I really hated all the formality, but it made them more comfortable, so I'd deal with it. "Just go gather your belongings. I'll hang out here and wait."

Rath, Cyvis and Vellia left the room. I felt them go, three minor drains on my demonic power, tethers that were far less draining than they used to be. I could probably manage three or four more. Not that I was overly eager to seek out more potential contractees. I already had three warlocks and my peerage to manage. Not to mention my business. Not to mention bringing Serafall's groups to and from Faerun. Not to mention the war.

I sighed, rubbing my forehead. Things were very hectic right now, and they were only going to get worse.

I stared up at the ceiling. "You're still here." I commented, not looking at Tristan. The paladin had been standing in the corner, silently observing as Rath became my warlock.

"You are not what I expected from a devil," he said slowly.

"It might be an act. I've heard devils can be pretty devilish in their dealings. Maybe I'm just trying to get you to agree to sign over your soul?"

His features contorted in confusion. "But you didn't lay a claim on his soul. I've heard of warlock pacts. I've met a fair few individuals that held them even before I knew Cyvis and Vellia numbered among them. The price is always either a soul or eternal servitude. All you claimed from Rath was his service when you asked for him."

I finally turned to look at him. "You read the contract?"

He shook his head. "I could feel the binding. I'm more in tune with that kind of thing than most."

"That sounds like a story."

Tristan pursed his lips. I thought he was done speaking. After a long pause, he proved me wrong.

"I once served a powerful lord in Cormyr. I worked closely with his court wizard on a number of matters. I learned from the experience."

I raised an eyebrow, sitting up straight. "Cormyr is a long way from here. How'd you end up on the Sword Coast?"

Tristan's features twisted in anger. "I was betrayed. The lord I served blamed me for one of his failings. I was forced to flee."

"Cyvis said you were looking for a lord to serve. Why try to serve someone else after your last lord stabbed you in the back?"

"I am a paladin. Our power comes from our oaths. Some pledge themselves to gods, others to justice. I pledged myself to service."

I raised an eyebrow. "Can't you just serve a goal of some kind?"

Tristan shook his head. "It does not work like that. I've already weakened considerably. I must find a lord to serve. That is all I know."

"Maybe this is your opportunity to learn something new? To become someone new?"

Tristan looked at me strangely before chuckling. "You are certainly unlike the devils from the stories I have heard."

I grinned. "Is that a good thing or a bad thing?"

"For me, it is good, and that is all that matters. I think I see why Cyvis and Vellia follow you. Perhaps serving you would not be so bad afterall."

I sat back, shocked. "That's a rapid change of heart."

"As I said, I am weakening. I have searched for a lord worthy of my service for over two years now. I am tired of wandering. Will you betray me, devil?"

"I don't betray my people." I said seriously. "The only reason I would ever come into conflict with them was if they turn on me first, and I am very careful to ensure they have no reason to turn against me."

"You said you planned to move the others to your home. I assume you reside in one of the Hells?"

I grinned. "Yes, one of them."

Tristan picked up on my amusement, eyes narrowing, but he didn't comment on it. "Would you take me along with you if I accepted your offer?"

I raised an eyebrow. "I'm surprised you're seriously considering this."

Tristan smiled. "Maybe it is time I try something new. Mortal lords failed me. Perhaps a devil lord will suit me where they did not?"

"Well, to answer your question, I would probably take you back with me. You missed this part, but I'm at war right now. I have a plan to make myself stronger, but I'll need my warlock's help for that. That, and I don't want Cyvis's abusive parents to have any way to reach her. It satisfies both objectives."

Tristan adopted a considering expression. "Will I fight in your war?"

I shook my head. "I'd likely keep all of you back. You might be strong here, but things operate on different scales where I'm from. In the process of helping me get stronger, you would grow stronger yourselves. Perhaps when you're strong enough I'd take you to battle with me, but I won't needlessly risk your lives."

"I wouldn't have expected a devil to care so much for their underlings."

"You said it yourself, I'm not your typical devil."

Tristan smiled. "No, you are not." He drew his sword, driving the point into the ground as he knelt. "I offer you my oath, my lord. I shall be your sword and shield. Your enemies shall never harm you while I draw breath. I ask to be your vassal, my lord."

I stood from the couch and laid a hand on his armored shoulder. "Protect me and mine and don't betray me, and I will never give you reason to regret your decision. Welcome to House Abaddon, Tristan Vale. Let me write up a contract and–"

Demonic power exploded around us, suffusing the room like a thick mist. Tristan gasped as the ambient power flowed into him. His eyes flashed a dark red.

I felt another link to my demonic power snap into place. This one was different. I had three warlocks now. I knew what that drain felt like. My link with Tristan didn't draw any more power than the others, but it felt…off. Less like a subordinate and more like a defender.

…Did I just accidentally a paladin?

Surely not. Paladins drew power from their oath, not their patron. Most of them anyway. Didn't some draw power from gods? I had no idea what was happening here.

'Medea?' I reached out to the bond I shared with my wife.

'Yes, honey?'

'Remember when I said I'd watched you make two contracts already and there shouldn't be any issues?'

I heard her chuckle. 'Do you need my help?'

'Not immediately, but I'd like you to check me over when I get back. I made one warlock and…potentially a paladin. Whatever the second one is, it isn't a warlock.'

Medea was silent for a moment. 'Well that certainly sounds interesting. Also, Serafall just contacted me. She's ready for transport.'

'Tell her I'm opening the Holes from here. I need to deal with my warlocks first. I'll come get her in like five minutes.'

'I'll let her know.'

Medea's presence faded from my mind. I concentrated, opening a Hole from Serafall's office to the workshop I'd prepared for her. The skeletons and armors would make sure none of the devils she brought with her wandered too far. I'd sort this situation out quickly then head over.

Luckily, my warlocks chose that moment to return. Vellia had a travel sack. Cyvis and Rath both only carried a small satchel. Bags of Holding if my guess was right.

I looked down at Tristan, still kneeling before me, taking deep breaths as he felt the demonic power flowing through him. "Do you have any belongings you need to grab before we go?"

Tristan slowly stood, shaking his head. "I've had to travel light. Everything I left in my tent will be easy to replace. I am ready to depart."

"If you're sure. Cyvis? Vellia? Rath?"

I received a series of affirmatives from my warlocks. Without another word, I pulled us all through a Hole.

They all looked around. I heard Cyvis gasp, excitement in her eyes. I'd brought us to the ballroom where I'd met my peerage earlier.

"I'll get each of you situated with a room momentarily." I said, drawing their attention. "For the near future, I want you all to meet here in the mornings. As I said, I need to get stronger, and I think all of you can help with that and grow stronger yourselves in the process. My castle is capable of creating an infinite army of creatures of varying types. I want you to fight weak monsters. As you kill them, you will grow stronger and I will absorb some of the strength you obtain through our bond."

"The castle can create an infinite amount of monsters?" Cyvis asked, breathless.

I grinned. "Welcome to Castle Abaddon, where the dreams of my enemies go to die."

I felt a satisfied hum tremble through the air as the castle itself seemed to puff up with pride.

"Hello, my love."

All eyes turned to a balcony leading to a hallway. A set of staircases ran up the wall opposite each other, meeting in the middle at an overlook. Medea stood above us all, intently studying Rath and Tristan.

I smiled. "Rath, Tristan, meet Lady Medea Abaddon, my wife."

Tristan knelt. "It is an honor, my lady."

Rath bowed at the waist. "An honor indeed, my lady."

"Could you make sure they each receive a room?" I asked as Medea floated down through the air to land at my side. "I need to go pick up Serafall."

Medea nodded. "Leave it to me."

I smiled, leaning in for a quick kiss. "You're the best."

"I know. Before you go," she reached out and grabbed my wrist as I went to step through a Hole. "Shang Tsung, Mothra, Keno and Aqua departed a short while ago. They should return soon."

I frowned. "Where did they go?"

"Shang Tsung wanted to visit his old home to remember where he started and see how far he'd come. I believe welcoming him into House Abaddon had a profound effect on him. He wasn't expecting it and doesn't know how to feel. Be gentle with him when he returns."

I nodded. "Thanks for the head's up. I'll talk to him later."

"One last thing." she said, staring intently into my eyes.

'I found something while I was looking for individuals I might be interested in taking for my own peerage.' Medea said in my mind, using our connection to show me what she'd found. 'Serafall has been good to us. I believe she would appreciate this, don't you?'

My eyes widened as I saw just what Medea had found. 'How the hell…? Didn't Aqua–'

'I found it with Aqua's help, honey.'

'You don't want her?'

'I do not believe she would be a good fit with us. I'm very picky. Even more so than you were, my love. Make Serafall the offer. At worst, she refuses, though I doubt she will.'

"I'll talk to her. See you later." I stole one more kiss and walked through a Hole.

"Bal," Serafall greeted, arms crossed over her chest as she supervised dozens of devils and a large number of humans walking around the cave in front of her. I even saw a minotaur. No idea where that guy came from.

"Everything alright?" Serafall asked. "I was expecting you back sooner."

"I got hung up dealing with some things. I'll tell you later. One of them was…important."

"On a scale of headache to stroke?"

"Probably a good migraine at least." Learning devils could apparently make paladins that were bound to their demonic power instead of just their oath would be interesting to say the least. I still wasn't even sure what had happened myself.

Serafall sighed. "It's a good thing I like you, Bal."

"So how are things going here? Is it working?"

"Yes, on all counts." Serafall said, a small smile growing on her face. "They're weaker than yours, and far weaker than Seraphine, but they're definitely warlocks. Apparently, we can even make warlock contracts with weaker devils. No idea how that works. I'll get Ajuka to look at them later."

"Weird, but a good thing, right?"

"Definitely a good thing, especially after what happened to the Baels. I'll need to get Sirzechs to make a bunch of warlocks so we're not in danger of losing the Power of Destruction."

A dark flash at the back of the cave signalled another contract forming.

Serafall nodded, satisfied as she uncrossed her arms. "That's the last of them. Alright, everyone!" she called. "Back through the Hole!"

Some devils grumbled, others rushed through the Hole, others took several seconds to start moving, too enthralled with their new warlocks to care that the Leviathan just gave them an order.

When they'd all finally filed through the Hole, I shut it behind them.

Serafall sighed, rubbing her temples. "That was the first group of nearly forty we have planned and I'm already exhausted. I need a seven-century vacation."

I chuckled at her distraught tone, drawing a glare from her.

"Afraid I can't help with that. But, I might be able to do something else." I said, the corner of my lip pulling up in a grin.

Serafall's eyes narrowed. "Bal, I swear on creation, if you pull some wild bullshit out of your ass I'm going to turn you into a popsicle."

I shook my head, amused. "Just come on." I opened another Hole, leading the way towards it. After a moment's hesitation, Serafall slowly followed me through.

I cast a minor illusion over us to obscure us as we flew down through the sky on devilish wings.

Below, small buildings lined cracked roads, winding through neighborhoods off towards a city center with buildings that stretched towards the clouds. The sky was dark. Moonlight shone down to illuminate areas unlit by streetlights. Stars peaked through gaps in the light cloudcover.

Serafall looked around, eyes narrow. "Where are we? You've never taken me here before."

"And hopefully, I'll never return." I said seriously, senses fixed intently on our surroundings. My amusement was gone. I was stressed now. "This is Medea's neck of the woods. There is some scary shit here, so I'd like to get this over with and leave."

Serafall paused, freezing in mid-air. "This is the world Medea's from?"

"Yes and no. It's a reflection that's basically the same but also all kinds of different. It's confusing. It's close enough that I still don't want to be here. I took a big risk when I recruited Medea, so I'd appreciate it if we hurried this up and left so I can never come back here."

Serafall nodded seriously, recognizing the anxious way I looked around us, as if the shadows themselves were going to jump out and strangle us.

We descended between the buildings. Our wings vanished as I led Serafall up to an isolated, deteriorating building. The windows were smashed and boarded up. Parts of the ceiling had collapsed. Tape was strewn about the entrance, condemning the structure and warning people to stay away.

"Lovely place." Serafall idly commented.

"I wouldn't have brought us here without a reason. Don't try to force things. Be patient. Offer her a place to live her own life, to be her own person. She's been through hell. I'd recommend a Knight for what it's worth."

Serafall became confused as I spoke. When I mentioned a Knight, she went pale, looking around in a new light. She rushed past me into the building.

I moved to follow her, then stopped myself.

Serafall on her own might be enough to spook her away. If I showed up, she'd almost definitely run. Best to trust Serafall to handle it.

I walked a short distance away from the buildings, still shrouded in my illusion, and leaned up against a tree to wait.

Minutes stretched. With each passing moment, I felt more and more uncomfortable.

I did not like being here. There were some people I'd desperately wanted to recruit for my peerage that I'd passed over because I didn't want to tangle with their worlds. I would have gone for Azhidaal and several others if Nirn wasn't so terrifying. I would have tried to recruit Miao Ying if Warhammer were not the supreme hellhole it was. I would have tried to recruit many people from DC and Marvel.

Medea was the biggest risk I took, one I'd take again and again knowing how it turned out, but there was a reason I hadn't come back here. Hopefully, we were too insignificant to appear as blips on the radar of the scary locals.

After what felt like an hour, but was probably only around fifteen minutes, Serafall walked out from the abandoned building. She walked hand in hand with a small girl.

The girl had pink hair. Her skin was tan. She wore a red and black cloak. It looked like she'd been crying, but there was a bright smile on her face. She had two demonic wings spreading wide from her back.

"Ready?" I asked, pushing off the tree.

Serafall nodded. "We're ready."

I opened a Hole.

The girl sucked in a breath, hiding behind Serafall, poking her head out to stare suspiciously at the dark void in space.

Serafall knelt, looking up at the girl with an encouraging smile on her face. "That's Balthazar, Chloe. He's a bit of a jerk sometimes, but he's one of my best friends. He won't hurt you. You can trust him. Come on!" She stood, taking the girl's hand and boldly walking towards the Hole. "We'll go through together."

Chloe von Einzbern, holder of the Archer Class Card, sent me one more suspicious look before taking a deep breath and walking through the Hole with Serafall.

I was through the moment they were, snapping the Hole shut behind me as I let out a tense breath.

There were some places in the multiverse I just had no interest in visiting. That was definitely one of them. I'd need to grab Aqua when she and Shang Tsung returned so she could seal that route off again.

Speaking of them, I wonder how it was going?


X


Shang Tsung slowly walked over sandy roads. He felt as if he was in a daze. It felt surreal to be back here.

Vendors shouted at passersby, trying to draw attention to the wares peddled at their stalls. Patrols of white uniformed guards passed scrutinizing gazes over the people walking on the road. Shang Tsung could remember many times those same guards had run him out of town after town.

Now, they were barely even a nuisance.

The power of a god flowed through his veins, what was this forgotten past next to what he'd achieved? He was an Abaddon now, member of one of the strongest houses in Hell, head of his own branch of said house.

Shang Tsung still couldn't believe it.

"Look!" Aqua called, pointing to one of the stalls serving some kind of roasted meat. "That looks tasty. What do you think?"

"Um… Maybe we should…" Keno started to say, edging away from the mystery meat.

"Oh, come on!" Aqua said, grabbing the smaller girl's arm and dragging her towards the stall.

Shang Tsung smiled as he watched the exchange.

He wasn't sure why he'd asked Aqua to bring him back here. There was nothing for him here now.

There was never anything here for him to begin with. His destiny was to wander from town to town, forever hungry, forever an outcast. One day, he would die in the sand and that would have been the end. No one would remember the name Shang Tsung. No one would mark his passing or care that he was gone.

That wasn't the case now. He had a family. He had friends. He had more than he could have ever dreamed of.

Fluttering encouragement.

Shang Tsung smiled, reaching up to gently run a finger along Mothra's thorax from where she was perched atop his head.

"Thank you, Mothra. I think I'm ready to go now. Once Aqua and Keno have sampled their food we can–"

A crowd passed by Shang Tsung. A skinny, malnourished woman brushed against his shoulder as she passed, mumbling an apology as she hurried on.

Shang Tsung's eyes narrowed. That woman had just stolen the pouch he wore at his waist. It was enchanted to hold far more than it appeared. Shang Tsung would take it back. It was his.

Shang Tsung turned, following the woman as she parted ways with the group she'd been walking with. Her clothing was little more than a blue rag fashioned into a tunic, torn and worn thin. She turned down an alley and started running.

In a flash of green flame, Shang Tsung appeared in front of her.

When he'd travelled to this world, he'd worn a simple cloak to allow himself to blend in. The moment he teleported, his armor manifested around him, revealing him for the terrifying fighter he was.

The woman gasped, moving too fast to stop as she collided into Shang Tsung.

Shang Tsung stared coldly at the woman, grabbing her wrists to prevent her from running. "You have something that belongs to me." He tore his pouch from her hand and pushed the woman away.

She collapsed with a shout of pain. A tattered hood fell off her face, revealing dark red hair stained with muck. Sharp features were marred by scrapes and bruises. The woman looked terrified, slowly crawling away, eyes fixed on Shang Tsung.

"Lord sor-sorcerer," she stuttered. "Please… Mercy. It was not my intent to insult you. I beg you, let me live."

Chiding chittering.

Mothra lifted off his head.

The woman on the ground gasped as Mothra assumed her humanoid form. Mothra leaned down over the woman, a comforting smile on her face as she laid a hand on her shoulder. Blue scales shed from Mothra's arms to fall on the beggar.

The beggar sighed. Cuts closed. Bruises healed. Years of aches and pains were soothed away by Mothra's power.

Shang Tsung felt his anger dim. He looked at the woman laid on the ground before him. He saw the desperation in her eyes, the fear. She was clearly malnourished. When was the last time she ate?

Shang Tsung remembered when he was little better. Before he'd stolen his cart and learned to part fools from their money, he'd nearly starved many times.

Shang Tsung knelt next to Mothra on the beggar's other side.

The beggar flinched away from him. "Please, my lord… I will–"

She froze as Shang Tsung lifted a hand. Green magic cascaded over her body, cleansing the mud and dust from her skin and clothes. Free of muck, the woman's muted hair became a vibrant red, like a rose.

As Shang Tsung began to lower his hand, he frowned, intently focused on the woman.

The woman didn't resist as he laid a hand on her forehead. She squeezed her eyes shut, waiting for the end.

It was all she could do. Shang Tsung understood her position well. He had been in her shoes not long ago. Anyone with true power could have crushed him like a bug with no repercussions. Such was their way in this world.

Concerned fluttering.

"I'm not going to hurt her, Mothra." Shang Tsung assured the Rook, his gaze intently focused on the beggar before him.

Shang Tsung was once the weakest member of Balthazar Abaddon's peerage. He'd often wondered why Balthazar had reincarnated him when he had other servants of such great power. It wasn't until his training with Medea began in earnest that he learned the truth. Balthazar had seen something in him, a hidden power lurking far beneath the surface, a power Shang Tsung would never have realized on his own. Only through Medea's instruction was he able to achieve his true potential.

Shang Tsung wondered if how he felt now was how Balthazar felt then. Kneeling here, staring at this pathetic beggar with nothing but the clothes on her back and a drive to live to see tomorrow, yet far beneath, Shang Tsung felt something. Potential, vast as the sea.

As he withdrew his hand, Shang Tsung realized the beggar's hair wasn't red like a rose. No, it was red like blood.

"What is your name?" Shang Tsung asked, his tone insistent, but not unpleasant.

The beggar's eyes snapped open. Shock was evident on her face. She'd expected to be dead by now. "S-Skarlet," she said.

"Skarlet," Shang Tsung repeated. He smiled, amused. Truly, the tables had turned. It was so strange to experience things from this side. "My name is Shang Tsung of House Abaddon, Skarlet. I am the Head of the Soul Branch of the Abaddon family. I do not expect these names to mean anything to you."

Skarlet may not have recognized the names, but she recognized the intensity with which Shang Tsung recited them, the authority. Color drained from her face. She knew she had wronged not only a sorcerer, but a high-born lord far beyond her station. She assumed a fate worse than death awaited her.

"My master," Shang Tsung continued, "Viscount Balthazar Abaddon, Lord of the House of Abaddon, once saw something in me. There was a time not too long ago where I lived a life not so dissimilar from your own. I was pathetic, directionless. My master pulled me from the dirt and gave me purpose. He elevated me far beyond anything I ever dreamed, far beyond what I deserved."

Skarlet was barely breathing. She knew she was trapped. She had no choice but to stay still and listen as the lord who held her life in his hands spoke, waiting for the inevitable moment where she would suffer for her ill-fated decision to steal from him.

Shang Tsung grinned. "I will tell you a secret now, Skarlet. I am a devil." Shang Tsung's wings spread wide behind his back, filling the alley.

Skarlet flinched as the wings appeared, she leaned away, body trembling as she stared up at Shang Tsung in terror.

"I was not always a devil, you know." Shang Tsung continued, speaking softly. "My master took a starving rat and elevated him into a prince. He made me into a devil, granted me powers beyond even those of the Khans. I once thought them to be the limit of what was possible. My master showed me how wrong I was. He gave me a chance to be better. He gave me a home. All he asked in return was my loyalty. He shall have it until the end of time. I would be nothing without him."

Shang Tsung raised his hand. In a dark flash of demonic power, an Evil Piece appeared resting in his palm, a Pawn.

"I now offer you that same opportunity, Skarlet." Shang Tsung said. "This world would leave you to starve in a ditch. It would not even mark your passing as your body is fed upon by carrion, forgotten. But, I offer an alternative."

Shang Tsung stood, holding his free hand down towards the beggar. "Come with me, Skarlet. Join my peerage, become a devil in my service. I will train you. In time, you will attain such power that the legends of this world would quake at your approach. You will stand on equal footing with gods. No longer will you struggle to survive in squalor. You will live as a queen in a castle. I will give you everything you've ever dreamed of and more. All I ask in return, all I will ever ask in return, is your absolute loyalty. Never turn your back on me. Never turn your back on Lord Abaddon, and you will always be welcome among us."

Skarlet was frozen in place. She stared up at Shang Tsung uncomprehendingly. This was impossible. There was no way a sorcerer lord was offering her a place in his house. She was a beggar, less than nothing. There was a catch here. There had to be. Right?

Skarlet flinched. The insect-like form of Mothra laid a comforting hand on Skarlet's shoulder, smiling.

A song of encouragement.

Skarlet swallowed audibly. Hesitant, she reached up, taking Shang Tsung's hand.

"I… I'll do it. I'll serve you." she said.

Shang Tsung smiled triumphantly as he helped her to her feet. "Welcome to the family, Skarlet." He pressed the Pawn into her chest.

Skarlet gasped. Her gasp turned to a scream as power exploded through her.

Devil wings tore from her back, ripping the rags she wore to shreds. Skarlet arched her back, looking to the sky as she roared. She'd never felt like this. She'd never felt so strong, so free.

"Everything okay over here?"

All eyes turned to the entrance to the alley. A woman with limbs of shadow and bleached blue hair chewed on a meat skewer she held in her hand. A smaller woman with golden blonde hair munched on her own skewer, standing on her tip-toes to peek over the bluenette's shoulder.

Aqua raised an eyebrow at Shang Tsung. "Do you often reincarnate naked women, or is this your first time?"

Aqua shook her head, biting down on her skewer to hold it between her teeth. Her Keyblade appeared in her hand, opening a dark keyhole in space. Aqua rummaged around in the keyhole, pulling out a crimson gown.

She walked forward, holding it out to the new devil. "It's not much, but it'll work until we get you home. I'm Aqua Abaddon, Balthazar Abaddon's Knight. That's Keno Abaddon back there, Bal's Pawn. It's good to meet you."

"Aqua, Keno, I'd like you to meet Skarlet, my Pawn, first of my peerage." Shang Tsung announced proudly.
