#9,453
Just like the last time I was in Serafall's office building, there was a valkyrie behind the desk with the receptionist. This time, there were also a host of men and women wearing furs and robes speaking to the many devils that worked under Serafall.

I was here to transport another group of devils to Faerun so they could contract warlocks, the fourth group thus far. Once the proof of concept was shown to be viable, Serafall had wasted no time pulling everyone she thought she could trust through Holes to make warlocks. I didn't recognize any of the devils Serafall had me transport, but then I didn't get out much. Supposedly Sirzechs and Ajuka would be contacting me soon about making their own, but they had yet to do so. With the war, both of them were very busy.

As I stepped into Serafall's office, I was surprised to see she wasn't alone.

An elderly man stood hunched at Serafall's side. Together, they looked down at a collection of maps atop Serafall's desk. Serafall was adorned in the same dark armor she'd worn when she appeared at my castle following Boreas's attack. The elderly man wore a dark robe covered in small runes, glowing with hidden power. They both looked up as I came in.

"Is everything alright, Serafall?" I asked, noting that the Satan was dressed for war, not a meeting.

"Things have officially kicked off." Serafall said seriously. "The Naberius Heir was just killed in his summer home by a group of amazons. Don't ask me why the idiot was vacationing in the mortal world when there's a war on. We also have reports of mages attempting to break into Hell. We shut down all of the main thoroughfares before we declared war, but it's inevitable they'll find a way in. I'd bet they already have. There's a lot of untamed wild in Hell, perfect for staging a forward operating base to strike from. Sirzechs is working overtime to keep the Pillars from acting alone. They already wanted blood after Zekram, now some of the idiots are thinking they'll attack Olympus alone and it'll end in anything other than their deaths. We're planning a counterattack, but we need to be smart about it."

The elderly, gray-haired man at her side coughed into his fist.

Serafall sighed. "Right, sorry. Bal, this is Odin of the Aesir. Odin, this is Viscount Balthazar Abaddon."

I bowed my head politely. I'd recognized the man of course – who wouldn't recognize the head of a pantheon? – but I hadn't addressed him because I didn't want to interrupt Serafall. Hearing another Pillar Devil was dead didn't concern me too much, the possibility of the Greeks gaining a foothold in Hell did.

"It is an honor to meet you, Lord Odin." I said respectfully.

Odin huffed, waving his hand. "None of that. I will not ask my allies to grovel. I've been looking forward to meeting you, Balthazar. I've been watching you for some time now, as I imagine many others have."

"And what have you observed?"

Odin grinned. "A calamitous young devil throwing a long-precariously balanced peace into discord through the use of powers never seen."

"Thank you?" I said, uncertain. I wasn't sure how to interpret that.

Odin laughed. "It was a compliment, my boy. This peace was always doomed to fail. Each pantheon has been scheming the best way to make themselves the only pantheon for hundreds of years. The fact your arrival gave the devils a path to assured victory is no crime. Do be careful though. I expect once the others discover what I have, you will be the prime target for dozens of assassination attempts. I expect the fae will try to enslave you as well. Death would be kinder than that fate."

"I've tried to keep what I can do secret for that very reason. I wasn't strong enough to be confident in my ability to resist them. I'm prepared now. Let them come."

Odin laughed again. "I like you, Balthazar."

"Not to interrupt," Serafall said, "But I called him here for a reason. We're pressed for time, so either get on with it or you'll have to wait for later. I need to secure some Naberius warlocks before the Greeks try to finish what they started with that Pillar."

Odin's good cheer faded. He frowned, forehead wrinkling unpleasantly. "Very well. Much like the other pantheons, I have also been scheming for centuries, Balthazar. Though my schemes were less sinister. I have grown the strength of Asgard as much as possible. My goal was not to destroy all others in the world, but to avert our own end. The other pantheons lack the noose of Ragnarok strung around their neck. All I have done, I have done to prepare my people for when that prophesied end comes so that we might avert the destruction I foresee."

"I assume we are speaking because you believe there is a way I can help?" I asked.

"Yes, I am very interested in your ability to walk between worlds, but for now, it is not why I wish to work with you. Through my ravens' eyes, I witnessed the aftermath of your lady wife freeing Typhon's children from their Sacred Gears. I wonder, is she capable of doing the reverse?"

My eyes widened slightly before I controlled my expression. Darting a questioning glance at Serafall, I saw she remained relaxed, giving me a small nod.

I didn't like that there was apparently a third faction on the field when my home was attacked. I liked it even less that none of us noticed them. Thankfully, it was a problem of the past. I doubted even Huginn and Muninn could breach Dimension Lost.

"Given time, yes, I believe she could." I answered Odin's question. "Why do you ask?"

"I have seen many visions of Ragnarok. There are so many different paths leading to the inevitable end. Some things remain constant throughout these variations. It is always Loki's meddling that begins the chain of destruction. It is always his spawn that end my home. I have done all I dare to remove them from the equation. It was always a delaying measure. Whether now or in a thousand years, Asgard will destroy itself unless they are dealt with permanently."

"So you want Loki's children sealed away in Sacred Gears? Why not just deal with Loki himself? You're Odin. I can't imagine he could resist you for long."

"Loki's nature is that of a trickster. He is gifted in his ability to avoid that which would harm him. That aside, I can't act myself, lest my own actions be the catalyst that begins Ragnarok. I am sure you are familiar with the term of a self-fullfilling prophecy. For now, Loki is content to be left alone. That will change eventually when he inevitably begins the end, but I cannot act against him lest I become Ragnarok's catalyst."

"Which is why you're looking for outside help, I take it? But isn't you talking to me you acting?"

"Yes, but for the first time in centuries, I have hope of averting this disaster. If I spend enough time focused on a single individual, I can see glimpses of their future and their intent. Only those with similar abilities are shielded from my sight. I'm sure Indra is none too happy with you for killing his little pet project. But you, Balthazar, are an entity I cannot see. Your future is clouded. At first I believed Medea had fashioned some sort of protection against my abilities to protect you from Remiel. It's no secret he has become obsessed with you in recent days. Then I learned of your true power. I cannot see your influence on our world if you regularly depart from it only to return with treasures and individuals who do not conform to the rules we are governed by. I decided to try to observe your peerage to model you with much the same result. Aqua and Keno were practically absent from my sight, as if they ventured away more frequently than you do. I imagine that gives Remiel difficulty seeing you as well."

I was silent for a moment as I absorbed that. Travelling between worlds had apparently given me the unintended side-effect of making it difficult to predict my actions with powers that saw the future. That was fantastic news. Remeil had been a constant worry ever since Serafall told us of him, turning into a dire worry after we learned he was partially responsible for the attack on the castle. If all we needed to do to fool his foresight was jump to another world every day or so, I would abuse that to its greatest effectiveness.

"So you think I'll be able to successfully stop Ragnarok since you can't see my future." I guessed at Odin's intentions.

"I am desperate for a solution, Balthazar. I will explore every path I can. Asgard will not fall because I sat idle, wallowing in misery at the inescapable end."

I thought for a moment, an idea coming to me. "Do you know where Loki is?"

Odin's one eye narrowed, watching me intently. "He answers to no one, but he does reside in Asgard on occasion. Beyond that, I do not know. I could locate him if you need to speak with him."

"I don't… Actually, yes. See if you can get him to agree to meet with me. I'll need help. I don't know if you can spare Thor, but any heavy-hitter you have who you're confident can deal with Loki would be welcome."

Odin frowned. "I have looked into futures where Loki is killed. His death is always the beginning of the end."

"Who said anything about killing him? Do you want to know the full plan or would you rather stay in the dark so you don't accidentally start Ragnarok yourself?"

"If it involves Loki, I must insist on hearing what you have in mind. I cannot afford to risk anything when the trickster is involved."

I outlined my plan to Odin. I explained how I'd already accomplished what I intended to do to Loki once before. Serafall muttered under her breath about how she should have realized earlier that that was how I did it.

Odin just laughed. There was a manic look on the god's face as he howled in joy.


X


Loki of the Aesir, the trickster, son of Fárbauti, walked into Odin's hall with a scowl on his face. He was not a pawn to be summoned at Odin's whim. Odin had called all of the Aesir to return to Asgard and prepare for war. Now he had summoned Loki for an audience. What business was it of Loki if Asgard planned to get involved in the devil's war? He cared little for the devils or for the Greeks. It was foolish of Odin to join either side in the conflict, but if the old fool insisted on making such a mistake, Loki would take advantage of the error to better his own position as he always did.

Odin thought himself wise. The old man's caution drove him to inaction, too afraid his actions would bring about the prophesied Ragnarok. Odin dedicated everything to increasing the strength of Asgard in the vain hope it would help stave off the end.

He was a fool. Odin focused his powerful sight on an end so far away as to blind him to the workings of the present. Even knowing Loki's nature, Odin didn't suspect the immediate threat of treachery.

The pieces were almost set. Loki's time was nigh. By leveraging the help of lesser beings and foreign gods, Loki's plan had advanced considerably. This Khaos Brigade was misguided, but useful. Once Loki took what he needed from them, he would divest himself of their chains. For now, he needed their aid, but soon, Loki would answer to no one but himself.

"You are late, Loki." Odin's voice boomed, displeasure thick in his tone. He sat hunched at the head of a long table, Frigg at his side. She wore a simple green dress, eyes cold as she tracked Loki's entry. Baldur sat at her side wearing an opal shirt with furs around his shoulders. His arms were crossed over his chest. Thor sat at Odin's right hand, once again forgoing a shirt, revealing the runic tattoos that spanned his chest and upper arms. Víðarr, a rare sight at these meetings, sat at Baldur's side, wearing a simple jacket. His feet rested on the table. The long leather boot on his foot gleamed in the firelight of the candles atop the chandelier. Tyr was the table's final occupant, sitting next to Thor. The god of war had a small frown on his face. All of the present Aesir sat tense, waiting on Loki's arrival.

A practiced smile spread across Loki's face as he dipped into a mocking bow. "Apologies, Allfather, but your summons caught me by surprise. I arrived as soon as I could."

"Take your seat." Odin said, his tone of voice ensuring Loki knew it was an order rather than a request.

Loki's smile slipped for a moment as he inspected Odin. The Allfather's eye was narrowed in fury. He wore the enchanted robe he donned to do battle, not the ceremonial rag he favored in times of peace. Had he come directly from his negotiations in Hell? What did the old fool want? What was so important that he had pulled his favored sons, his wife, and Tyr to this meeting?

"Quite the gathering," Loki began as he slid into the empty seat directly across from Odin. "Víðarr, I haven't seen you in ages. How have you fared in your journeys through the mortal world?"

Víðarr grunted, but didn't otherwise respond. His eyes, like his father's, were narrowed and angry. What was the purpose of this meeting? Loki didn't like being left in the dark.

"My lady Frigg, you are positively resplendent this day," Loki said, his words like honey. "The Allfather is truly the luckiest man in all the realms."

Frigg's forehead creased as she glared at Loki. "Sit and be silent."

Loki's eyes looked between the gathered Aesir. Each of them shared the same tense energy, like lions tensing to pounce.

Loki's visage leaned back in his chair, the picture of calm. Loki's true body slithered out of his illusion, invisible even to the Allfather's great vision.

This summons was suspect from the start. With Odin's sons and Tyr all gathered as if preparing for combat, things were worse than Loki was expecting. He'd thought Odin would punish him for one of the many minor tricks he pulled to distract Asgard from his true schemes. But this? This was bigger than that.

Loki slunk back to the door, watching the Aesir for any sign they noticed his departure. He did not yet leave. Despite himself, he was far too curious about this meeting to leave now. Why had Odin called them all together?

Sitting at the table as if nothing was wrong, Loki's copy looked around the room. "Are we waiting for any others, or are we ready to begin? I must admit, my curiosity has left me starving. What grave matter has called the greatest of the Aesir together into one place?"

Odin's intense scowl slowly faded. A peaceful smile spread across his lips. "The plucking of a thorn that has been stuck in my side for far too long, spreading its infection and threatening to destroy everything I hold dear. Gondul?"

A pained scream tore from Loki's throat as magical chains clamped down on his wrists and ankles. A glowing rune underneath his feet sent spears of bronze energy up into his arms, pinning them in place. Near the roof of the room, five shapes shimmered into being. Five valkyries fully armed for war floated down directly towards Loki's true body, ignoring his copy.

Loki snarled as he flared his power, scattering the magical chains that bound him, freeing himself from the spears of light in the process. So the Allfather had chosen to make his move. It was earlier than expected, but Loki was prepared. He just needed to escape this trap, then his retribution would be swift.

Green robes and gold armor materialized around Loki's form as he shimmered. Four copies of the Trickster god split off his true body, each casting a spell.

Odin stood, slamming his hand down onto the table. The all-encompassing might of Odin's magical power clapped down into the room, snuffing out the spells of Loki's copies and causing them to waver unnaturally in the air like a heat mirage. Simultaneously, the second invisibility spell Loki had woven around himself unraveled.

Thor sprung from his seat with a mighty roar. Mjolnir appeared in his hand as he leapt towards Loki.

A spear appeared in Loki's hand just in time to intercept the strike from the great hammer. Rather than crushing Loki's chest, the blow met the haft of his spear. The force from the blow sent Loki sprawling backwards, crashing into the stone wall of the chamber. Rubble rained around him as he struggled to get to his feet.

Loki screamed as more chains manifested around him, binding his arms and legs. A manacle snapped shut around his neck, yanking his head back into the wall.

Loki hissed, glaring hatefully at Odin. "You wrinkled fool!" he spat. "You don't know what you've unleashed. Your troubles will not end with my death. Your suffering has only begun!"

Loki knew a confrontation like this was inevitable. He had precautions in place. Whether he was alive to control them personally or they activated upon his death, Odin would suffer. One final trick.

Odin smiled cruelly. "Who said anything about killing you?"

Gondul, one of the greatest of the valkyries, supposedly retired, grabbed Loki's hair and wrenched his head back. Her eyes glowed with the power of an analytical spell.

"It is truly him, Allfather." Gondul reported.

"I know," Odin said, slowly walking around the table. He stood over Loki's bound form, eyes hard. "You have threatened our home for too long, my blood-brother. Were you anything other than a treacherous snake, Asgard would have been more rich for your presence. Do it."

'Do it?' Loki thought. Do what?

Darkness consumed Loki's world then was gone as quickly as it came, like the blinking of an eye.

Loki scrambled to his feet, free of the magical chains that bound him moments ago. His feet sank into the ground. Frowning, Loki scanned his surroundings.

Sand. Tan grains spread out in all directions. An uncaring sun beat down incessantly. Sweat beaded Loki's forehead.

What was this? It was no illusion. Loki was proficient enough with illusory magics to recognize reality when he faced it. This was real. Odin had sent him somewhere. But where?

The light from the sun vanished. A dark shadow fell over Loki.

Loki turned around, looking up with narrowed eyes.

A haggard, twitching form floated high above. Frayed hair stood at unnatural angle as a shivering devil looked down at him. Her clothes were nothing but rags unable to fully preserve her modesty. Her skin sagged unhealthily like she hadn't eaten in months.

"Meat," she said quietly. "Meat!" she exclaimed, diving towards Loki in a desperate frenzy.

The devil crumpled to the ground at Loki's side, a hole in her chest where Loki's spell struck her.

A sinking feeling consumed the trickster god as he looked around once more.

Sand. A void of sand in all directions.

Where was he?


X


The Baels, widely considered to be the strongest Clan in Hell, were the first to fall. They would not be the last.

As was right, Ares marched at the head of the first true army gathered to carry out his father's will. Athena had petitioned to lead the force in his place, but Great Zeus had denied her. She suffered from her own success. After finding a path Olympus could walk into Hell, Zeus held her back at their temporary base to further secure their position in the lands of their enemy. Thus, Ares was chosen to deliver their first blow against Hell. But he was not alone.

"It's exciting, isn't it?" Aphrodite asked, clad in nothing but her own power. She carried a heart-tipped spear and a shield, wreathed in the forceful aura of her war aspect. It was wrong to call her Aphrodite now. No, she was Aphrodite Areia. Each step she took shook the ground. Hair like sakura petals danced in a gentle breeze as she surveyed their enemy.

Ares stepped up to her side. His flesh was strong and dark with gleaming veins like igneous rock infused with magma, garbed in bronze armor that glowed with divine power. "It's a long time coming."

Beyond, their army of elementals, amazons, nereids, and Sacred Gear holders loyal to Olympus assaulted a city of devils. They were moving towards Clan Agares territory to eliminate them as the Baels were destroyed when they happened upon the undefended city. Their maps were not completely accurate. They would need to update them as they moved. Still, it was fortuitous. Every devil slain was a boon in this war.

These devils were not fighters. They tried, but they were being slain en masse. Weak peasants and minor nobles. There was little glory to be had from this field. Ares would save himself for the Agares. Ending their bloodline would be a battle worthy of him.

"Ares," Aphrodite Areia said, pointing with her spear. There was an eager grin on her face.

Ares looked up. A dark void opened in the sky above the city. He recognized the power. He grinned.

"Abaddon," Ares's hand found the hilt of his sword. Perhaps he would involve himself afterall. His father would be overjoyed if Ares brought the head of Balthazar Abaddon as tribute.

Balthazar Abaddon flew out of the Hole, wings spread wide, a set of dark armor materialized around his body, gleaming with violet runes scribed into the metal.

At Balthazar's side, a point of frigid blue emerged. Serafall Leviathan, armored for war floated in the air at Balthazar's side, already blasting icy spears down into the monsters flying up towards them while Balthazar summoned an inferno to burn the footsoldiers chasing a group of scared peasants.

Not just the Abaddon, but the Leviathan as well? She was a fool to come alone.

Ares drew his sword. Bronze energy crackled around him like lightning as he summoned his power. "Shall we kill a Satan?" he asked Aphrodite Areia.

"Yes," she breathed, her own power exploding as she took several steps forward, preparing to break into a sprint.

More Holes opened in the sky above the city. Ares paused to look up.

Mishappen monsters of shadow and crimson monsters made of armored rock fell from the sky, crushing into Ares' army. High in the sky, another Hole appeared. Ares froze. His grip on his sword felt weak.

No. That wasn't possible.

High in the sky, dark clouds gathered. The sky rumbled. A cyclone formed, swirling around a mountain of a man. Shirtless, runic tattoos glowing bright on his body, honey-colored hair whipping around erratically, Thor Odinson hefted Mjolnir high, lightning cracked with the motion.

"Asgard!" Thor bellowed.

More Holes opened. An army of valkyries dove through the Holes, casting spells, stabbing with spears, slashing with swords.

Thor's storm lit up the sky. Bolts of lightning fell in rapid succession like mallets thundering against a drum. Thor launched himself into the ground, crushing a hydra into paste.

"We need to leave." Ares said, already backing away from the horrifying sight in front of him. "Father… Yes, father must be warned. We need to warn them."

Aphrodite Areia was not listening. She only had eyes for Thor. "He is mine." she said, breathing excitedly as she marched forward.

"No," Ares darted forward, grabbing Aphrodite Areia's arm.

Aphrodite Areia spun on him, fury in her eyes. "Unhand me!"

"Father must be warned. We cannot fight them." Bronze light streamed from Ares, consuming them both.

The two Olympians vanished from the battlefield, leaving their army to its fate.

#9,563
For the first time in ages, the perpetual frown marring Odin's face was absent. In its place was a bright, hopeful smile.

Odin stared ahead, his vision focused on something far away. Spreading wide before his great sight, Odin saw a future without end. Countless paths winding between one-another into infinity. Before, all roads, no matter how disparate, all converged on one point. Ragnarok. The end. Inescapable. Absolute.

No more. Asgard finally had that which Odin had sought for millenia. A future.

Odin's vision expanded. He focused his power on several possible futures.

Scrying the future was difficult due to its fluidity. One seemingly insignificant action had the potential to upheave the future and set fate on a new course. When any number of such actions were occurring simultaneously, it made it difficult to predict with certainty what would come to pass, so Odin used his power as a guideline. Other seers saw with greater certainty, but there were advantages to Odin's version of seeing into the future.

Unlike those who saw single events, Odin could path several futures at once to observe the greatest threats to his home. Ragnarok was absent now, but there were still paths that led to Asgard's ruin.

The Greeks would not succeed in this war. The force arrayed against them was too great. With the Abaddon Lord's power added to the already immense strength of Hell and Asgard's combined forces, Olympus would fall. They would not be the only ones to attack.

Odin's sight stretched beyond the present, predicting hidden ambushes before they were even plotted, desperate attempts by frightened pantheons hopelessly clutching to their power.

Odin had not expected to be successful in his attempt to defeat Ragnarok with Balthazar's help, but any potential path to Asgard's salvation was one he would walk. Not only had Balthazar done the impossible, but he hadn't even needed to seal away Loki's children, some of Asgard's greatest monsters, to do it.

Odin grinned. Perhaps it was time he set those monsters against the snakes lurking in the grass?


X


Athena clenched her fist at her side. It was all she could do to refrain from lashing out at Ares.

For years, she served as Olympus's emissary to lands beyond their own. In her travels to Hell, she uncovered secrets she never mentioned, advantages she noted but never expected to use. The hidden paths Olympus used to enter Hell was one such secret. It should have led to them striking a mighty first blow against their foe. Instead, it led to the devastation of their advance force.

Elevated on his throne above the assembly of gods, Zeus's eyes narrowed in fury. "Asgard thinks to stand against us? They would ally with the scum that kidnap and reincarnate champions from across the supernatural? If they have chosen to stand with the devils, then they have chosen their own destruction."

"Father," Athena said, stepping free of the gathered gods to address Zeus directly. "The devils already outnumber us. Our greatest advantage was our superior number of powerful champions, our gods. With Asgard joining the devils, we have lost our advantage. Now the devils not only have their super devils and satans, but Asgard's gods as well."

Zeus scoffed dismissively. "The norse are weak. Their presence will complicate things, I grant you, but it will not change the outcome. They are few. We are many."

"We are divided, brother." Poseidon said, stepping up to stand at Athena's side. The typically carefree lord of the seas looked haggard. His dark hair was frayed and untamed as it fell past his shoulders. His green eyes were tired, sporting bags beneath them. His broad shoulders were hunched, he leaned heavily on his trident to support his weight.

Zeus made a show of looking around at the assembled gods beneath him. "Is all of Olympus not gathered in support of this purpose?"

"The oceans have split." Poseidon continued, eyes furious as he glared up at Zeus. "Oceanus has retreated to the depths with his court. The nereids and oceanids have undergone a schism. Those who haven't fled to the corners of the Earth still battle amongst themselves. Only a scant few still answer my call. We cannot fight in this condition."

Athena used Poseidon's momentum to make her own point. "We are fractured, father. We are far from our true strength, while the devils are united in their rage against us. Already, we have been forced to repel attacks against Olympus itself."

Zeus laughed. "Their 'attacks' were all easily defeated."

Athena grit her teeth. "Those attacks represented the few prideful devils who thought they could stand against us alone. The Satans have held back all those that would listen to them. When their true strike falls, it will fall like the tide. Continuing this conflict is untenable. I beseech you, allow me to petition Serafall for a truce."

A chilling breeze swept through the halls of Olympus. Light streaming through the windows dimmed as dark clouds gathered ahead. The sky rumbled.

Zeus's eyes narrowed. He sat frozen atop his throne. Athena could not move, pinned in place by his accusing glare.

"I would have thought you would be the last to show such cowardice, daughter." Zeus said, his voice deep and intimidating as a coming storm. "Our armies march secret paths into the devils' home. Our pantheon stands together, ready to face an enemy that has been growing strong beneath us for centuries. Yet not even a month past the start of this much-anticipated conflict, you counsel me to surrender?"

Athena cast her gaze to the marble floors of the hall, an omni-present pressure squeezing down on her. It was suddenly hard to breathe. "Not surrender, father. We need time. We would struggle to fight the devils as we are. We cannot fight the devils now that they have allied with Asgard."

Poseidon stepped forward. Unlike Athena, he stared straight at Zeus in challenge. "I concur. We all bore witness to what became of our initial force. Such an army should have razed that city with ease. The moment Balthazar Abaddon stepped onto the field, the battle was lost. The Abaddon Lord can appear anywhere at a moment's notice, bringing an army with him. He can transport Sirzechs Lucifer or Thor to any battlefield that is nearly lost in a moment, letting them turn the tide. Even if we were at our full strength, unburdened by civil conflict, we would need to find a way to deal with his presence before we continue this foolishness."

Zeus's face was carved from stone. It was impossible to tell what he was thinking as he sat in silence. No one moved.

"Artemis," Zeus finally said.

A small woman with mint-green hair stepped free of the gathered gods. She wore animal furs sewn into a simple tunic. A bow and a quiver of arrows were strapped to her back.

"Yes, father?" Artemis, Goddess of the Hunt said, voice soft but not meek. She spoke like a hunter stalking their prey, precise and calm, with no wasted sound.

"You will go to Hell. Take your hunters or venture alone, it matters not. Your task is this: You will kill Balthazar Abaddon. Bring me the devil's head as proof of your success." Zeus ordered.

"Balthazar is not the only Abaddon." Hermes said, a wicked smile on his face as he drifted through the air on his flying shoes.

Zeus nodded. "You will kill the sister as well, Artemis. What was her name? Katherine? It does not matter. She will be with the brat that enslaved the Nemean Lion."

Artemis bowed her head, expression unreadable. "I will depart at once, father." Artemis turned and walked straight through the gathered gods, forcing them to flee her path as she exited the hall.

The rumbling sky quieted. Light once more streamed into the hall of the gods as the clouds parted.

"With that," Zeus said as he sat back on his throne, looking very pleased with himself. "I have addressed your concerns, Athena. There will be no truce. Artemis will kill the Abaddons. With them gone, we will be free to act once more."

"That's not–" Athena began, cutting off as Poseidon reached out and grabbed her arm. He met her eyes, minutely shaking his head.

Athena clenched her fists. Now was not the time. She bowed her head. "As you say, father."

"Good," Zeus said, smiling wide. "Now, until Artemis kills the Abaddon filth, we must contend with the threat they pose. Ares, you will raise another army. We will strike once more. We will draw Balthazar and the devils' champions into a trap. When they arrive. We will be waiting. Do not fail me again."

Ares fell to the ground, kneeling. "It will be done, father."

Athena had to bite her tongue to keep from lashing out with her words. It was clear she would be unsuccessful if she petitioned Zeus now. She needed to reassess her strategy. Perhaps later, when Olympus was not gathered and he would not be seen as weak?

Athena spun on her heel, storming from the hall, shoving past a wickedly amused Aphrodite.

"Athena!" a voice called after her as she exited the hall.

Athena paused, moments from teleporting away. She turned to see Poseidon running up to her.

"What?" she said, curt.

"You know as well as I do that this is madness." Poseidon said in frantic, hushed tones. "If we allow this to continue, Olympus will be nothing but ash by the end."

"And what would you have me do, uncle? Father has no desire to listen to me. I have tried time and again to caution him away from this course."

"My fool of a brother may not listen, but perhaps others might."

Athena's eyes narrowed, scanning their surroundings to search for eavesdroppers. "What are you suggesting?" Athena said, voice falling to a whisper.

Poseidon leaned in to whisper in Athena's ear.

Athena's eyes widened.

Together, the two gods teleported away from Olympus.


X


Helios stared down at the slumbering form of Eos, a stern frown on his face.

In the days following the fall of Castle Bael, the dawn never came. There was the moon, then there was the sun. Nothing in between. The mortals believed it to be a scientific phenomenon they still had no name for. It was not.

Eos, bringer of the dawn, lay in stasis deep in the sanctity of Helios's hidden refuge. Neither gods nor demons could find them here. He'd made sure of it.

Helios ran a hand through Eos's golden hair. Her eyes remained closed. The wound Zekram Bael had inflicted on her persisted. Her left arm was gone. Parts of her ear had been caught in the strike, making it look like a rodent had taken a large bite out of the tip of her ear. It pained Helios to see her like this. Since being struck, she had fallen into a deep slumber. Nothing Helios nor his more mystically capable sister Selene tried could wake Eos.

That blast had been meant for him. Helios had been stupid, arrogant. He mocked Zekram when he thought the devil defeated. The poison injected into Zekram through his assassin's blade should have weakened Zekram more than it had. Zekram lashed out with one final blow. Eos knocked Helios away, taking the blast of pure annihilation in his place.

A silver hand was laid on Helios's shoulder.

"Let her rest." Selene said, gently pulling him away. "She is strong. This will not be the end of her."

"I do not know how to help her." Helios said, allowing his sister to pull him away.

"Perhaps it is time." Selene said leadingly.

Helios frowned. "They will not help us."

"Perhaps not, but were you laying there in her place, would Eos not try?"

Helios felt the stubborn pride bleed from his body. His pride led to Eos's current condition. It would not be what kept him from helping her.

"Gather Phaëthusa and Lampetië. We will depart shortly." Helios said, resigned.

Selene nodded, her dark hair bouncing with the motion. She left him, going to gather Helios's daughters from their chambers. They had scarcely gone outside since being rescued from the devils that took them.

Helios walked the halls of his home, stopping at a room far back, lost in the twists and turns of the halls. The room was small. One could stand in the middle and reach all four walls by spreading their arms wide. The room held a single item. A glass display case set against the far wall. Within the case, two glowing devil wings hung magically suspended. There they had been since Helios ripped them from Zekram's back. There they would remain, a reminder of what befell those that made enemies of the Sun.

Helios closed the door, leaving the room behind him. It was time to help his sister and his daughters.


X


Zariel, Archduke of Avernus walked with purpose. She stood tall. Her subjects bowed in respect and backed away from her as she passed. While this was nothing new, she was used to being the only entity to inspire such awe and fear in her underlings. Not that she minded the company. On the contrary, Zariel was quite taken with her companion. He was not a mere brute as she feared. No, he was powerful, but also insightful and intelligent. They'd already shared a great many pleasing conversations as Zariel led him through The Bronze Citadel, Avernus's capital.

"Now that we have seen much of the city, I must ask your impressions of my capital." Zariel said.

"It is impressive," Ajuka Beelzebub, foreign Satan of Technological Development, said. "There are many differences between our two worlds. Your technology is not nearly as advanced as our own, yet you have managed to create a semblance of some of our greater machines. It is impressive. Though your over-reliance on souls as a powersource is a great weakness."

"Perhaps you could assist me with creating an alternative?"

Ajuka nodded minutely. "Perhaps."

Ajuka Beelzebub had arrived with Balthazar Abaddon. Balthazar departed soon after, citing some prior obligation in Faerun. Zariel expected Ajuka would return to Elturel to find a warlock as Serafall Leviathan had done before him. Ajuka had surprised Zariel when he instead asked for a tour of her city. She was eager to oblige him. She had been hoping for an opportunity to interact with the man since she'd first observed his wanderings through her layer of the Nine Hells.

It was…nice. A welcome break in her eternal duty as the sentinel standing between the Abyss and the greater multiverse. For just a moment, she was able to forget the Blood War and simply exist in the moment. The crushing weight of Ajuka Beelzebub's titanic presence sent her underlings scurrying away in terror. To Zariel, it was comforting, a sanctuary of respite where she could momentarily forget the weight she bore on her shoulders.

Ajuka suddenly stopped walking. Zariel paused a moment later.

"Is there an issue, Satan Beelzebub?"

Ajuka didn't answer immediately. He looked to the right of the road. A blob of grey flesh sloughed towards an alley, desperate to vacate the presence of the two great devils.

Ajuka walked over to the blob. It began to tremble as Ajuka's oppressive power crushed down on it.

"Archduchess, this is a lemure, correct?" Ajuka asked, still staring down at the blob.

Zariel walked up next to Ajuka, glaring down at the sniveling creature in disgust. "It is. Forgive me. I should not have allowed such a creature to mar your view of my city." Zariel raised a hand, summoning fire to burn away the pathetic cretin that impugned her reputation with its mere presence.

Ajuka raised a hand haltingly. "A moment please, Archduchess."

Zariel looked questioningly at the Satan as she lowered her hand.

Spell circles appeared in front of Ajuka, all aimed down at the trembling creature as he analyzed it. The lemure appeared so terrified as to die of shock if they remained any longer.

"Virexa has told me much of your Hells and how they differ from my own." Ajuka said, still focused on the lemure. "A facet that interested me was what she said about how devils in the Nine Hells are able to attain greater forms as they grow stronger. Is it possible for this lowly lemure to grow to become a pit fiend?"

Zariel frowned, looking down at the lemure in a new light. "In theory it is possible. In practice it is a different matter. Out of thousands of lemure, perhaps one or two will ever grow to be anything other than what they began as. To grow so far as to become a pit fiend is… Even for other devils with many advantages, that is a rare achievement."

"But the potential exists. I wonder…" Ajuka trailed off, leaning down to inspect the lemure closer.

The lemure was trembling like a shaken bowl of jelly, desperately leaning away from Ajuka's attention.

"I suppose it is a worthy enough experiment." Ajuka held up his hand. In a flash of demonic power, a glowing red Pawn appeared in his hand.

Zariel's breath caught at the sight.

The Nine Hells upheaved following Serafall Leviathan's meeting with Dispatar. A new piece had been placed on the board. Quite literally. Word spread like wildfire that Dispatar now possessed a set of chess pieces able to be used to empower devils that would make them the Lord of Dis's most prized servants. Schemes and open conflict incited immediately. Many devils had perished in the pursuit of Dispatar's attention, desperate to earn the privilege of joining his peerage.

Their infighting proved worthless. So far, Dispatar had used only one of his peerage pieces. He'd told Zariel in a private meeting that it was a proof of concept, a decision made to ensure the pieces worked for devils of the Nine Hells just as they did for the devils of Ajuka's world.

While Zariel believed Dispatar had been validating their function, that was not the only reason why he selected the individual he did.

Zariel's Avernus was constantly under threat from the Abyss. Demon Lords and their underlings rode up the River Styx into Avernus, seeking dominion over the Nine Hells and the material plane beyond. Zariel and her forces stood as the sole bulwark between all of reality and annihilation at the demons' hands.

Demons were not the only force Zariel had to contend with in her home.

Due to ancient bindings, Avernus had long played host to a trapped divine visitor. Dispatar approached Zariel soon after receiving his peerage pieces, requesting her assistance in meeting with the deity who made Avernus her home.

Zariel and her generals escorted Dispatar to a cavern digging into the roots of Avernus. Her generals stayed back as Zariel and Dispatar bargained with the beast.

The five draconic heads of Tiamat grinned as one, amused by Dispatar's request. For centuries, Tiamat's servants had sent her offerings. Some to help her escape to the material plane. Others were simply to make her stay more pleasant. Some were vastly greater than others.

Centuries ago, one of Tiamat's favored clerics sent her an offering of four golden dragon eggs, the favored disciples of her greatest enemy and brother Bahamut. Tiamat raised the dragons, corrupting them with her power, turning them into something mighty and horrible.

Dispatar traded dark magics to Tiamat. In return, one of Tiamat's adopted daughters became Dispatar's Rook.

Zetan the Corrupter could now be seen residing in Dispatar's Iron Tower. Sometimes, the dragon took her true form to fly around the tower or perch atop its peak. At other times, she was seen within the tower itself in her devil form, glowing golden eyes glaring hatefully at any who approached Dispatar's throne with disrespect.

The filling of the single place in Dispatar's peerage did nothing to quell the hysteria of his underlings to earn their own position. It had the opposite effect. More devils slayed each other to usurp their standing in Dispatar's court. Dispatar often complained to Zariel that it was becoming a real problem.

These Evil Pieces were a wondrous item of untold power and potential. The thought that Ajuka was considering using one on a lemure… Zariel could not comprehend it.

"I do not know if Serafall or Carter told you this," Ajuka said, almost to himself. "But I invented the Evil Pieces. I made them centuries ago to bolster our numbers after a great war. I am their creator, yet I have only ever used one of them. My peerage remains unfilled. I cared more about researching than seeking greater power. I already had plenty of power." Ajuka smiled softly. "It feels right that my second peerage member is something of an experiment." Ajuka pressed the Pawn into the lemure.

In a flash of blinding red light, the lemure's body condensed into a small humanoid shape. Devil wings burst forth from its back.

A small boy with ashy gray hair looked up at Ajuka uncomprehendingly. "W-why?" the lemure said.

"You had the potential to become a pit fiend. I wonder if you can still evolve to become a pit fiend now that you are a devil in my peerage. Let's find out together." Ajuka held a hand down to the boy. The boy hesitantly took the Satan's hand and let himself be helped to his feet. He staggered unnaturally, as if unsure how to properly walk.

Zariel laughed, she couldn't help herself.

Ajuka frowned minutely. "Is there a problem, Archduchess."

Zariel shook her head, unable to banish the amused smile from her face. The situation was simply too ridiculous. When was the last time she was this amused? When was the last time she laughed.

…Had she laughed since she fell?

"There is no problem, Satan Beelzebub. It is amusing. Since Satan Leviathan gifted Dispatar his Evil Pieces, many in the Hells have fought to be recognized as worthy of Dispatar's attention. Here, you have elevated a lowly lemure. All of their politicking will amount to nothing. It is truly up to the whims of he who holds the Evil Pieces whom they choose."

Ajuka made an understanding sound. "That actually reminds me. Would you like a set of Evil Pieces, Archduchess?"

Zariel froze, eyes narrowing to slits. Certainly she had misheard him.

"I am afraid I misheard you, Satan Beelzebub."

"You didn't. Would you like a set of Evil Pieces?"

Zariel's tongue felt numb. For the first time in centuries, she wasn't ready with a retort. She didn't know what to say.

"What would you ask in return?" Zariel said carefully. Nothing was free. Even the Evil Pieces Serafall gave to Dispatar were given not out of kindness but to show the Nine Hells how important it was to ally with the foreign devils.

"Consider it payment for being such a fine host during your tour. I enjoyed your company and would like to thank you for it." Ajuka said, his tone of voice and features revealing no trace of a lie, only plain sincerity.

"I…" Zariel shocked herself. Did she just stutter? The Archduchess of Avernus did not stutter.

"I accept." Zariel said firmly.

Ajuka nodded, a satisfied smile on his face. He waved his hand.

A small gasp slipped past Zariel's lips as she felt a source of powerful magic bind itself to her. Instinctually, she raised a hand. A glowing red chess piece appeared in her hand. A Queen. Her Queen. She could feel it, connected to herself by a metaphysical binding not easily severed, perhaps impossible to sever.

Zariel swallowed, taking a moment to compose herself as she banished the Queen. "Thank you, Satan Ajuka."

Ajuka nodded. "You're welcome. And please, just call me Ajuka. Serafall's the one who deals with all of the official business. I'm just here to sightsee."

"Then you may call me, Zariel."

"Shall we continue our tour, Zariel?" Ajuka asked.

Zariel clenched her fist, unwilling to let the tumultuous emotions swirling in her chest show. "We shall."

Zariel continued leading Ajuka through her city, playing the perfect tour guide.

Long after Balthazar Abaddon retrieved Ajuka and the two departed for their own Hell, Zariel remained locked away in isolation, holding her Queen Piece close to her chest.

She hadn't received a gift in centuries. And it was a gift. Ajuka had no ulterior motive for giving her the Evil Pieces. He simply wanted to, so he did.

Zariel smiled at the small chess piece. She made sure no one saw her joy.

It would be troublesome to have to kill any witnesses.


X


Circe had little to do today. Despite the severity of the war Balthazar and Medea had been dragged into, there was now little that could conceivably affect Circe. She lived in a sentient castle protected by Annihilation Maker, hidden by Dimension Lost. Their enemies knew where Balthazar's lands were, but the castle could simply disappear into the mist if ever under threat.

Circe could create items to be used by the devils, but she had no interest in creating tools the devils could potentially use to harm her family. Circe did not enjoy violence. She was capable of visiting it upon those who wronged her, but she much preferred to keep to herself.

She would spend time with Anankos, but her son was out with his father, aunt and uncles, learning how to hunt as Coal put it, 'The way a giant Greek monster should'. Circe was not a giant Greek monster, so she was content to leave Anankos's training in this regard to the capable experts on his father's side of the family.

That left little for Circe to do. Were she still on her island, she would pass the time at her loom. Unfortunately, Circe hadn't thought to bring it with her when she and Anankos left. Perhaps she could make another?

Just as she was beginning to outline a list of supplies she would need for a new loom, a presence tickled the back of Circe's awareness.

Circe smiled, warm and happy. It had been too long.

A teleportation circle expanded out from beneath Circe to whisk her away. She reappeared in one of the many forests in Balthazar's territory. She'd come here before. Once with Anankos and Coal for a hunting lesson and once by herself to gather reagents for the potion she brewed from Khione's last breath. That was one of her more potent creations, rivalling even the brew that brought life to her son.

Circe walked through the trees, following the faint presence at the end of her mind. She stopped in front of a large tree with a thick trunk.

"I know you're here." Circe called, waiting patiently.

There was no reply. Close to a minute after Circe's call, a figure stepped out from behind the tree, footsteps making no sound as they moved over the ground.

A woman emerged. She was small in stature, but her limbs were well-muscled. She wore a tunic made from furs. Mint-colored hair fell down to the midpoint of her back. A bow and a quiver were strung over her shoulder.

Circe recognized the items. How could she not? She made that bow.

"Hello, Circe," Artemis, Greek Goddess of the Hunt, said in greeting.

"Hello, Artemis," Circe replied, a happy smile on her face. "How are you here?"

"Athena found ways for us to enter Hell. I used one of those paths to enter and walked the rest of the way here. I'm not the only one. I was surprised how many people are heading in this direction."

"We're aware. Balthazar and Medea are away. When they come back, we'll see what they want to do about the visitors, but enough about that. It's been too long since I've seen you. I feared I wouldn't see you until the conclusion of the war."

"You likely wouldn't have had I not come on orders." Artemis said, features impassive.

Circe's joy gave way to confusion, then concern. "Orders?"

"Father has ordered me to kill Balthazar Abaddon and his sister."

Circe frowned. "Oh."

Artemis grinned mischievously. "Zeus neglected to give me a timeline for this mission."

Circe's frown morphed into a warm smile. "Oh."

"I hear you have a son now," Artemis said conversationally, but Circe could hear the uncertainty and the hidden question in the words.

Circe laughed, walking up to Artemis and taking her arm, dragging her along behind her.

Artemis stumbled, awkwardly stuttering, though no words came.

"I do have a son," Circe said. "Anankos, son of Coal. His genesis is not what you assume. Coal and I respect one-another, but there is no more to it than that. Would you like to meet Anankos?"

Artemis looked away shyly, a faint blush dusting her cheeks. "I…I would." She laced her fingers through Circe's, leaning into the witch's side.

"Then come. I'm sure he would love to meet you."


X


Remiel trembled as he beheld the vision before his eyes.

The sky opened. Monsters pulled from nightmares fell like rain down upon the Silver City. Try as they might to stem the assault, Heaven's defenders proved insufficient to hold back the tide.

Remiel's fist clenched. His lips thinned into a determined line.

No. This would not come to pass. Remiel would not allow it. He had failed once, but he understood his enemy better now. He would not fail twice.

In his vision, the monsters fell from dark points of nothing in the sky. Holes. This was Balthazar Abaddon's doing. It was as Remiel had always feared, as he'd always known. Balthazar was a threat to the stability of their world. He was a threat to Heaven itself. He needed to be dealt with permanently.

Boreas had failed, but then how could he not have? The god was a fool. Even when Remiel supplied him with the recipe to total victory, the god blundered. There would be no lucky escape for Balthazar this time. Remiel would deal with this personally.

A hand rested on Remiel's shoulder.

"It is time, brother," Seleste said quietly.

Remiel nodded at his sister in thanks.

This time would be different. Remiel knew his enemy. Remiel knew the future he would avert. Balthazar would be distracted by the devils' war with Olympus. And, most importantly, Remiel was not alone.

"We fly, my brothers and sisters!" Remiel called.

Dozens of angels rose into the sky with him, following him as he began the descent to Earth. Together, they would save Heaven's Host. They would save humanity. They would save everything.
