#9,681
Was this how Serafall felt every time I dropped a massive problem in her lap? I hadn't done enough to pay that woman back for all the shit I put her through if she was constantly dealing with crap like this. I needed to get her some more magical girls ASAP.

"I'm sorry," I said, trying to rewire my brain so the sentence I just heard would actually compute. "What?"

"Several thousand refugees from the city the Greeks attacked and several hundred others from across the territories subordinate to Olympus have come seeking asylum." Shiroe repeated distractedly as he poured over a dozen ledgers in front of him. Latia Astaroth scribbled notes into another ledger at his side. Apparently he'd called her for help when he couldn't get in contact with me while I was in Baator.

"Okay, but why are they here?" I was still having trouble processing all of this.

"You saved the devils from the Greeks. They believe they will be safe under your aegis, especially after hearing you withstood Boreas's assault and emerged the victor." Latia said distractedly. "I believe the Greeks are here because of the rumors of you harboring Idyia and Thetis."

"Artemis is here too." Shiroe added.

I felt like I was stun-locked. The moment I began to understand what was going on I got hit with another surprise. "Artemis? You didn't think that telling me a Greek goddess was attacking took priority?"

"She's not attacking." Shiroe assured me. "Zeus sent her here to kill you but he didn't tell her when to kill you. She's been very clear that she plans to carry out his order on your deathbed. She's using it as an opportunity to get out from under his thumb."

"And we're just taking her word on that?"

"Circe trusts her, but I've got eyes on her. Circe took her to meet Anankos while Coal, Chimera, Regulus and Ladon were hunting with him. I sent Matatabi and Irene to join them so they could watch Artemis. She hasn't tried anything yet, so I've been focusing on the refugee crisis. If Artemis makes a move, we can pull everyone to safety with Dimension Lost."

I rubbed my forehead, feeling a migraine coming on.

I just got back from transporting six more groups of devils and Ajuka himself to Faerun so they could make warlocks. Serafall needed me back in a few hours so we could plan an attack on a Greek temple somewhere in the mortal world. With Hole, I was the best choice to transport our forces. Now I had to deal with this mess in my own home?

"How many people are asking for asylum? Do we have a hard number or are we estimating right now?" I asked, trying to process all this.

Shiroe shook his head as he flipped through another book. "We don't have an exact figure yet. The castle is creating creatures to count the refugees, but it is fighting me. Can I be an Abaddon, Balthazar? I don't need a branch or anything. It would really help speed things along. I'd already thought about it before, and with this situation, it's just practical."

"Shiroe, I name you Shiroe Abaddon." I said tiredly, immediately feeling a change come over the man.

Latia paused her note taking to stare up at me in confusion. "Just like that?"

"It's my Clan. I'll do what I want with it." I said a little more defensive than I meant. The exhaustion was starting to get to me.

Latia shrugged, unoffended at my curt response. "Fair enough."

"What do you want to do about this, Balthazar?" Shiroe asked, looking up from the ledgers. As he spoke, a shadowy creature entered the room and dropped three more books atop a stack on his desk before departing. Shiroe looked at the new tomes dejectedly before turning back to look at me. "There are a lot of people asking for refuge. Between the devils and the Greeks… Even if it were just one of the groups, we would struggle to deal with this logistically. We don't have the food stored to feed them all. With Idyia and Thetis, not to mention the other nereids and Oceanids in the group, water wouldn't be a problem, but housing is an issue. We can't feed and house this many people with no notice."

"Give me a second," I said tiredly.

I reached out to my mental connection with Medea. It was far away, as it always was when we were on separate worlds. 'Medea?'

'Yes, honey?'

'There's a…situation here. Have you found what you're looking for?'

When I brought today's first group of devils to Faerun, I also dropped Medea, Shang Tsung and Mothra into Baator. Medea had plans for True Longinus, but she believed she could do something better if she had something to 'corrupt' it. I didn't know exactly what she was looking for, but I figured the Nine Hells would be a good place to start. I didn't want her wandering around Baator alone, so I sent Shang Tsung and Mothra with her. Shang Tsung brought Skarlet along. Between the four of them, they'd be able to look after one-another. And with Shang Tsung there, they would be able to make it back themselves if they encountered anything too dangerous. He could also move them somewhere else if they didn't find what they were looking for.

Ever since absorbing Boreas and having his Pawn permanently promoted to Queen, Shang Tsung's power had exploded. He was constantly generating far more demonic power than anyone else in my peerage, beating out most of them combined. He shone almost as bright as a King Piece. That came with benefits.

Much like I used Bedeze's King Piece to power my trips between worlds, Shang Tsung had experimented and found he could now do the same. When assuming my form to copy Hole, Shang Tsung could walk between worlds. He was not as good with the ability as I was. Each trip left him more and more exhausted. He could only manage two trips in one day without risking passing out, but it was still a massive force multiplier. I now had another peerage member able to walk between worlds with near-impunity. Unlike Medea, Shang tsung could transport people other than himself as well.

'No, but I believe I am close. Do you need me to return?' Medea sent back through our bond.

I pursed my lips as I thought for a moment. I'd been planning to open a small village in my lands for a while now. All of the greater houses in Hell hosted at least a small settlement of vassals with some of the greater Houses boasting multiple large cities. The Bael family had over ten major settlements. I wouldn't be surprised if some of the devils now crowding my lands were refugees from those settlements fleeing the destruction of the Bael Pillar.

With the estimated numbers Shiroe was giving me, this would not be a small village, but it was probably the best chance I'd have to establish a settlement on my lands, especially if I wanted it done fast. The timing was terrible though. A war had just started. A good chunk of the citizens would be Greek. That wouldn't be a problem at any other time, but it was almost guaranteed that there were spies amongst the group trying to ferret out my secrets.

But what would happen if I turned them away? A host of minor goddesses let loose upon the Underworld while we're already dealing with enemies breaching into Hell? At least here, I can keep an eye on them.

'I'll take care of it,' I sent to Medea. 'Let me know when you're done. I'll bring you all back.'

'I will. Let me know if you change your mind and need my help.' Her presence faded from my mind.

I walked up to the wall of the room and laid a hand flat against it. I closed my eyes, reaching out to the intelligence of my castle.

I looked up at the ceiling. "I need you to create a host of creatures for me. Make spies that can watch the refugees for signs of sabotage or espionage. Make guards that can be used to maintain order between them. Make creatures that will be skilled enough to hastily construct small homes, buildings and roads. Once that's done, I want you to litter every acre of my territory with scouts and soldiers. Track down anyone who might have infiltrated my territory with one of these groups and either bring them back to the group or eliminate them if they try something. Send monsters to the border of my lands at the highest traffic points and set up checkpoints so something like this doesn't happen again. Can you do that?"

I felt a swell of pride from the castle. The floor hummed beneath my feet. Annihilation Maker spun to work, creating the workforce I asked for.

"So we're letting them stay?" Shiroe asked.

I nodded. "Get me an accurate count of how many people there are. I need to know how many people we need to feed and house."

"We don't have the supplies stored to…"

Shiroe trailed off as I held up a hand. "I'll deal with that. Just get me the count. And send a message to Serafall to let her know what's happening. Tell her sorry to cause another headache and I promise to do something nice for her." I closed my eyes, connecting to the scrying protections Medea placed around our lands.

Finding what I sought, I opened a Hole and stepped through it.

A cacophony of shouts and panicked cries assaulted my ears the moment I stepped through the Hole. The vast plain beneath me was invisible, hidden behind a packed crowd of devils, nymphs, nereids, oceanids, and all manner of different creatures. I even saw a hellhound mixed into the mass. The devils had gathered together. There was a gap between their group and the Greeks. Both sides were shouting at each-other. I saw glaring faces and powers manifesting. A fight was going to break out at some point if this continued.

Dozens of small Holes opened in the sky above the crowd, all connected to the one I held in my hand.

"Hello," I said through the Hole.

Instantly, the bickering halted. As one, every face in a sea of supernatural creatures turned to look up at me.

"My name is Viscount Balthazar Abaddon, Lord of the House of Abaddon. I understand you are all on my lands seeking refuge, correct?"

A wall of sound assaulted my ears. I couldn't make out a single word as every voice in the crowd began shouting.

"That's enough of that," I said irritably, flaring my power. Maybe it wasn't the best move to let my anger slip out like that, but I was exhausted, and these assholes were trespassing. Granted, I was planning to let them stay, but that didn't mean they hadn't trespassed to get here.

The crowd quieted. Everyone stood still, hanging on my every word.

"I don't have enough buildings to house you. I don't have enough food to feed you. I–"

Someone shouted in dismay, unleashing the rest as everyone began trying to shout over one-another.

"Enough!" I roared, demonic power blasting away from me. My voice echoed over the plain, carried by the Holes I'd created.

I took a moment to calm myself and let the crowd quiet.

"As I was saying, I do not have the means to support you. So I will acquire it. I do not have buildings for you to stay in, so they will be constructed. I do not have the food to feed you, so I will purchase it. This will take time. You will be patient and will not cause any problems while this is done. I am being overly generous not only by allowing you to stay here after trespassing on my lands, but by accommodating you. You will show gratitude. Anyone who takes issue with how I decide to house you is free to leave. Anyone who starts problems or initiates any form of violence will be dealt with, perhaps lethally. I am taking a substantial risk allowing you to stay here. You will appreciate that risk and not cause problems. If you have an issue with how I handle things, you are free to leave. Do I make myself clear?"

Silence answered me.

"Good," I said, letting some of the tension bleed out of me. I'd been running around Faerun for hours and now I had to deal with this mess. I needed a break.

Shadows rose out of the ground into lanky monsters with long claws. Hulking masses of red armor burst from the soil to lumber towards the group.

"These are my underlings," I announced. "Listen to them and do what they say."

Through my Holes, I heard more than one voice whisper 'Annihilation Maker'. It wasn't common knowledge before that Medea had made it so we could use Annihilation Maker. It was now. Hopefully that would keep people from trying to fuck with us.

I stepped through another Hole. "Keep an eye on them. Help Shiroe sort this mess out while I gather supplies. If anyone causes problems, deal with them as you see fit. They've been warned." I said, looking up to the ceiling.

The castle rumbled pleasantly as it received my order.

Sighing, I held up my hand, creating a small Hole. "Aqua, I need your help. Meet me in the ball room."

I closed the Hole and opened another, stepping into the castle's ball room. Spells flew through the air, scattering shadow creatures. Blades sung as they slashed down into hulking armors.

My warlocks and my paladin darted around the ground below, cutting through minions created by Annihilation Maker. With each monster slain, their strength grew. My own power swelled as they grew in strength. They'd only been at this for a few days and I already felt stronger than I had in years. Setting them to work like this was producing incredibly potent results far greater than my old method of sapping away my strength with Hole. It felt like cheating, but I couldn't be bothered to care. I'd need every advantage I could grab in the coming days.

"Hold off on any more monsters," I ordered the castle.

Shadows skulked back into the ground, armors lumbered out of the room. My warlocks and paladin all breathed heavy, turning to face me as I approached.

"My lord," Cyvis said, dipping into a curtsy.

I held up a hand. "Please save the formality for now. I have a headache."

Vellia frowned. "Is there something we can do to help, my lord?"

"That's why I'm here."

Before I could elaborate, a dark Keyhole opened as Aqua stepped up to my side. "You called?" she said.

"Good," I said, addressing everyone. "We're dealing with a refugee crisis. I don't have the food or the housing to take care of them all. I'll send Keno and Irene to purchase what they can locally, but it's not going to be enough on such short notice. Aqua and I are going to take your four back to Faerun. I want you to show us every market you know of and we'll buy them out of everything they have. Once we've exhausted our options there, I'll bring you four back here, and Aqua and I will keep jumping around to other places where we've been buying more materials and food."

"Where are we sending everything?" Aqua asked.

"Just drop everything outside the front door of the castle. The castle will create monsters with Annihilation Maker to carry everything to where it needs to go. Any other questions?"

"How will we acquire the goods, my lord?" Vellia asked. "Do you need us to steal the materials you require?" She didn't seem to have a problem with that idea, she just wanted to know the plan.

"I'm not keen on making enemies if I don't have to. Aqua can access the treasury as easily as I can. I have more money than some pantheons at this point. Just buy everything you can find and I doubt it'll make more than a small dent in my savings." I said.

When no further questions were asked, I turned to Aqua. "You take Vellia and Rath through the Sword Coast and any other place Rath's been. I'll take Cyvis and Tristan through Cormyr and some of the elven lands. We're going to get a very strange assortment of materials, but I have faith the castle will be able to make workable structures from everything."

The castle rumbled, filled with confidence.

"Let's get to it," I said.


X


I returned to the castle, physically and mentally exhausted. Tristan had seen a lot of places when he'd fled Cormy, leading to him knowing a great many places to acquire materials. Cyvis, similarly, travelled a lot as a child while her parents tried to build her into the role as their heir. It took a while to get through every city and buy out most of their food stalls and quarries. We didn't take everything lest we leave a town starving, but we bought up most products on offer and left soon after.

When we finally exhausted the lands they knew, I dropped them both off in the ballroom and continued on my own. I returned to the Elemental Nations to buy more food. I went to the Earthrealm connected to Shang Tsung's Outworld to buy drywall, shingles, and other modern materials. I stopped at each of my mines in Faerun and beyond to gather everything I could.

Aqua was similarly busy, galavanting all over Faerun before returning to the castle to grab Keno and head back to Keno's world to buy even more materials.

At the end of it all, we'd acquired the strangest assortment of building materials around. Shining mithril mixed with regular bricks. High Elven steel forged in Evereska supported timber sourced from Earthrealm.

Were I not so tired, I'd be awed at the mixture of so many worlds coming together into one city. The castle's monsters worked fast. Already, structures were beginning to take shape. I suppose it helped when you could create an infinite supply of labor tailor-made to accomplish whatever task you required at the drop of a hat.

Shiroe and Latia had finished their census. 7,349 devils and 942 one-time Greeks of various origins and species were now sheltered in my lands. The count kept increasing as more and more groups of devils and minor Greeks kept arriving, escorted by monsters created by Annihilation Maker from one of the checkpoints the castle set up. If I didn't have access to a multiverse's worth of resources to draw from, this would have been a massive problem. Even with my advantages, it was still a serious headache.

In human terms, over seven-thousand people wasn't very much. In devil terms, it was unprecedented. Since the rise of popularity of the Evil Pieces, devilkind's numbers had been swelling drastically, but many of the old Pillars and noble devils had gone extinct or were near-extinct. Even with the surplus of population from the Evil Pieces, we still had less than a million devils all told. I wasn't sure what the exact number was. Probably somewhere between three-hundred-thousand and seven-hundred-fifty-thousand at a brief guess, but it was nothing compared to the number of humans on Earth.

Over seven-thousand devils sought me out for protection rather than going to Lucifaad for the New Satan's help. They came to me over Pillars like the Sitri, Agares and Gremory that have been sturdy sentinels for centuries. No, they came to a near-extinct house that only recently rose to contend with the greater powers of the Underworld.

I didn't have the energy to deal with the implications of that right now.

I was taking a break. Suspended high in the air, I looked down on shadowy monsters as they hastily erected structures. Foundations needed to be set to make permanent housing. Most of the construction efforts were dedicated towards that while a smaller group of creatures sent up temporary tents and simple structures. Hulking beasts of red, armored rock distributed exotic fruit and strange meat no one on this Earth would recognize.

It was safe to assume that my secret would be out in the near future. There was little other explanation for how I was able to get all of this set up on such short notice. Maybe it was just the exhaustion, but I couldn't bring myself to care.

Before, I was deathly terrified about my secret getting out because it would paint a target on my back. People would come after me, come after my peerage, to try to force our cooperation. That wasn't such a scary thought any more. Medea bound two Longinus Sacred Gears to my castle, both of which synergized to give me an infinite army I could deploy anywhere I wished without even using Hole. If anyone attacked me again like Boreas did, I could simply disappear into the mist. I hadn't tested it yet, but I might even be able to work with Aqua to supercharge the castle's ability and move the entire castle away from Hell itself.

Even if someone managed to kill me, those two Longinus-class Sacred Gears would still be bound to my castle. My peerage would be able to make use of them. Any of my potential children would be able to make use of them. They would now serve the Abaddon family for all time, an eternal stick we could use to threaten anyone who wanted to fuck with us.

I sighed, closing my eyes and rubbing my forehead.

This was a headache. It would be worse without Shiroe. The man was working overtime, drawing up maps of the city-to-be on my land and working closely with the castle to make sure every arrival in my land was taken care of and that the monsters built their structures in a way that wouldn't create problems later. I doubted Shiroe had a background in city planning, but some talent he possessed from his game avatar was letting him cheat. He'd drawn up sewers, power stations, city centers, parks – all the utilities and niceties one would expect in a city with the conveniences of the modern world. If I were paying him, I'd give him a raise. As it was, he already had one of the debit cards I gave to everyone in my peerage with near-total access to my bank account. I'd make sure he used it to buy or do something nice for himself when all of this was dealt with.

I took a deep breath, slowly starting to wind down. I was tired. I'd done all I could for right now, so I was going to take a nap.

Moments from opening a Hole to my bed so I could sleep, I felt a ping through the wards. My drowsiness fled, washed away by a tide of adrenaline. Amethyst mist rose from the ground below me, sheltering the burgeoning structures of my city and whisking them away to safety. Confused refugees were sent away, their cries of alarm cut off as Dimension Lost shunted them elsewhere. Monsters rose from the mist, flying up into the air, screeching in challenge as they rose to meet their foe.

High in the sky, suspended on ivory wings, dozens of angels appeared from nowhere. They were everywhere. Hundreds of them.

A powerful pulse of magic crackled from below me. I caught sight of one of the refugees, a woman holding a torch whose face was obscured by a dark robe. She stepped away from Dimension Lost's mist as it moved to envelop her. A shadowy monster rose from her shadow. The monster made from Annihilation Maker struck towards her as she worked her magic only to be battered into nothing as the woman flicked her hand and unleashed a rush of magical force directly into the creature.

Magic suffused the air. The woman's torch flared bright, its flame rising to encompass her body. She disappeared.

The angels in the sky, summoned by whatever power the woman wielded, let out challenging cries and cheers.

One angel, leading the others, spread his arms wide, twelve brilliant wings unfurled behind him.

"Your reckoning has come, devil!" the angel cried. A shining sword of pure radiant power appeared in the archangel's hand. Four more angels flew up beside him. Each of these had ten wings.

"For the light of Heaven!" the angel called. He tucked his wings around his body, falling into a dive. Annihilation Maker monsters were sundered from his path as he unleashed radiant power into them.

Holes opened all around me.

"The entire Heavenly host appeared on my lands and is attacking. I need support now." I said clinically. More Holes opened above me, blasting spears, daggers and elemental fire towards the angels. The vast majority of the angels resisted or dodged my attacks. A scant few with only two wings were impaled or scorched by flame, tumbling uncontrollably on their wings as they fell to the ground dead. More angels were torn down by monsters flying on shadow wings.

The angels' numbers were so vast as to fill the entire sky, yet Annihilation Maker's monsters were unending. They continued to fly up and assault the angels. Most scattered into nothing before ever reaching the angel's charging line, destroyed by a cast spell or flung spear of radiant light. Some scored a hit before being destroyed. A rare few slew a single angel as they were slain.

Lightning crackled above. With a snap of thunder, a lightning bolt scored a path down through Annihilation Maker's horde. Dark clouds gathered as more and more lightning bolts fell. The wind picked up. Blades of air whipped up into a tornado that tore its way across the ground. Fire and ice wove within the tornado, flying free to destroy swathes of my monsters, clearing the angel's path towards the ground.

Dimension Lost's mist swelled up from the ground, condensing into a titanic mass like a mountain of fog. A thunderous rushing of air heralded the arrival of a grand structure. Dark walls standing strong. Spiked towers reaching towards the sky. The majesty of Castle Abaddon made itself known, transported through Dimension Lost's mist to the battlefield.

Immediately, the castle's gem turrets unleashed their spells, firing streams of magic into the sky like tracer rounds fired from anti-aircraft canons. Dark shadowy tendrils rose from the ground to tear at the shifting tornado destroying my monsters even as the tornado altered its course towards the castle

The angels were so shocked by the castle's sudden appearance that many of them faltered in their charge, spreading their wings wide to brake against the air. Several of them were blasted by the castle's magic. Some were even killed. It wasn't enough.

The angels regrouped and continued downwards. They'd lost several of their brothers and sisters. There was still a sea of divine messengers flooding down towards me. Even with Annihilation Maker, I couldn't fight this many alone.

"Balthazar, open a path for us to join you!"

"We're coming, Bal!"

"I am here, Balthazar!"

"Bal, open a Hole right fucking now!"

Many voices spoke through the Holes around me. I'd expected maybe one or two responses over the course of several minutes. Instead, almost everyone I reached out to was responding immediately.

A Hole opened at my side. It wasn't one of mine.

Kuisha led the way through, followed closely by Sairaorg and the rest of his peerage.

Pink hair crowned by horns emerged from another Hole, followed by a woman with pale skin and snake scales gently dotting her face. Roygun led her peerage into the air at my side.

The air crackled with demonic power as a man with bone-white hair in a dark coat floated through another Hole. A woman with shining skin and white hair engulfed in amber fire drifted through the Hole at his side. Diehauser looked almost as murderous as his Queen as they both glared up at the angels falling towards us. The rest of his peerage followed through the Hole behind him.

White mist spread from the final Hole. Jagged fractals of ice gathered and launched skyward, heralding the arrival of a dark-haired woman in black armor with glacial designs. Serafall Leviathan raised her arms, summoning an icy vortex to rip asunder the flaming tornado that had been destroying my monsters.

"We need to deal with this fast," Serafall said, sounding pissed. Her hair was levitating away from her body. Her eyes glowed a chilled blue. This was the most enraged I'd ever seen her. "The Greeks just launched an attack against Lucifaad. Sirzechs and Baldur are there, but they need help. I was about to call you in to transport others when you reached out. Everyone kill the angels until they run away, then we go back to Lucifaad. Remiel is mine."

The air split in Serafall's wake. A sonic boom shook the air as she rocketed into the sky, beelining directly towards the twelve-winged angel.

The rest of the angels had halted their charge again, looking between one-another in uncertainty at the force of devils arrayed against them.

"I've been looking forward to this," Roygun said, an evil grin on her face as she held out a hand.

An angel screamed, his body splitting in half as Crack tore him apart. The spray of his golden blood painted the once pristine wings of his brothers and sisters.

Angels roared in fury, resuming their charge. Devils rose to meet them.

I was getting really tired of people trying to attack me. I was going to work out that frustration on these idiot angels.

#9,769
For a long time now, I tried to keep my cards close to my chest. I was afraid if people knew what I could do, they would come after me. I was afraid unseen enemies would kill me or worse, that they'd kill those close to me. My initial desire to create a strong peerage was mostly borne of a desire to have people willing and able to defend me when my secrets finally got out. Then Magdaran sent me an innocent letter I'd wrongly interpreted as a bomb. Then I made Medea my Queen.

I steadily built my peerage with Medea. With each new addition, I cared less and less about raw strength and more about an individual's ability to mesh with those I'd already recruited. My peerage were no longer guards against unseen enemies, they were family.

Years ago, I set out to grow powerful and influential enough to stand on my own two feet. I'd done that and more. I was one of the strongest lords of Hell. I was one of the single most wealthy individuals in the supernatural. I had built a family around myself that I would do anything to protect.

Somewhere along the way, my main goal changed from keeping myself safe to keeping us safe. What was the purpose of money if I couldn't use it to buy teddy bears for Aqua? What was the point of gathering more and more land if I didn't let Coal hunt the mystical creatures that dwelled in those lands?

Where most devils would keep reaching for more and more, I was satisfied. I was more than satisfied. I was happy.

I'd built a life I never would have expected I'd live. I had everything I could ever want and more. I had no desire to reach for more.

But certain idiots couldn't leave well-enough alone.

The Greeks were one matter. I could see how, from a warped perspective, I had wronged them. Whatever. I was dealing with it. Heaven? What crime had I committed against the Silver City? Maybe they didn't like my wife breaking the Sacred Gears they used to enslave anything and everything their dearly departed daddy could get his grubby little hands on. Oh no! I broke their slave engines! I guess in their eyes that warrants a full invasion.

Even at the start of all this when my ambition was at its most fiery, I never wanted to stand among the world's titans. I didn't care about amassing so much power as to make pantheons bleed. That much attention really just sounded like a never-ending headache. Everything I'd done, I'd done to safeguard the future I was building for myself and my peerage, yet everyone seemed to think I had it out for them specifically on a personal level when they didn't factor into my decision making at all. Maybe from their perspective, I was a horrible threat to their way of life. I had no real way to know. I didn't live their life. I couldn't completely understand their perspective. I didn't care either way.

These bastards came to my home. They clearly didn't stop to think about how well that worked out for Boreas. The deceased god of the North Wind at least had a semblance of a plan that posed a genuine threat to me. But this pathetic attempt by the angels? No. They appear high in the skies above my home and charge downward, a shared battle cry on their lips. The fools must think dear dead daddy's great power is still with them.

Boreas hid his forces in Dimension Lost when he attacked me, making it nearly impossible to affect them. Without Aqua, we would have been in serious trouble while fighting him. The angels had no such protection. All they brought with them was a target rich environment.

The air above us was filled with dark spots like a body ridden with plague. Holes opened all around the Heavenly host. Above. To the side. Below.

The air screamed as six massive orbs of destructive force flew through six separate Holes as I unleashed bijuu bombs Matatabi had stored in my pocket spaces.

Angels screamed. Perfect feathers scattered to rain down as Heaven's unified charge was fractured under the force of titanic explosions. Annihilation Maker's monsters wasted no time flowing into the angels' broken ranks, sowing discord even if they weren't capable of doing much damage to the armored angels. They didn't need to. They were just the distraction.

"I will transport you wherever you need to go," I called to my gathered allies. The top two Rating Game peerages were present. Sairaorg's peerage was present. My peerage was emerging through Holes all around us. Above, Serafall was an icy blur, battling six powerful angels at once. She could use some help.

Coal roared as he appeared right next to her through a Hole, jaws clamping down on an eight-winged angel.

"Thank you for coming," I said calmly to my allies, lips thinning into a line. "Please assist me in destroying these creatures."

Roygun laughed, a merry sound. "With pleasure." She dashed through a Hole, her Queen on her heels. They appeared amidst the angels' ranks, hurling spells and rending angels apart with Crack. I opened more Holes around them, supporting them with elemental fire and an inexhaustible supply of enchanted weapons.

Pearl-colored energy exploded into being around Sairaorg. "Kuisha, stay with Bal to coordinate. Ladon, Chimera, Regulus, Ladon, you're all with me. Everyone else, guard Kuisha." Sairaorg's soared into the sky, kicking against the ground. Small, controlled explosions lit up the air beneath his feet, sending him soaring into the sky, the peerage members he named hot on his heels.

"I will support the Leviathan," Diehauser said, eyes narrowed as he glared up at the angels. "I leave the outliers to you, Balthazar." His body blurred as he dashed high into the sky, his peerage slowly following in a tight formation as they met the angel's shattered line.

My allies cut into the chaos I created in the angels' formation, gaining ground, but the angels were slowly recovering. Best for me to stop that from happening.

An illusion rendered me invisible as a Hole pulled me down to the ground. I floated horizontal, staring up at the sky, floating just a few feet off the ground. The lower vantage gave me a better view of the battle above. There were plenty of devils on the field able to fight up close and personal. In this battle, I would be most useful supporting from a distance.

Flames roared forth from a Hole behind Roygun, turning the angel striking at her from behind to ash. Glowing spears covered in runes launched out of a Hole above Sairaorg, turning the angels trying to flank him into a pincushion.

I wasn't sure how the angels thought this would go, but the reality of the situation was certainly not what they intended.

Golden blood fell like rain. Once pristine feathers were blasted from Holy wings to flutter to the ground. Limp angelic forms fell from the sky, swallowed before they could reach the ground by a starving mist that permeated the battlefield. Every moment, twisted shadows borne of nightmares and massive crimson forms of jagged rock and hatred emerged from the mist all around the angels, surrounding them.

I frowned. I heard screaming. My eyes scanned the sky, searching for the source.

There, high above the panicked mass of angels desperately trying to regroup to weather the combined assault of two Longinus-Class Sacred Gears and some of the strongest peerages in Hell, Diehauser and Serafall squared off against a group of angels held in reserve. Each angel had at least eight wings. Most had ten or twelve. One of the twelve-winged angels was screaming in fury, practically frothing at the mouth as he hurled light spears.

Holes opened in the paths of the light spears, absorbing them before Diehauser or Serafall had to worry about dodging.

I was far away, but I could still see the change that passed over the angel as his attack was thwarted by my power. He thrashed in the air, screaming curses. I caught something about instability and unholiness, but my attention was split. While the angel was throwing his tantrum, a group of seven angels tried to surround Chimera. Four of them fell with magical daggers buried in their body. The final three fell to Chimera's claws.

Lightning split the sky. Ladon howled in pain as a crackling bolt of energy struck him square in the chest. Black scales sprouted from his flesh as he began to change into his draconic form. Another lightning bolt clipped him in the shoulder, spinning him downward through the air before he caught himself on massive leathery wings.

Dark storm clouds gathered in opposition to Dimension Lost's mist. Electric energy crackled within the clouds, snapping out towards my allies. Any of the Annihilation Maker monsters that got too close to the clouds was instantly struck by a bolt of energy and sundered.

I slipped through another Hole to reposition myself, scanning the battlefield for the source of the clouds and the lightning. It wasn't unheard of for angels to be spellcasters, but more often than not, their power was based solely in holy power, not in controlling the weather. So who was throwing the lightning around? Was it the same witch who'd hidden among the refugees and opened the way for the angels to break through the wards at the edge of my lands?

Wind screamed in my ears. A hundred meters from the castle, another flaming tornado spun to life, spitting lightning towards my allies, launching massive chunks of earth towards the castle. Paradoxically, shards of ice flew out of the tornado of fire in all directions, cutting into the monsters created by Annihilation Maker. Many of the beasts were slain, but they were easily replaced. More creatures spawned from the mist of Dimension Lost and took to the sky to join the fight against the invaders.

The castle stood tall despite the tornado's assault. Every projectile was absorbed into Dimension Lost. Some were even launched back into the air towards the approaching angelic horde, though the castle relied mainly on Medea's gem turrets to attack.

I absorbed as many lightning strikes as I could into Holes before they could strike my allies, but a sparse number of them got past me. Luckily, they struck larger targets like Coal, Regulus or Ancas – devils able to take the hit and keep fighting. It wouldn't be long before whoever this lightning wielder was snuck a bolt past me to strike someone who couldn't take it. I needed to find them and eliminate them.

I closed one eye while searching the field with the other. The scrying protections Medea wove into the foundation of our lands lit up my awareness. The overpowering presence of holy energy was almost blinding, making it nearly impossible to spot anything through the tide of the angels' power. I wouldn't have been able to find my target if he wasn't special himself.

Suddenly, the flaming tornado and the rapid lightning strikes made sense. It wasn't a god fighting on the angels' side. Rather, it was a mortal carrying one of the strongest Sacred Gears in existence – the Longinus Zenith Tempest.

Zenith Tempest granted the holder supreme command over the elements, turning the wielder into a walking apocalypse. They could summon the weather to tear down a city. They could call on the waters of the ocean to wash away armies. Accounts from the past spoke of these very acts occurring when Zenith Tempest was wielded by someone long enough to master its power. From what little I remembered of him from my first life, Dulio Gesualdo, the current holder of Zenith Tempest, was skilled enough with his Sacred Gear to earn the attention of Michael himself. I needed to deal with him now.

While my allies continued shredding into the angels' rapidly deteriorating forces, I passed through another Hole.

I reappeared high above my lands, farther in the sky than even than where Serafall and Diehauser were dispatching another ten-winged angel. The screaming twelve-winged dove was turning hysterical, clutching his head and muttering something about 'it' being gone and how he could no longer see. I trusted Diehauser and Serafall to manage on their own for the time being. I would support them once the walking apocalypse was dealt with.

Dulio floated in the air, currents of wind holding him aloft above the battlefield. A group of angels floated around him in a protective wing. Each of them had eight wings.

"The Abaddon is here!" one of the angels screamed, eyes glowing bright gold as she hurled a light spear at me despite my invisibility.

A Hole opened in front of the spear while another opened behind the angel's head. Her spear vanished into the Hole between us while a different spear rocketed out of the Hole behind her head and tore through the front of her face. I would have hit her with her own spear if I wasn't so uncertain about whether or not angels could be harmed by their own holy power. Now was not the time to experiment or let idiotic pride cost me victory. I would do what had worked so far and kill all of these idiots. Medea, Shang Tsung and Irene could experiment with their corpses later.

Dulio spun around as the other angels rallied to attack me.

Elemental fire poured forth from several Holes, atomizing two more angels before they could react.

Dulio raised a hand. I felt my connection to my fire snap away as he used Zenith Tempest to wrest it out of my control.

I immediately closed every connection I had to the Elemental Plane of Fire. His command of the weather was already proving to be the largest threat to my allies on the battlefield. I couldn't risk Dulio gaining control of even more Elemental Fire.

Small, marble-sized Holes opened around Dulio as more of his angelic body guards fell to enchanted spears and daggers fired from my improvised Gate of Babylon.

Dulio grunted in pain as I forced demonic power through the Holes I held in my hands, channeled through the marble-sized openings around Dulio to greatly increase the pressure they struck with.

I grunted in pain as a blade of wind cut into me from behind. I maneuvered through a Hole, reappearing above Dulio. I raised my hands over my head, roaring in exertion as I created a massive orb of pure demonic power.

Dulio looked up, slashing his arms towards me to throw my own Elemental Fire at me on a current of cutting wind.

I grinned, letting the orb of demonic power I'd manifested scatter into nothing as I fled through a Hole, dodging Dulio's attack. He'd fallen for my trick. I was an Abbadon. My Clan Trait was Hole. I could strike from any angle I desired. I didn't need a fancy light show to defeat my opponents. They made for good distractions though.

The air screamed for an entirely different reason as four Tailed Beast Bombs appeared in the air all around Dulio.

The blonde man's green eyes widened in shock as he realized his predicament. He was so focused on me that he hadn't seen my attack coming. He raised his arm, attempting something when all four bombs detonated.

A titanic shockwave split the sky, knocking several angels into uncontrolled, tumbling freefall as an explosion as large as my castle lit up the sky.

'Honey, I need help,'

Medea suddenly speaking into my mind caught me so off guard I almost let a light spear hurled by an enraged angel strike me. I centered myself and opened a Hole to suck it away at the last second.

'I'm fighting an army of invading angels. Are you in immediate danger? Can it wait?' I sent back, punching demonic power through the throat of the angel that tried to skewer me as I searched the sky for Dulio. Those Tailed Beast Bombs had connected, but I wasn't counting the bastard dead until I saw a body. The flame tornado was still raging on the ground and the electrified clouds still suffused the sky, granted with far less zeal than they did previously.

'Angels? Invading? I'm coming back.'

'It's mostly handled. I just need to finish off Zenith Tempest and we…' My eyes narrowed.

There. Two angels each with six wings held Dulio's arms as they dragged him behind them through the air at breakneck speeds. Dulio looked rough. His clothes were blasted apart. Blood leaked from his ears and nose. His chest and face were heavily burned. Those Tailed Beast Bombs should have killed him outright. Either he managed to save himself with Zenith Tempest somehow or he had immensely powerful divine protections layered over him before the fight. Even with whatever he'd used to survive, he was barely able to keep his eyes open. The man was on his last legs.

'Zenith Tempest?'

I grinned. I recognized the intrigued tone in Medea's voice. I opened three Holes. The angels hauling Dulio away gagged as enchanted daggers tore into their throats. Dulio gasped in panic as a hand closed down around his throat like a vice. His lethargic eyes widened in panic as Medea's cruel grin emerged from the Hole in front of him.

"Rule Breaker!" A twisted knife fell.

Dulio screamed in agony as light poured out of his chest where Medea's dagger struck. Instantly, the flaming tornado unraveled. The dark clouds striking my monsters dimmed and were swallowed by the mists of Dimension Lost.

Medea tucked something away in her robe as she hastily looked around, frowning. "Why didn't you call me back immediately? I missed all the fun."

"You were busy. I would have brought you back if so many of our friends hadn't shown up. The angels really had no idea what they were facing." I said, watching the horrified expressions of several nearby angels as they realized their Longinus wielder just fell. The battle had been joined for less than ten minutes, and they'd already lost over a fourth of their number. Meanwhile, our side's only casualties were some bruises and lost Annihilation Maker monsters. Between myself, Kuisha and Dimension Lost, the vast majority of the angels' more powerful attacks were sucked away harmlessly, leaving our monsters and skilled fighters to tear the doves apart. Now that Dulio was gone, they didn't stand a chance, and they clearly knew it.

"I found what I was looking for, but it can wait until this is done. Shang Tsung and Skarlet are examining it while Mothra defends them. They can hold for a while."

As more and more angels took stock of their situation, the number of retreating angels steadily increased until the vast majority of the invasion force was running in all directions. They may have known about the defenses the castle used when fighting Boreas, but they clearly had no idea what my Queen had done to bind Dimension Lost and Annihilation Maker to the castle. This attack was suicidal, and they wouldn't have been so unbelievably stupid as to strike with the knowledge of what we were now capable of. It appeared my enemy underestimating me once more led to that enemy's ruin.

A thunderous boom had me retreating into a Hole before I recognized the cause.

"Serafall, are you–"

"The problem here is solved," Serafall cut me off seriously. "The angels are fleeing and Diehauser and I managed to take out two major seraphs. Raphael and Ryzoel died buying Remiel time to teleport away. I'll take the trade. Raphael would've been a bigger problem in the coming war with Heaven, and Ryze is…" She shook her head. "Nevermind that. Let everyone else clean up here. I need you to bring the two of us to Asgard now. We need to pick up some support and head directly to Lucifaad."

"What about–"

"Sirzechs was fighting Ares and Aphrodite when I left. Baldur was facing down a hydra and a dragon. The Greeks split their forces between Lilith and Lucifaad. We need to get back to Lucifaad now so we can repel that attack and head to Lilith to help Ajuka and Falbium."

A Hole opened near me.

"Go, Balthazar," Kuisha said through the Hole. "Sai and I will help Medea take care of things here. I will transport everyone to Lucifaad when all of the angels have been dealt with."

"Why can't Kuisha just–"

"Odin wants you, now move." Serafall all but demanded.

I cast one last look around. Dimension Lost shielded my lands. Annihilation Maker created monsters to tear down the few angels too stubborn to flee. Diehauser and Roygun's peerages killed the stronger angels and gave chase to the angels who were unable to teleport away as some others had. Whatever method they used to bypass Medea's wards clearly wasn't functioning anymore.

Medea laid a hand on my shoulder. "I will ensure everything is dealt with, then join you in Lucifaad."

"Fine," I said. "Let's make this quick."

I opened a Hole, pulling us to Asgard.

I was shocked by what awaited us. Odin was really pulling out all the stops, wasn't he?


X


Serafall and I stepped through a Hole, our wings exploding from our backs to catch us. High in the sky, we looked down on Lucifaad. Hell's capitol had seen better days, but it wasn't beyond saving yet.

Devils, elementals, harpies, sirens, griffins, and even a couple dragons flew in and around the city. The massive bodies of the green black, serpentine dragons swopped down to strike at buildings before climbing back into the sky. Groups of devils gathered together to repel the dragons' attacks, but they were assaulted from all sides by other flying monsters.

On the ground, fighting between buildings on shattered streets, more devils clashed with amazons and other Greek fighters. Even more monsters cluttered the roads – hellhounds, minotaurs, cyclopses. This was a true invasion, but it seemed the devils were holdings. Our side held many key areas of the city, sending reinforcements where they were needed and pulling troops back to rest. The ground was still covered in the bodies of our dead, but we weren't beaten yet.

Far to the east, the sky ruptured. Dark energy snapping at the air swirled into the sky. A point of pure nothing sent its power forth. Moving faster than any being I'd fought, clad in nothing but a corona of golden power, a nude woman wielding a heart-tipped spear and shield leapt up towards the point of destruction. Another figure, bronze skin gleaming with power, leapt at the point of darkness from the other side. This figure wore a chestplate, a helmet and greaves, but his arms were bare. He thrust his own spear towards the dark shape.

The shape twisted unnaturally, slipping between the two forms and flowing higher into the air. Tendrils of pure destructive power grew out of the shape, lashing downward towards its foes. The spear wielders spun away from the devastating attacks, already moving to strike again.

Further away, near the limits of the city, a smaller man in norse armor adorned in furs roared in challenge as he leapt into the air. He collided with one of the massive serpentine dragons, striking at the city, driving his sword deep into the dragon's flesh behind its head, securing his sword as a handhold he used to pull the dragon downward.

The dragon roared in pain, its flight thrown off course by the Norse god's strength. Baldur leapt free of the dragon's back moments before it crashed into the ground, tearing through a building on its way down.

"You know the plan." Serafall said quickly, eyes narrowed in fury towards where the destructive form of Sirzechs battled Aphrodite and Ares. Icy mist drifted off her body into the air.

I opened a Hole in front of her. "This will take you above them. Give them Hell."

I felt a physical force blast into me as Serafall's power exploded. She dashed through the Hole, appearing in the sky above Sirzechs. She held her arms out at her side and screamed. The clouds, flash froze as every point of moisture fell under her command. A scream of rage tearing past her lips, Serafall flung an entire sky's worth of ice down towards the Greek gods who thought to take our city.

I took a moment to assess the best way to help. I wasn't keen on fighting a god, or multiple gods for that matter, but that wasn't my task here. I was the support mage for this fight. I just needed to assess who needed help the most.

Serafall's sudden arrival had shocked Aphrodite and Ares. They'd emerged mostly unscathed from her initial, furious attack, sporting only minor cuts and bruises from the ice shards, but they were on the back foot. They fought a fighting retreat as Sirzechs fell upon them, destroying everything in his path. Serafall boxed them in with massive spikes of ice jutting from the ground whenever it looked like they were regaining their footing. For now, the Satans had the gods handled.

Best to help Baldur then.

A yawning void of darkness opened in the air above where Baldur pulled a dragon from the sky. The dragon was just starting to pull itself together, taking to the sky. It didn't make it far.

A howl split the air as if signalling the end of the world. All around the city, combat paused for a brief moment as Fenrir's cry cut through the sky. The massive beast who, had Ragnarok come to pass, would be known as Odin's Bane leapt through the Hole I opened, pouncing on the recovering dragon.

The dragon howled in agony, desperately thrashing as Fenrir's jaws closed around its neck. Blood squelched through Fenrir's jaws as he slowly crushed down on the dragon.

The other Greek dragon roared in fury, spinning down through the air towards Fenrir's back. A second Hole opened in the dragon's path.

The dragon's charge was stopped dead. The beast was sent flying backwards through the air, groaning weakly as Thor rocketed out of the Hole, riding Mjolnir through the sky. Lightning gathered around his body, crackling away to strike harpies and elementals. Thor's entire body was bathed in a corona of electric power. A blue demon to match the dark void that was Sirzech's form of destruction.

Floating in the air, the electricity-covered form of Thor turned to me, eyes glowing with power. "They are ready, Balthazar. Call them." With a snap of thunder, he struck towards the ground, crushing into the dragon he'd sent flying.

I held my arms out at my sides, opening Holes all over the city, dotting the sky. A warhorn sounded from somewhere, heralding the arrival of a host of warriors falling from the sky. They wore sturdy armor adorned in feathers and furs. Their weapons varied from axes and swords to spears and warhammers. Each of the warrior women flew on hawk-like wings. The valkyries descended upon Lucifaad, striking at the Greek invaders.

Below, the first dragon's struggle ceased as its body went limp. Fenrir released its body, throwing his head back to howl in triumph, his roar mixing with the call of the warhorn.

All at once, the tide of the battle shifted. The devils had been slowly falling back to weather the tide of the Greeks. Now, many Greeks openly fled. Some tried to teleport, panicking when Lucifaad's wards barred their transit. Others regrouped, readying to face the might of the valkyries.

"No!" A cry of abject anguish washed over the battlefield.

I turned, grinning evilly at the sight.

I hadn't seen how it happened, but Sirzechs somehow caught Ares by the throat. His other arm was punched through Ares's chest. Everywhere Sirzechs' form of pure destruction touched the God of War, his body began to disintegrate outward. Ares opened his mouth uncomprehendingly as his chest evaporated around Sirzechs' arm. He gagged as Sirzechs' fingers on his throat dug through his deteriorating flesh.

Aphrodite wailed in agony and fury. Golden power erupted from her body, glowing so bright as to blind any who beheld her. She leapt from the ground towards Sirzechs. Thor intercepted her part-way to her target, sending the both gods crashing to the city streets below. His electric aura mixed with her golden corona, lighting up the sky.

I wasn't the only one to witness the defeat and slow death of Ares. Before it was only a handful. Now, whole swathes of Greek fighters turned and fled. A few, mainly the amazons, did the opposite. They howled in rage and charged as one, meeting the valkyrie tide blow for blow, but their allies were leaving them en masse.

The Battle of Lucifaad was all but decided in our favor. It was time to see to the situation in Lilith.

A Hole swallowed me, pulling me away.

Despite its prominence in Hell, I'd never been to Lilith before. I did most of my personal business in Lucifaad. It was where my office building was. It was where Serafall was headquartered. While my business had a presence in Lilith, Latia and Kuisha were the only ones to actually do anything here. I had no frame of reference for what this city looked like prior to this destruction.

Lilith looked far worse off than Lucifaad had. Whatever defense the devils had been able to marshall in Lucifaad clearly hadn't worked as effectively here.

Buildings were torn from their foundations. Rubble painted the roads. What structures weren't destroyed or torn up sported serious damage.

High in the sky, an elderly woman wearing a green dress floated with her hands out at her sides. A sickle was clasped tight in her right hand. Power exploded around her. Hurricane-force winds tore through the entire city at her command. Ice and frost gathered, falling as massive icicles to crush all in their path. This was Demeter, Goddess of the Harvest, Harbinger of the changing of the Seasons.

At her side floated two others. The first was a woman in a white dress with a shawl of peacock feathers. She stared down at the city disapprovingly. The Queen of Olympus, the Goddess of Marriage. Hera.

At her side, a mountain of a man lounged on a throne of clouds. His pure white hair and beard were clouds. The air around him crackled with his power. Every few seconds, he would flick his wrist, sending a bolt of powerful lightning down into the city. The tyrant himself. Zeus, Godking of Olympus, Lord of the Sky.

Falbium Asmodeus hovered beneath the trio of gods, sweat beading his brow as he maintained dozens of powerful magical shields. Asmodeus absorbed the worst of the Demeter and Zeus's attacks, but, powerful as he was, he was only one man. He wasn't able to block everything, leaving the city below to suffer under Olympus's might.

Ajuka Beelzebub flew in a wide circle around the floating Olympians, striking out with his magic. A god in golden armor with wings on his shoes pursued Ajuka, harrying the Super Devil to ensure he never had time to set up any truly devastating attacks. Whenever Ajuka turned his attention fully to Hermes to rid himself of the annoyance of the Messenger God, Zeus would alter his attention, flinging lightning bolts at Ajuka to buy Hermes an opportunity to escape before returning his attention to the destruction of the city.

It was no wonder Lilith was in such dire straights. Falbium and Ajuka were doing everything they could to buy the defenders on the ground a chance. It wasn't enough. The tide of Greek monsters and amazons washed over the devils like a seemingly unstoppable force.

Holes opened all around the street. Elemental Fire poured forth, scoring monsters and amazons alike to ash.

Devils paused in their desperate flight, looking up at where I floated high above them.

More Holes opened. Enchanted weapons fell, not launched, at the feet of the devils.

"Defend yourselves," I said through my Holes, my voice carried across the entire city. "Help has arrived."

I looked back up at the sky. A spike of dread punched into my chest as I met Zeus's eyes. He was looking right at me. His relaxed, almost uncaring air was gone. He stood from his throne of clouds, footfalls echoing through the air as he walked down the air itself as if stepping down a staircase.

"Finally we meet, insect," Zeus said. The air carried his voice. Despite the cast distance between us, I heard him as if he'd spoken right next to me. "Look around, little devil. You are to blame for all of this. Offer me your life, and I will consider sparing your parasitic race."

"Do you ever tire of hearing yourself talk?"

A man with a hunched back emerged from a Hole at my side. His feet came to rest on glowing runes that appeared with each step. He stood high in the sky, staring up at Zeus, unimpressed. A dark cloak covered in runes fluttered in a gentle breeze. The dark haft of a bronze-tipped spear rested easily in his hand like a walking stick.

Zeus growled. "Odin, still consorting with the scum of the world, I see."

"Zeus," Odin said, sounding tired of the conversation. "Still fucking your sister, I see. Looking resplendent as always, Hera. As is befitting of the Goddess of Marriage. Tell me dear, when was the last time he warmed another woman's bed? Two weeks ago? Or could he not control himself even that long?"

"Hold. Your. Tongue." Zeus ground out through clenched teeth. Lightning danced around his body. Dark, rumbling stormclouds gathered overhead.

"Actually, it's in your best interest that I keep talking." Odin said, gently tapping his eye-patch. "I've been peering into the future. It's amazing how much is open to you when everything you hold dear isn't poised on the brink of destruction."

Zeus's furious glare softened in surprise.

Odin laughed. "That's right, you glorified phone charger, Ragnarok is averted. Me and mine are free to interact with the world as if we'll actually be here long enough to matter. I've seen a lot of ways things can end between us. None of them are good for you personally. You're too much of a prick to let yourself live through this, but the people you lead are a different story."

Almost all fighting had halted. The devils in the city armed themselves with the weapons I provided and regrouped. The amazons pulled back, warily watching the confrontation between Odin and Zeus. Ajuka and Falbium regrouped. Falbium let his shields fall, subtly trying to catch his breath as Dememter ceased her assault, hanging on Odin's words. Hermes flitted through the air around Zeus, glaring at Odin and I.

Odin held up a finger. "To being, I will speak of the future where your people have the ability to forge their own path, the future you are going to fuck up for them, sees Olympus standing after your fall. Another will rise to the throne. It just won't be you."

"That will never happen," Zeus spat. "I will not fall."

"See? That's why I said you'd fuck it up. I don't need to see the future to predict you, you dim-witted dolt. Even with my vast understanding of the cosmos, I cannot for the life of me understand how you possibly won your war with the Titans. Hades and Poseidon had to have done all the important work. All you're good for is smashing things."

Zeus's fist clenched. A clap of thunder shook the sky. He held out his hand and caught the falling lightning bolt, it swelled in his hand as he added his power to it. "I am going to kill you, Odin. Asgard will be without its ruler. Then, Ragnarok or no, it shall fall."

Odin's grin pulled into a serious line. "And that brings me to what will actually happen. You being you, you'll make it so this path is all but certain. Olympus will fall, destroyed by an unending tide the few who remain cannot resist. Its once proud gods will be forced to seek refuge amongst other powers. Some will be welcomed into other homes, living far more fulfilling lives than they led beneath you. Others will suffer fates far worse than death. They will have you to thank for that, Zeus."

"I tire of your prattling. It is time we finish this."

Odin shook his head. "No. not yet. Your time will come, but it will not come here."

A Hole opened behind Odin. The runes beneath Odin's feet spun into a large platform to accommodate a large procession. The armored form of Frigg led the way, stepping up to her husband's side. Tyr's towering form crouched through the Hole, standing tall, armored and carrying a sword and shield. Freyja was next, armored similarly to her valkyries. Last came Víðarr, massive boot clicking against the rune platform Odin created. Unlike the others, he wore little armor, just a belt and furs. An axe hung from the belt at his side.

"By all means, Zeus," Odin said, good humor gone as he stared up at Zeus. "Strike. For all that you lack in intelligence, you do make up for it in strength. Strike, King of Olympus. I wonder if you can defeat all of us."

Zeus stared down at Odin, unflinching. He raised the bolt in his hand.

A hand came to rest on Zeus's arm, pulling it back down.

Zeus's head whipped around to glare at Hera. Hera shook her head.

Zeus shook with fury. With a roar, he hurled his lightning bolt towards a point in the city below where the devils were regrouping. Falbium summoned a shield to absorb it. He needn't have bothered.

Zeus's lightning bolt vanished as it was swallowed by a Hole. Zeus was seething as he glared at me.

"I will kill you, boy." Zeus turned his ire to Odin. "And I will burn away everything your people ever built. I will destroy even the memory of Asgard. Hecate!"

The air above Zeus shimmered. I tried to hide my shock as a woman appeared. I felt no trace of her presence. She was a ghost until this moment.

She wore dark robes and carried a dark torch. I recognized her. It was the witch that opened my lands' wards for the angels' assault before fleeing. The Greeks must have coordinated with the angels to try to attack multiple targets while I was occupied with an assault on my lands so I wouldn't be able to bring support to the battlefields. It might even have worked if the angels had known to expect Dimension Lost and Annihilation Maker. I needed to have a talk with Medea about somehow preventing the Greek Goddess of Magic from tampering with our wards in the future.

A green flame flared to life atop Hecate's torch. The flame spilled into the air. Demeter and Hermes floated down to be near her as the flames fell like a waterfall towards the ground. The amazons and monsters rushed across the ground towards the flame.

I moved to open Holes to prevent the ground forces from escaping when Odin grabbed my hand, shaking his head.

"Not today, Balthazar. Let them go. Most will fall with Olympus. Some will survive to lead better lives. They deserve that chance." Odin said.

After a moment's hesitation, I lowered my hand, watching the Greek forces as they sprinted into the curtain of flame falling away from Hecate like a curtain. Each creature that stepped through the fire vanished from the battlefield.

Even moving at supernatural speeds, it took almost a full five minutes for the Greeks to travel across the city and flee through Hecate's spell. Soon, all that was left was the Greek gods themselves.

"I look forward to mounting your head on my throne, Odin." Zeus said, stepping into the fire. The others followed him.

Hecate was the last. She pulled back her hood. Raven hair fell free to dance in the wind. Glowing violet eyes met mine, beseeching. I felt a presence brushing against my mind like fingers brushing against the surface of a pond.

'We–'

'Balthazar is mine!' Medea screamed into my head. The foreign voice was violently ejected from my head as I felt Medea's presence rush to the forefront of my mind, shoving out everything else.

Hecate visibly recoiled in the air as if she'd been slapped across the face, eyes flying wide. She huffed, frustrated. She met my gaze once more, eyes softening. "Please," she said softly, voice barely reaching my ears. The curtain of flame rose around her, pulling her away.

What in creation was that? Did Hecate just try to take over my mind?

Odin scoffed. "Prick always needs to get the last word. The world will be better for being rid of him. I think it's time we head back to Lucifaad, my boy. I expect my sons are doing well, but it is wise to support them all the same."

I shook my head. Sorting out whatever Hecate had tried could wait for later. Lucifaad was still under attack. "Right."

I opened a Hole near us and another next to Ajuka and Falbium. Odin's assembled gods filed through the Hole. I was the last one through.

I expected to emerge back onto a raging battlefield. I didn't expect to be met with cheering. Devils flew all around, roaring in victory, weapons raised high in celebration.

It took me a moment to find Serafall floating up in the air at Sirzechs' side. Both watched the celebration impassively. I stepped through a Hole to join them.

"What happened?" I asked.

"We won," Sirzechs said, though he didn't sound happy about that. "A wave of green fire swept over the city. It was some sort of teleportation spell. The Greeks fled through it. Aphrodite escaped before we could stop her."

"What happened in Lilith?" Serafall asked.

I frowned. "The damage was bad. Once Odin showed up, Zeus left rather than fight him."

"Zeus was there personally?" Serafall asked. "Fuck! I should have had you take us there first."

Sirzechs shook his head. "You didn't know."

We lapsed into silence as we stared down at the city. Many devils celebrated their victory. A large number also lay dead on the streets below. Olympus hit our capital and did significant damage. They hit Lilith and reduced the majority of the city to rubble. This didn't feel much like winning.

Ajuka and Falbium joined us in the sky, silently drifting up to stare down at the city with us. Four Satans and a random devil lord who could walk between worlds looked down at what our enemy had done to our home.

"I heard Heaven has joined the fight against us." Ajuka said quietly.

"I'll deal with it." I said before anyone else could speak, glaring at nothing.

Serafall's eyes narrowed. "What do you mean?"

I met her gaze. "I'm really tired of people fucking with me. You're already gearing up to hit Olympus. Let me worry about Heaven."

"Balthazar," Sirzechs said slowly. "Heaven has many capable defenders. Michael, Uriel, Metatron – you can't fight them alone."

"Who said anything about me fighting them?" I asked. "No, I'm wiping them off the map and salting the ashes. This is the last time anyone will think about fucking with us."

"Bal," Serafall said softly, laying a hand on my shoulder. "At least tell me your plan. I'm just as pissed at them as you are. Let me help."

I didn't see any issue with that. I quickly laid out the beginnings of my battle plan. It wasn't very complicated. I had Hole. I had Dimension Lost. I had Annihilation Maker. The plan practically made itself.

Serafall grinned, an evil joy sparkling in her eyes.
