#9,910
Despite the turmoil of nerves and anxiety spinning about his chest, Azazel kept a relaxed grin on his face as he was escorted to Serafall Leviathan's office by none other than Gondul, formerly Leader of the Valkyrior, herself.

"So, they've got you coming out of retirement, huh?" Azazel asked in good humor.

Gondul didn't seem amused. "That is what happens when a pantheon goes to war, Azazel."

"Seen much action yet?"

Gondul grunted. Azazel got the message and shut up. There were limits, and he was pushing them.

"Try anything and you're not getting out of here." Gondul said, as if she was just stating a fact. She opened the door to Serafall's office and motioned Azazel inside.

"Much obliged," Azazel said with a mock salute.

He took in the room as he entered. It wasn't the first time he'd been to Serafall's office, but it was the first time in a while. The last issue they'd had to resolve was something about a devil reincarnating a Fallen. Or was it a half-fallen? He couldn't remember. He had a lot on his mind right now.

The decorations on the walls were still the same – paintings and small shelves with supernatural nick-nacks – but the feel of the air was different. Serafall sat behind her desk, poring over pages of reports. She was wearing dark armor Azazel had only seen her wear one other time. He was wearing armor too that last time.

He'd heard about the attacks in Lucifaad and Lilith of course, it was why he was here, but he would have expected Serafall to change into something more comfortable for this meeting.

"It's good to see you, Serafall, and can I say, you're looking positively–"

"Say what you're here to say or leave." Serafall cut him off, still not looking at him. "I don't have time to play your games right now, Azazel."

Azazel's grin slipped off his face. "You want to be serious? Fine."

He grabbed one of the chairs opposite Serafall's desk and loudly dragged it right up to the edge of Serafall's desk. He accomplished his goal, getting her to finally look up at him from her papers. He could have done with less hostility in her gaze though.

"I heard about the attacks. All of the attacks. I know my idiot siblings tried to hit Balthazar again." Azazel explained.

The temperature in the office dropped. Serafall's eyes adopted a dangerous, icy glow. "I expect Heaven is trying to keep their embarrassment quiet. It hasn't even been an hour. What agents do you have in my office?"

"Believe it or not, I didn't hear this from one of my spies. It would have been simpler if I did. Instead…" Azazel sighed, rubbing his forehead. Best to just come out with it. "Remiel Fell."

Serafall's eyes narrowed. "Explain."

"I don't know if it was pride or wrath or some other sin, but he's not pure anymore. The Silver City will never welcome him back."

"So you took him in." Serafall said dangerously.

Azazel held up his hands. "Woah! I'm not stupid. I knew taking him in would be as good as declaring war. The Grigori was made by the Fallen, but we represent far more than just the Fallen now. I'd be putting all of that at risk for one idiot that can't seem to accept when he's beaten or when he's being a colossal dumbass. He came to me and asked for help with some hairbrained scheme to kill Balthazar Abaddon, but I turned him away. Even if I was willing to risk the Grigori to shelter him, he's too unhinged to be a reliable asset. He is obsessed with Balthazar." Azazel sighed. "That obsession is going to kill Heaven."

"What do you mean?"

"Don't play dumb, Serafall. You're going to retaliate for that attack. With Asgard backing you up, I don't see it going well for Heaven. I… I came to hopefully offer an alternative."

"An alternative to what?"

"War. Let me work as a go-between. I don't want my siblings to kill you any more than I want you to kill them. I can work with you to–"

"That's unnecessary. The problem is sorted. You can go now." Serafall cut him off, returning her attention to her reports.

Azazel's eyes narrowed. She was being awfully dismissive. Normally, Serafall would jump at the opportunity to resolve things peacefully. She'd been working for years to create a more stable political climate in the supernatural. Had the war soured her outlook?

"Look Serafall, I know that–"

"You can go." Serafall repeated, more firmly.

The door to the office opened. Gondul appeared in the doorway. "I will see you out, Governor."

Azazel didn't move. His mind worked over the problem. Serafall no longer seemed interested in a peaceful resolution. That meant she would likely seek a militaristic resolution. But she had no way of knowing how a battle with Heaven would go. Heaven's angels were made of an element that was the fundamental antithesis of devils. The devils outnumbered the angels, but the angels still had plenty of cards in their deck to even the odds. Sure, the presence of Asgard threw a wrench in things, but it still wasn't a sure thing, especially with Olympus involved. If Serafall was this confident, she would need an equalizer, something that she was certain would make Heaven's advantages obsolete.

Azazel's eyes widened, remembering the rambling warnings of his insane brother before he kicked Remiel out of his office and forbade him from coming back.

"Annihilation Maker," Azazel breathed. "You're going to use Dimension Lost and Annihilation Maker."

Serafall's eyes snapped back up to look at Azazel. "I have no idea what you're talking about, Azazel. For the good of our continued relationship, I suggest you leave and keep your nose out of this fight."

Azazel's palms were sweaty. He ignored Gondul as she walked up to his side, looming threateningly. He only had eyes for Serafall.

He'd figured it out. He knew Serafall's plan. It was brilliant. It was terrifying. This… The world was going to change overnight. The world would watch as the impossible happened, and everyone would fear the same happening to them.

There was nothing Azazel could do. No, there was something. It was a vain hope, hollow, but he would try all the same. He owed his siblings, pious pricks though they were.

"Give me one week," Azazel said. "Give me one week to try to convert my siblings. I will make as many of them Fall as I can. I'll take them into the Grigori and you won't need to worry about fighting them. They're already devastated after the failed attack against Balthazar. I can convert them. I know you, Serafall. Even after all this, you don't want a complete genocide. Let me save as many of them as I can. In exchange, the Grigori will formally ally with you against Olympus. Baraqiel, Shemhazai and I will draft up a formal alliance. There's a lot we can offer each other."

Serafall was silent for a moment as she regarded him. "Years ago, I would have leapt at the opportunity to formally ally with you, Azazel. Now? I don't really need to. I have other much more impactful allies that I won't have to worry about stabbing me in the back at an inconvenient time. Why should I entertain this?"

"I've been researching Sacred Gears for millenia. I can–"

"And I have Medea." Serafall said, sounding bored. "The angels attacked because of what she can do. Don't pretend not to know her presence makes the value of that offer very low. Try again."

Azazel took a breath. "I've wanted to work with Ajuka for years. I'm sure he's wanted the same. Neither of us could say anything because we were enemies, but if we work together, that will change. Think of what we could do together. I've made an original, functioning Sacred Gear that mimics the power of the stronger dragon-type Sacred Gears. I've been studying Ajuka's Evil Pieces for a long time and I think I know how to improve them. Can you imagine a world where every Evil Piece was a Mutation Piece?"

Serafall frowned. "That would be dangerous."

"Then we find a way to trigger it when we want and only when we want. I can help Ajuka figure out a way to control when Mutation Pieces occur. You know how valuable I am, Serafall. You know how great an ally the Grigori would be."

"If I can trust you." she countered.

Azazel's gaze hardened. "I will personally deal with anyone that threatens this alliance."

Serafall was silent.

Gondul watched her closely, ready to remove Azazel if directed.

"Fine," Serafall finally said. "But here's my non-negotiable counter offer: You have twelve hours to convert as many angels as you can. Then it starts."

Azazel felt his mouth go dry. "Twelve hours? You can't be serious. I need to–"

"You said it yourself, the angels are panicked and fractured after their humiliating failure. We will take advantage of that. I will not put the outcome of this war at risk because a third party wanted more time. Whether you use your window or not is on you. Twelve hours. Take it or leave it."

"Done," Azazel said quickly. He wanted to save as many of his siblings as he could. He needed more time to save them, but he couldn't put the Grigori in danger. Serafall had given him the opportunity to secure the Grigori's future against all enemies for the low price of cooperating with her as he'd always wanted to do. Azazel would need to clear house to get rid of the few outspoken voices that had been against this kind of alliance for some time, but one or two voices silenced was worth the security of everyone he commanded as Governor of the Fallen. These were times that would be looked back on for the rest of history. Azazel needed to secure his people's future, so he would.

"I'll send Shemhazai and Baraqiel to go over details." Azazel said, distracted. "I need to go to Heaven now."

Serafall waved him away, attention returning to her reports. "Go. Please don't stab me in the back, Azazel. I've always liked you even though you're irritating. I don't want to have to kill you."

With those morose words, Azazel sped from the office. He left the Underworld as fast as possible. He made a quick call to Shemhazai then took flight on his wings. For the first time in millenia, he was returning home.

Hopefully, he'd be able to make his siblings listen. Even one of them Falling into his protection would be a victory.

There was nothing he could do for the rest.


X


Katarea Leviathan was born to rule Hell. It was her destiny, her birthright. For years, she had plotted and planned, working with the other true heirs to the thrones of Hell. Together, they would rise from their forced exile to become who they were meant to be.

That was how it was supposed to be. That was how it should have been. Now, that was nothing but a fractured dream, a languid hope unattainable.

Katarea had done her part. When she observed the mass of refugees flooding onto Balthazar Abaddon's lands, she'd seen her opportunity. She joined them. They would be her path to an audience with the Lord of the Abaddon Clan. She would converse with him, win him to their side. If he refused to comply, she would remove him.

Her plan hinged on her allies completing their own tasks. Throughout the years spent working with them, Katarea had come to find her allies…lacking in certain respects. They were lazy, prideful. They spoke a lot but acted rarely. Katarea allowed this. The privilege of their blood afforded them some concessions. Katarea could not forgive their most recent, most devastating failure. Were the other heirs of the true Satans not already dead, she would kill them herself to rid her organization of their weakness. Now, she had no organization. She was alone.

Shalba and Creuserey marshalled their armies outside Lilith as planned. When the Greeks struck, they should have been prepared. It was their opportunity to be seen by the denizens of Hell as the saviors the New Satans could not be. Instead, the peasants witnessed Demeter freeze Shalba solid and shattered his body. They watched as Zeus casually flicked a lightning bolt that obliterated Creuserey as if he was little more than an ant. The army they'd amassed to defend and occupy Lilith in their victory was routed, torn apart by amazons and wayward power hurled by Demeter and Zeus.

In an instant, everything Katarea had built crumbled into nothing. Was this to be the end?

No. No, it was not the end. She endured. Her allies had proven wanting, but she was still destined to rule Hell. Shalba and Creuserey led her followers to their deaths, but she would gather new followers. She would make stronger allies. She would start with Balthazar Abaddon.

Already, word of his exploits on the battlefield were spreading like wildfire. Battle had joined less than a day ago, yet the Underworld roared his name and sung his praises. Katarea would use that to her advantage. She would approach Balthazar and slowly mold him into the ally she needed. She could not show her true face for fear of prejudice, so she disguised herself with minor charms. When she was freed from Dimension Lost's mists to join the other refugees, she introduced herself as Evelyn. It was perfect.

At least it should have been. She didn't expect the creature she was speaking to would be intelligent enough to sense something was different about her. She didn't expect Medea Abaddon herself would appear in front of her and dispel her illusion. She didn't expect Dimension Lost would swallow her before she could explain herself to Balthazar's wife.

Katarea held her head high, refusing to show weakness even as she sat trapped in a cell. Moments after discovering her true identity, Medea used Dimension Lost to send Katarea to Serafall. The pretender locked Katarea away, claiming she was a problem to be dealt with later. The insult. Katarea rightly belonged in Serafall's position, yet the bitch thought to treat her as nothing more than an inconvenience? The insolence.

Katarea's cell creaked open. Katarea stood as Serafall entered the small space.

"Serafall," Katarea greeted, keeping her expression cordially controlled. "I would like–"

"I don't care," Serafall cut her off. "I'm going to talk and you're going to listen. I don't have time to deal with you properly right now, so today is your lucky day. It would be a bad look for me to kill another devil while we're embroiled in war with another faction. I don't want to kill another devil while we're at war with other factions. Despite all the bullshit you've put me through, I'm offering you an olive branch, Katarea."

Serafall held out her hand. Katarea held back a snarl as an Evil Piece appeared in Serafall's hand, a Bishop.

"This is your one chance," Serafall said, eyes dangerous. "I don't want to kill you, but I'm not stupid enough to leave you to your own devices. You'll try to take advantage of this chaos to create even more chaos. Accept a place in my peerage. Join my family and put all of this behind us."

"You dare," Katarea hissed, unable to contain her fury. "You dare suggest I, the true heir to the Leviathan, serve you?" Katarea spit on Serafall's hand.

Serafall's expression hardened as her Bishop disappeared.

Katarea's shoulders rose and fell rapidly with her enraged breathing. "I will never submit to you, pretender! When I am free, I will–" Katarea gagged, clutching at her throat.

Serafall stared Katarea down, expression cold as ice. "I didn't want this. My offer was genuine. We could have grown past this together. We could have built a better future for our people together. Instead, you chose this. Goodbye, Katarea." Serafall spun on her heel, swiftly exiting the cell. She didn't close the door behind her. There was no need.

Katarea collapsed to the ground, desperately grasping at the icicle buried in her throat.

No… No! This couldn't be how it ended. She was the Leviathan! She would…

Katarea Leviathan's muscles went limp. She stared deadly out the door of her cell, crimson pooling beneath her.


X


Remiel tore through the sky, desperately flapping his wings to carry him higher and higher. Tears flowed like rivers down his face. He told himself it was from the air biting his skin, stabbing his eyes. He kept his gaze fixed straight ahead, refusing to look back. All the same, he caught a glimpse of darkness every time he beat his wings.

No! He could still fix this. There had to be a way. He could look to the future and…

He couldn't See. His Sight was gone.

Dark feathers fluttered at the edge of his vision as he flapped his wings.

Remiel squeezed his eyes shut.

No! Michael could help. Uriel could help. There had to be something he could do. Azazel refused to aid him, but if he could just kill that blasted devil, he would be welcome in his Father's home once more. He needed to–

Heaven was separate from reality, but angels still needed to fly to get there. As they flew, they travelled elsewhere to get to Heaven. They never encountered anyone other than other angels. So Remiel was caught completely by surprise when, eyes still squeezed shut to avoid seeing his wings, he collided with another body in mid-air.

Remiel's eyes snapped open. He summoned a Light spear, preparing to defend himself.

"Put it down, idiot!"

Remiel's Light spear disappeared. His jaw hung open as he came face to face with Azazel.

Azazel was glaring at him, helping another angel steady herself after Remiel had knocked into her.

Zarall. Remiel recognised her. She was one of the ones to join his assault. Why…why were her wings black?

Remiel looked around. Filling the sky, angels flew all around Azazel, watching Remiel with furious expressions. Each of them sported a pair of dark wings sprouting from their backs. Most of them had joined him in the attack on Balthazar Abaddon. There were others who hadn't, glaring just as hatefully at him as those who had fought with him.

"What is happening?" Remiel asked. If only he still had his Sight, he could See what this was.

"You happened, you bastard!" Zarall screamed, flying towards him as if to charge.

Azazel placed himself between them, holding Zarall back.

"No," Azazel said. "Leave him. He isn't worth it."

"We lost everything because of him!" Zarall cried.

"Not everything," Azazel said, hugging her close to him. "Not yet. Don't let him take your life too."

"Azazel, what is–" Remiel was cut off.

"Leave, Remiel," Azazel said dangerously. He cradled the sobbing form of Zarall, eyes fixed on Remiel. "You're no more welcome in Heaven than you are in the Grigori."

"Why…why have you Fallen?" Remiel couldn't breathe. He needed to understand. What was happening?

"This is the only way we live through this, brother," another angel said, descending down to hover at Azazel's side. Remiel recognized him. Ansiel, a powerful Cherubim, now Fallen, who served as a guardian of Heaven's Gates. "This is the only way we preserve even a memory of Heaven."

"No," Remiel denied, shaking his head. "This is not the end. So long as we have faith, we will–"

"Faith in what?" another angel cried. Onoel. Remiel hadn't interacted with her much. From what he knew, she granted minor miracles to devout followers of the Lord. "Father is dead!" she screeched.

Remiel staggerd in the air as if he'd been punched. "How…?" They shouldn't know that. Only a select few angels were privvy to the truth. Michael thought it was best to preserve the faith of their brothers and sisters by continuing on as if their Father was still with them. He was in a way. The Lord never truly left you.

"I told them," Azazel said simply. "The Sacred Gear system glitched out a while back and has been deteriorating since. That was the first clue. It wasn't the only one. Michael hasn't done as good a job covering things up as you all would have liked."

"Azazel, why…?" Remiel could barely think. He didn't know what was happening. He needed to understand.

"Because I care about my siblings. Despite everything, I wanted to save as many as I could." Azazel said sadly, accepting.

Remiel shook his head. "No, this is not the end. If you are with us, Azazel, we can–"

"Shut up!" another angel screamed. Mihael who watched over true believers in South America. "You've brought us to ruin, yet still you insist we should continue into the inferno. How has Heaven's Guiding Light failed so far!"

Remiel swallowed a lump in his throat. "My Sight is not what it was when Father was alive, but with Michael and Uriel's help, we can restore it and–"

"You knew!" another angel. Theliel. "You knew you couldn't see the full picture but you led us to our end anyway!"

"I…"

"You've doomed us!" Karael, shepard of Saints.

"The Fall of Heaven is on your hands!" Akriel of the Virtues.

"Leave, Remiel! Heaven would have been better off without you!" Sofiel, Principality of Venice.

"You didn't even have the dignity to die with Raphael!" Dominion Omniel.

Remiel covered his ears, tucking his wings and diving back towards the ground. He couldn't listen anymore. He could not stand to hear one more accusatory cry from his siblings.

They didn't understand. He did what he had to. It wasn't his fault. It was the blasted Abaddon.

Remiel's features twisted in fury. He screamed as he dove towards the ground.

He would make it right.


X


Athena sighed. Thunder roared in the chamber behind her. Athena had given up trying to speak to her father. Hera still tried to soothe his rage, but Zeus was not having it. The whole of Olympus trembled with his fury.

"I take it things didn't go well?"

Athena looked up. Poseidon leaned against a nearby pillar, pushing off of it to walk towards Athena.

"Ares is dead, killed by Sirzechs Lucifer. Ajuka Beelzebub killed Glaucus and Proteus before Father arrived on the battlefield. The cities were damaged, but not razed. The morale of our armies is in disarray after yet another disastrous retreat. The valkyries and devils slaughtered most of the amazons, leaving us with few organized, well-trained troops."

"So it is exactly as you predicted." Poseidon said.

Athena sighed tiredly. "Yes, it is exactly as I predicted."

"How long do you think we have?"

Mount Olympus shook as a thunderbolt split the sky. The mountain trembled as if in fear of Zeus's rage.

"A day. Two at most." Athena said.

"How many will blindly follow my idiot brother to their deaths?"

"Not all. Still too many."

"Then we do what we can with those willing to listen to us. Are you ready?"

Athena shook her head. "I still do not know if this will work."

Despite the seriousness of their predicament, Poseidon smiled, amused. "Why do you think we haven't heard from Artemis? We are bound to follow Zeus's commands to the letter, not the spirit."

Athena swallowed nervously. "Very well."

Together, Athena and Poseidon marched into Zeus's throne room.

The entire room shook. Blue energy danced along the walls. Zeus howled in rage. Hera stood at his side, desperately trying to reign in his fury.

"Brother!" Poseidon boldly called.

Zeus's murderous eyes snapped to Poseidon. Energy crackled around his body. "What!" the King of Olympus snapped.

"I have a plan to repay the devils and the foolish Asgardians for their affront."

The sky rumbled, but the sound lowered in intensity. Poseidon had Zeus's full focus. "What is this plan?"

"With your leave, I will take a number of gods from Olympus. We will strike where the Asgardians least expect it. Tell me brother, what is the true source of their power?"

"I have no patience for your games, Poseidon. Explain your plan."

"Odin claims to have averted Ragnarok. I believe, with the right team, I can ensure the end of Asgard is resumed. Not only resumed, but hastened."

Zeus's eyes narrowed. "How?"

Poseidon didn't shrink under Zeus's gaze. "Leave that to me and Athena. We will need some others to bring this to fruition. Hecate, Apoll–"

"Take whoever you need. Just eradicate those fools!"

Poseidon bowed. "By your leave, brother."

Athena bowed at his side. Together, they left the hall. Lightning snapped furiously overhead as they departed.

"That was much easier than I assumed it would be." Athena said. She stopped walking as the full weight of what she was about to do settled over her. She looked around the cloudy paradise of Olympus. The beautiful statues. The trees grown from myth. The golden ambrosia that flowed like water.

She would likely never see it again.

"Never underestimate my brother's ability to hold a grudge. Also, never underestimate his ability to make a foolish decision." Poseidon said. "Gather those you've spoken to. I will do the same. Meet me at Olympus's gate in one hour. I will take us to my palace beneath the ocean where we will plan our next move." Poseidon scattered into a spray of sea water that splashed against the rocks.

Athena walked as if in a dream, slowly taking in all she could, desperately trying to commit the paradise of her home to memory.

At the end of this, Olympus would never be the same if it remained at all. Athena wouldn't know what would become of it for some time. She had tried all she could to save her it, but Zeus was too insistent on leading them all to their doom. There was little Athena could do to go against him, bound as she was to follow him. All she could do was save as much of this glorious dream as she could.


X


Medea stood in the center of a dimming ritual circle, a triumphant smile on her face. Finally, it was done.

In her hand, Sephiroth Graal glowed with supreme power. The inert remnants of the once all-powerful True Longinus lay on the ground at her feet. The spear, once shrouded in a Holy corona, now looked rusted with a copper film. The corrosion was slowly spreading over the spear. In an hour, it would crumble away.

Medea would not let that happen.

Medea would have time to test the power Sephiroth Graal, now enhanced by True Longinus's power, later. She still had work to do.

Medea bent down and picked up the rusted spear. Copper shavings flaked off the spear where her fingers touched it.

"Shang Tsung," Medea called, holding a hand behind her distractedly. She did not look away from the spear.

Medea felt an explosion of magical power as Shang Tsung raised his hand. A perfect crystal sphere floated through the air into Medea's waiting hand. Within the sphere, rageful fire and malicious shadow swirled, batting ineffectually against the enchanted sphere confining them.

What felt like a lifetime ago, Medea accompanied Balthazar on many of his excursions to search for potential locations to open a mine. Medea enjoyed the opportunity to spend time with her future husband. Unfortunately, her time was quickly monopolized by other matters, leaving Aqua to accompany Balthazar in her stead.

During one of these excursions, Balthazar had taken her to a world he spoke of often. It was the world where he failed to recruit Talion as his Knight. While they did have active mines in that world, they were few and far between. Balthazar was cautious of drawing the ire of certain powers. He lamented that he was unwilling to do more in the world for it had many hidden treasures.

When Medea asked her King about these hidden treasures, he gave her little more than a sentence about each. A mountain of gold guarded by a slumbering dragon. A potent volcano playing home to the greatest evil in the land. A wonderous creation of the elves hidden by secrets.

Balthazar had laughed. Medea had focused on his words after that, filing them away in her memory.

'There's even a great mine we could take over if we really wanted to. The veins are already mapped out and there's probably some lingering equipment down there so it would be perfect. 'Would' being the key word. I don't want to mess with Durin's Bane, so that'll never happen.'

Medea wasn't sure why that story stuck out to her as the most important of those Balthazar entertained her with during their excursion. That should have been the end of it.

Until now.

Frustrated with her inability to find anything that would suit her needs in Avernus, Medea almost gave up on her search. It was then that her memory supplied her with Balthazar's words, spoken to her from a time before he took her as his wife. Shang Tsung transported their group to that world. Medea used her scryings and familiars. It only took her an hour to locate the mine Balthazar spoke of. It only took an hour to find the monster that her husband believed was better left alone.

After a minor delay to secure her home from the upstart angels seeking its ruin, Medea returned to that world with the rest of Balthazar's peerage, leaving only Shiroe behind so he could continue overseeing the logistics of caring for the many new vassals of the Abaddon lands.

Balthazar thought many of the refugees would flee after the attack, fearing for their safety. Medea loved her husband, but he was not the best at predicting people's behavior.

He was wrong, of course. A host of angels descended from the sky upon them. The refugees were not slain or even harmed. Each of them was safely sheltered in Dimension Lost for the duration of the battle before being released when the angel threat was dealt with. In one afternoon, Balthazar had assured their loyalty. They were chanting his name. They sung his praises and begged for the opportunity to repay Balthazar for what he was doing for them, for saving them from Heaven, for sheltering them, for feeding them.

Medea would see about ensuring they were given tasks that would help Clan Abaddon later. She had other matters to see to first.

With nearly the full might of Balthazar's peerage at her back – supported by Perseus, Skarlet and Patroclus – the great monster called Durin's Bane stood no chance.

Titanic in size though the creature of flame and shadow was, Coal and Matatabi were larger. Powerful though its magic was, it could not hope to combat the combined might of Medea, Irene, Keno and Aqua. The best was strong, striking fast with its flaming sword. It was too slow to land a single hit on Perseus, Achilles or Patroclus.

The monster fell. As it did, Shang Tsung stepped forward, having been standing by precisely so he would be ready for this moment.

Shang Tsung snatched the corrupted lifeforce of the creature, what could be approximated as its twisted soul, and sealed it before it could dissipate.

The moment this act was complete, Medea felt a tremor in the air, a rumble in the ground. It was as if the environment was responding negatively to what Shang Tsung had just done.

Medea decided it would be unwise to wait and see exactly what was happening. The peerage retreated to Hell. Medea had Aqua retrieve the majority of the skeletons and animated armors staffing their mines. When she returned, Aqua locked the world away for extra protection. By locking the world away, they had lost access to the mines in that world, but Medea did not care. They had an overabundance of resources to draw from. If they ever ran low on anything, they could simply find another world to create a foothold in. Medea did not like the way the world was seemingly responding to their actions against the creature. It was better to be cautious and leave than overconfident and risk injury or worse.

Medea held the crystal orb containing the soulstuff of Durin's Bane in her hand. Her eyes glowed as she chanted. The ritual circle beneath her flared to life once more, its blue color overtaken by a searing orange flame.

Medea completed her chant with a shout, stabbing the point of True Longinus into the soulsphere. The sphere shattered. An unholy wail filled the air as the flaming shadow of Durin's Bane was sucked into the spear.

The rust on True Longinus burned away. Veins of living orange fire burned into the shaft of the spear. The spear's blade was scorched black like a solid shadow.

"Achilles, Aqua," Medea said, voice clipped.

Achilles stepped into the center of the ritual circle. Aqua stepped up to the circle's edge, her Keyblade in her hand.

Achilles lifted the spear out of Medea's hands. Aqua stabbed forward with her Keyblade. There was a locking sound as a beam of golden energy shot from Aqua's Keyblade, forming a connection between Achilles and the spear and locking it in place.

Once more, the ritual circle beneath Medea's feet dimmed as it went inert.

Achilles couldn't look away from the flaming spear in his hands. Misty shadows drifted off of the weapon to dissipate into the air.

"What can it do?" Achilles asked. True Longinus, empowered by the Lord of Heaven's power, was capable of slaying gods. Medea drained that power away to empower Sephiroth Graal, replacing it with something else, something otherworldly.

"We will test its limits and…" Medea trailed off, a suspicious frown on her face as ice pooled on the ground in the corner of the room.

Medea turned as the ice grew from the floor into a bipedal shape. Feminine curves formed as more ice grew from its body. Blue mist spilled off her form to dissipate into the air.

Aqua and Shang Tsung watched her carefully. Achilles spun his new spear into a low stance, ready for whatever may happen.

"Lady Abaddon," the ice woman said, her voice a whisper barely strong enough to break through the air.

Medea turned to fully face the woman, holding her arms out at her slides, feeling the the walls of her home thrum in answer. "What is this? Who are you?"

The woman looked confused at Medea's reaction, as if Medea responding to an intruder with hostility wer something surprising.

"I am… No, no longer. I was the castle, Lady Abaddon. You have nothing to fear from me." This time, the voice, still so quiet a passing breeze might scamper it, emerged from everywhere. The walls and floor. The chandelier. The ceiling. All spoke in unison with the moving of the icy woman's lips.

Medea's eyes widened in shock. Analysis spells flashed around her as she sought to verify the woman's claim. In an instant, Medea learned everything there was to know about the woman of ice before her. Medea sucked in a surprised breath of air at what she found.

This…things never worked in her favor unless it was specifically by her design. Surely this wasn't…?

Slowly, Medea took careful steps towards the woman. Aqua and Achilles stepped to Medea's sides to flank her. Shang Tsung watched from behind, gaze intently focused on the ice woman.

The woman of ice did not move. Eyes of solid, chilled blue like glass watched Medea as she approached. Medea laid a hand on the icy woman's face. It was cold to the touch, yet impossibly warm. A flurry of emotions rose in Medea's chest. She couldn't speak. How had this happened?

Medea's eyes widened as she realized what had caused this. A mistake of magic. A glitch in the world. This presence before her should not be, yet here she was.

Throughout her life, there were many magical workings Medea created that had unintended side-effects. Some were a minor inconvenience. Some were detrimental to her plans. Some were outright dangerous to herself or others she cared for. This appeared to be one of the frightfully rare pleasant mishaps she had encountered as a result of her magics.

Medea knew what happened. She wasn't sure exactly why the series of events leading to the genesis of this woman had functioned, but she could piece together what the ingredients were.

When Medea found herself holding yet another Longinus-Class Sacred Gear, she wasn't sure what to do with it. Initially, she offered to bind Zenith Tempest to Shiroe. While he had made great strides in his magic, he was still the weakest member of Balthazar's peerage.

Shiroe did not want the Sacred Gear. He seemed hesitant, shameful as he told Medea he would rather avoid fighting if he could. He was content to handle the administrative matters of Clan Abaddon. Working with Latia on the refugee crisis had made him interested in perhaps taking a primary role in Bael, Abaddon and Astaroth Trading Co. in the future when the war was well behind them.

Medea saw no issue with Shiroe's request. Soon, there would be no reason to call upon him to fight outside of Rating Games, which he assured Medea he would have no issue participating in. He seemed to want to avoid life-or-death combat, but he did enjoy sparring with Aqua, Keno and Coal.

That left Medea with another Longinus to find a home for. She could not take it for herself. All three chambers in her reliquary were full. She could potentially alter her Sacred Gear to hold a fourth, but that risked weakening the bindings on Sephiroth Graal, Incinerate Anthem and Alphecca Tyrant. Those three Sacred Gears all bound to the reliquary bolstered one-another's strength and stabilized each other. Three was also a powerful number mystically. No, Medea wouldn't take it for herself.

Irene didn't want it. She could summon the weather with her own magic.

Keno didn't want it. She preferred her crystals and could copy any spell she desired, Sacred Gear or no.

Shang Tsung didn't want it, explaining he had already consumed the power of a god with power over storms.

Medea was hesitant to give it to Skarlet because she was so new. Perhaps in time, but not now.

In the end, Medea enlisted Aqua and Irene's help to bind it to the castle with Dimension Lost and Annihilation Maker. If they ever found someone worthy of it, Medea would retrieve it and rebind it to that individual.

That was her thought. She should have expected things would not go according to plan.

When Medea had originally built her castle, her perfect home to spend eternity with her husband, she'd saturated every brick and every beam with her magic. Her power lived and breathed in the walls of the castle. It was a security measure to ensure no one would ever threaten them. When Annihilation Maker and Dimension Lost were added to those protections, the purely magical nature of the castle responded. A minor intelligence was born.

Medea was concerned at first, but the intelligence was supremely loyal to herself and her husband, eager and willing to serve them. Medea monitored the situation, but left well-enough alone. There was too much else for her to focus on with the war well and truly under way. That should have been the end of it.

Then Medea added Zenith Tempest to the already overly-saturated castle. It appeared that addition to the castle's already burgeoning intelligence had consequences.

Three was a powerful number. A Longinus-Class Sacred gear was powerful enough to shake the heavens. Three Longinus-Class Sacred Gears was sufficient to remake the world entire if applied properly.

The castle's intelligence had evolved, creating the icy woman standing before Medea now. The avatar both was and was not the castle. It was born of the castle but not tethered to it. Medea felt it could split itself away. This spirit had developed a mind all its own, free to wander its own path, yet able to return to the castle if it desired.

Medea felt the soul of the creature before her. It was saturated with her magic. It shone with the power of three Longinus Sacred Gears. It was tainted by the immense demonic presence of Balthazar's station as the Lord of Abaddon and a Viscount of Hell.

No longer was the castle's mind merely a far-away presence thrumming through the walls. No, now it was a true, independant entity. The castle was using Zenith Tempest's power to exist in an avatar of pure ice. It could likely do the same with fire, stone, lightning, all the elements accessible through Zenith Tempest's power. Perhaps it could even craft a body using Annihilation Maker?

Three sources of power. Sacred Gears. Medea's magic. Balthazar's demonic power. Another magical anomoly creating the perfect conditions for the entity before her to be born.

Medea's daughter. Her and Balthazar's first child.

There were tears in Medea's eyes as she looked upon the frozen face of the woman before her.

"What is wrong, Lady Abaddon?" the figure asked.

"Mother," Medea said, finally finding her voice.

Frozen eyes blinked. "I do not understand."

"You were born of my magic and Balthazar's demonic power. You are our daughter."

A frozen head tilted in confusion. Several seconds passed.

Aqua and Shang Tsung looked at Medea in open shock. Achilles, seeing there was no danger, had gone back to inspecting his new spear.

The frozen woman righted herself. Her lips curled up almost imperceptibly, but Medea was studying her as if to memorize her every feature. She saw.

"Mother," the woman said. Before, her words were spoken flat with no emotion. Now, there was a trace of joy.

Medea's words caught in her throat as she heard the word. Silent, she wrapped her arms around the frozen woman and pulled her into a crushing hug.

What felt like an eternity ago, Medea answered the call of the grail from the Throne of Heroes seeking a wish. Her wish was not some grand request for immortality, rebirth or the rewriting of history. No, all she desired was a chance to find that which she was denied in life. That which Jason and the gods had torn from her.

She wanted happiness. She wanted a family.

Medea had found happiness. She and Balthazar were going to build a family. She hadn't expected it to happen so soon. She could not be more happy it had.

"Um…" Aqua awkwardly spoke from the side. "It's…good to meet you… Sorry, I didn't catch your name?"

Medea pulled back slightly, just enough to look her daughter in the eyes, but she kept her safe in her arms. Her daughter was frowning.

"I am… I do not know my name. I am no longer Castle Abaddon, though it is what I once was. Perhaps that–"

"Aya," Medea cut her off. She would not allow her daughter's name to be that of the castle she was born from. No. Her name would be Aya. Simple. Beautiful. Free of any burden that might exist with the names of great heroes from the past. It would belong solely to her daughter, hers to do with it whatever she would. Medea would not have her daughter crushed under the weight of legacy. No. She would live as she chose, and Medea would lover her for it.

"Aya," she said, the corners of her lips slightly pulling up happily. "I like it."

"Then you are Aya." Medea said, a single tear running down her face. Words could not express what she was feeling right now. She had known this spirit, her daughter, for barely a minute. Yet already, Medea knew she would kill and die for her.

Aya frowned. Medea felt a dangerous urge to murder whatever made her daughter sad.

"I came here for a reason, mother. Helio– Great-grandfather is here. He approached one of the checkpoints father had me set up at the borders of the land and asked to speak with you."

Medea's happy smile as she studied her daughter's face vanished, replaced by a furious scowl. How dare anyone interrupt this moment, least of all him.

"Has he threatened you? Is he attacking us?" Even as she asked the question, Medea's vision was overtaken by the senses of the familiars she seeded throughout their lands. A raven's eye saw the golden-armored form of the radiantly glowing Titan of the Sun. Helios, her grandfather, stood surrounded by monsters created by Annihilation Maker.

"He says he is not here to fight. I am preparing to destroy him if I have to. What should I do?"

"Prepare to pull everything away with Dimension Lost. I will speak with him."

"Yes, mother,"

Medea fully co-opted her raven familiar. It let out a piercing caw, drawing Helios's eyes to it. The raven landed in front of him, diving into the ground and scattering into a pool of shadow, the shadow condensed, drifting upwards into a vaguely human shape.

"You tried to kill my husband. You are interrupting something precious. You are not welcome here." Medea said through the illusion.

Helios frowned. "You married the devil?"

"Not that it is your business, but yes. Have you come to attempt to destroy my happiness a second time? If so, depart before I destroy you."

Helios frowned. "I…acted too rashly. Circe spoke to me. I did not realize you were reincarnated of your own will. I should have been notified. I did not even know you were alive, Medea."

"My life is mine to live as I please. Why are you here?"

Helios's lips thinned into a line. "I may not be…the easiest to get along with, but I do care. I would revisit our relationship at another time. For now, I need your help."

"Why would I help you after everything you've done? This war began with events you caused when you tried to murder my husband."

Helios frowned. "I know. I will make my peace with you in time. It is not me you must help. Eos is dying."

Medea pursed her lips, silently watching Helios through her illusion. "What do you mean?"

"Zekram Bael struck her with his Power of Destruction. She was stable before. That is no longer the case. She is slowly disintegrating. There is nothing I can do. Selene believes you might be able to help her."

Medea did not respond.

Helios's eyebrows furrowed. "You are displeased with my actions. I understand. It was not Eos who wronged you. Her only crime was to assist me in freeing my daughters, your aunts, from Zekram Bael's slavery. She bears no blame in what I have done to your husband. I will make my amends, but she requires aid now. Without it, she will pass."

Medea was silent for a long time.

"Where is Eos?" she finally said.

"She is safe in my palace." Helios answered promptly.

"I will not go there with you. If you wish her healed, you will bring her here to me." Helios was many things, but he wasn't a liar. He would not claim Eos was dying if she was hale and hearty. Even so, Medea would not risk going to another location with him. If she were to assist her great-aunt, it would be on her terms, in her lands where the power was in her hands.

"I assumed as much. Selene is waiting to transport them. You must lower the wards."

"I will not. Have Selene transport Eos outside the border. I will use Dimension Lost to bring Eos into the castle. You will remain outside."

Helios considered for a moment. "Acceptable. Inform me if you are unable to assist her or if her condition worsens."

"Mother,"

Medea blinked out of her familiar, turning to her side to see Aya, now standing in a body of pure fire, at her side. So she could adopt other forms. Her daughter was so talented.

"Selene is here now. Eos is badly hurt. Her body isn't all there. Should I bring Eos inside?"

"Yes, Aya. I'll see what I can do." Medea looked up pointedly at Aqua, Shang Tsung and Achilles. None of them had left since completing the ritual. They all nodded, understanding Medea's silent command to be prepared for treachery.

An amethyst mist gathered in the center of the ritual circle. As it dispersed, it left a body in its wake.

Medea sucked in a breath. Eos was horribly wounded, worse even than Medea had expected. Both of her legs were gone. She was fully missing one arm at the shoulder and the other arm was deteriorating from the elbow up. The side of her face was scarred and deformed. The Titan had been brought low. Even with Shang Tsung's potions, even with Mothra's healing powers, it likely wouldn't be enough to save her.

Medea pursed her lips. She opened her hand. A small star appeared in her hands, gleaming so bright as to dim all other light. Medea grasped the jewel-encrusted grail in her hands, kneeling down to Eos's side.

Sephiroth Graal was powerful before. Empowered by True Longinus's power, could it heal a Titan consumed by destruction?

Medea laid a hand on Eos's chest. The grail in her hand glowed bright, filling her with power.

Medea gasped as powerful energy coursed through her body, through her hand into Eos.

Aqua and Achilles let out gasps of wonder as Eos's body slowly healed itself. Her scars faded. Her limbs reformed as a wave of pure silver energy passed over the phantom space they used to be.

The whole process took only half-a-minute. Once it was over, Medea put Sephiraoth Graal back into her reliquary, frowning down at Eos's still closed eyes.

Eos sat bolt upright with a gasp.

"Aya! Send her back!" Medea said in shock.

Eos frantically looked around, shuffling backwards awkwardly as mist enveloped her. She was gone.

"Take her and go," Medea said to Helios through her illusion, watching as Helios helped his sister to her feet and hugged her tight. "We will discuss your apology at a later time."

Helios turned to the illusion, opening his mouth.

Medea let the illusion fade. She did not have the energy to deal with her grandfather any more right now. There was too much else on her mind.

Aya perked up, her orange, flaming body flashing blue with heated fire. "Father has returned."

Medea smiled. "Let's go meet him." She was so excited to introduce him to his daughter. She hoped he approved of the name. It was too late to change it now. She'd let him name their next child to make up for choosing Aya's name without his input.

Medea stepped into a shadow, reappearing in the entry hall. Balthazar was conversing with Shiroe, gathering details about the state of the refugees.

Medea charged him and leapt into his arms.

Balthazar was caught by surprise, barely managing to catch her. He stumbled backwards as his arms around around her.

"Welcome home, honey!" Medea said happily.

Balthazar's serious expression melted into a warm smile. Medea loved the way he looked at her.

Balthazar leaned in to steal a kiss as he set her down. "Hello, my love. How is everything here? Have any other problems cropped up?"

Medea took a step back, smiling bright. "The opposite. Something wonderful happened!"

"And what was that?"

Ice grew out of the ground.

Balthazar flinched, falling into a defensive stance as an icy form appeared at Medea's side.

Aya looked different. Paper-thin ice that crumpled against the air like cloth garbed her form. Frills stood at the hem of her sleeves and collar. An icy apron sat atop her dress. She wore a headband, keeping locks of frozen hair at bay.

Medea pursed her lips. "What are you wearing, dear?"

Aya looked away shyly. "Aqua showed me a picture of Grayfia Lucifer wearing something like it. I thought it was cute."

Medea laid a hand on Aya's cheek. "You look lovely."

"I'm sorry," Balthazar said, looking between them in confusion. "Who is this?"

Medea smiled warmly. "I told you that something wonderful happened." Medea took Aya's hand. "Balthazar, this is Aya."

Aya stood frozen, different from before. She was nervous. Medea squeezed her hand comfortingly. There was nothing to fear. She knew Balthazar would be overjoyed.

Balthazar nodded politely. "Hello, Aya."

Aya stuck her chin up, standing tall under Balthazar's eye. "Hello, father. Welcome home."

#10,002
For some time now, I'd been on the backfoot, reactionary. The comfortable days of silence where I could gather power and foster allies in the shadows was well and truly over. Whether I wanted it or not, I was a major player in the supernatural now, my reach and influence spanning far beyond hell. I'd hoped to stay nothing more than a merchant. That changed the moment I became the lynchpin that caused a war.

My clan would soon be seen as its own global power when news of the Longinus Sacred Gears in our possession became common knowledge. And it would become common knowledge. There was no way to put that genie back in the bottle after what just happened with the angels.

Boreas and Helios attacking me that first time in the mortal world set off a very unpleasant chain of events. Every step, I panicked and grasped at anything within reach that might help protect me in the aftermath of whatever event had just impacted me. Honestly, it might have started with Bedeze. If he hadn't tried to steal everything I'd built, I probably would have stayed comfortably hidden in the background for longer. It was only because of the threat he posed that I showed my hand, that I revealed my peerage in the Rating Game.

Now, I'd just returned home from a meeting with the Four Satans, the rulers of Hell themselves. They were coordinating with me. I was to be the spearhead that pierced Heaven. They were going to act as my support, cleaning up the stragglers I didn't destroy.

It didn't feel real. When did I become the harbinger of the destruction of a realm that had been synonymous with the sky, here before the beginning of all things that should have been here after the end of existence? It felt big. I felt small by comparison. It was hard to wrap my head around. A road of violent twists and turns brought me here. If I'd had my way, everyone would have just left me alone to live my life and I wouldn't have done half of what I'd done.

At least, that was what I thought before this exact moment.

My brain had just rebooted. My thoughts were awhirl with details of the attack I'd planned with the Satans. The plan was simple – the best plans were – but there were still some finer details I was hashing out in my mind. Shiroe had just filled me in on the current situation with the refugees. Against all logic, Annihilation Maker's monsters had already managed to construct liveable structures. Now the main task was getting everyone situated and making sure they had simple items for daily use – toiletries, furniture, spare clothes and such.

A single world quieted the storm in my head, silenced all thoughts save one single word.

Father.

I stood slack, staring dumbly at the creature in front of me. A body of pure ice accented by chilled blue fire gathered around its shoulders and hair stood before me. The body was feminine, wearing a maid dress of ice that moved like silk. The icy woman stood tall. Perhaps it was the ice she was made from, but it seemed as if she didn't move at all. She was stock still, watching me intently, waiting.

I opened my mouth. My jaw worked dumbly, but no sound came.

I took a single, careful step forward. Then another.

I wasn't imagining things. The woman grew more tense as I approached, almost leaning away from me as I neared. She was nervous.

Slowly so as not to startle her, I reached up, gently laying my hand against her cheek.

When I offered my peerage a place in Clan Abaddon, naming several of them as my family, Medea and I had discovered the near-imperceptible devilish touch that the devils of Baator could sense in us. As I named each of them Abaddon, they each gained a semblance of that trace, similar to mine, though distinctly different.

Staring into the eyes of the icy woman before me, I felt a power and presence nearly identical to my own. It would be identical were that all I felt. No, it was mixed with Medea's magic. The two powers had joined to create something new.

I didn't know how it happened. I had no idea what process could have possibly given rise to the miracle before me. All I knew was that if anyone threatened the entity before me…

I would burn their entire pantheon.

My arms snapped out. The icy woman flinched at the unexpected speed. She let out a surprised gasp as I pulled her into a crushing hug. Despite her body being composed entirely of ice, the cold didn't burn. It felt impossibly warm, comforting.

"Aya," I nearly choked on the name as I said it, on my daughter's name. "I…" Words failed me. I pulled her even closer.

It was as if a spell had broken. Aya's stiff posture vanished as she fell against me, laying her head on my shoulder. Medea was suddenly there, wrapping her arms around us both, sandwiching Aya between us.

When I first set out on this path, the moment I awoke to consciousness and realized where I was, my ambitions were never so great as those commonly associated with devils. I wanted freedom in a world who counted different flavors of slavery amongst its various factions' practices. I wanted my own home in a world where ancient bloodlines ruled and anything lesser needed to scrape and beg for anything more.

I never wanted to rise to be the strongest power in the world. I never wanted to step onto the supernatural stage as a force equal to pantheons. All I wanted, all I truly wanted, was what I'd never been able to find in my first life.

I wanted peace. I wanted a partner. I wanted love. I wanted a family. I wanted a future with that family.

Medea and I had talked about children, but that was something that would happen in the future. The future. Some far-off, ephemeral concept that didn't truly exist. It never felt real. All I could see was the immediate danger poised to strike against everything I had built.

In an instant, the illusory dream of my future became real. I held in my arms everything I'd ever wanted in both of my lives.

There were tears in my eyes. I blinked them away, holding Aya and Medea tight.

Time lost meaning. I stood there basking in a euphoric realization that I had everything I could have ever wanted. I only came back to reality as Medea and Aya slowly pulled away. I didn't want to let them go, but holding the two of them in a crushing hug for all eternity didn't seem practical.

As we parted, I looked over Aya's icy body again. I could feel the mixture of mine and Medea's power permeating her form, but why was she ice? I didn't recall Medea telling me she was pregnant when I last saw her a little over an hour ago. Even if she had, while I wasn't a biologist, I doubted the result of such a thing would be a fully grown ice woman.

I looked between Aya and Medea. "How…?" I couldn't think of how to phrase my question. Luckily, Medea understood.

"Zenith Tempest," Medea said, smiling softly as she looked at Aya. "When I added it to the castle, the spirit born from Annihilation Maker and Dimension Lost changed, became…more."

"I am…not the castle as I once was, though I may still command and control it as if I were. It is hard to describe." Aya said, her voice an echoing whisper that barely reached your ears.

My smile faded as I followed that line of logic. "Wait, does that mean the castle has the Sacred Gears, or do you?"

Aya met my eyes. She raised her right hand. A small dog the size of a tiny child's toy appeared in her hand. It was made of red, twisted shadows. The dog yipped, wagging its tail as it hopped around in her hand.

"We share them. It is…hard to explain. We were joined when the Sacred Gears were bound to us. I retain their power in this new state just as the castle will still have access to their use." Aya explained. She bent down and let the small dog hop from her hand to the castle floor.

The dog kept barking happily. Its barks grew louder as it grew in size. When it was the size of a fully grown german shepherd, its growth halted. The dog paused, sniffing at the air. One of Medea's shadowy cat familiars peeked out from the arch leading down a hall. The dog yelped happily, claws scratching against the ground as it chased Medea's familiar down the hall.

"What's wrong?" Medea asked, stepping up next to me and laying a hand on my shoulder.

While she and Aya had watched the dog, I stared at the floor deep in thought, a frown on my face.

If Aya were the one in control of the Sacred Gears, I might need to change my plan. I didn't want my daughter's first act in the world to be one of genocide.

As I went to reply to Medea, a new figure appeared in a flash of pink energy.

"Balthazar," Serafall greeted hurriedly. Like when I left our meeting, she was wearing her dark armor. "Are you ready to… Hello," Serafall said, looking up at Aya.

Aya lifted the sides of her icy dress as she dipped into a shallow curtsy. "Hello, Serafall Leviathan. I am glad to properly meet you."

Serafall slowly turned to look at me. "Did you somehow get a third Bishop and recruit another inter-pantheon incident in the time since I last saw you like fifteen minutes ago?"

I smiled, wide and proud. I walked up next to Aya and wrapped an arm around her shoulders, pulling her into my side. Aya looked away shyly.

"Serafall," I said. "Meet Aya. My daughter."

Serafall stared straight at me. There was no change in her expression for several seconds. Finally, she robotically turned to look at Aya like her head was an ungreased joint. Her eyes flashed with an analysis spell.

Serafall's jaw fell open. "How the…" She trailed off, a bright smile slowly overtaking her face. "Aya-chan!" Serafall screeched.

I was knocked to the side, unable to react in time as Serafall turned into a blur. She scooped Aya up into her arms and held her to the sky like a baboon presenting the new king.

"Hi, Aya-chan! It's good to meet you! I'm your auntie Sera! I'm going to be your babysitter when your mom and dad have date nights! I'll introduce you to my peerage and we'll have so much fun! We're going to watch shows and cosplay and karaoke and eat cake and dance and–"

"Serafall," I cut in, smiling. "Please let her put her feet back on the ground."

Aya looked hopelessly confused about the whole situation. Dangling in the air with Serafall holding her up by her armpits, she looked searchingly at Medea and I, seeking an answer for what to do. I'd help her if I could, but even after spending as much time around her as I had, I'd yet to find a right answer for how to deal with the hurricane of Serafall.

Serafall brought Aya back down and hugged her tight, humming happily. "I wish I could stay here forever."

Serafall frowned, a tired sigh deflating her as she stepped away from Aya. She lightly patted Aya's head. "Sadly, duty calls. Aya, it was lovely meeting you. You and I will sit down sometime and talk about anything and everything. I have to steal your dad for a bit, but we'll be back soon." Looking at me, her expression turned serious. "Are you ready?"

"About that, we might need to alter the plan." I said.

Serafall's eyebrows furrowed. "What do you mean? We're all ready to go."

"Aya has Annihilation Maker, Dimension Lost and Zenith Tempest. Part of her genesis was bound to the Sacred Gears." I answered. Aya said the castle could still use the Sacred Gears, but I didn't know the mechanics of that yet. Did Aya have to okay it? Did the castle using them hurt her? I needed to figure out what I was working with before I unleashed a pantheon-destroying amount of power with the potential to recoil back and hurt my daughter.

Serafall pursed her lips. "Fuck."

I nodded in agreement. "Yes. Fuck."

"I do not see the issue." Aya said, confused. "I heard mother explain the plan to the peerage. I am able to act in the necessary capacity."

I smiled at her, taking her hand. "I appreciate that, honey, but I don't want you to have to do something like this, especially so soon after waking up."

Aya's eyes narrowed. "The angels attacked us. I was not what I am when it happened, but I remember the event. They sought our destruction. They will not stop. This is our opportunity. This will stop them. I have already created the monsters you requested before you left. They stand by for deployment where you directed, father."

"Aya…" I said, trying to articulate what I wanted to say. It was clear Aya was not a typical child. I still didn't have all of the details of her birth, but from what I was gathering, it took more after Medea's Greek, 'born from thought and the will of the world' side of the family than my bare-basic devil lust method. She was far more mature than she should be. I was in a meeting for a couple hours. When I got back, I had a daughter. She wasn't even half-a-day old. Maturity or not, I didn't want to march her to battle.

Aya smiled softly. "I understand your hesitation, father. You do not need to worry about me. I will be fine."

Medea laid a hand on my shoulder. "I won't leave her side."

I shared a serious look with Medea. I saw the same dangerous fire I felt in my chest reflected in her eyes. I took Medea's hand, squeezing her hand. "Don't let anything happen to her."

Medea nodded seriously. A dangerous glint appeared in her eyes. I knew, like me, she would eviscerate anything that hurt Aya.

Serafall watched us all closely. "If you're sure about this…?"

I walked up and hugged Aya. "I'm sorry. This shouldn't be our first family activity. When we're done, we can go on a picnic, okay?"

"I do not resent that we are doing what must be done, father. I look forward to our picnic." Aya said. I could have sworn I heard amusement in her voice.

I took a deep breath, turning back to Serafall. "Let's go."


X


The Silver City. Paradise. Heaven. A place humans dreamed of. A place of pleasures and just rewards for the faithful and deserving. A symbol of hope.

The home of the bastards that tried to kill me.

I was a devil, a creature of revolting sin. Our kind was barred from ever stepping foot in Heaven. Ancient protections laid into the realm's structure by the big man himself blocked our way. Any time the angels needed to deal with devils for one reason or another, a meeting was set in the mortal world on neutral ground. They refused to sully their paradise with our sin.

In Heaven, they were safe. In their Heavenly echo chamber, they could lord over the world, assured that they were righteous and all others had lost their way. None save pure angels could enter Heaven. That was how it had always been and how it would always be.

That's what they thought, what they wrongly assumed. They didn't know about Aqua. They didn't know what Hole and Dimension Lost could do when empowered by a King Piece.

Angels drifted about the Silver City. Some were joyous. Some were saddened. Some were conflicted. Some were stalwart. They prepared for war, for another attack against the hellspawn that dared to sully their creator's great plan.

As one, angels looked to the sky in surprise. They felt a disturbance. They saw something impossible. Something that didn't belong in Heaven was paradoxically here. That was impossible.

Amethyst mist mixed with golden clouds. Dark Holes consumed the shining light of Heaven as they appeared across the entire sky.

Some angels were intelligent. They realized before the rest they were under attack. It didn't help them.

Tailed Beast Bombs rained down from the Holes in the sky. Elemental fire roared forth from the mist in the bombs' wake.

The angels panicked. Some sought shelter. Some erected shields to absorb the attacks. Some shields, those set by Heaven's greatest defenders, held. The rest shattered under the might of mountain-destroying explosions.

The gentle music always able to be heard throughout Heaven was drowned out by thunderous explosions, shaking the air and quaking the ground. Angel screams rose into the air in the wake of the bombs' explosions.

Slowly, the survivors began organizing. They prepared to meet the force that would certainly follow that opening attack.

Then the second wave of Tailed Beast Bombs fell.

Angels clumped together, erecting shields together to better withstand the onslaught. Holes opened beneath their shields, unleashing elemental fire directly on top of them. Their shields failed. The bombs destroyed what the fire didn't burn.

The angels realized more waves would come. They saw that clumping together would lead to targeted attacks from fire. They spread out, shouting over the cacophony of screams and explosions to coordinate as well as they could. As one, they prepared for the next wave of Tailed Beast Bombs.

Holes opened to surround each angel. There were so many points of black in the air that the angels could barely see through the maze of Holes.

High-pitched, horrifying screams filled the air as shadowy lumps burst forth from the Holes. The dark oozes morphed into different forms in midflight. Some turned into long serpents, winding their bodies around angels and stabbing their fangs into the angels' necks. Some turned into bipedal forms, latching onto angels with their hands while their head turned into a gaping jaw with long razor teeth that burrowed into the angels' chests.

"To me, my brothers and sisters!"

Panicked angels looked to the sky. There, sword aimed high, crowned by a golden halo, twelve wings spread wide behind him, Uriel dispatched another of the ooze monsters.

"We will destroy this threat to–"

A lone angel wailed in agony, staring dejectedly where Uriel was just swallowed into a Hole. He was there, a shining beacon of Hope and Light, and then he was gone. There was no trace of him.

The angel wailed again, her pure white wings flashed black as she fell through the clouds, fleeing the monsters raining down on Heaven.

Twelve more oozes fell through the air where Uriel was. The oozes altered their form. One became a winged monstrosity with six legs and arms stretching from its back. It dove into a line of angels, snapping and tearing with its jaws.

"To the Hall!"

Despair-filled angels looked to the new voice. Metatron dodged between Holes and shapeshifting shadows to pull angel after angel from their deaths.

"Michael can use Father's system to protect us there. Move!" Metatron narrowly avoided flying through another Hole, leading the way back to the Hall of Heaven where God's system was strongest.

The angels rallied, fighting their way through the unending downpour of oozes. They formed ranks, cutting through the invaders to protect a group of angels in the midst of the group that erected shields to defend against the unending onslaught of elemental fire. The battle was viscous, but they would rise to the occasion. They were within sight of the Hall. They would make it.

A large Hole opened in their path. A giant creature as tall as a skyscraper fell through the Hole. Sinewy wings spread wide to encompass the sky.

Another angels' wings flashed black as he dove down through the clouds, fleeing in terror.

The monstrous creature laughed as the angel fled. Red muscles like armored rock mixed with shadows snapped taut as the bipedal, demonic monster raised a sword high, striking down towards the angels.

Suddenly, Metatron was there. Metatron caught the demon's sword with his blade of Light.

"Go!" Metatron cried, batting the demon's sword aside and dodging its semi-truck-sized fist. Metatron summoned a column of Light to blast the demon back. "I will buy you time!"

Some angels cried in protest, refusing to leave Metatron alone. They were dragged with the greater group as they desperately rushed for the Hall.

Angels along the outside of the group were pulled from their desperate flight by oozes snatching onto their legs or wings. Angels inside the clump were burned away by elemental fire as they let their guard slip for a moment. They were almost there. Their group was not the only one. Ahead, they could see a group of cherubim holding the door against a tide of ooze monsters, covering angels arriving in pairs or alone. They were regrouping. They could win.

Desperate, the angels at the head of the group tore through the doors, bypassing the cherubim fighting with all they were worth to keep the enemy from the Hall. If they could just get to Michael, he would know what to do.

The angels burst into the Hall, colliding heavily with the backs of their kin. The angels in the room were slowly backing away, wings flashing black then back to white.

An angel flew up to see over the mass. She needed to see what was happening. What she saw caused her to freeze.

Holes were spread throughout the ceiling of the Hall. Columns lay in piles of rubble. The great marble floor was cratered. Four figures flew in the air, defiling this most Holy place.

A dark-haired woman in dark armor, frost clinging to her body. A man with green hair in a dark robe, staring dispassionately at the angels still flooding into the room. A bald man with dark marks on his face and heavy silver pauldrons.

And in the middle, a flickering, humanoid shape of pure destruction drifted. Sirzechs Lucifer held Michael by the throat. Michael's body was limp, wings drooped behind him. There was a hole in his chest.

Sirzechs Lucifer turned to look at the assembled angels. He dropped Michael's body as he floated towards them, flanked by his allies. Together, the Four Satans bore down on the angels.

"They're inside!" someone in the back of the group screamed. A moment later, an ooze enveloped their body, dragging them to the ground.

Amidst the screaming and roar of flames, angels shoved against one-another. Those who saw the Satans, who witnessed the death of Michael, desperately tried to flee, their wings flickering black. Those who were stuck outside, desperately pushed back against their brethren, fleeing the oozes for what they believed to be the safety of the Hall.

More and more angels fell, taken by ooze, by fire, or by ice.

Other angels Fell. They dove through the clouds, fleeing Heaven and leaving it to its fate. Some justified it to themselves, saying that this way, Heaven would carry on. Others simply wanted to live.

Fire rained from the sky of Heaven, washing over the meager resistance still existing amongst Heaven's defenders.

Metatron was the last left standing. As he fell, he fell atop a pile of his enemies.

Sirzechs Lucifer stepped up to Michael's throne, the throne once reserved for Heaven's creator. He raised his hand.

The Throne of Heaven was consumed by a wave of pure Destruction.

"God," Serafall Leviathan said experimentally. When none of the Satans flinched in pain as they had since birth whenever the name of Heaven's Lord was spoken in their presence, Serafall grinned evilly. "The system's gone."

"Heaven will fall without it." Ajuka Beelzebub said, detached. "It is time we left."

"You hear that, Bal?" Serafall asked, looking up.

"I'm listening," My voice spoke from every Hole around them. "Just walk through any Hole you want. I'll bring you all back here. I still have Uriel trapped. What do you want me to do with him?"

"We'll deal with that later." Sirzechs said, watching as the Hall of Heaven began to unravel around them. Soon, Heaven would collapse into nothing. "We need to leave."

Together, the Four Satans walked through a Hole, departing Heaven as it crumbled in their wake.
